IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolyRadiusdef

noncomputable def dhPolyRadius (Ω : Set (∀ i, X i)) (i : ι) : ENNReal :=
  ⨆ x ∈ Ω, ENNReal.ofReal ‖x i‖

The polyradius of a region Ω ⊆ ∏ X i (§6.1 of the Szpiro paper): its i-th component is R_i(Ω) = sup {|x_i| : x ∈ Ω}, taken in [0, ∞] so that it is defined for every region.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolydiscdef

def dhPolydisc (r : ι → ENNReal) : Set (∀ i, X i) :=
  {x | ∀ i, ENNReal.ofReal ‖x i‖ ≤ r i}

The closed polydisc D(0, r) = {x | |x_i| ≤ r_i for all i} of polyradius r.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhHulldef

noncomputable def dhHull (Ω : Set (∀ i, X i)) : Set (∀ i, X i) :=
  dhPolydisc (dhPolyRadius Ω)

The hull of a region (§6.1): the polydisc of its polyradius, hull(Ω) = D(0, R(Ω)).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_subset_hulltheorem

theorem dh_subset_hull (Ω : Set (∀ i, X i)) : Ω ⊆ dhHull Ω

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolyRadius_monotheorem

theorem dhPolyRadius_mono {Ω Ω' : Set (∀ i, X i)} (h : Ω ⊆ Ω') (i : ι) :
  dhPolyRadius Ω i ≤ dhPolyRadius Ω' i

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolyRadius_polydisc_letheorem

theorem dhPolyRadius_polydisc_le (r : ι → ENNReal) (i : ι) :
  dhPolyRadius (dhPolydisc (X := X) r) i ≤ r i

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhHull_polydisctheorem

theorem dhHull_polydisc (r : ι → ENNReal) : dhHull (dhPolydisc (X := X) r) = dhPolydisc r

The hull of a polydisc is the polydisc itself, whether or not its radii are attained.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhHull_isHullMaptheorem

theorem dhHull_isHullMap :
  IsHullMap Set.univ (Set.range (dhPolydisc (X := X))) (dhHull (X := X))

The polydisc hull satisfies the conditions (P1), (P2), (P3) of IUT III Remark 3.9.5 (ii), with all regions as ℙ and the polydiscs as ℍ.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolyRadius_iUniontheorem

theorem dhPolyRadius_iUnion {κ : Type*} (Ω : κ → Set (∀ i, X i)) (j : ι) :
  dhPolyRadius (⋃ k, Ω k) j = ⨆ k, dhPolyRadius (Ω k) j

The j-th radius of a union is the supremum of the j-th radii (§6.1, possibly ∞).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhPolyRadius_multheorem

theorem dhPolyRadius_mul (α : ∀ i, X i) (Ω : Set (∀ i, X i)) (i : ι) :
  dhPolyRadius ((fun x => α * x) '' Ω) i = ENNReal.ofReal ‖α i‖ * dhPolyRadius Ω i

Scaling (§6.1): for α ∈ ∏ X i, R_i(α · Ω) = |α_i| · R_i(Ω).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhDiagMapdef

noncomputable def dhDiagMap : (Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) →ₗ[ℚ_[p]] (Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) :=
  Matrix.toLin' (Matrix.diagonal ![(p : ℚ_[p]), (p : ℚ_[p])⁻¹])

The ℚ_p-linear map diag(p, p⁻¹) of ℚ_p².

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhDiagMap_det_normtheorem

theorem dhDiagMap_det_norm : ‖LinearMap.det (dhDiagMap p)‖ = 1

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_det_one_not_hull_subsettheorem

theorem dh_det_one_not_hull_subset :
  ‖LinearMap.det (dhDiagMap p)‖ = 1 ∧
    (dhDiagMap p) '' dhPolydisc (fun _ => 1) ⊆ (dhDiagMap p) '' dhPolydisc (fun _ => 1) ∧
    ¬ dhHull (dhPolydisc (X := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) (fun _ => 1)) ⊆
      dhHull ((dhDiagMap p) '' dhPolydisc (fun _ => 1))

The sufficient condition of §6.1 of the Szpiro paper, as printed, fails (page 19, a sentence rather than a numbered display): "A ⊂~ B if there exists some ℚ_p-linear transformation T : L → L with |det(T)|_p = 1 and T(A) ⊂ B", where L is a finite direct sum of p-adic fields and A ⊂~ B means hull(A) ⊂ hull(B). On L = ℚ_p ⊕ ℚ_p, with T = diag(p, p⁻¹), A the unit polydisc and B = T(A), the hull of A is not contained in the hull of B. This T is multiplication by the invertible element (p, p⁻¹) of L; for a unit of O_L the paper's example holds (dhPolyRadius_mul). The itemized justifications of (6.3) to (6.8) do not cite this condition; whether a later step relies on it implicitly was not determined.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_exp_one_mul_log_lttheorem

theorem dh_exp_one_mul_log_lt (hp2 : 2 ≤ p) : Real.exp 1 * Real.log p < p

e · ln p < p for every natural number p ≥ 2; equivalently c_p = (e ln p)⁻¹ > 1 / p.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_mul_le_powtheorem

theorem dh_mul_le_pow {k : ℕ} (hp2 : 2 ≤ p) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : p * k ≤ p ^ k

p · k ≤ p ^ k for p ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_log_units_subset_disctheorem

theorem dh_log_units_subset_disc :
  Set.range (fun u : ℤ_[p]ˣ => padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p])) ⊆
    {z : ℚ_[p] | ‖z‖ ≤ (Real.log p * Real.exp 1)⁻¹}

**Lemma 4.2.3 (1) of the Szpiro paper for K = ℚ_p** (so e(K/ℚ_p) = 1): log(ℤ_p^×) ⊆ D(0, 1 / (ln(p) · exp(1))).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_crude_log_estimatetheorem

theorem dh_crude_log_estimate {a : ℚ_[p]} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hv : 1 < a.valuation) :
  ‖padicLogOnePlus p a‖ < (Real.exp 1 * Real.log p)⁻¹ / a.valuation

**Lemma 4.2.1 of the Szpiro paper (crude estimate) for a ∈ ℚ_p**: if ord_p(a) > 1, then |log(1 + a)|_p < c_p / ord_p(a) with c_p = (exp(1) ln(p))⁻¹. The paper states it for a ∈ ℂ_p; here a ∈ ℚ_p ⊆ ℂ_p and ord_p is Padic.valuation.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhQPilotDegreeOfDatadef

noncomputable def dhQPilotDegreeOfData (l : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (d0 : ℝ)) * ∑ v ∈ S, (ordq v : ℝ) / (2 * l) * inertia v * Real.log (resChar v)

The normalized degree of the q-pilot divisor of Definition 3.8.1, computed from given data: a finite set S of bad places v of F_0 with ord_v(q_v), the inertia degree f_v, the residue characteristic p_v, d_0 = [F_0 : ℚ] and the prime l: deĝ(P_q) = (1/d_0) Σ_{v ∈ S} (ord_v(q_v)/(2l)) f_v ln p_v. Nothing here asserts that the numbers come from Tate parameters of an elliptic curve.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhThetaPilotDegreeOfDatadef

noncomputable def dhThetaPilotDegreeOfData (l j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (d0 : ℝ)) * ∑ v ∈ S, (j : ℝ) ^ 2 * ordq v / (2 * l) * inertia v * Real.log (resChar v)

The normalized degree of the j-th component P_{Θ,j} of the theta pilot divisor of Definition 3.8.2, from the same data: coefficients ord_v(q_v^{j²/2l}) = j² ord_v(q_v)/(2l).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhThetaPilotLgpDegreeOfDatadef

noncomputable def dhThetaPilotLgpDegreeOfData (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / (n : ℝ)) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, dhThetaPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 (2 * n + 1) j

The label average deĝ_lgp(P_Θ) = (2/(l−1)) Σ_{j=1}^{(l−1)/2} deĝ(P_{Θ,j}) for l = 2n + 1, so that 2/(l−1) = 1/n.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhThetaPilotDegreeOfData_eqtheorem

theorem dhThetaPilotDegreeOfData_eq (l j : ℕ) :
  dhThetaPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 l j =
    (j : ℝ) ^ 2 * dhQPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 l

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_sum_sqtheorem

theorem dh_sum_sq (n : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ((j : ℝ) ^ 2) = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) / 6

Σ_{j=1}^n j² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhThetaPilotLgp_eq_mul_qPilottheorem

theorem dhThetaPilotLgp_eq_mul_qPilot {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  dhThetaPilotLgpDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 n =
    ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) * ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 1) / 12) *
      dhQPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 (2 * n + 1)

The relation between the pilots (§3.8, derived direction): for l = 2n + 1, deĝ_lgp(P_Θ) = (l(l+1)/12) · deĝ(P_q).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_printed_pilot_relation_forces_zerotheorem

theorem dh_printed_pilot_relation_forces_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
  (h : dhQPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 (2 * n + 1) =
    ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) * ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 1) / 12) *
      dhThetaPilotLgpDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 n) :
  dhQPilotDegreeOfData S ordq inertia resChar d0 (2 * n + 1) = 0

Display (3.3) of the Szpiro paper as printed (§3.8, page 14) reads deĝ(P_q) = (l(l+1)/12) deĝ_lgp(P_Θ), the factor on the other side from the computation printed directly below it, which gives deĝ_lgp(P_Θ) = (l(l+1)/12) deĝ(P_q) (dhThetaPilotLgp_eq_mul_qPilot). Together with the derived relation the display as printed forces deĝ(P_q) = 0 as soon as l ≥ 5. The display as printed differs from the derived relation; the proof of Theorem 7.12.1 (page 28), the left side of (8.9) and Remark 3.8.3 use the derived relation, so the paper's conclusions do not depend on the display as printed, as far as the text shows.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_qPilot_11a1theorem

theorem dh_qPilot_11a1 :
  dhQPilotDegreeOfData ({11} : Finset ℕ) (fun _ => 5) (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 11) 1 13 =
    Real.log (11 ^ 5) / (2 * 13)

The curve 11a1 (§2.10 of the initial theta data paper): with F_0 = ℚ, the single bad place 11, ord_{11}(q) = 5, f = 1 and l = 13, the q-pilot degree is ln(11⁵)/(2 · 13), that is ln|Δ^min_{E/ℚ}|/(2l) for the minimal discriminant Δ = −11⁵.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_invariants_11a1theorem

theorem dh_invariants_11a1 :
  ((496 : ℤ) ^ 3 - 20008 ^ 2) = 1728 * (-(11 ^ 5)) ∧
    ((496 : ℚ) ^ 3 / (-(11 ^ 5)) = -(2 ^ 12 * 31 ^ 3) / 11 ^ 5)

The invariants of 11a1 recorded in §2.10: c_4 = 496, c_6 = 20008 give Δ = (c_4³ − c_6²)/1728 = −11⁵ and j = c_4³/Δ = −2¹² 31³ / 11⁵.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_congruence_11a1theorem

theorem dh_congruence_11a1 :
  ¬ 13 ∣ 11 ∧ ¬ 13 ∣ 5 ∧ 5 ≤ 13 ∧ 2 * 6 * 48 * 480 = 276480 ∧
    ∀ d, d ∣ 276480 → ¬ 13 ∣ d

The congruence conditions of pre theta data for 11a1 with l = 13 (§2.10): 13 ∤ 11, 13 ∤ ord(q) = 5, 13 ≥ 5, and 13 divides no divisor of 276480 = 2 · 6 · 48 · 480, the bound for [F : ℚ] read off from the table of |GL_2(F_r)|, r = 2, 3, 5, and the adjunction of √−1.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_card_Icc_onetheorem

theorem dh_card_Icc_one (n : ℕ) : ((Icc 1 n).card : ℝ) = n

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_avg_le_of_letheorem

theorem dh_avg_le_of_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {f : ℕ → ℝ} {c : ℝ}
  (h : ∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, f j ≤ c) : 1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, f j ≤ c

An average over j ∈ {1, …, n} of terms bounded by c is bounded by c.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_avg_idtheorem

theorem dh_avg_id {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, (j : ℝ) = ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 1) / 4

(1/n) Σ_{j=1}^n j = (n+1)/2, which is (l+1)/4 for l = 2n + 1 (§7.7).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_avg_succtheorem

theorem dh_avg_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ((j : ℝ) + 1) = ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 5) / 4

(1/n) Σ_{j=1}^n (j+1) = (n+3)/2, which is (l+5)/4 for l = 2n + 1 (§7.9, §7.10, §7.11).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_l1_sub_linf_letheorem

theorem dh_l1_sub_linf_le {κ : Type*} (s : Finset κ) (hs : s.Nonempty) (a : κ → ℝ) {M : ℝ}
  (hM : ∀ i ∈ s, a i ≤ M) :
  ∑ i ∈ s, a i - M ≤ ((s.card : ℝ) - 1) / s.card * ∑ i ∈ s, a i

Lemma 7.7.1 (1) of the Szpiro paper, in the form used: for a finite family a with an upper bound M (for instance M = ‖a‖_∞), ‖a‖_1 − M ≤ ((n−1)/n) ‖a‖_1 where n is the number of terms. Nonnegativity is not needed.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_avg_one_sub_pow_letheorem

theorem dh_avg_one_sub_pow_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ P) (h1 : P ≤ 1) :
  1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, (1 - P ^ (j + 1)) ≤ 1 - P ^ (n + 1)

Display (7.11) of the Szpiro paper (§7.8, page 26; the ramification term III_p): for 0 ≤ P ≤ 1, (1/n) Σ_{j=1}^n (1 − P^{j+1}) ≤ 1 − P^{n+1}, with n + 1 = (l+1)/2.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_log_bp_negtheorem

theorem dh_log_bp_neg {x : ℝ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) : Real.log ((Real.exp 1 * Real.log x)⁻¹) < 0

ln b_p < 0 for every x ≥ 2, where b_x = 1/(exp(1) ln x) (§1, §6.3).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_log_bp_le_neg_twotheorem

theorem dh_log_bp_le_neg_two {x : ℝ} (hx : 16 ≤ x) :
  Real.log ((Real.exp 1 * Real.log x)⁻¹) ≤ -2

ln b_p ≤ −2 for every x ≥ 16.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_IV_boundtheorem

theorem dh_IV_bound {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {P lb : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ P) (h1 : P ≤ 1) (hlb : lb ≤ 0) :
  lb * (1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ((j : ℝ) + 1) * (1 - P ^ (j + 1))) ≤
    ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 5) / 4 * lb * (1 - P ^ 2)

The correct direction of the bound on IV_p (§7.9 of the Szpiro paper, where display (7.12) prints the other factor): since ln b_p ≤ 0, enlarging the factor 1 − P^{j+1} bounds IV_p from below; the bound from above uses the smallest factor 1 − P²: ln(b) · (1/n) Σ (j+1)(1 − P^{j+1}) ≤ ((l+5)/4) ln(b) (1 − P²).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_IV_printed_bound_failstheorem

theorem dh_IV_printed_bound_fails {lb : ℝ} (hlb : lb < 0) :
  ((2 * 3 + 1 : ℝ) + 5) / 4 * lb * (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (3 + 1)) <
    lb * (1 / (3 : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ (Icc 1 3 : Finset ℕ),
      ((j : ℝ) + 1) * (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1)))

Display (7.12) of the Szpiro paper as printed fails (§7.9, page 26): IV_p ≤ ((l+5)/4) ln(b_p)(1 − P_unr,p^{l+1/2}), the exponent printed verbatim as l+1/2, where the paper computes IV_p = ln(b_p) (2/(l−1)) Σ_{j=1}^{(l−1)/2} (j+1)(1 − P^{j+1}). Here the exponent is read as (l+1)/2 = n + 1, the exponent of Theorem 7.12.1; the exponent exactly as printed, l + 1/2, is treated in dh_IV_printed_exponent_bound_fails. With l = 7 (n = 3; by inference the smallest admissible prime, see the module docstring), P_unr = 1/2 and any ln b < 0, the value (21/8) ln b of IV_p exceeds the right side (45/16) ln b. ln b_p < 0 for every prime with b_p = (e ln p)⁻¹ (dh_log_bp_neg), and for p ≤ 13 under the other parse of b_p. Values 0 < P_unr,p < 1 need F_0 ≠ ℚ; whether they occur is not examined. The proof of Theorem 7.12.1 uses (7.12) in its first display; the correct upper bound is dh_IV_bound.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_IV_printed_exponent_bound_failstheorem

theorem dh_IV_printed_exponent_bound_fails {lb : ℝ} (hlb : lb < 0) :
  ((2 * 3 + 1 : ℝ) + 5) / 4 * lb * (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 * 3 + 1 : ℝ) + 1 / 2)) <
    lb * (1 / (3 : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ (Icc 1 3 : Finset ℕ),
      ((j : ℝ) + 1) * (1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1)))

Display (7.12) of the Szpiro paper as printed, with the exponent exactly as printed, fails (§7.9, page 26): IV_p ≤ ((l+5)/4) ln(b_p)(1 − P_unr,p^{l+1/2}), with l + 1/2 a real exponent. With l = 7, P_unr = 1/2 and any ln b < 0, the value (21/8) ln b of IV_p exceeds the right side 3 (1 − 2^{−15/2}) ln b ≈ 2.9834 ln b (at ln b = ln b_11 ≈ −1.8746: −4.92 against −5.59). The same provisos as for dh_IV_printed_bound_fails apply.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_combined_bound_failstheorem

theorem dh_combined_bound_fails {lb : ℝ} (hlb : lb ≤ -2) :
  (1 - (9 / 10 : ℝ) ^ (3 + 1)) * (lb + 5 / ((2 * 3 + 1 : ℝ) + 4)) <
    4 / ((2 * 3 + 1 : ℝ) + 5) *
      (1 / (3 : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ (Icc 1 3 : Finset ℕ),
        (1 - (9 / 10 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1)) * (1 + ((j : ℝ) + 1) * lb))

**The step from the four terms to the summand of A_{l,V} in the proof of Theorem 7.12.1 fails at l = 7, P_unr = 9/10, p ≥ 17** (pages 27 to 28). This is not a numbered display: it is the passage, through (7.11), (7.12) and the division by (l+5)/4, from the exact terms to the summand of A_{l,V} in (7.15). The proof turns III_p + IV_p, whose exact values the paper prints in §7.8 and §7.9 as (2/(l−1)) Σ_j (1 − P^{j+1}) and ln(b_p)(2/(l−1)) Σ_j (j+1)(1 − P^{j+1}), into the summand (1 − P^{(l+1)/2})(ln b_p + 5/(l+4)) of A_{l,V}. With l = 7 (by inference the smallest admissible prime), P_unr = 9/10 and ln b ≤ −2 (true for every prime p ≥ 17 with b_p = (e ln p)⁻¹, dh_log_bp_le_neg_two), (4/(l+5))(III_p + IV_p) is larger than that summand. Values 0 < P_unr,p < 1 need F_0 ≠ ℚ; whether they occur is not examined. The theorem concerns this one step only; it says nothing about Theorem 7.12.1 itself.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_combined_bound_P_zerotheorem

theorem dh_combined_bound_P_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (lb : ℝ) :
  4 / ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 5) *
      (1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, (1 - (0 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1)) * (1 + ((j : ℝ) + 1) * lb)) ≤
    (1 - (0 : ℝ) ^ (n + 1)) * (lb + 5 / ((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 4))

For P_unr = 0 (every place over p ramified) the step to the summand of A_{l,V} holds for every l = 2n + 1 and every ln b. (For F_0 = ℚ, P_unr ∈ {0, 1}; the case P_unr = 1 is not treated here.)

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_coeff_sixtheorem

theorem dh_coeff_six {l : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l) :
  (l * (l + 1) / 12 - 1) * (1 / (2 * l)) * (4 / (l + 5)) =
    1 / (6 + 24 * (l + 3) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12))

The coefficient identity of the proof of Theorem 7.12.1: (l(l+1)/12 − 1) (1/(2l)) (4/(l+5)) = 1/(6 + ε_l) with ε_l = 24(l+3)/(l² + l − 12).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_coeff_twentyfourtheorem

theorem dh_coeff_twentyfour {l : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l) :
  (l * (l + 1) / 12 - 1) * (1 / (2 * l)) * (1 / (l + 5)) =
    1 / (24 + 96 * (l + 3) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12))

The coefficient identity of the proof of Theorem 8.2.1: (l(l+1)/12 − 1) (1/(2l)) (1/(l+5)) = 1/(24 + ε_l) with ε_l = 96(l+3)/(l² + l − 12).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_probSzpiro_of_intermediatetheorem

theorem dh_probSzpiro_of_intermediate {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {l : ℝ} (hl : l = 2 * n + 1)
  (S : Finset ℕ) (Punr logb loge : ℕ → ℝ) {logDiff X dq dθ : ℝ}
  (hP0 : ∀ p ∈ S, 0 ≤ Punr p) (hP1 : ∀ p ∈ S, Punr p ≤ 1) (hD : 0 ≤ logDiff)
  (hθ : dθ = l * (l + 1) / 12 * dq) (hq : dq = X / (2 * l))
  (hinter : -dq ≤ -dθ + (l + 1) / 4 * logDiff +
    ∑ p ∈ S, (1 - Punr p ^ (n + 1)) * (1 + (l + 5) / 4 * logb p) +
    (l + 5) / 4 * ∑ p ∈ S, loge p + (l + 5) / 4 * Real.log Real.pi) :
  1 / (6 + 24 * (l + 3) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12)) * X ≤
    logDiff + ∑ p ∈ S, loge p +
      (Real.log Real.pi + ∑ p ∈ S, (1 - Punr p ^ (n + 1)) * (logb p + 5 / (l + 4)))

The final algebra of the proof of Theorem 7.12.1 (Probabilistic Szpiro), conditional. Hypotheses: hθ, hq: the pilot relations deĝ_lgp(P_Θ) = (l(l+1)/12) deĝ(P_q) (dhThetaPilotLgp_eq_mul_qPilot) and deĝ(P_q) = X/(2l) with X = ln|Δ^min_{E/F}|/[F:ℚ] (display (3.2), which rests on Tate uniformization, Ogg's formula and Lemma 3.6.1, none of which is formalized); hinter: the first display of the proof (page 28, unnumbered), which the paper obtains from Theorem 7.5.1, Lemma 6.3.1, Claim 5.0.1 and the bounds (7.6), (7.8), (7.11), (7.12) and (7.14), with Σ_p over a finite set S, logDiff = ln Diff̄(V̲/ℚ), Punr p = P_{unr,p}, logb p = ln b_p, loge p = ln ē_p. The display prints the exponent verbatim as l+1/2, in (1 − P_unr,p^{l+1/2}); hinter reads it as (l+1)/2 = n + 1, the exponent of (7.15), under which the final algebra closes (with l + 1/2 taken literally, the passage to (7.15) at a prime with ln b_p + 4/(l+5) > 0 would need 1 − P^{l+1/2} ≤ 1 − P^{(l+1)/2}, which goes the other way). The side conditions hP0, hP1 (0 ≤ P_{unr,p} ≤ 1) and hD (ln Diff̄ ≥ 0) hold by definition and are not displays of the paper. Conclusion: display (7.15) of Theorem 7.12.1 as printed, with 5/(l+4). No hypothesis restates the conclusion; the theorem checks only the final algebra and says nothing about whether hinter holds or about Theorem 7.12.1 itself. The paper derives hinter using display (7.12), whose printed form fails when 0 < P_{unr,p} < 1 (dh_IV_printed_bound_fails).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_exp_eight_lttheorem

theorem dh_exp_eight_lt : Real.exp 8 < 6840

exp 8 < 6840, so ln 6840 > 8: the threshold e⁸ ≈ 2981 is what the last step of the proof of Theorem 7.13.1 (Baby Szpiro) needs.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_baby_final_steptheorem

theorem dh_baby_final_step {D d : ℝ} (hD : Real.exp 8 ≤ D) (hd : Real.exp 8 ≤ d) :
  Real.log (D * d) + Real.log D * Real.log d + Real.log D ≤
      (Real.log D + 2) * (Real.log d + 2) ∧
    (Real.log D + 2) * (Real.log d + 2) ≤
      Real.log (d ^ (5 / 4 : ℝ)) * Real.log (D ^ (5 / 4 : ℝ))

The last step of the proof of Theorem 7.13.1 (Baby Szpiro) (page 29): for D, d ≥ e⁸, ln(Dd) + ln(D) ln(d) + ln(D) ≤ (ln D + 2)(ln d + 2) ≤ ln(d^{5/4}) ln(D^{5/4}), with D = |Disc(K/ℚ)| and d = [K:ℚ]. The paper asserts D, d ≥ |SL_2(F_l)| ≥ 6840; see dh_SL2_card_values. Whether D, d ≥ e⁸ holds for every curve in the paper's setting was not determined.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_SL2_card_valuestheorem

theorem dh_SL2_card_values :
  5 * (5 ^ 2 - 1) = 120 ∧ 7 * (7 ^ 2 - 1) = 336 ∧ 11 * (11 ^ 2 - 1) = 1320 ∧
    13 * (13 ^ 2 - 1) = 2184 ∧ 17 * (17 ^ 2 - 1) = 4896 ∧ 19 * (19 ^ 2 - 1) = 6840 ∧
    ∀ l : ℕ, l ≤ 18 → l * (l ^ 2 - 1) < 6840

**The claim "SL_2(F_l) ≥ 6840" of the proof of Theorem 7.13.1 as printed** (page 29, a sentence rather than a numbered display). This theorem proves the arithmetic of l(l² − 1) only: it takes the values 120, 336, 1320, 2184, 4896, 6840 at l = 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, and is below 6840 for every l ≤ 18. The formula |SL_2(F_l)| = l(l² − 1) is standard and is not proved here. With it, the group-order bound holds only from l = 19 on, so it fails for l = 7, 11, 13, 17 (inside the range l ≥ 7, itself an inference; see the module docstring), including the value l = 13 of the 11a1 example. The step that follows needs only D, d ≥ e⁸ (dh_exp_eight_lt, dh_baby_final_step); whether the conclusion depends on the printed claim beyond that was not determined.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_omega_printed_bound_failstheorem

theorem dh_omega_printed_bound_fails {N : ℕ} (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
  Real.log N / Real.log N ^ 2 < (N.divisors.card : ℝ) ∧
    Real.log N / Real.log N ^ 2 < (N.primeFactors.card : ℝ)

**The bound "ω(N) ≤ ln(N)/ln²(N)" of the proof of Theorem 7.13.1 as printed** (page 29, an unnumbered display after (7.19) and (7.20)), with ln²(N) = (ln N)², **fails for every N ≥ 3**, both for the number of divisors (the definition of ω printed there) and for the number of distinct prime factors: the right side is 1/ln N < 1. For the iterated-logarithm reading see dh_omega_loglog_bound_fails. The next step of the proof needs only ω(D) ≤ ln D; for the number of distinct prime factors this holds for D ≥ 7 (not formalized here), for the number of divisors it does not (D = 12). So the conclusion of Theorem 7.13.1 does not rest on the printed bound, as far as the text shows, provided ω counts distinct prime factors.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_omega_loglog_bound_failstheorem

theorem dh_omega_loglog_bound_fails :
  Real.log 210 / Real.log (Real.log 210) < ((210 : ℕ).primeFactors.card : ℝ) ∧
    Real.log 210 / Real.log (Real.log 210) < ((210 : ℕ).divisors.card : ℝ)

**The bound "ω(N) ≤ ln(N)/ln²(N)" of the proof of Theorem 7.13.1 as printed, read with ln²(N) = ln ln N, also fails**: at N = 210 = 2 · 3 · 5 · 7, ln 210 / ln ln 210 < 4, while 210 has four distinct prime factors and sixteen divisors.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_GL2_card_letheorem

theorem dh_GL2_card_le (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] :
  Nat.card (GL (Fin 2) (ZMod l)) ≤ l ^ 4 ∧ 48 * 480 = 23040 ∧ 23040 * 12 = 276480

The group orders in Lemma 8.1.1: |GL_2(F_l)| ≤ l⁴, and the constants of the tower: |GL_2(F_3)| · |GL_2(F_5)| = 48 · 480 = 23040 (for F/F_2'), 12 (for F_2'/F_0) and 23040 · 12 = 276480.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_explicit_pre_resulttheorem

theorem dh_explicit_pre_result {l X Fdeg LD LC Ssmall Slarge Sinf logB Pi : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l)
  (hF : 0 < Fdeg) (hPi : 0 ≤ Pi) (hlogB : 1 / 2 ≤ logB)
  (hred : (l * (l + 1) / 12 - 1) * (1 / (2 * l)) * (X / Fdeg) ≤ Ssmall + Slarge + Sinf)
  (hsmall : Ssmall ≤ ((l + 3) * logB + 1) * Pi)
  (hlarge : Slarge ≤ (l + 5) / 2 * (2 * (LD / Fdeg + LC / Fdeg)))
  (hinf : Sinf ≤ (l + 5) / 4 * Real.log Real.pi) :
  1 / (24 + 96 * (l + 3) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12)) * X ≤
    (logB * Pi + Real.log Real.pi) * Fdeg + LD + LC

Display (8.10) of the proof of Theorem 8.2.1 (Explicit Szpiro), conditional (page 35). Hypotheses: hred is (8.9) with its left side rewritten through the pilot relations and its right side split into the three sums, as printed on page 35; hsmall is the penultimate line of the proof of (8.7) (page 34), ((l+3) ln B + 1) π(B), whose +1 the printed last line drops; hlarge is the per-prime bound ((l+5)/2) ln(p) 1_ram(p) that ends the proof of (8.4) (page 32; the printed (8.4) has (l+5)/4), summed and combined with (8.5), as on page 35; hinf is (8.3) (page 31). The side conditions hl, hF, hPi and hlogB (ln B ≥ 1/2, true for B = 276480 l⁴ d_0) are not displays. No hypothesis restates the conclusion; the +1 is absorbed after division by l + 5. Variables: X = ln|Δ^min_{E/F}|, Fdeg = [F:ℚ], LD = ln|Disc(F/ℚ)|, LC = ln|Cond(E/F)|, Pi = π(B), logB = ln B; Ssmall, Slarge, Sinf are the three sums of E²_p.

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_explicit_constanttheorem

theorem dh_explicit_constant {l d0 Fdeg Pi B : ℝ} (hl : 1 ≤ l) (hd0 : 1 ≤ d0) (hF0 : 0 ≤ Fdeg)
  (hF : Fdeg ≤ 276480 * d0) (hB : B = l ^ 4 * 276480 * d0)
  (hDusart : Pi ≤ B / Real.log B * (1 + 1.3 / Real.log B)) :
  (Real.log B * Pi + Real.log Real.pi) * Fdeg ≤
    276480 ^ 2 * (1 + 1.3 / Real.log 276480) * d0 ^ 2 * l ^ 4 +
      276480 * Real.log Real.pi * d0

The last bound of the proof of Theorem 8.2.1 (page 35), with Dusart's estimate, display (8.8), taken at the one point x = B as an explicit hypothesis (hDusart: π(B) ≤ (B/ln B)(1 + 1.3/ln B), Dusart, Ramanujan J. 45 (2018)) and [F:ℚ] ≤ d_1 d_0 with d_1 = 276480 (the bound on [F:F_0] of Lemma 8.1.1): (ln(B) π(B) + ln π)[F:ℚ] ≤ d_1² (1 + 1.3/ln d_1) d_0² l⁴ + d_1 ln(π) d_0 for B = l⁴ d_1 d_0. The middle expression printed on page 35 multiplies ln π by l⁴ d_0 as well; the final line A_0 d_0² l⁴ + B_0 d_0 follows from the form proved here, not from that middle expression. The paper's A_0 = 84372107405 and B_0 = 316495 are the ceilings of the two coefficients (a decimal computation, not proved here).

IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dh_explicit_exptheorem

theorem dh_explicit_exp {Δ Cond Disc ε C : ℝ} (hΔ : 0 < Δ) (hC : 0 < Cond) (hD : 0 < Disc)
  (hε : 0 < 24 + ε) (h : 1 / (24 + ε) * Real.log Δ ≤ C + Real.log Disc + Real.log Cond) :
  Δ ≤ Real.exp ((24 + ε) * C) * (Cond * Disc) ^ (24 + ε)

Exponentiating (8.10): if (1/(24+ε)) ln|Δ| ≤ C + ln|Disc| + ln|Cond|, then |Δ| ≤ exp((24+ε) C) · (|Cond| · |Disc|)^{24+ε}. With C = A_0 d_0² l⁴ + B_0 d_0 this gives the prefactor exp((24 + ε_l) C); display (8.1) prints the prefactor exp(C). This theorem concerns the exponentiation step only, not Theorem 8.2.1.

IUT.Applications.ExplicitEstimates

IUT/Applications/ExplicitEstimates.lean · imports IUT.Applications.ABC, IUT.ABC.Variants

Explicit estimates in IUT: the explicit abc-type inequalities and their arithmetic

Module documentation

Source: S. Mochizuki, I. Fesenko, Y. Hoshi, A. Minamide, W. Porowski, Explicit Estimates in Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory (58 pages). In that paper the PDF page number equals the printed page number. Pages read for this file: 1 to 8, 21 to 23, 26 to 28, 32 to 57. Pages checked against rendered images: 3 to 8, 21, 22, 23, 26, 27, 28, 32 to 57 (every display used below was read from a render).

The paper states numerically explicit versions of the inequalities of IUT IV, Corollary 2.2, conditional on IUT I to III in a slightly modified form (the "μ₆-version", its Sections 3 and 4). This file is not a formalization of that theory. It does three things.

  1. It states, as propositions that are not proved here and not assumed anywhere in this library, two explicit inequalities of the paper for integer triples:
    • Thm5_4Claim: Theorem 5.4 (= Theorem B of the introduction), page 46 and 47;
    • Thm5_3iiRationalClaim: the case L = ℚ of Theorem 5.3 (ii), page 43, restricted to coprime integer triples; and the paper's elementary Lemma 5.7 (page 50) as Lemma5_7Claim, which the paper proves on pages 50 to 52 and which is not proved here. The conclusion of Corollary 5.8 (page 53) is Cor5_8Statement.
  2. It proves implications with these propositions as explicit hypotheses: Corollary 5.8 from Thm5_3iiRationalClaim and Lemma5_7Claim (following the proof on pages 53 and 54, including the reduction to coprime triples), and the passage from either explicit inequality to the abc bound with exponent 3/2 + ε or 3 + ε.
  3. It checks elementary numerical steps of the proofs of Theorem 5.1, Corollary 5.2, Theorem 5.3 and Theorem 5.4 (pages 34, 35, 40, 42, 43, 45, 48).

Why nothing here implies Challenge.ABC: the abc conjecture has exponent 1 + ε on the radical. Theorem 5.4 bounds |abc| by a constant times rad(abc)^(3(1+ε)), which bounds the largest of the three numbers by rad^(3+3ε); Theorem 5.3 (ii) for ℚ bounds the largest by rad^(3(1+ε)/2). Exponents 3/2 + ε and 3 + ε are weaker than 1 + ε, and no argument from them to exponent 1 + ε is known. The conclusions below are therefore stated with the library's fixed exponent bound IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponent κ for κ = 3/2 + ε and κ = 3 + ε, never for κ = 1 + ε.

Interpretation recorded for Thm5_3iiRationalClaim (page 43): for L = ℚ one has d = 1, Δ_ℚ = 1, and for nonzero integers a, b, c with gcd(a, b) = 1 and a + b + c = 0 the height H_ℚ(a, b, c) (product over all places of max{|a|_v, |b|_v, |c|_v}) equals max{|a|, |b|, |c|} (every nonarchimedean factor is 1), and rad_ℚ(a, b, c) (product of p over primes at which the three absolute values are not all equal) equals rad(|abc|). These identifications use the usual normalized absolute values on ℚ; the paper's general conventions of its Section 0 were not read for this file.

Coprimality: the paper says "nonzero coprime integers" (Theorem 5.4) and "coprime positive integers" (Lemma 5.7). Under a + b + c = 0 (respectively x^p + y^p = z^p), coprimality of the first two numbers is equivalent to coprimality of all three and to pairwise coprimality; the statements below use gcd of the first two.

Public declarations

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.hOnedef

noncomputable def hOne (ε : ℝ) : ℝ := 3.4 * 10 ^ 30 * ε ^ (-(166 : ℝ) / 81)

The constant h_1(ε) = 3.4 · 10^30 · ε^(−166/81) of Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.2 (pages 36 and 43), case d = 1.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.Thm5_4Claimdef

def Thm5_4Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b + c = 0 →
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
      |((a * b * c : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ 2 ^ 4 * max (exp (1.7 * 10 ^ 30 * ε ^ (-(166 : ℝ) / 81)))
        ((rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) ^ (3 * (1 + ε)))

Theorem 5.4 (Theorem B) of the paper, as a proposition; not proved here and not assumed anywhere. Pages 46 and 47 (statement also on page 4). For nonzero integers a, b, c with gcd(a, b) = 1 and a + b + c = 0, and every real 0 < ε ≤ 1, |abc| ≤ 2^4 · max{exp(1.7 · 10^30 · ε^(−166/81)), rad(abc)^(3(1+ε))}. The paper derives it from Theorem 5.3, hence from its modified version of IUT I to III.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.Thm5_3iiRationalClaimdef

def Thm5_3iiRationalClaim : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b + c = 0 →
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 →
      max (max |(a : ℝ)| |(b : ℝ)|) |(c : ℝ)| ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ ((5 : ℝ) / 2) *
        max (exp (1 / 4 * hOne ε)) ((rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) ^ (3 * (1 + ε) / 2))

**Theorem 5.3 (ii) of the paper for L = ℚ and coprime integer triples, as a proposition; not proved here and not assumed anywhere.** Page 43. With d = 1 and Δ_ℚ = 1: max{|a|, |b|, |c|} ≤ 2^(5/2) · max{exp(h_1(ε)/4), rad(abc)^(3(1+ε)/2)}. The identification of H_ℚ and rad_ℚ for coprime integers is the interpretation recorded in the module docstring. The paper's Theorem 5.3 is stated for all mono-complex fields and all nonzero a, b, c; this is only the specialization used in Corollary 5.8.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.Lemma5_7Claimdef

def Lemma5_7Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → 3 ≤ p → ∀ x y z : ℕ, 0 < x → 0 < y → 0 < z → Nat.Coprime x y →
    x ^ p + y ^ p = z ^ p → (p + 1) ^ p < 2 * z

Lemma 5.7 of the paper, as a proposition; not proved here. Page 50: for a prime p ≥ 3 and coprime positive integers x, y, z with x^p + y^p = z^p, one has z > (p+1)^p / 2, written here as (p+1)^p < 2z. The paper proves it by elementary means on pages 48 to 52 (Lemmas 5.5 and 5.6); it does not depend on IUT.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.Cor5_8Statementdef

def Cor5_8Statement : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → (1.615 * 10 ^ 14 : ℝ) < p → ∀ x y z : ℕ, 0 < x → 0 < y → 0 < z →
    x ^ p + y ^ p ≠ z ^ p

The conclusion of Corollary 5.8 of the paper (page 53; Corollary C on page 5): for every prime p > 1.615 · 10^14 there are no positive integers x, y, z with x^p + y^p = z^p.

For nonzero integers, the radical of |(x^p)(y^p)(z^p)| is the radical of xyz.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.c_le_of_thm5_4Claimtheorem

theorem c_le_of_thm5_4Claim (h : Thm5_4Claim) {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b)
  (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) (habc : a + b = c) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  (c : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ 4 * max (exp (1.7 * 10 ^ 30 * ε ^ (-(166 : ℝ) / 81)))
    ((rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (3 * (1 + ε)))

**Theorem 5.4, specialized to positive triples a + b = c.** Applying the statement to (a, b, -c) and using c ≤ abc: c ≤ 2^4 · max{exp(1.7 · 10^30 · ε^(−166/81)), rad(abc)^(3(1+ε))}.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.c_le_of_thm5_3iiRationalClaimtheorem

theorem c_le_of_thm5_3iiRationalClaim (h : Thm5_3iiRationalClaim) {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hb : 0 < b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) (habc : a + b = c) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε)
  (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :

    max (exp (1 / 4 * hOne ε)) ((rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (3 * (1 + ε) / 2))

**Theorem 5.3 (ii) for ℚ, specialized to positive triples a + b = c.** Applying the statement to (a, b, -c): c ≤ 2^(5/2) · max{exp(h_1(ε)/4), rad(abc)^(3(1+ε)/2)}.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.abcWithExponent_three_add_of_thm5_4Claimtheorem

theorem abcWithExponent_three_add_of_thm5_4Claim (h : Thm5_4Claim) :
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ABCWithExponent (3 + ε)

**Theorem 5.4 implies the abc bound with exponent 3 + ε for every ε > 0.** Given ε > 0, apply c_le_of_thm5_4Claim with ε' = min(ε/3, 1) and bound the maximum by the product. The exponent 3 + ε is weaker than the 1 + ε of Challenge.ABC.

IUT.ExplicitEstimates.abcWithExponent_three_halves_add_of_thm5_3iiRationalClaimtheorem

theorem abcWithExponent_three_halves_add_of_thm5_3iiRationalClaim (h : Thm5_3iiRationalClaim) :
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ABCWithExponent (3 / 2 + ε)

**Theorem 5.3 (ii) for ℚ implies the abc bound with exponent 3/2 + ε for every ε > 0.** Given ε > 0, apply c_le_of_thm5_3iiRationalClaim with ε' = min(2ε/3, 1), so 3(1+ε')/2 ≤ 3/2 + ε. The exponent 3/2 + ε is weaker than the 1 + ε of Challenge.ABC.

Proof of Proposition 2.2 (i) (page 22), the algebraic part: if log x ≥ 47.66 then 1.17 / log x ≤ 0.0246, and x / (log x − 1.0246) ≤ 1.022 · x / log x for x > 0. The estimate log(η_prm) ≥ 47.66 itself and the cited bound of Axler are not checked here.

IUT.Applications.HeightComparison

IUT/Applications/HeightComparison.lean · imports IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField, IUT.PaperIV.LegendreFrey

Height comparison on the λ-line

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Corollary 2.2 and the first part of its proof (pages 41 to 43); Mochizuki, Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position ([GenEll]), §1 (the normalized degree and heights, page 4; Definition 1.2, page 5; Proposition 1.4, page 6; Definition 1.5, page 8; Proposition 1.6, page 9). Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 41 to 43; [GenEll] pages 4 to 6, 8 and 9. Pages checked against rendered images: all of these. [GenEll] page 4 states that the normalized degree (1/[F : ℚ]) deg_F is invariant under finite extension of F, so that ht is defined on X(ℚ̄); Definition 1.2 (ii) on page 5 prints α ≲ β as β - α ≤ C, a direction reversed by the published correction (2) recorded in IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField; the statements below are explicit inequalities and do not use ≲.

What the pages print. Corollary 2.2 (i) (page 41) asserts the equality of bounded discrepancy classes (1/6) log(𝔮^{†2}) ≈ (1/6) log(𝔮^∀) ≈ (1/6) ht_∞ ≈ ht_{ω_X(D)} on a compactly bounded subset K_V of U_X(ℚ̄), X = ℙ¹_ℚ the λ-line of the Legendre form and D = {0, 1, ∞}, where ht_∞ is the normalized height of the pullback of the divisor at infinity of the compactified moduli stack of elliptic curves. The proof (page 43) obtains the last equality from the fact that this pullback has degree 6 while ω_X(D) has degree 1, citing [GenEll] Proposition 1.4 (i), (iii). The pages print no explicit inequality between heights and no constant; the comparison with 1 - λ or 1/λ is not used on these pages. The comparison between log(𝔮) and ht_∞ (page 43) rests on the q-parameters of the elliptic curves at the nonarchimedean primes and on condition (*_{j-inv}) at the prime 2.

What this file proves. Heights are IUT.VojtaNumberField.heightNF (Mathlib's Height.logHeight₁ divided by [K : ℚ]), and j = IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ, the j-invariant 2⁸(λ² - λ + 1)³ / (λ²(λ - 1)²) of the Legendre curve.

  1. Height of the j-invariant (htCmp_abs_heightNF_legendreJ_sub_le): for every number field K and every y ∈ K, |ht(j(y)) - 6 ht(y)| ≤ log 41 + 8 log 2 = log 10496; one-sided forms ht(j(y)) ≤ 6 ht(y) + log 27 + 8 log 2 and 6 ht(y) ≤ ht(j(y)) + log 41 + 8 log 2. The constant is the same for all number fields (htCmp_exists_uniform_constant). At y = 0, 1 both sides vanish (Lean's convention x / 0 = 0), so no hypothesis on y is needed. This is an explicit form, for the Weil heights of j and of λ, of the degree 6 comparison behind (1/6) ht_∞ ≈ ht_{ω_X(D)}. The proof works place by place over any field with Mathlib's Height.AdmissibleAbsValues: with N = (y² - y + 1)³, D = y²(y - 1)², the upper bound uses max(|N|_v, |D|_v) ≤ 27 max(1, |y|_v)⁶ at archimedean places and ≤ max(1, |y|_v)⁶ at the others; the lower bound uses the resultant certificate y¹¹ = (y⁵ + 3y⁴ - 3y³) N + (6y⁵ - 8y⁴ + 11y³ - 6y² + 3y) D and 1 = (1 + 3y - 3y²) N + (6 - 8y + 11y² - 6y³ + 3y⁴) D (checked by ring), which gives max(1, |y|_v)⁶ ≤ 41 max(|N|_v, |D|_v) at archimedean places and the same with 1 at the others; the product formula removes Σ_v log |D|_v; the factor 2⁸ costs 8 log 2.
  2. Triples (htCmp_heightNF_legendreJ_triple): for coprime positive a + b = c and λ = a / c, 6 log c - log(64/27) ≤ ht(j(λ)) ≤ 6 log c + 8 log 2 in ℚ, from IUT.ABCSpecialization.logHeight₁_of_triple (ht(λ) = log c) and the bounds of IUT.LegendreFrey.
  3. Conductor and height (htCmp_logCondNF_le): for every number field K and x ∈ K \ {0, 1}, log-cond(x) ≤ 3 ht(x) + log 2 with log-cond = logCondNF. At a prime where x meets D, x, 1/x or 1/(1 - x) has absolute value at least the norm of the prime; summing gives the finite parts of ht(x) + ht(1/x) + ht((x - 1)⁻¹) ≤ 3 ht(x) + log 2. This is the instance D = {0, 1, ∞} of [GenEll] Proposition 1.6 (page 9, log-cond_D ≲ ht_D, with ht_D of degree 3), with the explicit constant log 2. It is the easy direction; it says nothing about the open inequality ht ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff + log-cond) + C of VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree.

Not proved.

  • Invariance of heightNF under field extension (heightNF L (algebraMap K L y) = heightNF K y for number fields K ⊆ L; [GenEll] page 4 asserts the corresponding invariance of the normalized degree) is not used here; it is proved in IUT/Applications/HeightExtension.lean (htExt_heightNF_algebraMap).
  • The comparison of (1/6) log(𝔮^∀) and (1/6) log(𝔮^{†2}) with (1/6) ht_∞ (page 43). It needs the q-parameter of an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction at a nonarchimedean prime (Tate's uniformization); Mathlib has no Tate curve and no q-parameter, so log(𝔮^∀) is not defined here. The function ht_∞ itself (height attached to the divisor at infinity of the compactified moduli stack) and ht_{ω_X(D)} are not defined either; the theorems above are stated for Weil heights, whose identification with these functions up to bounded functions is not formalized.
  • The inequalities log(𝔣^{F_tpd}) ≤ log-cond_D(x_E) ≤ log(𝔣^{F_tpd}) + log(2l) (page 43) need the conductor of the elliptic curve, which Mathlib does not define.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpPlaceSumdef

noncomputable def htCmpPlaceSum (f : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.archAbsVal.map f).sum +
    ∑ᶠ v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K), f v.val

The sum of a real function over all places of K: the archimedean absolute values, with multiplicity, and then the nonarchimedean ones (a finsum). This is the shape of Height.logHeight₁_eq.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_logHeight₁_eq_placeSumtheorem

theorem htCmp_logHeight₁_eq_placeSum (x : K) :
  Height.logHeight₁ x = htCmpPlaceSum (fun v ↦ log⁺ (v x))

The logarithmic height is the place sum of log⁺ |x|_v.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_hasFiniteSupporttheorem

theorem htCmp_hasFiniteSupport (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (h0 : φ 0 = 0) (h1 : φ 1 = 0) (x : K) :
  Function.HasFiniteSupport
    (fun v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K) ↦ φ (v.val x))

A function of |x|_v that vanishes at 0 and at 1 has finite support on the nonarchimedean places.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_placeSum_log_eq_zerotheorem

theorem htCmp_placeSum_log_eq_zero {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
  htCmpPlaceSum (fun v ↦ Real.log (v x)) = 0

The product formula in logarithmic form. For x ≠ 0, the place sum of log |x|_v is 0.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpPlaceSum_addtheorem

theorem htCmpPlaceSum_add {f g : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → ℝ}
  (hf : Function.HasFiniteSupport
    (fun v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K) ↦ f v.val))
  (hg : Function.HasFiniteSupport
    (fun v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K) ↦ g v.val)) :
  htCmpPlaceSum (fun v ↦ f v + g v) = htCmpPlaceSum f + htCmpPlaceSum g

The place sum is additive for functions of finite support on the nonarchimedean places.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpPlaceSum_multheorem

theorem htCmpPlaceSum_mul (r : ℝ) (f : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → ℝ) :
  htCmpPlaceSum (fun v ↦ r * f v) = r * htCmpPlaceSum f

The place sum commutes with multiplication by a constant.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpPlaceSum_letheorem

theorem htCmpPlaceSum_le {f g : AbsoluteValue K ℝ → ℝ} (c : ℝ)
  (hf : Function.HasFiniteSupport
    (fun v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K) ↦ f v.val))
  (hg : Function.HasFiniteSupport
    (fun v : Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K) ↦ g v.val))
  (harch : ∀ v, f v ≤ g v + c)
  (hnon : ∀ v ∈ Height.AdmissibleAbsValues.nonarchAbsVal (K := K), f v ≤ g v) :
  htCmpPlaceSum f ≤ htCmpPlaceSum g + Height.totalWeight K * c

Comparison of place sums. If f ≤ g + c at the archimedean places and f ≤ g at the nonarchimedean places, then the place sum of f is at most that of g plus totalWeight K · c.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_abv_intCast_letheorem

theorem htCmp_abv_intCast_le (v : AbsoluteValue K ℝ) (z : ℤ) : v (z : K) ≤ |(z : ℝ)|

An absolute value of an integer is at most its absolute value.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_abv_poly_letheorem

theorem htCmp_abv_poly_le (v : AbsoluteValue K ℝ) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ) (y : K) :
  v (∑ i, (c i : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) ≤ (∑ i, |(c i : ℝ)|) * max 1 (v y) ^ n

Archimedean bound for an integer polynomial. |Σ cᵢ yⁱ|_v ≤ (Σ |cᵢ|) max(1, |y|_v)ⁿ for a polynomial of degree at most n.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_nonarch_poly_letheorem

theorem htCmp_nonarch_poly_le {v : AbsoluteValue K ℝ} (hv : IsNonarchimedean v) {n : ℕ}
  (c : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ) (y : K) :
  v (∑ i, (c i : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) ≤ max 1 (v y) ^ n

Nonarchimedean bound for an integer polynomial. |Σ cᵢ yⁱ|_v ≤ max(1, |y|_v)ⁿ.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpNumdef

def htCmpNum (y : K) : K := (y ^ 2 - y + 1) ^ 3

The numerator (y² - y + 1)³ of legendreJ y / 2⁸.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpDendef

def htCmpDen (y : K) : K := y ^ 2 * (y - 1) ^ 2

The denominator y²(y - 1)² of legendreJ y.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_legendreJ_eqtheorem

theorem htCmp_legendreJ_eq (y : K) : legendreJ y = 2 ^ 8 * (htCmpNum y / htCmpDen y)

legendreJ y = 2⁸ (N(y) / D(y)).

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpDen_eq_zero_ifftheorem

theorem htCmpDen_eq_zero_iff (y : K) : htCmpDen y = 0 ↔ y = 0 ∨ y = 1

The denominator vanishes exactly at 0 and 1.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpNum_eq_sumtheorem

theorem htCmpNum_eq_sum (y : K) :
  htCmpNum y = ∑ i, (((![1, -3, 6, -7, 6, -3, 1] : Fin 7 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)

N(y) = y⁶ - 3y⁵ + 6y⁴ - 7y³ + 6y² - 3y + 1 as a sum over its coefficients.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmpDen_eq_sumtheorem

theorem htCmpDen_eq_sum (y : K) :
  htCmpDen y = ∑ i, (((![0, 0, 1, -2, 1, 0, 0] : Fin 7 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)

D(y) = y⁴ - 2y³ + y² as a sum over its coefficients (degree at most 6).

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_certificate_onetheorem

theorem htCmp_certificate_one (y : K) :
  y ^ 11 =
    (∑ i, (((![0, 0, 0, -3, 3, 1] : Fin 6 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) * htCmpNum y +
    (∑ i, (((![0, 3, -6, 11, -8, 6] : Fin 6 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) * htCmpDen y

Resultant certificate, first identity. y¹¹ = A₁(y) N(y) + B₁(y) D(y) with A₁ = y⁵ + 3y⁴ - 3y³, B₁ = 6y⁵ - 8y⁴ + 11y³ - 6y² + 3y, N = (y² - y + 1)³, D = y²(y - 1)².

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_certificate_twotheorem

theorem htCmp_certificate_two (y : K) :
  1 =
    (∑ i, (((![1, 3, -3, 0, 0, 0] : Fin 6 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) * htCmpNum y +
    (∑ i, (((![6, -8, 11, -6, 3, 0] : Fin 6 → ℤ) i : ℤ) : K) * y ^ (i : ℕ)) * htCmpDen y

Resultant certificate, second identity. 1 = A₂(y) N(y) + B₂(y) D(y) with A₂ = 1 + 3y - 3y², B₂ = 6 - 8y + 11y² - 6y³ + 3y⁴.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_coeffSum_numtheorem

  (∑ i, |((((![1, -3, 6, -7, 6, -3, 1] : Fin 7 → ℤ) i : ℤ)) : ℝ)|) = 27

The sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of N is 27.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_coeffSum_dentheorem

theorem htCmp_coeffSum_den :
  (∑ i, |((((![0, 0, 1, -2, 1, 0, 0] : Fin 7 → ℤ) i : ℤ)) : ℝ)|) = 4

The sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of D is 4.

**The j-height at the point of a coprime triple.** For positive coprime a + b = c and λ = a / c: 6 log c - log(64/27) ≤ ht(j(λ)) ≤ 6 log c + 8 log 2, with ht = heightNF ℚ. It combines IUT.ABCSpecialization.logHeight₁_of_triple (ht(λ) = log c) with the explicit bounds of IUT.LegendreFrey.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_toNNReal_getheorem

theorem htCmp_toNNReal_ge {e : NNReal} (he0 : e ≠ 0) (he : 1 ≤ e) {m : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)}
  (hm0 : m ≠ 0) (hm1 : m ≠ 1) :
  e ≤ WithZeroMulInt.toNNReal he0 m ∨ e ≤ WithZeroMulInt.toNNReal he0 m⁻¹

If m ∈ ℤᵐ⁰ is neither 0 nor 1 and e ≥ 1, then e ≤ e^{log m} or e ≤ e^{log m⁻¹} (through WithZeroMulInt.toNNReal).

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_finitePlace_getheorem

theorem htCmp_finitePlace_ge {w : FinitePlace K} {z : K} (hz : z ≠ 0)
  (hv : (FinitePlace.maximalIdeal w).valuation K z ≠ 1) :
  (Ideal.absNorm (FinitePlace.maximalIdeal w).asIdeal : ℝ) ≤ w z ∨
    (Ideal.absNorm (FinitePlace.maximalIdeal w).asIdeal : ℝ) ≤ w z⁻¹

At a finite place w where the valuation of z ≠ 0 is not 1, |z|_w or |z⁻¹|_w is at least the norm of the prime of w.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_cond_term_letheorem

theorem htCmp_cond_term_le (w : FinitePlace K) {x : K} (h0 : x ≠ 0) (h1 : x ≠ 1) :
  (open Classical in
    if MeetsBoundaryAt K (FinitePlace.maximalIdeal w) x then
      Real.log (Nat.card (𝓞 K ⧸ (FinitePlace.maximalIdeal w).asIdeal)) else 0) ≤
    log⁺ (w x) + log⁺ (w x⁻¹) + log⁺ (w (x - 1)⁻¹)

Pointwise bound. At a finite place w with prime 𝔭, the contribution of 𝔭 to the log-conductor of x ∉ {0, 1} is at most log⁺|x|_w + log⁺|x⁻¹|_w + log⁺|(x - 1)⁻¹|_w.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_finsum_posLog_letheorem

theorem htCmp_finsum_posLog_le (z : K) :
  ∑ᶠ w : FinitePlace K, log⁺ (w z) ≤ Height.logHeight₁ z

The finite part of the height is at most the height.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_hasFiniteSupport_finitePlacetheorem

theorem htCmp_hasFiniteSupport_finitePlace (z : K) :
  Function.HasFiniteSupport (fun w : FinitePlace K ↦ log⁺ (w z))

log⁺ |z|_w has finite support on the finite places of a number field.

IUT.HeightComparison.htCmp_logCondNF_letheorem

theorem htCmp_logCondNF_le (x : K) (h0 : x ≠ 0) (h1 : x ≠ 1) :
  logCondNF K x ≤ 3 * heightNF K x + Real.log 2

The log-conductor is bounded by three times the height. For every number field K and x ∈ K with x ≠ 0, 1: log-cond(x) ≤ 3 ht(x) + log 2, with log-cond = logCondNF and ht = heightNF. This is the instance D = {0, 1, ∞} of [GenEll] Proposition 1.6 (log-cond_D ≲ ht_D, page 9), with the explicit constant log 2. It is the easy direction and says nothing about the open inequality ht ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff + log-cond) + C (IUT.VojtaNumberField.VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree).

IUT.Applications.HeightExtension

IUT/Applications/HeightExtension.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback

The height, log-different and log-conductor under extension of the number field

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position ([GenEll]), §1: page 4 (the normalized degree, its invariance under finite extension for arithmetic line bundles, and the definition of ht_𝓜(x) on X(ℚ̄)), Definition 1.2 (page 5) and Definition 1.5 (i), (iii), (iv) (page 8: minimal field of definition, log-different, log-conductor); Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Definition 1.9 (i) (page 22). Pages read for this file: [GenEll] pages 3, 4, 5 and 8; IUT IV page 22. Pages checked against rendered images: all of these.

What the pages print. [GenEll] page 4: with deg_F = (1/[F : ℚ]) deg_F (normalized), "for any finite extension K of F, it follows that deg_K(𝓛|_{Spec 𝒪_K}) = deg_F(𝓛)" for arithmetic line bundles on Spec 𝒪_F; "In particular, ... for any x ∈ X(ℚ̄) ... it makes sense to define ht_𝓜(x) = deg_F(x_F^* 𝓜), where x_F : Spec(𝒪_F) → X is any morphism that gives rise to x." So the height does not depend on the number field F through which the point is read. Definition 1.2 (i) (page 5) names this function ht_𝓜 : X(ℚ̄) → ℝ. Definition 1.5 (iii), (iv) (page 8), by contrast, define log-diff_X(x) and log-cond_D(x) only for x ∈ X(F) with F "a minimal field of definition of x" (Definition 1.5 (i)): the pages do not assert that these two functions are unchanged when x is read in a larger field. For the log-different this fails (item 2 below); for the log-conductor item 3 below gives the exact change. IUT IV page 22 (Definition 1.9 (i)) prints the invariance deg(𝔞|_K) = deg(𝔞) of the normalized degree of arithmetic divisors, proved in IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback as degPb_normalizedDeg_pullback.

What this file proves, for the functions heightNF, logDiffNF, logCondNF of IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField on the line minus {0, 1, ∞}.

  1. Height (htExt_heightNF_algebraMap): for number fields K ⊆ L and y ∈ K, heightNF L y = heightNF K y. The proof writes Mathlib's Height.logHeight₁ y (the sum of mult(v) log⁺ |y|_v over the infinite places and of log⁺ |y|_v over the finite places) as the degree deg_K of an effective arithmetic divisor htExtPoleDiv y (the polar divisor of y: coefficient max(0, -ord_v(y)) at a finite place, [K_v : ℝ] log⁺ |y|_v at an archimedean place), shows that its pull-back to L along degPbPullback is the polar divisor of y in L (htExt_pullback_poleDiv), and applies degPb_degF_pullback. This is the invariance of [GenEll] page 4 for the Weil height on ℙ¹. It extends the case K = ℚ of IUT.VojtaNumberField.heightNF_algebraMap_rat; htExt_heightNF_ringHom gives the same for any ring homomorphism K →+* L, in particular for isomorphisms of number fields.
  2. Log-different: htExt_logDiffNF_le (log-diff_K ≤ log-diff_L, from the tower formula degPb_logDiffNF_tower) and htExt_logDiffNF_rat_lt_cyclotomicThree (log-diff_ℚ = 0 < (1/2) log 3 = log-diff_{ℚ(ζ₃)}): it is not invariant.
  3. Log-conductor: for y ∈ K \ {0, 1} and the finite set S of primes of K at which y meets {0, 1, ∞}, the identity htExt_finrank_mul_logCondNF_sub: [L : ℚ] (log-cond_K(y) - log-cond_L(y)) = Σ_{v ∈ S} Σ_{w | v} (e(w|v) - 1) log q_w. Hence log-cond_L(y) ≤ log-cond_K(y) (htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_le), with equality when L/K is unramified at the primes of L where y meets the boundary (htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_eq_of_unramified). The sum log-diff + log-cond does not decrease (IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_logDiffNF_add_logCondNF_le).
  4. Reading on the minimal field: for x in a number field L, with ℚ(x) the intermediate field IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {x} and g its generator, g generates ℚ(x) (htExt_adjoin_gen_eq_top), heightNF ℚ(x) g = heightNF L x (htExt_heightNF_adjoin), and an inequality ht ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff + log-cond) + C at g in ℚ(x) gives the same inequality at x in L (htExt_ineq_algebraMap, htExt_ineq_of_adjoin).
  5. The registered statement VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d already reads each point on its minimal field (its hypothesis IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {x} = ⊤). The theorem htExt_degreeAtMost_iff_anyField proves it equivalent, with the same constant, to htExtDegreeAtMostAnyFieldStatement d, in which the point x is read in any number field F of degree at most d containing it, with log-diff and log-cond evaluated at F. That form is an open family of statements of this project, not a statement of the papers; neither form is proved here.
  6. Nonvacuity: y = 1/3 has normalized height log 3 in ℚ and in the quadratic field ℚ(ζ₃) = ℚ(√-3) (Mathlib's CyclotomicField 3 ℚ), htExt_heightNF_oneThird.

Not proved.

  • The identification of heightNF with the height ht_{ω_P(C)} of [GenEll] page 4 attached to an arithmetic line bundle (see IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField); only the Weil height is treated.
  • An example where the log-conductor strictly drops (a point whose conductor contains a prime that ramifies in L); only the identity, the inequality and the unramified equality are proved.
  • Equality of log-diff + log-cond along an extension unramified at every prime (it would need the relative different to be the unit ideal).
  • Statements for the compactly bounded subsets of IUT.Applications.CompactlyBounded: the analogous equivalence for cbDegreeAtMostStatement would also need that membership cbMem of x does not depend on the field in which it is read (every embedding of L restricts to an embedding of ℚ(x) and every embedding of ℚ(x) extends to L). The extension of embeddings into ℂ and into ℚ̄_p is not formalized here.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExtPoleCoeffdef

noncomputable def htExtPoleCoeff (y : K) : Valuations K → ℝ
  | .inl v => max 0 (-(degPbOrd v y : ℝ))
  | .inr w => (w.mult : ℝ) * Real.posLog (w y)

The coefficients of the polar divisor of y: max(0, -ord_v(y)) at a finite place v and [K_v : ℝ]·log⁺ |y|_v at an archimedean place v, with [K_v : ℝ] = InfinitePlace.mult v.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExtPoleCoeff_support_finitetheorem

theorem htExtPoleCoeff_support_finite {y : K} (hy : y ≠ 0) :
  (Function.support (htExtPoleCoeff y)).Finite

IUT.HeightExtension.htExtPoleDivdef

noncomputable def htExtPoleDiv (y : Kˣ) : ADiv K :=
  Finsupp.ofSupportFinite (htExtPoleCoeff (y : K)) (htExtPoleCoeff_support_finite y.ne_zero)

**The polar divisor of y ∈ K^×**, an effective arithmetic divisor whose degree deg_K is Height.logHeight₁ y (htExt_degF_poleDiv).

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_posLog_finitePlacetheorem

theorem htExt_posLog_finitePlace {y : K} (hy : y ≠ 0) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  Real.posLog (FinitePlace.mk v y) =
    Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal) * max 0 (-(degPbOrd v y : ℝ))

At a finite place, log⁺ |y|_v = log q_v · max(0, -ord_v(y)).

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_degF_poleDivtheorem

theorem htExt_degF_poleDiv (y : Kˣ) : degF (htExtPoleDiv y) = Height.logHeight₁ (y : K)

The degree of the polar divisor is the height: deg_K(htExtPoleDiv y) = Height.logHeight₁ y, Mathlib's unnormalized logarithmic height on the number field K.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_pullback_poleDivtheorem

theorem htExt_pullback_poleDiv (y : Kˣ) :
  degPbPullback L (htExtPoleDiv y) =
    htExtPoleDiv (Units.map (algebraMap K L).toMonoidHom y)

The pull-back of the polar divisor is the polar divisor: (htExtPoleDiv y)|_L = htExtPoleDiv y with y viewed in L. At a finite place w | v, e(w|v)·max(0, -ord_v(y)) = max(0, -ord_w(y)); at an archimedean place w | v, [L_w : K_v]·[K_v : ℝ]·log⁺ |y|_v = [L_w : ℝ]·log⁺ |y|_w.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logHeight₁_algebraMaptheorem

theorem htExt_logHeight₁_algebraMap (y : K) :
  Height.logHeight₁ (algebraMap K L y) = Module.finrank K L * Height.logHeight₁ y

Height.logHeight₁ computed in L is [L : K] times its value in K.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_heightNF_algebraMaptheorem

theorem htExt_heightNF_algebraMap (y : K) :
  heightNF L (algebraMap K L y) = heightNF K y

The normalized height does not depend on the number field ([GenEll] page 4: ht(x) may be computed through any morphism Spec 𝒪_F → X giving rise to x): for number fields K ⊆ L and y ∈ K, heightNF L y = heightNF K y.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_heightNF_ringHomtheorem

theorem htExt_heightNF_ringHom (f : K →+* L) (y : K) : heightNF L (f y) = heightNF K y

The normalized height is invariant under every ring homomorphism of number fields, in particular under isomorphisms: heightNF L (f y) = heightNF K y for f : K →+* L.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logDiffNF_letheorem

theorem htExt_logDiffNF_le : logDiffNF K ≤ logDiffNF L

The log-different does not decrease under extension: log-diff_K ≤ log-diff_L, from the tower formula log-diff_L = log-diff_K + (1/[L : ℚ]) log N(𝔇_{L/K}).

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logDiffNF_rat_lt_cyclotomicThreetheorem

theorem htExt_logDiffNF_rat_lt_cyclotomicThree :
  logDiffNF ℚ < logDiffNF (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ)

The log-different is not invariant under extension: log-diff_ℚ = 0, while for the quadratic field ℚ(ζ₃) (Mathlib's CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) log-diff = (1/2) log 3 > 0.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logCondNF_eq_sumtheorem

theorem htExt_logCondNF_eq_sum (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) {y : K}
  (hS : ∀ v, v ∈ S ↔ MeetsBoundaryAt K v y) :
  logCondNF K y = (∑ v ∈ S, Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)) / Module.finrank ℚ K

The log-conductor as a finite sum: if S is exactly the set of primes of 𝓞 K at which y meets {0, 1, ∞}, then log-cond_K(y) = (1/[K : ℚ]) Σ_{v ∈ S} log q_v.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_eq_sumtheorem

theorem htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_eq_sum (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) {y : K}
  (hS : ∀ v, v ∈ S ↔ MeetsBoundaryAt K v y) :
  logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y) =
    (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L), Real.log (Ideal.absNorm q.1)) /
      Module.finrank ℚ L

The log-conductor of y ∈ K read in L, as a finite sum over the primes of 𝓞 L above S: log-cond_L(y) = (1/[L : ℚ]) Σ_{v ∈ S} Σ_{w | v} log q_w.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_finrank_mul_logCondNF_subtheorem

theorem htExt_finrank_mul_logCondNF_sub (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) {y : K}
  (hS : ∀ v, v ∈ S ↔ MeetsBoundaryAt K v y) :
  (Module.finrank ℚ L : ℝ) * (logCondNF K y - logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y)) =
    ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L),
      ((q.1.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ) - 1) * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm q.1)

The change of the log-conductor under extension: if S is the set of primes of 𝓞 K at which y meets {0, 1, ∞}, then [L : ℚ]·(log-cond_K(y) - log-cond_L(y)) = Σ_{v ∈ S} Σ_{w | v} (e(w|v) - 1)·log q_w.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExtConductorSetdef

noncomputable def htExtConductorSet {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1) :
    Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :=
  (degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_finite hy0 hy1).toFinset

The finite set of primes at which a point y ∉ {0, 1} meets {0, 1, ∞}.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_mem_conductorSettheorem

theorem htExt_mem_conductorSet {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1)
  (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : v ∈ htExtConductorSet hy0 hy1 ↔ MeetsBoundaryAt K v y

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_letheorem

theorem htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_le {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1) :
  logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y) ≤ logCondNF K y

The log-conductor does not increase under extension: for y ∈ K \ {0, 1}, log-cond_L(y) ≤ log-cond_K(y). The reduced conductor loses (e(w|v) - 1) log q_w at each ramified prime w over the conductor.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_eq_of_unramifiedtheorem

theorem htExt_logCondNF_algebraMap_eq_of_unramified {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1)
  (hun : ∀ w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L), MeetsBoundaryAt L w (algebraMap K L y) →
    w.asIdeal.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) = 1) :
  logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y) = logCondNF K y

The log-conductor is invariant under extensions unramified at the conductor: for y ∈ K \ {0, 1}, if every prime w of 𝓞 L at which y meets {0, 1, ∞} is unramified over K (e(w|v) = 1), then log-cond_L(y) = log-cond_K(y).

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_ineq_algebraMaptheorem

theorem htExt_ineq_algebraMap {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] (L : Type*) [Field L]
  [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1) {ε C : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 ≤ 1 + ε) (h : heightNF K y ≤ (1 + ε) * (logDiffNF K + logCondNF K y) + C) :
  heightNF L (algebraMap K L y) ≤
    (1 + ε) * (logDiffNF L + logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y)) + C

The inequality transfers to larger fields. For number fields K ⊆ L, y ∈ K \ {0, 1} and 1 + ε ≥ 0: if ht(y) ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff + log-cond)(y) + C with y read in K, then the same holds with y read in L. The height is unchanged (htExt_heightNF_algebraMap) and log-diff + log-cond does not decrease (degPb_logDiffNF_add_logCondNF_le).

The generator x of ℚ(x) ⊆ L generates ℚ(x) as a field: ℚ(x) is the minimal field of definition of x ([GenEll] Definition 1.5 (i)).

**The height of x read in L equals its height read in its minimal field ℚ(x).**

theorem htExt_gen_ne_zero {x : L} (hx0 : x ≠ 0) :

theorem htExt_gen_ne_one {x : L} (hx1 : x ≠ 1) :

theorem htExt_ineq_of_adjoin {x : L} (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hx1 : x ≠ 1) {ε C : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ 1 + ε)
  (h : heightNF (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {x}) (IntermediateField.AdjoinSimple.gen ℚ x) ≤

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_finrank_adjoin_letheorem

theorem htExt_finrank_adjoin_le (x : L) :

The degree of ℚ(x) is at most the degree of L.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExtDegreeAtMostAnyFieldStatementdef

def htExtDegreeAtMostAnyFieldStatement (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [NumberField F] (x : F),
    Module.finrank ℚ F ≤ d → x ≠ 0 → x ≠ 1 →
      heightNF F x ≤ (1 + ε) * (logDiffNF F + logCondNF F x) + C

An open family of statements of this project, not a theorem and not a statement of the papers: the inequality of VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d with each point x read in an arbitrary number field F of degree at most d containing it, and log-diff, log-cond evaluated at F instead of at the minimal field of definition of x. It is equivalent to VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d (htExt_degreeAtMost_iff_anyField).

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_degreeAtMost_iff_anyFieldtheorem

theorem htExt_degreeAtMost_iff_anyField (d : ℕ) :
  VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d ↔ htExtDegreeAtMostAnyFieldStatement d

**The registered statement, which reads each point on its minimal field, is equivalent to the statement reading each point in any number field of degree at most d containing it**, with the same constants. One direction restricts to fields generated by the point; the other passes from F to ℚ(x) ⊆ F, of degree at most [F : ℚ] ≤ d, by htExt_ineq_of_adjoin. Neither side is proved.

IUT.HeightExtension.htExt_heightNF_oneThirdtheorem

theorem htExt_heightNF_oneThird :
  Module.finrank ℚ (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) = 2 ∧
    heightNF ℚ (1 / 3) = Real.log 3 ∧
    heightNF (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) (algebraMap ℚ (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) (1 / 3)) =
      Real.log 3

Nonvacuity. ℚ(ζ₃) = ℚ(√-3) (Mathlib's CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) is a quadratic field, and the point 1/3 has the same normalized height log 3 in ℚ and in ℚ(ζ₃).

IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField

IUT/Applications/VojtaNumberField.lean · imports IUT.Applications.ABCSpecialization

Points of bounded degree on the line minus three points

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Theorem A and the sentence after it (page 3), the notation recalled before Corollary 2.2 (page 40), Corollary 2.2 (pages 41 to 43, read for the setting, condition (C2) and part (iii)), Corollary 2.3 with its proof (pages 54 and 55) and Remark 2.3.1 (pages 55 and 56). Second source: Mochizuki, Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position ([GenEll]), §1 (arithmetic divisors and normalized degree, page 4; Definition 1.2 and Example 1.3, pages 5 and 6; Proposition 1.4, page 6; Remark 1.4.1, Definition 1.5 and Remark 1.5.1, pages 8 and 9; Propositions 1.6 and 1.7, page 9) and §2 (Theorem 2.1 and its proof, pages 11 to 13), with its list of corrections, Comments on "Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position" (July 2016, pages 1 and 2). Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 3, 40 to 43 and 54 to 56; [GenEll] pages 4 to 6, 8, 9 and 11 to 13; the corrections, pages 1 and 2. Pages checked against rendered images: all of these.

What this file is. It defines, with Mathlib objects only, the three functions of [GenEll] Definition 1.5 for the projective line P = ℙ¹_ℚ and the divisor C = {0, 1, ∞} at points of U_P(ℚ̄) = P(ℚ̄) \ C over number fields: the normalized height heightNF, the normalized log-different logDiffNF and the normalized log-conductor logCondNF. It states, as an open proposition, the bounded degree inequality for these points (VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree, with its fixed degree pieces VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d). It proves that the degree one piece is equivalent to VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational of IUT.Applications.ABCSpecialization, hence to the abc conjecture Challenge.ABC, so that the bounded degree statement implies Challenge.ABC. It does not prove the bounded degree statement, and nothing here bears on whether the proofs in the papers are correct.

Which statements of the papers. IUT IV, Corollary 2.3 (page 54): for a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve X over a number field, a reduced divisor D ⊆ X with U_X = X \ D hyperbolic, a positive integer d and ε > 0, "one has an inequality of 'bounded discrepancy classes' ht_{ω_X(D)} ≲ (1 + ε)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) of functions on U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d}, i.e., the function (1 + ε)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) - ht_{ω_X(D)} is bounded below by a constant on U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d}". So the constant depends on X, D, d and ε, and on nothing else. Its proof (pages 54 and 55) says that this "coincides precisely with the content of [GenEll], Theorem 2.1, (i)". VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree is the instance X = ℙ¹_ℚ, D = {0, 1, ∞} of that statement (here ω_X(D) ≅ 𝒪(1), of degree -2 + 3 = 1), that is, the instance P, C of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 (i) (page 11), with the height normalized as described below. It is not the corollary: all other curves are dropped. The set U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d} is the union of the U_X(F) over number fields F with [F : ℚ] ≤ d ([GenEll] Example 1.3 (i), page 5; IUT IV page 40); a point of it is recorded here as a pair (F, x) where F is a number field, x ∈ F \ {0, 1}, and F is generated by x (ℚ⟮x⟯ = ⊤), so that F is the minimal field of definition of the point in the sense of [GenEll] Definition 1.5 (i) (page 8), which is the field at which Definition 1.5 (iii), (iv) evaluate the log-different and the log-conductor. The bound [F : ℚ] ≤ d is then the degree of the point. The quantifier ∀ F : Type ranges over number fields in the lowest universe; every number field has a copy there, so nothing is lost. Each point is represented by every pair (F, x) isomorphic to it; the statement quantifies over all of them. The log-different and the log-conductor are proved invariant under isomorphisms of pairs (logCondNF_ringEquiv, and NumberField.discr_eq_discr_of_ringEquiv for the discriminant); for the height it is proved in IUT/Applications/HeightExtension.lean (htExt_heightNF_ringHom, for any ring homomorphism of number fields).

**The relation ≲.** α ≲ β means α(x) - β(x) ≤ C for a constant C: [GenEll] Definition 1.2 (ii) (page 5) after correction (2), which reverses the printed direction, repeated as IUT IV Remark 2.3.1 (ii) (page 55).

The three functions. [GenEll] page 4 defines an arithmetic divisor on a number field F as a finite sum Σ c_v v over the places of F, the degree deg_F sending a finite place v to log(q_v) (q_v the cardinality of the residue field) and an archimedean place to 1, and the normalized degree (1 / [F : ℚ]) deg_F, which is invariant under finite extension of F.

  • Height. ht_𝓜(x) is the normalized degree of the pullback of an arithmetic line bundle on a model (page 4); its bounded discrepancy class depends only on the line bundle on X_ℚ (Proposition 1.4 (iii), page 6; Remark 1.4.1, page 8). Here heightNF F x is Mathlib's Height.logHeight₁ x divided by [F : ℚ]. Mathlib's Height.logHeight₁ on a number field (NumberField.logHeight₁_eq) is the unnormalized sum Σ_{v infinite} mult(v) log⁺ |x|_v + Σ_{v finite} log⁺ |x|_v, where the finite places carry the absolute value |x|_v = N(𝔭)^{-v_𝔭(x)}; so it is [F : ℚ] times the absolute logarithmic Weil height. Mathlib also defines NumberField.absLogHeight₁ (through ℚ⟮x⟯ and the exponent 1 / [ℚ⟮x⟯ : ℚ]) but proves nothing about it, and it has no lemma on invariance of heights under field extension. This file proves heightNF_algebraMap_rat: for every number field F and rational q, heightNF F q = Height.logHeight₁ q = log max(|num q|, den q). As in IUT.Applications.ABCSpecialization, the identification of the height attached to ω_P(C) ≅ 𝒪(1) with the Weil height up to a bounded function is a standard computation not contained in [GenEll] and not formalized here; since ≲ absorbs bounded functions it does not change the statement.
  • Log-different (Definition 1.5 (iii), page 8): "the different ideal of F determines an effective arithmetic divisor δ_x ∈ ADiv(F) which is supported in V(F)^non", and log-diff_X(x) = deg_F(δ_x) normalized. With the normalization of page 4 this is (1 / [F : ℚ]) log N(𝔇_F), 𝔇_F the different ideal of 𝓞_F over ℤ, and by Mathlib's NumberField.absNorm_differentIdeal it equals (1 / [F : ℚ]) log |disc F|, with the absolute discriminant (logDiffNF_eq). It does not depend on x beyond F = ℚ(x).
  • Log-conductor (Definition 1.5 (iv), page 8, with correction (12): "conductor of x with respect to D"): pull D back along Spec 𝓞_F → X to the effective divisor D_x; the conductor is (D_x)_red, and log-cond_D(x) is its normalized degree. For the model ℙ¹_ℤ of P with D the closure of the sections 0, 1, ∞, write x near a prime 𝔭 of 𝓞_F as (a : b) with a, b ∈ 𝓞_F not both in 𝔭; the section meets 0, ∞, 1 at 𝔭 exactly when a, b, a - b lies in 𝔭. So 𝔭 lies in the support of D_x exactly when there are no a, b ∈ 𝓞_F with a, b, a - b ∉ 𝔭 and x b = a; this is MeetsBoundaryAt, and logCondNF F x = (1 / [F : ℚ]) Σ log q_𝔭 over these primes, each counted once, with q_𝔭 the cardinality of 𝓞_F / 𝔭. The pullback description is the definition; the theorem meetsBoundaryAt_iff_valuation proves that it is the set of primes with v_𝔭(x) ≠ 0 or v_𝔭(x - 1) ≠ 0 (equivalently, v_𝔭(x) ≠ 0 or v_𝔭(x - 1) > 0, since v_𝔭(x - 1) < 0 forces v_𝔭(x) < 0). Another model of (P, C) changes the log-conductor only at finitely many primes, hence by a bounded function (Remark 1.5.1, pages 8 and 9), which ≲ absorbs.

Normalization checks. At a rational point q ∉ {0, 1} the three functions are log max(|num q|, den q), 0 and log (ratConductor q) (heightNF_rat, logDiffNF_rat, logCondNF_rat): these are the functions of VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational. At the point x = -ζ₃ (a primitive sixth root of unity) of the quadratic field ℚ(ζ₃), which generates it: the height is 0, the log-different is (1/2) log 3 (the discriminant is -3), and the log-conductor is 0, because x and x - 1 = ζ₃² are units. These are stated for every number field K with IsCyclotomicExtension {3} ℚ K, and instantiated at Mathlib's CyclotomicField 3 ℚ in exists_point_cyclotomicFieldThree (instance search does not find that instance here, so the proof supplies CyclotomicField.isCyclotomicExtension by name).

The compactly bounded form is stated elsewhere. [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 (ii) (page 11) asserts the same inequality on K_V ∩ U_P(ℚ̄)^{≤d} for every compactly bounded subset K_V ⊆ U_P(ℚ̄) whose support contains a fixed finite set Σ of primes; IUT IV takes Σ = {2} and adds the condition (*_{j-inv}) (pages 41 and 55). By Example 1.3 (ii) (pages 5 and 6) with corrections (8), (9) and Remark 2.3.1 (vi) (page 56), K_V is given by a finite set V of places of ℚ containing the archimedean one and, for v ∈ V, a nonempty compact domain K_v of U(ℂ) stable under complex conjugation (archimedean v), or a nonempty Gal(ℚ̄_v / ℚ_v)-stable subset K_v ⊆ U(ℚ̄_v) whose intersection with X(K) is a compact domain for every finite extension K ⊆ ℚ̄_v of ℚ_v (finite v); x ∈ X(F) lies in K_V when for each v ∈ V the [F : ℚ] points of X(ℂ), respectively X(ℚ̄_v), determined by x lie in K_v. These are points of ℚ̄_v, not of the completions of F. Mathlib has ℚ̄_p (PadicAlgCl p) with its norm, and ring homomorphisms from F into it; a faithful definition would quantify over the finite intermediate extensions of PadicAlgCl p / ℚ_[p] with their subspace topologies and over the ℚ_[p]-automorphisms of PadicAlgCl p. This file does not build that definition; IUT/Applications/CompactlyBounded.lean does, states form (ii) as genEllTheorem2_1iiStatement, and proves that it follows from VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree by restriction (proof of Theorem 2.1: "The fact that (i) ⟹ (ii) is immediate from the definitions"). That form (ii) implies Challenge.ABC is not shown.

**Open items between IUT IV and VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree.** None of these is formalized.

  1. IUT IV Theorem 1.10, applied to the initial Θ-data built in Corollary 2.2.
  2. IUT IV Corollary 2.2 (pages 41 to 43): for compactly bounded K_V whose support contains 2 and which satisfies (*_{j-inv}), (i) an equality of bounded discrepancy classes (1/6) log(𝔮^∀) ≈ ht_{ω_X(D)} on K_V, (ii) condition (C2) bounding (1/6) log(𝔮^∀) by (1 + ε_E)(log-diff_X(x_E) + log-cond_D(x_E)) + C_K outside a finite set, (iii) the bound ε_E ≤ ε outside a finite set. With them the proof of Corollary 2.3 (page 55) derives form (ii) of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 for Σ = {2}, noting that (*_{j-inv}) is vacuous for fixed d.
  3. The passage (ii) ⟹ (i) of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 (pages 11 to 13): a connected finite étale Galois covering U_Y → U_X with ramification index e over D, which raises the degree bound to d' = d deg(Y/X); the reduction to D = ∅; the compactness argument at the places of V; the noncritical Belyi map φ : X → P of an earlier paper of Mochizuki (cited as [Mzk1] Theorem 2.5), unramified over U_P and noncritical at the limit points; Propositions 1.4, 1.6 and 1.7; and correction (5) to the last display. Even for X = P and d = 1 this route uses form (ii) at the degree d' > 1.
  4. The identification of ht_{ω_P(C)} with the Weil height up to a bounded function (above).

Main results.

  • meetsBoundaryAt_iff_valuation: the pullback description of the conductor is the valuation description.
  • logDiffNF_eq, heightNF_nonneg, logDiffNF_nonneg, logCondNF_nonneg.
  • logCondNF_one_sub, logCondNF_inv, heightNF_inv, abs_heightNF_one_sub_sub_le, adjoin_one_sub_eq_top_iff, adjoin_inv_eq_top_iff: behavior under x ↦ 1 - x and x ↦ 1 / x, which generate the six permutations of {0, 1, ∞}.
  • heightNF_algebraMap_rat, heightNF_rat, logDiffNF_rat, logCondNF_rat: the values at rational points.
  • logCondNF_ringEquiv: invariance of the log-conductor under isomorphisms of number fields.
  • degreeAtMostOne_iff_rational, degreeAtMostOne_iff_ABC, degreeAtMost_mono, abc_of_degreeAtMost, abc_of_boundedDegree.
  • heightNF_sixthRoot, logDiffNF_cyclotomicThree, logCondNF_sixthRoot, adjoin_sixthRoot_eq_top, exists_point_cyclotomicFieldThree: the example in ℚ(ζ₃).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.ReducesAwayFromBoundarydef

def ReducesAwayFromBoundary (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (y : K) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : 𝓞 K, a ∉ v.asIdeal ∧ b ∉ v.asIdeal ∧ a - b ∉ v.asIdeal ∧
    y * algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b = algebraMap (𝓞 K) K a

The point y of ℙ¹(K) reduces at the prime v of 𝓞_K to a point of ℙ¹ \ {0, 1, ∞}: there are a, b ∈ 𝓞_K with y b = a and none of a, b, a - b in v, that is, y = (a : b) near v with the coordinates of the three points 0, ∞, 1 all nonzero modulo v.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.MeetsBoundaryAtdef

def MeetsBoundaryAt (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (y : K) : Prop :=
  ¬ ReducesAwayFromBoundary K v y

The prime v of 𝓞_K lies in the support of the pullback of D = {0, 1, ∞} along the section Spec 𝓞_K → ℙ¹_ℤ defined by y ([GenEll] Definition 1.5 (iv), page 8): the point y reduces modulo v to 0, 1 or ∞.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.heightNFdef

noncomputable def heightNF (y : K) : ℝ :=
  Height.logHeight₁ y / Module.finrank ℚ K

The normalized logarithmic height of y ∈ K: Mathlib's Height.logHeight₁ y, which on a number field is Σ_{v infinite} mult(v) log⁺ |y|_v + Σ_{v finite} log⁺ |y|_v, divided by [K : ℚ] (the normalized degree of [GenEll] page 4).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logDiffNFdef

noncomputable def logDiffNF : ℝ :=
  Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (differentIdeal ℤ (𝓞 K))) / Module.finrank ℚ K

The normalized log-different of K ([GenEll] Definition 1.5 (iii), page 8, for a point whose minimal field of definition is K): (1 / [K : ℚ]) log N(𝔇_K), with 𝔇_K the different ideal of 𝓞_K over ℤ. It equals (1 / [K : ℚ]) log |disc K| (logDiffNF_eq).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logCondNFdef

noncomputable def logCondNF (y : K) : ℝ :=
  (∑ᶠ v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K),
    if MeetsBoundaryAt K v y then Real.log (Nat.card (𝓞 K ⧸ v.asIdeal)) else 0) /
    Module.finrank ℚ K

The normalized log-conductor of y ∈ K with respect to D = {0, 1, ∞} ([GenEll] Definition 1.5 (iv), page 8, with correction (12), for the model ℙ¹_ℤ with the three sections): (1 / [K : ℚ]) Σ log q_v over the primes v of 𝓞_K at which y meets D, each counted once, where q_v is the cardinality of the residue field 𝓞_K / v.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMostdef

def VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [NumberField F] (x : F),
    IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {x} = ⊤ → Module.finrank ℚ F ≤ d → x ≠ 0 → x ≠ 1 →
      heightNF F x ≤ (1 + ε) * (logDiffNF F + logCondNF F x) + C

**An open statement, not a theorem: the instance X = ℙ¹_ℚ, D = {0, 1, ∞} of the conclusion of IUT IV, Corollary 2.3, for points of degree at most d.** For every ε > 0 there is a constant C such that for every number field F generated by a point x ∈ F \ {0, 1} with [F : ℚ] ≤ d, ht(x) ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff(x) + log-cond(x)) + C. Here F is the minimal field of definition of the point ([GenEll] Definition 1.5 (i)), and the three functions are heightNF, logDiffNF and logCondNF. The constant depends on d and ε only, as in Corollary 2.3 (page 54). This file proves that the case d = 1 is equivalent to the abc conjecture (degreeAtMostOne_iff_ABC).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegreedef

def VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d

**An open statement, not a theorem: the instance X = ℙ¹_ℚ, D = {0, 1, ∞} of IUT IV, Corollary 2.3, equivalently of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 (i).** For every positive integer d, the inequality ht ≲ (1 + ε)(log-diff + log-cond) holds on the points of ℙ¹ \ {0, 1, ∞} of degree at most d, for every ε > 0. It implies the abc conjecture (abc_of_boundedDegree); the converse is not proved here.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.finrank_pos_realtheorem

theorem finrank_pos_real : (0 : ℝ) < Module.finrank ℚ K

The degree [K : ℚ] is positive.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.meetsBoundaryAt_iff_valuationtheorem

theorem meetsBoundaryAt_iff_valuation (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (y : K) :
  MeetsBoundaryAt K v y ↔ v.valuation K y ≠ 1 ∨ v.valuation K (y - 1) ≠ 1

The pullback description of the conductor is the valuation description: y meets {0, 1, ∞} at v exactly when v(y) ≠ 0 or v(y - 1) ≠ 0 (additively), that is, when the multiplicative v-adic valuation of y or of y - 1 is not 1.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logDiffNF_eqtheorem

theorem logDiffNF_eq : logDiffNF K = Real.log |(discr K : ℝ)| / Module.finrank ℚ K

The log-different is (1 / [K : ℚ]) log |disc K|, by Mathlib's NumberField.absNorm_differentIdeal.

theorem meetsBoundaryAt_one_sub_iff (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (y : K) :
  MeetsBoundaryAt K v (1 - y) ↔ MeetsBoundaryAt K v y

The point 1 - y meets {0, 1, ∞} at the same primes as y (x ↦ 1 - x exchanges 0 and 1 and fixes ∞).

The point 1 / y meets {0, 1, ∞} at the same primes as y (x ↦ 1 / x exchanges 0 and ∞ and fixes 1).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.mulHeight₁_algebraMap_rattheorem

theorem mulHeight₁_algebraMap_rat (q : ℚ) :
  Height.mulHeight₁ (algebraMap ℚ K q) = Height.mulHeight₁ q ^ Module.finrank ℚ K

For rational q, the multiplicative height of q in K is the [K : ℚ]-th power of its height in ℚ: at each finite place the coprime numerator and denominator of q give the maximum 1, and at each infinite place the maximum is max(|num q|, den q).

theorem logHeight₁_algebraMap_rat (q : ℚ) :
