For rational q, Height.logHeight₁ q computed in K is [K : ℚ] times its value in ℚ.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.heightNF_algebraMap_rattheorem

theorem heightNF_algebraMap_rat (q : ℚ) :
  heightNF K (algebraMap ℚ K q) = Height.logHeight₁ q

The normalized height of a rational number does not depend on the number field: it is Height.logHeight₁ q = log max(|num q|, den q) in every number field.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.meetsBoundaryAt_rat_ifftheorem

theorem meetsBoundaryAt_rat_iff (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 ℚ)) (q : ℚ) :
  MeetsBoundaryAt ℚ v q ↔

A rational number q meets {0, 1, ∞} at the prime v of 𝓞_ℚ exactly when the prime number p generating v divides num q, num q - den q (the numerator of q - 1) or den q.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logIfDvddef

log p if the prime p divides m, else 0.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.finsum_logIfDvdtheorem

  (∑ᶠ p : {p : ℕ // p.Prime}, logIfDvd m p) = Real.log ((∏ p ∈ m.primeFactors, p : ℕ) : ℝ)

The sum of log p over the primes dividing m ≠ 0 is the logarithm of the product of these primes.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.ratConductor_eq_prod_primeFactorstheorem

theorem ratConductor_eq_prod_primeFactors (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1) :
  ratConductor q = ∏ p ∈ (q.num.natAbs * (q.num - q.den).natAbs * q.den).primeFactors, p

The conductor of a rational number q ∉ {0, 1} is the product of the primes dividing |num q| · |num q - den q| · den q.

**The log-conductor of a rational point is log (ratConductor q).**

IUT.VojtaNumberField.reducesAwayFromBoundary_ringEquiv_ifftheorem

theorem reducesAwayFromBoundary_ringEquiv_iff (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (y : K) :
  ReducesAwayFromBoundary L
      (HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv (RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e) v) (e y) ↔
    ReducesAwayFromBoundary K v y

An isomorphism of number fields carries local representations (a : b) to local representations, and back.

      (HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv (RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e) v).asIdeal) =
    Nat.card (𝓞 K ⧸ v.asIdeal)

The residue fields at corresponding primes have the same cardinality.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logCondNF_ringEquivtheorem

The log-conductor is invariant under isomorphisms of number fields.

  VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational

The degree one case implies the statement on rational points, by taking F = ℚ.

theorem degreeAtMostOne_of_rational (h : VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational) :
  VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost 1

The statement on rational points implies the degree one case: a number field F of degree one is isomorphic to ℚ through algebraMap ℚ F, the height of a rational number is the same in F (heightNF_algebraMap_rat), and the log-different and the log-conductor are carried over by the isomorphism.

The degree one case is equivalent to the statement on rational points.

theorem degreeAtMostOne_iff_ABC :
  VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost 1 ↔ Challenge.ABC

The degree one case is equivalent to the abc conjecture. Neither side is proved here.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.degreeAtMost_monotheorem

The statement for points of degree at most d implies the statement for degree at most d' when d' ≤ d: the same constant works.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.abc_of_degreeAtMosttheorem

theorem abc_of_degreeAtMost {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (h : VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d) :
  Challenge.ABC

**For every d ≥ 1, the statement for points of degree at most d implies the abc conjecture.** For d = 0 the statement is vacuous: no number field has degree 0.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.abc_of_boundedDegreetheorem

theorem abc_of_boundedDegree (h : VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree) : Challenge.ABC

The bounded degree statement implies the abc conjecture. Neither is proved here.

  -IsCyclotomicExtension.zeta 3 ℚ K

The point -ζ₃ of ℚ(ζ₃), a primitive sixth root of unity, with ζ₃ Mathlib's chosen primitive cube root of unity IsCyclotomicExtension.zeta 3 ℚ K.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.finrank_cyclotomicThreetheorem

theorem finrank_cyclotomicThree : Module.finrank ℚ K = 2

ℚ(ζ₃) has degree 2.

-ζ₃ generates ℚ(ζ₃).

**The height of -ζ₃ is 0**: it is a root of unity.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logDiffNF_cyclotomicThreetheorem

theorem logDiffNF_cyclotomicThree : logDiffNF K = Real.log 3 / 2

**The log-different of ℚ(ζ₃) is (1/2) log 3**: its discriminant is -3 (IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.discr_prime).

IUT.VojtaNumberField.logCondNF_sixthRoottheorem

theorem logCondNF_sixthRoot : logCondNF K (sixthRoot K) = 0

**The log-conductor of -ζ₃ is 0**: x = -ζ₃ and x - 1 = ζ₃² are units, so x meets {0, 1, ∞} at no prime.

IUT.VojtaNumberField.exists_point_cyclotomicFieldThreetheorem

theorem exists_point_cyclotomicFieldThree :
  Module.finrank ℚ (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) = 2 ∧
    logDiffNF (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) = Real.log 3 / 2 ∧
    ∃ x : CyclotomicField 3 ℚ, IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {x} = ⊤ ∧ x ≠ 0 ∧ x ≠ 1 ∧
      heightNF (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) x = 0 ∧ logCondNF (CyclotomicField 3 ℚ) x = 0

A concrete point of degree two. In Mathlib's CyclotomicField 3 ℚ, of degree 2 and log-different (1/2) log 3, the point -ζ₃ generates the field, lies outside {0, 1}, and has height 0 and log-conductor 0.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit

IUT/Applications/ZhouExplicit.lean · imports IUT.Applications.ABC, IUT.ABC.Variants, IUT.PaperIV.Theorem1_10.StepV

Zhou's explicit consequences of inter-universal Teichmüller theory over ℚ (elementary part)

Module documentation

Sources:

  • Zhong-Peng Zhou, The inter-universal Teichmüller theory and new Diophantine results over the rational numbers. I, arXiv 2503.14510, version 1 (called Zhou I below): Definition 1.7 (i) and Definition 1.8 (page 11), Lemma 1.3 (page 7), Lemma 1.4 (page 8), Lemma 1.5 (page 9), Proposition 1.9 and Proposition 1.10 with its proof (pages 12 and 13), Corollary 1.13 (page 14), Proposition 2.7 with its proof (page 21), Lemma 3.1 (page 25), Theorem 3.2 with its proof (pages 27 to 29), Corollary 3.3 with its proof (page 29).
  • Zhong-Peng Zhou, The inter-universal Teichmüller theory and new Diophantine results over rational numbers. II, arXiv 2510.05448 (Zhou II): Remark 1.1.1 (page 6), which claims that the results of IUT I to IV hold for "2-torsion initial Θ-data". Nothing in this file uses it.

Pages read for this file: Zhou I pages 1 to 38 (the whole paper); Zhou II pages 1 to 24 and 36. Formulas were taken from the TeX sources of both papers and compared with the extracted text of the PDFs; no page was checked against a rendered image.

What this file is and is not

This file is not a formalization of Zhou's Definition 1.8, nor of IUT III, Corollary 3.12. The number −|log(Θ)| of Zhou I, Definition 1.8, is the log-volume of holomorphic hulls in tensor products ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_{k_i} of rings of integers of local fields, normalized as in [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7. Neither these tensor products and their normalizations nor the log-volume are available in this library or in Mathlib, so the model cannot be given with its real meaning. What is formalized is its numerical shadow: the procession average over j ∈ {1, …, l*} and the sum over places (Definition 1.8 (ii), (iii) for F_mod = ℚ, where the weighted average over tuples of places is trivial), applied to local real numbers that are hypotheses, bounded above by the right side of Lemma 1.4 (1.1) and of Lemma 1.5.

The model, the inequality of Proposition 1.9 (−(1/2l)·log 𝔮 ≤ −|log(Θ)|, "the μ6-version of [IUT III], Corollary 3.12") and every explicit statement here are the author's (Zhou's) formulations. Zhou I introduces the model as "a modified version of [IUT IV], Theorem 1.10 and [ExpEst], Theorem 5.1"; Proposition 1.9 is assumed there with a one-sentence proof. In particular Zhou's a_v, b_v (zhouA, zhouB below) differ from the a_i, b_i of IUT IV, Proposition 1.2 (IUT.PaperIV.Proposition1_2.a, b).

Contents
  1. zhouA, zhouB: the constants of Definition 1.7 (i); a_v = -b_v = 1/e_v when e_v ≤ p_v - 2 (zhouA_eq_inv_of_le, zhouB_eq_neg_inv_of_le), the case p - 1 ≤ e ≤ p(p - 1) of the proof of Proposition 1.10 (zhouB_eq_of_mid, zhouA_add_zhouB_le_of_mid).
  2. The chain from the model inequality (Proposition 1.9) and the local bounds (Lemmas 1.4, 1.5) to the inequality (1.11-eq7 in the TeX) of the proof of Proposition 1.10: zhou_prop110_of_model.
  3. Proposition 2.7 from Corollary 1.13 (the coefficient identity): zhou_prop27_of_cor113.
  4. Lemma 3.1 (ii), the averaging lemma, in full: zhou_lemma31_ii.
  5. Theorem 3.2 (i) and Corollary 3.3 as statements (ZhouTheorem32i, ZhouCorollary33), the transfer from the N-level inequality of the proof (3-2-eq4) to Theorem 3.2 (i) (zhouTheorem32i_of_nLevel), and Corollary 3.3 from Theorem 3.2 (i) (zhouCorollary33_of_theorem32i).
  6. The relation to the abc conjecture: Corollary 3.3 gives the library's fixed exponent bound IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponent κ (c ≤ K·rad(abc)^κ) for every κ > 3/2 (abcWithExponent_of_zhouCorollary33).
Open statements and what is not proved

ZhouTheorem32i, ZhouCorollary33, ZhouNLevelBound and ZhouComputedRange are open statements, and so is IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponent κ for every κ > 1 (for κ ≤ 1 the library proves it false, IUT.ABC.Variants.not_abcWithExponent_of_le_one). None of the first four is proved here, and each is conditional in the papers on Proposition 1.9 (the μ6-version of IUT III, Corollary 3.12), on Lemmas 1.1 to 1.5 (local field theory, partly "proved similarly to" IUT IV, Proposition 1.2), on the construction of initial Θ-data in Section 2, on analytic prime number estimates (Lemma 2.8, citing Dusart and Rosser and Schoenfeld), on a real inequality asserted in the proof of Theorem 3.2, and on computations in the author's code repository that are not published in the papers (ZhouComputedRange is one of them). Not formalized: Lemma 1.4 itself (it needs the tensor products), Corollary 1.13 (the algorithm for Vol(R)), Lemma 2.8, Proposition 2.9, and the analytic part of Theorem 3.2 for log N ≥ e^31.

What does not follow: ZhouCorollary33 does not imply Challenge.ABC; the exponent it gives on rad(abc) for c is (3 + 3ε)/2 > 3/2, never 1 + ε for small ε. Conversely Challenge.ABC gives no explicit constant, so it does not imply ZhouCorollary33 or ZhouTheorem32i; it implies only bounds of the same shape with unspecified constants.

Public declarations

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouAdef

noncomputable def zhouA (p e : ℕ) : ℝ := 1 / (e : ℝ) * ⌈((e : ℝ) + 1) / ((p : ℝ) - 1)⌉

Zhou I, Definition 1.7 (i) and Lemma 1.3: a_v = (1/e_v)·⌈(e_v + 1)/(p_v - 1)⌉, as a function of the residue characteristic p and the ramification index e.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouBdef

noncomputable def zhouB (p e : ℕ) : ℝ := ⨆ n : ℕ, ((n : ℝ) - (p : ℝ) ^ n / e)

Zhou I, Definition 1.7 (i) and Lemma 1.3: b_v = sup_{n ≥ 0} (n - p_v^n / e_v). The supremum is Mathlib's iSup over ℕ; it is attained (the theorems below exhibit the maximizing n in the cases used).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_bernoullitheorem

theorem zhou_bernoulli {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (n : ℕ) : 1 + n * (p - 1) ≤ p ^ n

Bernoulli's inequality 1 + n(p - 1) ≤ p^n for real p ≥ 1.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouA_eq_inv_of_letheorem

theorem zhouA_eq_inv_of_le {p e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hep : e + 2 ≤ p) :
  zhouA p e = 1 / (e : ℝ)

Zhou I, Definition 1.7 (i): a_v = 1/e_v when 1 ≤ e_v ≤ p_v - 2.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouB_eq_neg_inv_of_letheorem

theorem zhouB_eq_neg_inv_of_le {p e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hep : e + 2 ≤ p) :
  zhouB p e = -(1 / (e : ℝ))

Zhou I, Definition 1.7 (i): b_v = -1/e_v when 1 ≤ e_v ≤ p_v - 2 (attained at n = 0, by n·e + 1 ≤ p^n).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouB_eq_of_midtheorem

theorem zhouB_eq_of_mid {p e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (h1 : p ≤ e + 1) (h2 : e ≤ p * (p - 1)) :
  zhouB p e = 1 - (p : ℝ) / e

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: b_p = 1 - p/e_p when p - 1 ≤ e_p ≤ p(p - 1) (attained at n = 1).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_ceil_div_letheorem

theorem zhou_ceil_div_le (k : ℤ) {m : ℤ} (hm : 0 < m) :
  (⌈(k : ℝ) / m⌉ : ℝ) ≤ ((k : ℝ) + m - 1) / m

For integers k and m > 0, ⌈k/m⌉ ≤ (k + m - 1)/m.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouA_letheorem

theorem zhouA_le {p e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  zhouA p e ≤ 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) + 1 / (e : ℝ)

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: a_p ≤ 1/(p - 1) + 1/e_p.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouA_add_zhouB_of_letheorem

theorem zhouA_add_zhouB_of_le {p e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hep : e + 2 ≤ p) :
  zhouA p e + zhouB p e = 0

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: a_p + b_p = 0 when e_p ≤ p - 2.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouA_add_zhouB_le_of_midtheorem

theorem zhouA_add_zhouB_le_of_mid {p e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (h1 : p ≤ e + 1)
  (h2 : e ≤ p * (p - 1)) :
  zhouA p e + zhouB p e ≤ 1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) + 1 - ((p : ℝ) - 1) / e

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: when p - 1 ≤ e_p ≤ p(p - 1), a_p + b_p ≤ 1/(p - 1) + 1 - (p - 1)/e_p.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouVp2pdef

noncomputable def zhouVp2p (p : ℕ) : ℝ := if p = 2 then 2 else 1

v_p(2p) for a prime p: 2 if p = 2, 1 otherwise.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouVp2p_letheorem

theorem zhouVp2p_le {p e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (he : 1 ≤ e) {d : ℝ} (hd : 1 - 1 / (e : ℝ) ≤ d) :
  zhouVp2p p ≤ d + zhouA p e

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: if d_p ≥ 1 - 1/e_p (Lemma 1.2), then d_p + a_p ≥ v_p(2p).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouProcessionAveragedef

noncomputable def zhouProcessionAverage (m : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 / (m : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 m, f j

Zhou I, Definition 1.8 (ii), the procession normalization: (1/l*)·∑_{j=1}^{l*} f(j), with m = l*.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouLogVolumeQdef

noncomputable def zhouLogVolumeQ (m : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (volArc : ℕ → ℝ)
    (vol : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  zhouProcessionAverage m volArc + ∑ p ∈ P, zhouProcessionAverage m (vol p)

The numerical shadow of Zhou I, Definition 1.8 (iii), for F_mod = ℚ: the archimedean term plus the sum over a finite set P of primes of the procession averages of local real numbers vol p j (standing for −|log(Θ)|_{v_p, j}) and volArc j (for −|log(Θ)|_{v_ℝ, j}). For F_mod = ℚ the weighted average of Definition 1.8 (ii) over tuples of places has one term. The paper sums over all of 𝕍_ℚ; here the primes outside P are absent, which is the case only if their terms vanish (not addressed).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouLemma14Bounddef

noncomputable def zhouLemma14Bound (l : ℝ) (p e : ℕ) (d vq : ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (max (⌈-((j : ℝ) ^ 2 / (2 * l)) * vq + j * d + (j + 1) * zhouA p e⌉ : ℝ)
      (-((j : ℝ) ^ 2 / (2 * l)) * vq + zhouVp2p p * (j + 1)) + (j + 1) * zhouB p e)
    * Real.log p

The right side of Zhou I, Lemma 1.4 (1.1), at the tuple (v_p, …, v_p) of length j + 1 (as in (1.11-eq3) of the proof of Proposition 1.10, where F_mod = ℚ): with |I| = j + 1 copies of one field, d'_I = j·d_p, a_I = (j+1)·a_p, b_I = (j+1)·b_p, and degree λ = (j²/2l)·v_p(q_p).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouLemma14Bound_letheorem

theorem zhouLemma14Bound_le {l : ℝ} (hl : 0 < l) {p e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (he : 1 ≤ e)
  {d vq : ℝ} (hd : 1 - 1 / (e : ℝ) ≤ d) (hdint : ∃ s : ℤ, d = s / e)
  (hq : ∃ t : ℤ, vq * e = 2 * l * t) (j : ℕ) :
  zhouLemma14Bound l p e d vq j
    ≤ (-((j : ℝ) ^ 2 / (2 * l)) * vq + (j + 1) * (d + zhouA p e + zhouB p e))
      * Real.log p

The proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, (1.11-eq4) and (1.11-eq5): if 2l ∣ e_p·v_p(q_p), d_p ∈ (1/e_p)ℤ and d_p ≥ 1 - 1/e_p, the right side of Lemma 1.4 is at most (-(j²/2l)·v_p(q_p) + (j+1)(d_p + a_p + b_p))·log p.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouProcessionAverage_monotheorem

theorem zhouProcessionAverage_mono {m : ℕ} {f g : ℕ → ℝ} (h : ∀ j ∈ Icc 1 m, f j ≤ g j) :
  zhouProcessionAverage m f ≤ zhouProcessionAverage m g

Monotonicity of the procession average.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_procession_identitytheorem

theorem zhou_procession_identity (Q X : ℝ) (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
  zhouProcessionAverage m (fun j => -((j : ℝ) ^ 2 / (2 * (2 * m + 1))) * Q + (j + 1) * X)
    = -(((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) + 1) / 24) * Q + ((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) + 5) / 4 * X

The averaging of the proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13, with l = 2m + 1, m = l*: (1/l*)·∑_{j=1}^{l*} (-(j²/2l)·Q + (j+1)·X) = -((l+1)/24)·Q + ((l+5)/4)·X. (The same computation as IUT.PaperIV.Theorem1_10.procession_average.)

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_prop110_coefficienttheorem

theorem zhou_prop110_coefficient {l Q X : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l)
  (h : -(1 / (2 * l)) * Q ≤ -((l + 1) / 24) * Q + (l + 5) / 4 * X) :
  1 / 6 * Q ≤ (l ^ 2 + 5 * l) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12) * X

The last step of the proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10, page 13: for l ≥ 5, -(1/2l)·Q ≤ -((l+1)/24)·Q + ((l+5)/4)·X gives (1/6)·Q ≤ ((l² + 5l)/(l² + l - 12))·X.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_prop110_of_modeltheorem

theorem zhou_prop110_of_model (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, 2 ≤ p)
  (e : ℕ → ℕ) (he : ∀ p ∈ P, 1 ≤ e p) (d vq : ℕ → ℝ)
  (hd : ∀ p ∈ P, 1 - 1 / (e p : ℝ) ≤ d p) (hdint : ∀ p ∈ P, ∃ s : ℤ, d p = s / e p)
  (hq : ∀ p ∈ P, ∃ t : ℤ, vq p * e p = 2 * (2 * m + 1 : ℝ) * t)
  (vol : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (volArc : ℕ → ℝ)
  (hloc : ∀ p ∈ P, ∀ j ∈ Icc 1 m,
    vol p j ≤ zhouLemma14Bound (2 * m + 1) p (e p) (d p) (vq p) j)
  (harc : ∀ j ∈ Icc 1 m, volArc j ≤ (j + 1) * Real.log Real.pi)
  (hmodel : -(1 / (2 * (2 * m + 1 : ℝ))) * ∑ p ∈ P, vq p * Real.log p
    ≤ zhouLogVolumeQ m P volArc vol) :
  1 / 6 * ∑ p ∈ P, vq p * Real.log p
    ≤ ((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) ^ 2 + 5 * (2 * m + 1)) / ((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (2 * m + 1) - 12)
      * (Real.log Real.pi
        + ∑ p ∈ P, (d p + zhouA p (e p) + zhouB p (e p)) * Real.log p)

From the model inequality to (1.11-eq7) of the proof of Zhou I, Proposition 1.10. Let l = 2m + 1 with m = l* ≥ 2 (so l ≥ 5), P a finite set of primes, and at each p ∈ P a ramification index e_p ≥ 1, a different index d_p ∈ (1/e_p)ℤ with d_p ≥ 1 - 1/e_p (Lemma 1.2), and v_p(q_p) with 2l ∣ e_p·v_p(q_p) ((1.8-eq), from the 2l-torsion). Assume: * hloc: each local term vol p j (standing for −|log(Θ)|_{v_p, j}) is at most the right side of Lemma 1.4 (1.1) at the tuple (v_p, …, v_p); * harc: each archimedean term is at most (j+1)·log π (Lemma 1.5 with |I| = j + 1); * hmodel: Proposition 1.9 in the numerical form -(1/2l)·log 𝔮 ≤ −|log(Θ)|, with log 𝔮 = ∑_p v_p(q_p)·log p and −|log(Θ)| as in zhouLogVolumeQ. Then (1/6)·log 𝔮 ≤ ((l² + 5l)/(l² + l - 12))·(log π + ∑_p (d_p + a_p + b_p)·log p). hmodel is the assumed IUT input (Zhou's form of the μ6-version of IUT III, Corollary 3.12); hloc and harc stand for Lemmas 1.4 and 1.5, which are not formalized.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_prop27_coefficienttheorem

theorem zhou_prop27_coefficient {l : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l) :
  (l ^ 2 + 5 * l) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12) * (1 - 1 / (3 * l))
    = 1 + (11 * l + 31) / (3 * l ^ 2 + 3 * l - 36)

The coefficient identity behind Zhou I, Proposition 2.7, page 21: ((l² + 5l)/(l² + l - 12))·(1 - 1/(3l)) = 1 + (11l + 31)/(3l² + 3l - 36).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_prop27_of_cor113theorem

theorem zhou_prop27_of_cor113 {l LN' R Rl V : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l) (hRl : 0 ≤ Rl)
  (hcor : 1 / 6 * (2 * LN') ≤ (l ^ 2 + 5 * l) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12)
    * ((1 - 1 / (3 * l)) * R - 1 / 3 * (1 - 1 / l) * Rl) + V) :
  LN' ≤ (3 + (11 * l + 31) / (l ^ 2 + l - 12)) * R + 3 * V

Zhou I, Proposition 2.7, from Corollary 1.13 (the step "(2-1-eq1) follows directly from Corollary 1.13", page 21). For μ6-initial Θ-data of type (l, N², N'²) admitting a dataset with e_0 = 3, Corollary 1.13 reads (1/6)·log(N'²) ≤ ((l²+5l)/(l²+l-12))·((1 - 1/(3l))·log rad(N²) - (1/3)(1 - 1/l)·log rad(N_l)) + Vol. With LN' = log N', R = log rad N = log rad N² and R_l = log rad(N_l) ≥ 0, this gives log N' ≤ (3 + (11l + 31)/(l² + l - 12))·R + 3·Vol, the hypothesis (3-1-eq1) of Lemma 3.1 (there log N'_l = ∑_{p ≠ l, l ∤ v_p(N)} v_p(N)·log p). Corollary 1.13 itself is a hypothesis.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouCoeffdef

noncomputable def zhouCoeff (l : ℕ) : ℝ := (11 * (l : ℝ) + 31) / ((l : ℝ) ^ 2 + l - 12)

The coefficient (11l + 31)/(l² + l - 12) of Zhou I, Proposition 2.7 and Lemma 3.1.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_lemma31_iitheorem

theorem zhou_lemma31_ii (N : ℕ) (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : ∀ l ∈ S, l.Prime)
  (hSne : S.Nonempty) (k : ℕ)
  (hk : ∀ T ∈ S.powersetCard k, Real.log N < (∏ p ∈ T, (p : ℝ)) * Real.log 2)
  (Vol : ℕ → ℝ)
  (hpart : ∀ l ∈ S, ∑ p ∈ N.primeFactors with (p ≠ l ∧ ¬ l ∣ N.factorization p),
      (N.factorization p : ℝ) * Real.log p
    ≤ (3 + zhouCoeff l) * Real.log (rad N) + 3 * Vol l) :
  Real.log N ≤ (3 + 1 / (S.card : ℝ) * ∑ l ∈ S, zhouCoeff l) * Real.log (rad N)
    + 3 / (S.card : ℝ) * ∑ l ∈ S, Vol l + k * Real.log N / S.card

Zhou I, Lemma 3.1 (ii), page 25. Let N be a natural number, h = log N, S a finite nonempty set of primes with n = |S|, and k such that every k-element subset of S has product > h/log 2 (this is the paper's k(S) > h/log 2, since k(S), the product of the k smallest elements of S, is the least such product). Suppose that for each l ∈ S ∑_{p ≠ l, l ∤ v_p(N)} v_p(N)·log p ≤ (3 + (11l+31)/(l²+l-12))·log rad N + 3·Vol(l) (3-1-eq1). Then h ≤ (3 + a_1)·log rad N + a_2 + k·h/n with a_1 = (1/n)∑_{l ∈ S} (11l+31)/(l²+l-12) and a_2 = (3/n)∑_{l ∈ S} Vol(l). The paper also assumes N > 0, l ≥ 5 for l ∈ S, n ≥ 2, 2 ≤ k ≤ n and Vol(l) ≥ 0; the proof does not use them, and they are dropped here.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouNdef

def zhouN (a b c : ℤ) : ℕ := (a * b * c).natAbs / Nat.gcd 16 (a * b * c).natAbs

N = |abc|/gcd(16, abc) of the proof of Zhou I, Theorem 3.2 (and Proposition 2.7).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.ZhouTheorem32idef

def ZhouTheorem32i : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b = c →
    700 ≤ Real.log ((a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) →
    Real.log ((a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ)
      ≤ 3 * Real.log (rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ)
        + 8 * Real.sqrt (Real.log ((a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ)
          * Real.log (Real.log ((a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ)))

Zhou I, Theorem 3.2 (i) (page 27), the author's statement; not proved here. For nonzero integers a, b, c with gcd(a, b) = 1 and a + b = c: if log|abc| ≥ 700, then log|abc| ≤ 3·log rad(abc) + 8·√(log|abc|·log log|abc|). ("Coprime" for the triple is read as gcd(a, b) = 1, equivalent to pairwise coprimality since a + b = c.)

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.ZhouNLevelBounddef

def ZhouNLevelBound (h₀ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b = c →
    h₀ ≤ Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) →
    Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) - 3 * Real.log (rad (zhouN a b c) : ℝ) + 4 * Real.log 2
      < 8 * Real.sqrt (Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ)))

The inequality (3-2-eq4) of the proof of Zhou I, Theorem 3.2, page 28, for log N ≥ h_0: log N - 3·log rad N + 4·log 2 < 8·√(log N · log log N) with N = |abc|/gcd(16, abc). The paper asserts it for h_0 = 680, from (3-2-eq3) (for log N ≥ e^31: Proposition 2.9, Lemma 3.1, Lemma 2.8 and a real inequality) and from ZhouComputedRange (for 680 ≤ log N ≤ e^31).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.ZhouComputedRangedef

def ZhouComputedRange : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b = c →
    680 ≤ Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) → Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp 31 →
    Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) - 3 * Real.log (rad (zhouN a b c) : ℝ) + 4 * Real.log 2
      < 8 * Real.sqrt (Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (zhouN a b c : ℝ)))

The range of the proof of Zhou I, Theorem 3.2 (i), page 28, covered by "the computation in [code_of_zpzhou]" and not by an argument in the paper: (3-2-eq4) for 680 ≤ log N ≤ e^31.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_rad_le_of_dvdtheorem

theorem zhou_rad_le_of_dvd {m n : ℕ} (h : m ∣ n) (hn : n ≠ 0) : rad m ≤ rad n

The radical is monotone for divisibility: m ∣ n, n ≠ 0 give rad m ≤ rad n.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouTheorem32i_of_nLeveltheorem

theorem zhouTheorem32i_of_nLevel (h : ZhouNLevelBound 680) : ZhouTheorem32i

The transfer step of the proof of Zhou I, Theorem 3.2 (i), pages 28 and 29: the N-level inequality (3-2-eq4) for log N ≥ 680 gives Theorem 3.2 (i), using log N ≤ log|abc| ≤ log N + 4·log 2 and rad N ≤ rad(abc).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.ZhouCorollary33def

def ZhouCorollary33 : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ 1 / 10 →
    ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → Int.gcd a b = 1 → a + b = c →
      ((a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ)
        ≤ max (Real.exp (400 * ε⁻¹ ^ 2 * Real.log ε⁻¹))
          ((rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) ^ (3 + 3 * ε))

Zhou I, Corollary 3.3 (page 29), the author's statement; not proved here. For 0 < ε ≤ 1/10 and nonzero integers a, b, c with gcd(a, b) = 1 and a + b = c: |abc| ≤ max{exp(400·ε^{-2}·log(ε^{-1})), rad(abc)^{3 + 3ε}}.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_log_ten_gttheorem

theorem zhou_log_ten_gt : (2.28 : ℝ) < Real.log 10

log 10 > 2.28, from 2^33 < 10^10 and log 2 > 0.6931471803.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_log_four_hundred_lttheorem

theorem zhou_log_four_hundred_lt : Real.log 400 < (6.24 : ℝ)

log 400 < 6.24, from 400 < 2^9 and log 2 < 0.6931471808.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_log_le_div_exp_onetheorem

theorem zhou_log_le_div_exp_one {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) : Real.log y ≤ y / Real.exp 1

log y ≤ y/e for y > 0.

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_cor33_scalartheorem

theorem zhou_cor33_scalar {x : ℝ} (hx : 10 ≤ x) :
  64 * (1 + x) ^ 2 * Real.log (400 * x ^ 2 * Real.log x) < 400 * x ^ 2 * Real.log x

The scalar inequality (3-3-eq1) of the proof of Zhou I, Corollary 3.3, page 29: for x = ε^{-1} ≥ 10, h_0 = 400·x²·log x and u_0 = 64·(1 + x)², u_0·log h_0 < h_0. (The paper proves f(x) = log h_0 - log log h_0 - log u_0 > 0 from f(10) > 0 and f' > 0; here it is proved from log x ≥ log 10 > 2.28, log 400 < 6.24, log log x ≤ (log x)/e and (1 + x)² ≤ 1.21·x².)

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhou_log_mul_letheorem

theorem zhou_log_mul_le {a b : ℝ} (ha : Real.exp 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) :
  Real.log b * a ≤ Real.log a * b

For e ≤ a ≤ b: log b · a ≤ log a · b (the monotonicity of y/log y used in the proof of Zhou I, Corollary 3.3, (3-3-eq2)).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.zhouCorollary33_of_theorem32itheorem

theorem zhouCorollary33_of_theorem32i (h : ZhouTheorem32i) : ZhouCorollary33

Zhou I, Corollary 3.3 from Theorem 3.2 (i) (the proof on page 29).

IUT.Applications.ZhouExplicit.abcWithExponent_of_zhouCorollary33theorem

theorem abcWithExponent_of_zhouCorollary33 (h : ZhouCorollary33) (κ : ℝ) (hκ : 3 / 2 < κ) :
  IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponent κ

**Zhou's Corollary 3.3 gives the fixed exponent bound IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponent κ for every κ > 3/2.** From ab ≥ a + b - 1 = c - 1 we get abc ≥ c(c - 1) ≥ c²/2, so Corollary 3.3 with 3 + 3ε ≤ 2κ gives c² ≤ 2·exp(h_0(ε))·rad(abc)^{3 + 3ε}. Nothing better than 3/2 follows, and in particular not Challenge.ABC (exponent 1 + ε).

Variants of the abc statement

Signed and fixed exponent forms of the abc statement, each proved equivalent to Challenge.ABC, and elementary facts about abc triples. Nothing here says whether the abc conjecture holds.

IUT.ABC.Elementary

IUT/ABC/Elementary.lean · imports IUT.ABC.Variants

Elementary results around the abc conjecture from the literature

Module documentation

This file collects elementary statements, each proved, taken from recent papers on the abc conjecture, together with four named statements that are not proved here (a claim of an unrefereed preprint, an open finiteness statement, a theorem of a paper, and a classical divisor bound used as an explicit hypothesis). Nothing here says whether the abc conjecture holds. No page of the IUT papers is used.

Sources (formulas taken from the TeX sources; pages read for this file are the sections named; no page was checked against a rendered image):

  • C. Soulé, On the abc conjecture, arXiv 2611.05217 (November 2026, unrefereed preprint), Introduction, statements of Theorems A and B.
  • J. Cuevas Barrientos and H. Pasten, On the greatest prime factor of polynomial values and subexponential Szpiro in families, arXiv 2504.15971, Section 4 (Lemma 4.2) and Section 5 (the unnumbered display 4^P(M) ≥ ∏_{p ≤ P(M)} p ≥ rad(M)).
  • K. Joshi, Construction of Arithmetic Teichmuller spaces II: Proof of a local prototype of Mochizuki's Corollary 3.12, arXiv 2303.01662, Section 9, Theorem 9.2.1 and its proof.
  • R. Laniewski and K. Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, arXiv 2610.03212 (preprint), Sections 2 to 5: Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.2, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.4, Definition 4.1, Proposition 4.2.
  • M. van Frankenhuijsen, Two Restricted ABC Conjectures, arXiv 2010.09493, Sections 2 and 4: Lemmas 2.3, 2.4, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3.
  • P. Vojta, A more general abc conjecture, arXiv math/9806171, Proposition 2.6.
  • H. Pasten, Shimura curves and the abc conjecture, arXiv 1705.09251, Theorem 1.11 and Theorem 16.7.
Named statements that are not proved here
  • SouleTheoremBClaim: Theorem B of Soulé, c ≤ A(ε)·rad(abc)^(24 + ε). A claim of an unrefereed preprint. Proved: Challenge.ABC → SouleTheoremBClaim (souleTheoremBClaim_of_ABC) and SouleTheoremBClaim → ABCWithExponent κ for every κ > 24 (abcWithExponent_of_souleTheoremBClaim).
  • LaniewskiMullerMassBound: for every ε > 0 only finitely many triples have logarithmic mass Y = log(abc)/log rad(abc) > 3 + ε. Implied by Challenge.ABC (laniewskiMullerMassBound_of_ABC); it implies that only finitely many triples have quality > 3/2 + ε (finite_quality_gt_of_laniewskiMullerMassBound). Laniewski and Müller, Lemma 3.3, state that it is equivalent to Szpiro's conjecture for Frey curves; that equivalence needs the minimal discriminant and the conductor of the Frey curve and is not formalized.
  • PastenDivisorBound: Pasten's d(abc) < K_ε·rad(abc)^(8/3 + ε), a theorem of that paper (proved there with modularity and Shimura curves) that is not proved in this library. It is implied by Challenge.ABC (pastenDivisorBound_of_ABC), by an elementary argument (d(n) ≤ 2√n) that is not taken from the paper.
  • DivisorCountPowerBound: the classical divisor bound d(n) ≤ C_δ·n^δ for every δ > 0. It is not in Mathlib and is used only as an explicit hypothesis of divisorCount_le_rad_rpow_of_ABC.
Items not formalized
  • van Frankenhuijsen, Lemma 2.4 (r_K(a : 1-a : 1) ≤ 3[K:ℚ] + 3h_K(a : 1-a : 1)): the radical r_K of a number field point is not in Mathlib. Over ℚ, for a point with coprime integer coordinates it reduces to 1 + log rad(abc) ≤ 3 + 3 log max, which follows from IUT.ABC.Variants.rad_le_mul_mul and IUT.ABC.Variants.mul_mul_lt_cube.
  • Laniewski and Müller, Lemma 3.3 (the passage to Szpiro's conjecture): see above.
Public declarations

IUT.ABC.Elementary.SouleTheoremBClaimdef

def SouleTheoremBClaim : Prop := ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ABCWithExponent (24 + ε)

Theorem B of C. Soulé, On the abc conjecture, arXiv 2611.05217, as stated there: for every ε > 0 there is A(ε) > 0 such that all positive integers a, b, c with no common divisor and a + b = c satisfy c ≤ A(ε)·N^(24 + ε), N the product of the primes dividing abc. "No common divisor" is read as Nat.Coprime a b, which is equivalent since a + b = c; the constant and the non-strict inequality are those of ABCWithExponent. This is a claim of an unrefereed preprint of November 2026: the paper claims Theorem A (an effective Mordell bound for genus 2 curves) and states that Theorem B follows from it by work of Moret-Bailly. It is not proved or assumed anywhere in this library. It is strictly weaker than the abc conjecture as a statement: the conjecture implies it (souleTheoremBClaim_of_ABC), while it gives no bound with an exponent 24 or smaller, so it does not give the conjecture by any argument in this library.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.souleTheoremBClaim_of_ABCtheorem

theorem souleTheoremBClaim_of_ABC (h : ABC) : SouleTheoremBClaim

The abc conjecture implies Soulé's Theorem B.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.abcWithExponent_of_souleTheoremBClaimtheorem

theorem abcWithExponent_of_souleTheoremBClaim (h : SouleTheoremBClaim) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 24 < κ) :
  ABCWithExponent κ

Soulé's Theorem B gives the fixed exponent bound for every exponent κ > 24.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.souleTheoremBClaim_ifftheorem

theorem souleTheoremBClaim_iff :
  SouleTheoremBClaim ↔ ∀ κ : ℝ, 24 < κ → ABCWithExponent κ

Soulé's Theorem B is the fixed exponent bound for every exponent κ > 24.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.largestPrimeFactorOfdef

def largestPrimeFactorOf (M : ℕ) : ℕ := M.primeFactors.sup id

The largest prime factor P(M) of M, with the convention P(M) = 0 for M ≤ 1 (the supremum of the empty set of prime factors).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.rad_le_four_pow_largestPrimeFactorOftheorem

theorem rad_le_four_pow_largestPrimeFactorOf (M : ℕ) : rad M ≤ 4 ^ largestPrimeFactorOf M

**rad M ≤ 4^P(M)**, the display 4^P(M) ≥ ∏_{p ≤ P(M)} p ≥ rad(M) of Section 5 of J. Cuevas Barrientos and H. Pasten, On the greatest prime factor of polynomial values and subexponential Szpiro in families, arXiv 2504.15971 (unnumbered; stated there for M > 1). The radical divides the primorial of P(M), which is at most 4^P(M) by Mathlib's primorial_le_four_pow. With P(M) = 0 for M ≤ 1 it holds for every M.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.log_rad_le_largestPrimeFactorOf_mul_log_fourtheorem

theorem log_rad_le_largestPrimeFactorOf_mul_log_four (M : ℕ) :
  Real.log (rad M : ℝ) ≤ largestPrimeFactorOf M * Real.log 4

The logarithmic form: log rad M ≤ P(M)·log 4. So a lower bound for log rad M is a lower bound for the largest prime factor, as used in Section 5 of Cuevas Barrientos and Pasten.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.sum_Icc_sq_eqtheorem

theorem sum_Icc_sq_eq (n : ℕ) :
  ∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ((j : ℝ) ^ 2) = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) / 6

∑_{j=1}^{n} j² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.joshi_coefficient_eqtheorem

theorem joshi_coefficient_eq (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  (∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ((j : ℝ) ^ 2 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) * (1 / (2 * (2 * n + 1)))
    = 1 / 12 * (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ))

The coefficient identity of the proof of Theorem 9.2.1 of K. Joshi, Construction of Arithmetic Teichmuller spaces II: Proof of a local prototype of Mochizuki's Corollary 3.12, arXiv 2303.01662. With l = 2l* + 1 and n = l* ≥ 1: (∑_{j=1}^{l*} j²/l*²)·(1/(2l)) = (1/12)(1 + 1/l*).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.joshi_quarter_eqtheorem

theorem joshi_quarter_eq (n : ℕ) :
  1 / 4 * (1 - 1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 1)) = n / (2 * (2 * n + 1))

The right side of the comparison in the proof of Joshi's Theorem 9.2.1: (1/4)(1 - 1/l) = l*/(2l) for l = 2l* + 1.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.joshi_coefficient_lt_ifftheorem

theorem joshi_coefficient_lt_iff (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  1 / 12 * (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ)) < 1 / 4 * (1 - 1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 1)) ↔ 2 ≤ n

The comparison of the proof of Joshi's Theorem 9.2.1, with the threshold made exact: for l = 2l* + 1 with l* ≥ 1, (1/12)(1 + 1/l*) < (1/4)(1 - 1/l) holds if and only if l* ≥ 2, that is l ≥ 5. The paper says "if ℓ is sufficiently large"; the difference of the two sides is (4l* + 1)(l* - 1)/(12·l*·l).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.joshi_coefficient_eq_at_threetheorem

theorem joshi_coefficient_eq_at_three :
  1 / 12 * (1 + 1 / ((1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) = 1 / 4 * (1 - 1 / (2 * ((1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1))

At l = 3 (l* = 1) the two sides of Joshi's comparison are equal (both 1/6), so the strict inequality needs l ≥ 5.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.joshi_coefficient_eq_div_iut4theorem

theorem joshi_coefficient_eq_div_iut4 (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  1 / 12 * (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ)) = 1 / (n : ℝ) * (((2 * n + 1 : ℝ) + 1) / 24)

Relation to IUT IV, Theorem 1.10. The coefficient (l + 1)/24 of log 𝔮 in the procession-normalized bound of IUT IV, proof of Theorem 1.10, Step (v) (page 29; in this library IUT.PaperIV.Theorem1_10.procession_average_l) is the average (1/l*)·∑_{j=1}^{l*} j²/(2l). Joshi's coefficient averages j²/l*² instead, a different normalization: (1/12)(1 + 1/l*) = (1/l*)·(l + 1)/24.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lmMassdef

noncomputable def lmMass (a b c : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ) / Real.log (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ)

The logarithmic mass (weak quality) Y = log(abc)/log rad(abc) of R. Laniewski and K. Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, arXiv 2610.03212, Definition 2.1. The quality X = log c/log rad(abc) of the same definition is IUT.ABC.FormalConjectures.quality.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.LaniewskiMullerMassBounddef

def LaniewskiMullerMassBound : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → {t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < t.1 ∧ t.1 < t.2.1 ∧ Nat.Coprime t.1 t.2.1 ∧
    t.1 + t.2.1 = t.2.2 ∧ 3 + ε < lmMass t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2}.Finite

The mass bound of Laniewski and Müller, Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4, arXiv 2610.03212: for every ε > 0 only finitely many triples have Y > 3 + ε. Their triples are coprime positive integers a + b = c with a < b. Laniewski and Müller, Lemma 3.3, state that this is equivalent to Szpiro's conjecture for Frey curves (finitely many triples with Szpiro ratio > 6 + ε); that equivalence uses the minimal discriminant and the conductor of the Frey curve and is not formalized. This is an open statement, implied by the abc conjecture (laniewskiMullerMassBound_of_ABC).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.log_rad_pos_of_tripletheorem

theorem log_rad_pos_of_triple {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  0 < Real.log (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ)

For positive a + b = c, 0 < log rad(abc).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.laniewskiMullerMassBound_of_ABCtheorem

theorem laniewskiMullerMassBound_of_ABC (h : ABC) : LaniewskiMullerMassBound

Laniewski and Müller, Proposition 3.4 (i), elementary part. The abc conjecture implies the mass bound. Their proof: Y = λX < 3X (Lemma 2.2). Combined with their Lemma 3.3 (not formalized) this is "abc implies Szpiro for Frey curves".

IUT.ABC.Elementary.sq_le_two_mul_mul_multheorem

theorem sq_le_two_mul_mul_mul {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  c ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (a * b * c)

For positive a + b = c: c² ≤ 2abc, since a + b ≤ 2ab.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.finite_quality_gt_of_laniewskiMullerMassBoundtheorem

theorem finite_quality_gt_of_laniewskiMullerMassBound (h : LaniewskiMullerMassBound) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) :
  {t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < t.1 ∧ t.1 < t.2.1 ∧ Nat.Coprime t.1 t.2.1 ∧ t.1 + t.2.1 = t.2.2 ∧
    3 / 2 + ε < FormalConjectures.quality t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2}.Finite

Laniewski and Müller, Proposition 3.4 (ii), elementary part. The mass bound implies that for every ε > 0 only finitely many triples have quality X > 3/2 + ε. The paper argues with X = Y/λ and liminf λ ≥ 2 as rad(abc) → ∞, which uses the finiteness of triples with a given radical (Mahler). The proof here avoids it: from abc ≥ c²/2 one gets 2 log c ≤ log 2 + log(abc), so a triple with Y ≤ 3 + ε and X > 3/2 + ε has ε·log c < (3/2 + ε)·log 2, hence c is bounded.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.IsLMPresentationdef

def IsLMPresentation (a b c P : ℕ) : Prop := P ∣ a * b * c ∧ rad P = rad (a * b * c)

A presentation of a triple in the sense of Laniewski and Müller, Definition 4.1: a positive integer P with P ∣ abc and rad P = rad(abc) (positivity follows from P ∣ abc when abc > 0).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lmExponentFactordef

noncomputable def lmExponentFactor (a b c P : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ) / Real.log (P : ℝ)

The exponent factor f = log(abc)/log P of Laniewski and Müller, Definition 4.1.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lmApproximationGaindef

noncomputable def lmApproximationGain (c P : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.log (c : ℝ) / Real.log (P : ℝ)

The approximation gain G_a = log c/log P of Laniewski and Müller, Definition 4.1.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lmPowerGaindef

noncomputable def lmPowerGain (a b c P : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (P : ℝ) / Real.log (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ)

The power gain G_p = log P/log rad(abc) of Laniewski and Müller, Definition 4.1.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lmBalancedef

noncomputable def lmBalance (a b c : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ) / Real.log (c : ℝ)

The balance λ = log(abc)/log c of Laniewski and Müller, Definition 2.1.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.rad_le_and_le_of_isLMPresentationtheorem

theorem rad_le_and_le_of_isLMPresentation {a b c P : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hP : IsLMPresentation a b c P) :
  rad (a * b * c) ≤ P ∧ P ≤ a * b * c

For a presentation P of a positive triple: rad(abc) ≤ P ≤ abc.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.log_bounds_of_isLMPresentationtheorem

theorem log_bounds_of_isLMPresentation {a b c P : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hP : IsLMPresentation a b c P) :
  0 < Real.log (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ∧ Real.log (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ≤ Real.log (P : ℝ) ∧
    Real.log (P : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ) ∧ 0 < Real.log (c : ℝ)

The logarithms of a presentation: 0 < log rad(abc) ≤ log P ≤ log(abc) and 0 < log c.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lm_dictionary_identitiestheorem

theorem lm_dictionary_identities {a b c P : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hP : IsLMPresentation a b c P) :
  lmApproximationGain c P * lmPowerGain a b c P = FormalConjectures.quality a b c ∧
    lmExponentFactor a b c P * lmPowerGain a b c P = lmMass a b c ∧
    lmBalance a b c * lmApproximationGain c P = lmExponentFactor a b c P

Laniewski and Müller, Proposition 4.2, the identities: for a presentation P of a positive triple, G_a·G_p = X, f·G_p = Y and λ·G_a = f. Neither coprimality nor a < b is needed.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.lm_dictionary_boundstheorem

theorem lm_dictionary_bounds {a b c P : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hP : IsLMPresentation a b c P) :
  1 ≤ lmExponentFactor a b c P ∧ lmExponentFactor a b c P ≤ lmMass a b c ∧
    1 ≤ lmPowerGain a b c P ∧ lmPowerGain a b c P ≤ lmMass a b c ∧
    1 / lmBalance a b c ≤ lmApproximationGain c P ∧
    lmApproximationGain c P ≤ FormalConjectures.quality a b c

Laniewski and Müller, Proposition 4.2, the bounds: for a presentation P of a positive triple, 1 ≤ f ≤ Y, 1 ≤ G_p ≤ Y and 1/λ ≤ G_a ≤ X.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.finset_gcd_eq_one_of_isCoprimetheorem

theorem finset_gcd_eq_one_of_isCoprime {x : Fin 3 → ℤ} (h : IsCoprime (x 0) (x 2)) :
  Finset.univ.gcd x = 1

A triple of integers whose first and last entries are coprime has gcd = 1, in the normalized form Finset.univ.gcd x = 1 used by Mathlib's height of a tuple.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma23_rattheorem

theorem vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma23_rat {p q : ℤ} (hpq : IsCoprime p q) (n : ℕ) :
  Height.logHeight (((↑) : ℤ → ℚ) ∘ ![p ^ n, q ^ n - p ^ n, q ^ n])
      ≤ n * Height.logHeight (((↑) : ℤ → ℚ) ∘ ![p, q - p, q]) + Real.log 2 ∧
    n * Height.logHeight (((↑) : ℤ → ℚ) ∘ ![p, q - p, q]) - n * Real.log 2
      ≤ Height.logHeight (((↑) : ℤ → ℚ) ∘ ![p ^ n, q ^ n - p ^ n, q ^ n])

*Lemma 2.3 of M. van Frankenhuijsen, *Two Restricted ABC Conjectures, arXiv 2010.09493, for K = ℚ.** For a = p/q with coprime integers p, q, the point (a : 1 - a : 1) has the primitive integer representative (p : q - p : q), and (aⁿ : 1 - aⁿ : 1) has (pⁿ : qⁿ - pⁿ : qⁿ). With Mathlib's logarithmic height Height.logHeight of a tuple over ℚ: h(aⁿ : 1 - aⁿ : 1) ≤ n·h(a : 1 - a : 1) + log 2 and h(aⁿ : 1 - aⁿ : 1) ≥ n·h(a : 1 - a : 1) - n·log 2. The heights are computed by Mathlib's Rat.logHeight_eq_max_abs_of_gcd_eq_one; the general number field case is not formalized.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma41_inttheorem

theorem vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma41_int {p : ℕ} {a : ℤ} {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k)
  (h : (p : ℤ) ^ k ∣ a - 1) : (p : ℤ) ^ (k + 1) ∣ a ^ p - 1

**Lemma 4.1 of van Frankenhuijsen, arXiv 2010.09493, for K = ℚ and integers.** If p^k ∣ a - 1 with k ≥ 1 (for p prime: v_p(a - 1) ≥ k ≥ 1), then p^(k + 1) ∣ a^p - 1. The paper states it for a in a completion K_v with p the residue characteristic; this is the case K = ℚ, a ∈ ℤ. The argument does not use that p is prime, so the hypothesis is dropped. The proof is the paper's: a^p - 1 = (a - 1)·∑_{m < p} a^m and the sum is ≡ p ≡ 0 (mod p).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma42theorem

theorem vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma42 {α : ℂ} (hα : ‖α‖ = 1) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) :
  ∃ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ 8 * Real.pi * Real.exp d ∧
    ‖α ^ m - 1‖ < Real.exp (-d) / 4

Lemma 4.2 of van Frankenhuijsen, arXiv 2010.09493. For a complex number α with |α| = 1 and a real d > 0 there is an exponent 1 ≤ m ≤ 8π·e^d with |α^m - 1| < e^(-d)/4. The proof uses Dirichlet's approximation theorem (Mathlib's Real.exists_int_int_abs_mul_sub_le) instead of the paper's ordering of the points α^j.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma43theorem

theorem vanFrankenhuijsen_lemma43 {a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d)
  (hlog : |Real.log ‖a‖| < Real.exp (-2 * d) / (32 * Real.pi)) :
  ∃ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m ∧ (m : ℝ) ≤ 8 * Real.pi * Real.exp d ∧ ‖a ^ m - 1‖ < Real.exp (-d)

Lemma 4.3 of van Frankenhuijsen, arXiv 2010.09493. For a complex number a ≠ 0 and a real d > 0 with |log|a|| < e^(-2d)/(32π) there is an exponent 1 ≤ m ≤ 8π·e^d with |a^m - 1| < e^(-d). The hypothesis a ≠ 0 is implicit in the paper (log|a| must be defined); it is needed here because Mathlib sets Real.log 0 = 0. The estimate of |a|^m - 1 uses |e^y - 1| ≤ 2|y| for |y| ≤ 1 in place of the paper's 1/(1 - e^(-d)/4).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.exists_coprime_triple_rad_lt_multheorem

theorem exists_coprime_triple_rad_lt_mul {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ a.Coprime b ∧ a + b = c ∧
    (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) < ε * c

**Restatement of IUT.ABC.Variants.exists_coprime_triple_gt_mul_rad** as an existence statement with <, in the shape of P. Vojta, A more general abc conjecture, arXiv math/9806171, Proposition 2.6 for n = 3: for every ε > 0 there is a coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c with rad(abc) < ε·c. The paper's form (≤ on a Zariski-dense set) is infinite_coprime_triples_rad_le_mul.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.infinite_coprime_triples_rad_le_multheorem

theorem infinite_coprime_triples_rad_le_mul {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  {t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < t.1 ∧ 0 < t.2.1 ∧ Nat.Coprime t.1 t.2.1 ∧ t.1 + t.2.1 = t.2.2 ∧
    (rad (t.1 * t.2.1 * t.2.2) : ℝ) ≤ ε * t.2.2}.Infinite

**Vojta, Proposition 2.6, the case n = 3** (arXiv math/9806171; the paper says "for n = 3 this is already well known" and gives no proof). For every ε > 0 the set of coprime triples of positive integers a + b = c with rad(abc) ≤ ε·c is infinite. Vojta's statement is a Zariski-dense set of points [x_0 : x_1 : x_2] with pairwise coprime coordinates on the line x_0 + x_1 + x_2 = 0; on that line a set is Zariski dense if and only if it is infinite, and the points [a : b : -c] from distinct positive triples are distinct. The triples used are 1 + (3^(2^k) - 1) = 3^(2^k) (IUT.ABC.Variants.two_pow_mul_rad_family_lt).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.cuevasPasten_lemma42theorem

theorem cuevasPasten_lemma42 {k : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k] {f g : Polynomial k}
  (hfg : IsCoprime f g) (hnc : 0 < f.natDegree ∨ 0 < g.natDegree) :
  0 < (f ^ 2 + g ^ 3).natDegree

Lemma 4.2 of J. Cuevas Barrientos and H. Pasten, arXiv 2504.15971, over any field of characteristic zero (the paper works over ℂ): for coprime polynomials f, g, not both constant, f² + g³ is not constant. The paper's proof uses the Riemann–Hurwitz formula for a map to the elliptic curve y² = x³ + 1; here it follows from Mathlib's Polynomial.flt_catalan with exponents (2, 3, 6), for which 3·6 + 6·2 + 2·3 = 2·3·6.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.PastenDivisorBounddef

def PastenDivisorBound : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < c → Nat.Coprime a b →
    a + b = c → ((a * b * c).divisors.card : ℝ) < K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (8 / 3 + ε)

Theorem 16.7 (Theorem 1.11 in the introduction) of H. Pasten, Shimura curves and the abc conjecture, arXiv 1705.09251, the "d(abc)-Theorem": for every ε > 0 there is K_ε > 0 such that all coprime positive integers a + b = c satisfy d(abc) < K_ε·rad(abc)^(8/3 + ε), where d(n) is the number of divisors of n. The inequality is strict as in the paper. This is a theorem of that paper, proved there with modularity, Shimura curves and linear forms in logarithms; it is not proved in this library. The abc conjecture implies it (pastenDivisorBound_of_ABC).

IUT.ABC.Elementary.card_divisors_le_two_mul_real_sqrttheorem

theorem card_divisors_le_two_mul_real_sqrt (n : ℕ) :
  (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt n

d(n) ≤ 2√n: a divisor d with d² > n is n/e for the divisor e = n/d with e² < n, and the divisors e with e² ≤ n are at most ⌊√n⌋ in number.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.pastenDivisorBound_of_ABCtheorem

theorem pastenDivisorBound_of_ABC (h : ABC) : PastenDivisorBound

**The abc conjecture implies Pasten's d(abc) bound.** From d(n) ≤ 2√n and abc < c³, d(abc) < 2c^(3/2); the abc conjecture with ε = 1/2 gives c ≤ K·rad(abc)^(3/2), hence d(abc) < 2K^(3/2)·rad(abc)^(9/4), and 9/4 < 8/3. This elementary implication is not taken from Pasten's paper.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.DivisorCountPowerBounddef

def DivisorCountPowerBound : Prop :=
  ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ δ

The classical divisor bound d(n) ≤ C_δ·n^δ for every δ > 0. It is a classical theorem that is not in Mathlib; it is not proved here and is used only as an explicit hypothesis of divisorCount_le_rad_rpow_of_ABC.

IUT.ABC.Elementary.divisorCount_le_rad_rpow_of_ABCtheorem

theorem divisorCount_le_rad_rpow_of_ABC (hdiv : DivisorCountPowerBound) (h : ABC) {η : ℝ}
  (hη : 0 < η) :
  ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < c → Nat.Coprime a b → a + b = c →
    ((a * b * c).divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ η

**Conditional on the divisor bound, the abc conjecture gives d(abc) ≤ K_η·rad(abc)^η for every η > 0**, a better exponent than Pasten's 8/3 + ε. From abc < c³, the abc conjecture with ε = 1 (c ≤ K·rad(abc)²) and d(n) ≤ C·n^(η/6).

IUT.ABC.Unconditional

IUT/ABC/Unconditional.lean · imports IUT.ABC.Variants

Unconditional theorems and an exact reduction around the abc conjecture

Module documentation

This file proves unconditional statements about triples a + b = c and one reduction of the abc conjecture to a restricted form, equivalent to it for every D ≥ 1 (the instance D = 0 holds vacuously). Nothing here says whether the abc conjecture holds, and no page of the IUT papers is used.

**Triples supported on {2, 3}.** A coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c whose product has no prime factor other than 2 and 3 is, up to the order of a and b, one of 1 + 1 = 2, 1 + 2 = 3, 1 + 3 = 4, 1 + 8 = 9 (uncond_triples_two_three, with the converse uncond_triples_two_three_mem). The proof solves 3^y + 1 = 2^x modulo 8 and 2^x + 1 = 3^y modulo 4 and by factoring 3^(2k) - 1. Consequently the largest quality log c / log rad(abc) on this family is log 9 / log 6, attained by 1 + 8 = 9 (uncond_quality_le_two_three, uncond_quality_one_eight_nine). These are classical facts (Catalan type equations with the bases 2 and 3); no source page was read for them.

**Restriction to triples with D ∣ abc.** uncondABCRestrictedToStatement D is the abc conjecture, with the quantifiers, the constant and the inequality of Challenge.ABC, for the triples with D ∣ abc only. For every D ≥ 1 it is equivalent to Challenge.ABC (uncondABCRestrictedToStatement_iff); for D ≥ 1 it is therefore an open statement, and nothing here proves it; for D = 0 it holds vacuously. The nontrivial direction is the power trick: from (a, b, c) pass to (a^n, c^n - a^n, c^n) with n = D φ(D). Then D divides the new product (uncond_dvd_power_triple, by Euler's theorem modulo each prime power of D), the new radical is at most rad(abc) n c^(n - 1) (uncond_rad_power_triple_le, from c^n - a^n = b ∑ c^i a^(n - 1 - i)), and the factor c^(n - 1) is absorbed: with the restricted statement used at δ = ε / (n (1 + ε)), one gets c^t ≤ K n^(1 + δ) rad(abc)^(1 + δ) with t = 1 - (n - 1) δ > 0, and (1 + δ) / t ≤ 1 + ε (uncond_power_trick_real). So the loss is absorbed into ε because n depends on D only. Source of the idea: M. van Frankenhuijsen, Two restricted abc conjectures, arXiv 2010.09493, pages 1 and 2 (Ellenberg's theorem, with the Euler indicator n = φ(D) and the cover x ↦ x^n; read and checked against rendered images), and Theorem 4.5 with its proof and the two lemmas of Section 2 on heights of powers that it uses (read in the TeX source, not rendered). The exponent n = D φ(D) (larger than the φ(D) of the source, which makes the case p ∣ ac immediate) and the inequalities are worked out for this file.

**Mason–Stothers on ℙ¹.** For coprime nonzero polynomials A, B over a field of characteristic zero, not both constant, max(deg A, deg B) + 2 ≤ deg rad(A B (B - A)) + δ, where δ = 0 if A, B, B - A have the same degree (the point at infinity is not mapped into {0, 1, ∞} by A/B) and δ = 1 otherwise (uncond_masonStothers_projective). This is the count of the points over {0, 1, ∞} given by the Riemann–Hurwitz formula; the case δ = 1 is Mathlib's Polynomial.abc, and the case δ = 0 gains 1 from the cancellation of the leading terms of the Wronskian. It is a theorem about polynomials and implies nothing about integers.

An infinite family. For primes p < q ≤ 2p, the triple (p², q², p² + q²) is coprime with 2c ≤ 5 rad(abc) (uncond_two_mul_le_five_mul_rad); by Bertrand's postulate the set of coprime triples with 2c ≤ 5 rad(abc) is infinite (uncond_infinite_two_mul_le_five_mul_rad).

Two roots of bounded degree. For a field K, x ∈ K and n ≥ 1, an intermediate field L of an algebraic closure contains u, v with u^n = x, v^n = 1 - x and [L : K] ≤ n² (uncond_exists_roots_finrank_le). This is the first step of the passage to the Fermat curve X^n + Y^n = Z^n with the map [X : Y : Z] ↦ [X^n : Z^n] of degree n² in V. Dimitrov, Effectivity in Mochizuki's work on the abc-conjecture, arXiv 1601.03572, page 9 (Section 5; the choice of Q ∈ π_n⁻¹(P)); page 3 (the statement of the main theorem) was read for context. Both pages were checked against rendered images. The degree bound is not stated as such on page 9; it is the degree n² of the map stated there. The hypotheses x ≠ 0, 1 are not needed for this step. Nothing further along that route is formalized.

Not proved
  • No unconditional upper or lower bound beyond those above (for example bounds on c in terms of the number of prime factors of abc by counting S-units) is stated: none was proved.
  • The equality case A = t^n, B = t^n + 1 of uncond_masonStothers_projective is checked by hand in the docstring, not formalized (it needs the squarefreeness of t^n + 1).
Public declarations

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_three_pow_mod_eighttheorem

theorem uncond_three_pow_mod_eight (y : ℕ) : 3 ^ y % 8 = 1 ∨ 3 ^ y % 8 = 3

3^y modulo 8 is 1 or 3.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_three_pow_add_one_eq_two_powtheorem

theorem uncond_three_pow_add_one_eq_two_pow {x y : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) (h : 3 ^ y + 1 = 2 ^ x) :
  y = 1 ∧ x = 2

The only solution of 3^y + 1 = 2^x with y ≥ 1 is y = 1, x = 2. Modulo 8, the left side is 2 or 4, so x ≤ 2.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_two_pow_add_one_eq_three_powtheorem

theorem uncond_two_pow_add_one_eq_three_pow {x y : ℕ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (h : 2 ^ x + 1 = 3 ^ y) :
  (x = 1 ∧ y = 1) ∨ (x = 3 ∧ y = 2)

The solutions of 2^x + 1 = 3^y with x ≥ 1 are (x, y) = (1, 1) and (3, 2). For x ≥ 2, modulo 4 the exponent y is even, y = 2k, and 3^k + 1 divides 2^x = (3^k + 1)(3^k - 1), so it is a power of 2; then k = 1 by uncond_three_pow_add_one_eq_two_pow.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_prime_not_dvd_boththeorem

theorem uncond_prime_not_dvd_both {b c p : ℕ} (hbc : b.Coprime c) (hp : p.Prime) (hb : p ∣ b)
  (hc : p ∣ c) : False

A prime dividing both members of a coprime pair does not exist.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_eq_pow_of_supporttheorem

theorem uncond_eq_pow_of_support {b c q : ℕ} (hb0 : b ≠ 0) (hbc : b.Coprime c) (hqc : q ∣ c)
  (hq : q = 2 ∨ q = 3) (hS : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ b → p = 2 ∨ p = 3) :
  (q = 3 → ∃ e, b = 2 ^ e) ∧ (q = 2 → ∃ e, b = 3 ^ e)

A positive number all of whose prime divisors are 2 or 3, and which is coprime to a number divisible by q, where q is 2 or 3, is a power of the other prime.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_triples_two_threetheorem

theorem uncond_triples_two_three {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hS : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ a * b * c → p = 2 ∨ p = 3) :
  (a, b, c) = (1, 1, 2) ∨ (a, b, c) = (1, 2, 3) ∨ (a, b, c) = (2, 1, 3) ∨
    (a, b, c) = (1, 3, 4) ∨ (a, b, c) = (3, 1, 4) ∨ (a, b, c) = (1, 8, 9) ∨
    (a, b, c) = (8, 1, 9)

**The coprime triples supported on {2, 3}.** Let a, b, c be positive integers with a and b coprime, a + b = c, and every prime factor of abc equal to 2 or 3. Then the triple is one of (1, 1, 2), (1, 2, 3), (2, 1, 3), (1, 3, 4), (3, 1, 4), (1, 8, 9), (8, 1, 9). The three numbers are pairwise coprime, so at most two of them exceed 1; since c ≥ 2, one of a, b is 1. The other two are then coprime powers of 2 and 3 differing by 1, and uncond_three_pow_add_one_eq_two_pow and uncond_two_pow_add_one_eq_three_pow list the solutions.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_triples_two_three_memtheorem

theorem uncond_triples_two_three_mem :
  ∀ t ∈ ({(1, 1, 2), (1, 2, 3), (2, 1, 3), (1, 3, 4), (3, 1, 4), (1, 8, 9), (8, 1, 9)} :
    Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)), 0 < t.1 ∧ 0 < t.2.1 ∧ t.1.Coprime t.2.1 ∧ t.1 + t.2.1 = t.2.2 ∧
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ t.1 * t.2.1 * t.2.2 → p = 2 ∨ p = 3

Conversely, the seven triples of uncond_triples_two_three are coprime triples supported on {2, 3}.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_quality_le_two_threetheorem

theorem uncond_quality_le_two_three {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hS : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ a * b * c → p = 2 ∨ p = 3) :
  Real.log c / Real.log (rad (a * b * c)) ≤ Real.log 9 / Real.log 6

**The maximal quality on the triples supported on {2, 3}** is log 9 / log 6, attained by 1 + 8 = 9: every coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c whose product has only the prime factors 2 and 3 has log c / log rad(abc) ≤ log 9 / log 6.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_quality_one_eight_ninetheorem

theorem uncond_quality_one_eight_nine :
  Real.log ((9 : ℕ) : ℝ) / Real.log (rad (1 * 8 * 9)) = Real.log 9 / Real.log 6

The bound of uncond_quality_le_two_three is attained by 1 + 8 = 9.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncondABCRestrictedToStatementdef

def uncondABCRestrictedToStatement (D : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < c →
    Nat.Coprime a b → a + b = c → D ∣ a * b * c → (c : ℝ) ≤ K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)

**The abc conjecture restricted to triples with D ∣ abc.** For every real ε > 0 there is a real K > 0 such that every coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c with D dividing abc satisfies c ≤ K * rad(abc)^(1 + ε). The quantifiers, the constant and the non-strict inequality are those of Challenge.ABC; the only change is the extra hypothesis D ∣ a * b * c. This is an open statement for every D ≥ 1: it is equivalent to Challenge.ABC (uncondABCRestrictedToStatement_iff). For D = 0 it is vacuously true, since abc > 0.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncondPowerExponentdef

def uncondPowerExponent (D : ℕ) : ℕ := D * D.totient

The exponent of the power trick: n = D * φ(D).

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_one_le_powerExponenttheorem

theorem uncond_one_le_powerExponent {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) : 1 ≤ uncondPowerExponent D

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_dvd_power_tripletheorem

theorem uncond_dvd_power_triple {D a c : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (hle : a ≤ c) :
  D ∣ a ^ uncondPowerExponent D * (c ^ uncondPowerExponent D - a ^ uncondPowerExponent D) *
    c ^ uncondPowerExponent D

Divisibility after the power map. For D ≥ 1, n = D * φ(D), and a ≤ c, D divides a^n * (c^n - a^n) * c^n. For a prime power p^k ∣ D: if p divides a or c then p^k divides a^n or c^n, because k < p^k ≤ D ≤ n; otherwise Euler's theorem modulo p^k, with φ(p^k) ∣ φ(D) ∣ n, gives a^n ≡ 1 ≡ c^n.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_rad_power_triple_letheorem

theorem uncond_rad_power_triple_le {a b c n : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  rad (a ^ n * (c ^ n - a ^ n) * c ^ n) ≤ rad (a * b * c) * (n * c ^ (n - 1))

The radical after the power map. For positive a, b with a + b = c and n ≥ 1, rad(a^n * (c^n - a^n) * c^n) ≤ rad(abc) * (n * c^(n - 1)). Indeed c^n - a^n = b * S with S = ∑_{i < n} c^i a^(n - 1 - i) ≤ n c^(n - 1), the product divides (abc)^n * S, and the radical of that is at most rad(abc) * S.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_power_trick_realtheorem

theorem uncond_power_trick_real {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {ε x R K : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hx : 1 ≤ x)
  (hR : 1 ≤ R) (hK : 0 < K)
  (h : x ^ n ≤ K * (R * (n * x ^ (n - 1))) ^ (1 + ε / (n * (1 + ε)))) :
  x ≤ (K * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε / (n * (1 + ε)))) ^ (1 - ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (ε / (n * (1 + ε))))⁻¹ *
    R ^ (1 + ε)

The real inequality of the power trick. Let n ≥ 1, ε > 0, δ = ε / (n (1 + ε)), t = 1 - (n - 1) δ, x ≥ 1, R ≥ 1 and K > 0. If x^n ≤ K (R n x^(n - 1))^(1 + δ) then x ≤ (K n^(1 + δ))^(1 / t) R^(1 + ε). The exponent bookkeeping: t > 0, x^n = x^((n - 1)(1 + δ)) x^t, and (1 + δ) / t ≤ 1 + ε because (1 + ε) t - (1 + δ) = δ ε ≥ 0.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_ABC_of_restrictedtheorem

theorem uncond_ABC_of_restricted {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (h : uncondABCRestrictedToStatement D) :
  ABC

The power trick. For D ≥ 1, the abc conjecture restricted to triples with D ∣ abc implies the abc conjecture. Given ε > 0, let n = D φ(D) and apply the restricted statement with δ = ε / (n (1 + ε)) to (a^n, c^n - a^n, c^n), a coprime triple with D dividing the product (uncond_dvd_power_triple) and radical at most rad(abc) n c^(n - 1) (uncond_rad_power_triple_le); then uncond_power_trick_real absorbs the loss into the exponent 1 + ε. Source of the idea: van Frankenhuijsen, arXiv 2010.09493, the introduction (Ellenberg's theorem, pages 1 and 2) and Theorem 4.5, where a/c is replaced by (a/c)^n. The exponent n = D φ(D) and the inequalities here are worked out for this file.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_restricted_of_ABCtheorem

theorem uncond_restricted_of_ABC (h : ABC) (D : ℕ) : uncondABCRestrictedToStatement D

The abc conjecture implies its restriction to triples with D ∣ abc.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncondABCRestrictedToStatement_ifftheorem

theorem uncondABCRestrictedToStatement_iff {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) :
  uncondABCRestrictedToStatement D ↔ ABC

**For every D ≥ 1, the abc conjecture restricted to triples with D ∣ abc is equivalent to the abc conjecture.**

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_divRadical_dvd_wronskiantheorem

theorem uncond_divRadical_dvd_wronskian {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k]
  {a b c : Polynomial k} (hab : IsCoprime a b) (hsum : a + b + c = 0) :
  EuclideanDomain.divRadical (a * b * c) ∣ Polynomial.wronskian a b

For nonzero a, b, c with a and b coprime and a + b + c = 0, the non-radical part of abc divides the Wronskian W(a, b). This is the divisibility step of the proof of Mathlib's Polynomial.abc, repeated here because it is not exported there.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncondInfinityOffTripoddef

def uncondInfinityOffTripod {k : Type*} [Field k] (A B : Polynomial k) : Prop :=
  A.natDegree = B.natDegree ∧ (B - A).natDegree = B.natDegree

Whether the point at infinity of ℙ¹ is mapped by t ↦ A(t)/B(t) to a point outside the tripod {0, 1, ∞}: this happens exactly when A, B and B - A have the same degree.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_masonStothers_projectivetheorem

theorem uncond_masonStothers_projective {k : Type*} [Field k] [CharZero k] [DecidableEq k]
  {A B : Polynomial k} (hA : A ≠ 0) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hAB : IsCoprime A B)
  (hnc : ¬ (A.natDegree = 0 ∧ B.natDegree = 0)) :
  max A.natDegree B.natDegree + 2 ≤
    (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (A * B * (B - A))).natDegree +
      (if uncondInfinityOffTripod A B then 0 else 1)

**Mason–Stothers for the rational function A/B on ℙ¹, with the point at infinity.** Let k be a field of characteristic zero and A, B nonzero coprime polynomials, not both constant (so that f = A/B is a nonconstant rational function of degree d = max(deg A, deg B)). The number of points of ℙ¹ over 0, 1, ∞ is at least d + 2: the finite ones are the distinct roots of A·B·(B - A), counted by deg rad(A·B·(B - A)), and infinity is one of them unless A, B, B - A have the same degree (uncondInfinityOffTripod). So max(deg A, deg B) + 2 ≤ deg rad(A·B·(B - A)) + (0 if infinity is off the tripod, else 1). When infinity lies over the tripod this is Mathlib's Polynomial.abc. When it does not, the Wronskian W(A, B) = W(A, B - λA) with λ = lc(B)/lc(A) has degree at most 2d - 2, one less than in the general bound, which gives the extra 1. Example (not formalized): A = t^n, B = t^n + 1 has d = n, infinity over 1, and both sides equal n + 2.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_two_mul_le_five_mul_radtheorem

theorem uncond_two_mul_le_five_mul_rad {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q)
  (hq2 : q ≤ 2 * p) :
  (p ^ 2).Coprime (q ^ 2) ∧
    2 * (p ^ 2 + q ^ 2) ≤ 5 * rad (p ^ 2 * q ^ 2 * (p ^ 2 + q ^ 2))

For primes p < q ≤ 2p, the triple a = p², b = q², c = p² + q² is coprime and satisfies 2c ≤ 5 rad(abc): pq divides rad(abc), and 5pq - 2(p² + q²) = (2p - q)(2q - p) ≥ 0.

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_infinite_two_mul_le_five_mul_radtheorem

theorem uncond_infinite_two_mul_le_five_mul_rad :
  {t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < t.1 ∧ 0 < t.2.1 ∧ t.1.Coprime t.2.1 ∧ t.1 + t.2.1 = t.2.2 ∧
    2 * t.2.2 ≤ 5 * rad (t.1 * t.2.1 * t.2.2)}.Infinite

**Infinitely many coprime triples with 2c ≤ 5 rad(abc).** By Bertrand's postulate, for every prime p there is a prime q with p < q ≤ 2p, and uncond_two_mul_le_five_mul_rad applies to (p², q², p² + q²).

IUT.ABC.Unconditional.uncond_exists_roots_finrank_letheorem

theorem uncond_exists_roots_finrank_le {K : Type*} [Field K] (x : K) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
  ∃ L : IntermediateField K (AlgebraicClosure K), ∃ u v : L,
    u ^ n = algebraMap K L x ∧ v ^ n = 1 - algebraMap K L x ∧
    FiniteDimensional K L ∧ Module.finrank K L ≤ n ^ 2

**Adjoining an n-th root of x and of 1 - x.** For a field K, an element x of K and n ≥ 1, there is a finite extension L of K (an intermediate field of an algebraic closure) containing u, v with u^n = x, v^n = 1 - x and [L : K] ≤ n². This is the first step of the passage to the Fermat curve u^n + v^n = 1 (Dimitrov, arXiv 1601.03572; see the module docstring). The hypotheses x ≠ 0, 1 of that source are not needed for this step. Proof: L = K(u) ⊔ K(v); each of K(u), K(v) has degree the degree of a minimal polynomial dividing X^n - x or X^n - (1 - x), so at most n, and the degree of a compositum is at most the product.

IUT.ABC.Variants

IUT/ABC/Variants.lean · imports IUT.Applications.ABCFormalConjectures

Variants of the abc conjecture and elementary facts about abc triples

Module documentation

This file collects reformulations of the abc conjecture and elementary, unconditional facts about triples a + b = c that other formalizations commonly use as reference points. Nothing here says whether the abc conjecture holds. No page of the IUT papers is used.

**Reformulations, each proved equivalent to Challenge.ABC.**

  • ABCInt: the signed integer form, with nonzero pairwise coprime integers a + b + c = 0 and the bound max(|a|, |b|, |c|) ≤ K * rad(|abc|)^(1 + ε); ABCIntSum is the same with a + b = c and signs arbitrary. The shape (a constant K > 0 and the non-strict ≤) is the shape of Challenge.ABC, so the comparison is exact. Equivalences: abcInt_iff_ABC, abcIntSum_iff_ABC.
  • ABCWithExponent κ: the bound c ≤ K * rad(abc)^κ with one fixed exponent κ. The conjecture is ∀ ε > 0, ABCWithExponent (1 + ε) (abc_iff_forall_abcWithExponent, true by definition). For one fixed κ > 1 the statement ABCWithExponent κ is implied by the conjecture (abcWithExponent_of_ABC) and is strictly weaker as a statement: knowing it for one κ > 1 gives no bound with any smaller exponent, so it does not give the conjecture by any argument in this file. Results and claims with one fixed exponent larger than 1 (for example of the form 24 + ε) appear in the literature; each is a statement of this weaker shape, not the conjecture. For κ ≤ 1 the statement is false (not_abcWithExponent_of_le_one).

The quality form q(a, b, c) = log c / log rad(abc) and its finiteness statement are already in IUT.ABC.FormalConjectures (quality, qualityVariant, qualityVariant_iff_ABC); this file reuses that definition of the quality and does not restate the finiteness form.

Elementary facts.

  • Trivial bounds: 2 ≤ rad(abc) (two_le_rad_of_triple), rad(abc) ≤ abc (rad_le_mul_mul), abc < c^3 (mul_mul_lt_cube), and 6 ≤ rad(abc) once c ≥ 3 (six_le_rad_of_three_le); the triple 1 + 1 = 2 with rad = 2 shows that c ≥ 3 is needed (rad_one_one_two). The bound c < rad(abc)^2 is a conjecture and is not stated.
  • Lemma 2.2 of R. Laniewski and K. Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains (page 2, read and checked against a rendered image). Their triples are coprime positive a + b = c with a < b, and their balance is λ = log(abc) / log c. The lemma says 2 < λ < 3 when a ≥ 2 and 2 - 1 / ((c - 1) log c) < λ < 2 when a = 1. All four inequalities are proved here, multiplied out by log c > 0: log_mul_mul_lt_three_mul_log, two_mul_log_lt_log_mul_mul, log_mul_mul_lt_two_mul_log_of_one, two_mul_log_sub_lt_log_mul_mul_of_one. The hypothesis a ≥ 2 of the lower bound λ > 2 is needed (1 + 2 = 3: abc = 6 < 9 = c^2), and so is a < b, which the lemma takes from the definition of a triple (2 + 2 = 4: abc = 16 = c^2, so λ = 2). Coprimality is not used by the lower bound once a < b.
  • Classical examples: 1 + 8 = 9 with rad = 6 and quality greater than 1; Reyssat's triple 2 + 3^10 * 109 = 23^5 with rad = 15042 and quality greater than 1.62; 1 + 2 * 3^7 = 5^4 * 7 with rad = 210 and quality greater than 1.56.
  • The exponent 1 + ε cannot be replaced by 1: the triples 1 + (3^(2^k) - 1) = 3^(2^k) satisfy 2^k * rad(abc) < 3 c, because 2^(k + 1) divides 3^(2^k) - 1 (two_pow_mul_rad_family_lt). Hence for every real K there is a coprime triple with c > K * rad(abc) (exists_coprime_triple_gt_mul_rad), and ABCWithExponent 1 is false (not_abcWithExponent_one). This guards against a statement of the conjecture with ε = 0.

The polynomial analog. Mathlib proves the Mason–Stothers theorem (Polynomial.abc, in Mathlib/NumberTheory/FLT/MasonStothers.lean): for nonzero polynomials a, b, c over a field with a and b coprime and a + b + c = 0, either all three derivatives vanish or each degree is less than the degree of radical (a * b * c). masonStothers_natDegree_lt restates it for a + b = c. This is the function field analog of the abc conjecture; it is a theorem, and it implies nothing about the statement for integers.

Public declarations

IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCIntdef

def ABCInt : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 →
    IsCoprime a b → IsCoprime a c → IsCoprime b c → a + b + c = 0 →
      ((max a.natAbs (max b.natAbs c.natAbs) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        K * (rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)

The abc conjecture, signed integer form. For every real ε > 0 there is a real K > 0 such that all nonzero, pairwise coprime integers a, b, c with a + b + c = 0 satisfy max(|a|, |b|, |c|) ≤ K * rad(|abc|)^(1 + ε). The absolute values are Int.natAbs, and the constant and the non-strict inequality are those of Challenge.ABC. Equivalent to Challenge.ABC (abcInt_iff_ABC).

IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCIntSumdef

def ABCIntSum : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 →
    IsCoprime a b → IsCoprime a c → IsCoprime b c → a + b = c →
      ((max a.natAbs (max b.natAbs c.natAbs) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        K * (rad (a * b * c).natAbs : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)

**The abc conjecture, signed form with a + b = c.** As ABCInt, with a + b = c in place of a + b + c = 0 and the signs of a, b, c arbitrary. Equivalent to Challenge.ABC (abcIntSum_iff_ABC).

IUT.ABC.Variants.abc_symmetric_of_ABCtheorem

theorem abc_symmetric_of_ABC (h : ABC) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ A B C : ℕ, 0 < A → 0 < B → 0 < C →
    A.Coprime B → A.Coprime C → B.Coprime C → (A + B = C ∨ A + C = B ∨ B + C = A) →
      ((max A (max B C) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ K * (rad (A * B * C) : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)

The constant form, made symmetric: for pairwise coprime positive A, B, C one of which is the sum of the other two, the largest is bounded by K * rad(ABC)^(1 + ε).

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcInt_of_ABCtheorem

theorem abcInt_of_ABC (h : ABC) : ABCInt

The constant form implies the signed integer form. Of three nonzero integers with sum 0, the absolute value of one is the sum of the other two absolute values.

IUT.ABC.Variants.coprime_sum_of_coprimetheorem

theorem coprime_sum_of_coprime {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) (h : a + b = c) :
  a.Coprime c ∧ b.Coprime c

For positive a, b with a + b = c, coprimality of a and b gives coprimality of a and c and of b and c.

IUT.ABC.Variants.ABC_of_abcInttheorem

theorem ABC_of_abcInt (h : ABCInt) : ABC

The signed integer form implies the constant form: apply it to (a, b, -c).

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcInt_iff_ABCtheorem

theorem abcInt_iff_ABC : ABCInt ↔ ABC

**The signed integer form is equivalent to Challenge.ABC.**

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcIntSum_iff_abcInttheorem

theorem abcIntSum_iff_abcInt : ABCIntSum ↔ ABCInt

The two signed forms are equivalent: replace c by -c.

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcIntSum_iff_ABCtheorem

theorem abcIntSum_iff_ABC : ABCIntSum ↔ ABC

**The signed form with a + b = c is equivalent to Challenge.ABC.**

IUT.ABC.Variants.ABCWithExponentdef

def ABCWithExponent (κ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ a b c : ℕ, 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < c → Nat.Coprime a b → a + b = c →
    (c : ℝ) ≤ K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) ^ κ

The bound of the abc conjecture with one fixed exponent κ: there is a real K > 0 such that every coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c satisfies c ≤ K * rad(abc)^κ. The hypotheses, the constant and the non-strict inequality are those of Challenge.ABC. The abc conjecture is ∀ ε > 0, ABCWithExponent (1 + ε) (abc_iff_forall_abcWithExponent). For one fixed κ > 1 this proposition is implied by the conjecture and is an open, strictly weaker statement; it does not give the conjecture. For κ ≤ 1 it is false (not_abcWithExponent_of_le_one).

IUT.ABC.Variants.abc_iff_forall_abcWithExponenttheorem

theorem abc_iff_forall_abcWithExponent : ABC ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ABCWithExponent (1 + ε)

The abc conjecture is the fixed exponent bound for every exponent 1 + ε with ε > 0.

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcWithExponent_monotheorem

theorem abcWithExponent_mono {κ κ' : ℝ} (h : κ ≤ κ') :
  ABCWithExponent κ → ABCWithExponent κ'

The fixed exponent bound is monotone in the exponent, because rad(abc) ≥ 1.

IUT.ABC.Variants.abcWithExponent_of_ABCtheorem

theorem abcWithExponent_of_ABC (h : ABC) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 1 < κ) : ABCWithExponent κ

The abc conjecture implies the fixed exponent bound for every exponent κ > 1.

IUT.ABC.Variants.two_le_rad_of_tripletheorem

theorem two_le_rad_of_triple {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  2 ≤ rad (a * b * c)

For positive a, b with a + b = c, rad(abc) ≥ 2.

IUT.ABC.Variants.rad_le_mul_multheorem

theorem rad_le_mul_mul {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  rad (a * b * c) ≤ a * b * c

For positive a, b with a + b = c, rad(abc) ≤ abc.

IUT.ABC.Variants.mul_mul_lt_cubetheorem

theorem mul_mul_lt_cube {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  a * b * c < c ^ 3

For positive a, b with a + b = c, abc < c^3.

IUT.ABC.Variants.six_le_rad_of_three_letheorem

theorem six_le_rad_of_three_le {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hc : 3 ≤ c) : 6 ≤ rad (a * b * c)

For a coprime triple of positive integers a + b = c with c ≥ 3, rad(abc) ≥ 6: a prime divisor of c and a prime divisor of whichever of a, b is at least 2 are distinct, so their product, which is at least 2 * 3, divides rad(abc). The bound is attained by 1 + 2 = 3.

IUT.ABC.Variants.rad_one_one_twotheorem

theorem rad_one_one_two : rad (1 * 1 * 2) = 2

The hypothesis c ≥ 3 of six_le_rad_of_three_le is needed: 1 + 1 = 2 has rad(1 * 1 * 2) = 2.

IUT.ABC.Variants.log_mul_mul_lt_three_mul_logtheorem

theorem log_mul_mul_lt_three_mul_log {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ) < 3 * Real.log c

For positive a, b with a + b = c: log(abc) < 3 log c, that is, the balance is less than 3 (Laniewski and Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, Lemma 2.2, page 2). No coprimality and no order of a, b is needed.

IUT.ABC.Variants.sq_lt_mul_mul_of_two_letheorem

theorem sq_lt_mul_mul_of_two_le {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  c ^ 2 < a * b * c

For 2 ≤ a < b with a + b = c: c^2 < abc, because ab ≥ 2b > a + b = c.

IUT.ABC.Variants.two_mul_log_lt_log_mul_multheorem

theorem two_mul_log_lt_log_mul_mul {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  2 * Real.log c < Real.log ((a * b * c : ℕ) : ℝ)

For 2 ≤ a < b with a + b = c: 2 log c < log(abc), that is, the balance is greater than 2 (Laniewski and Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, Lemma 2.2, page 2). Coprimality is not needed. Both other hypotheses are needed: not_sq_lt_of_a_eq_one and not_sq_lt_of_a_eq_b.

For 1 + b = c with b > 0: log(abc) < 2 log c, that is, the balance is less than 2 when a = 1 (Laniewski and Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, Lemma 2.2, page 2).

For 1 + b = c with b ≥ 2: 2 log c - 1 / (c - 1) < log(abc), that is, λ > 2 - 1 / ((c - 1) log c) when a = 1 (Laniewski and Müller, The quality plane of abc-triples and the decomposition into gains, Lemma 2.2, page 2). The proof is theirs: log(c / (c - 1)) < c / (c - 1) - 1 = 1 / (c - 1).

The triples 1 + (3^(2^k) - 1) = 3^(2^k) satisfy 2^k * rad(abc) < 3 c. With 3^(2^k) - 1 = 2^(k + 1) m, the radical is at most 2 * m * 3.

    K * (rad (a * b * c) : ℝ) < c
