IUT.ABC.Variants.masonStothers_natDegree_lttheorem

theorem masonStothers_natDegree_lt {k : Type*} [Field k] [DecidableEq k] {a b c : Polynomial k}
  (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hab : IsCoprime a b) (hsum : a + b = c)
  (hder : ¬ (Polynomial.derivative a = 0 ∧ Polynomial.derivative b = 0 ∧
    Polynomial.derivative c = 0)) :
  c.natDegree < (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical (a * b * c)).natDegree

**Mason–Stothers for a + b = c.** For nonzero polynomials over a field with a and b coprime, a + b = c, and not all three derivatives zero, the degree of c is less than the degree of the radical of abc. This restates Mathlib's Polynomial.abc (stated there for a + b + c = 0). It is the function field analog of the abc conjecture, a theorem, and it implies nothing about the integer statement.

Prerequisites

General mathematics needed by the papers.

IUT.Prerequisites.Anabelioid

IUT/Prerequisites/Anabelioid.lean · imports IUT.Prerequisites.SemiGraph

Connected anabelioids and semi-graphs of anabelioids

Module documentation

Sources:

  • Mochizuki, The Geometry of Anabelioids, Section 1.1, PDF pages 9 and 10 (pages 9, 10 and 11 read for this file and checked against rendered images): the category B(G) of finite sets with continuous G-action for a profinite group G (page 9), Definition 1.1.1 (connected anabelioid), Remark 1.1.1.1, Definition 1.1.2 (morphisms, isomorphisms, basepoints and fundamental groups of connected anabelioids), Remarks 1.1.2.1 to 1.1.2.3.
  • Mochizuki, Semi-graphs of Anabelioids, Definition 2.1, PDF page 22 (pages 22 and 23 read for this file and checked against rendered images), and the definition of connected objects in Section 0, page 7 (read from the rendered image).
  • Comments on "Semi-graphs of Anabelioids" (May 2020), read in full from the text layer; items (9) and (14) checked against rendered images (pages 3 and 7 of the comments). Item (9) says that the assertion in the second display of Remark 2.4.2 of Semi-graphs of Anabelioids is false as stated (Dehn twists give counterexamples), replaces it by a weaker assertion, and adds the hypothesis that every edge abuts to at least one vertex in the discussion that follows it; item (14) corrects "underlying graph" to "underlying semi-graph" in Definition 2.4 (iii). Neither Remark 2.4.2 nor Definition 2.4 is formalized here, so no corrected statement enters this file; Remark 2.4.2 concerns morphisms of semi-graphs of anabelioids, which are not formalized (see below).

Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory I, Section 2 (pages 44 and 45, read from rendered images), works with a semi-graph of anabelioids 𝒢 and the semi-graph of anabelioids attached to a connected sub-semi-graph; Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 are stated in that notation. This file supplies the definition. It proves no numbered result of the papers.

What is formalized
  • FiniteGSets G: the category B(G) of finite sets with continuous action of a profinite group G, built as Mathlib's ContAction FintypeCat G (finite sets with the discrete topology).
  • finiteGSets_galoisCategory: B(G) is a Galois category in the sense of Mathlib (CategoryTheory.GaloisCategory), proved by Mathlib.
  • IsConnectedAnabelioid: Definition 1.1.1, a category equivalent to some B(G).
  • isConnectedAnabelioid_of_galoisCategory: every Galois category in the sense of Mathlib is a connected anabelioid, which is one direction of Remark 1.1.1.1; it is proved from Mathlib's equivalence of a Galois category with the finite continuous Aut F-sets of a fiber functor.
  • AnabelioidMorphism, AnabelioidMorphism.IsIsomorphism, AnabelioidBasepoint, basepointFundamentalGroup: Definition 1.1.2.
  • connectedObjectSubcategory: the full subcategory of connected objects, with connectedness taken from Mathlib (PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected).
  • ConnectedAnabelioid and SemiGraphOfAnabelioids: Definition 2.1 of Semi-graphs of Anabelioids, with a nonvacuity example constantSemiGraphOfAnabelioids.
Interpretation choices, recorded
  • Universes. The paper works in a fixed Grothendieck universe V with a V-small category of finite sets. Here B(G) for G : ProfiniteGrp.{u} uses FintypeCat.{w}, and the predicate IsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} fixes both universe levels; a category is a connected anabelioid at those levels.
  • Exact functors. Page 9 defines an exact functor as one preserving finite limits and finite colimits; this is Mathlib's ExactFunctor (C ⥤ₑ D). A morphism X → Y of connected anabelioids is an exact functor Y ⥤ₑ X (Definition 1.1.2 (i)); AnabelioidMorphism X Y is that type for any two categories, and is used here only between connected anabelioids. The paper takes the 2-categorical point of view (Remark 1.1.2.1): morphisms are considered up to isomorphism of functors. No composition or 2-categorical structure is defined here.
  • Connected objects. Semi-graphs of Anabelioids, page 7, calls a nonempty (non-initial) object connected when it is not isomorphic to a coproduct of two nonempty objects. Mathlib's PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (Lenstra's definition) asks that the object be not initial and have no subobject other than itself and initial ones. That the two notions agree in a Galois category is not proved here.
  • Definition 2.1 (c) asks for a morphism b_* : 𝒢_e → 𝒢_v for each branch b of e abutting to a vertex v; this is branchMorphism b v h, an exact functor 𝒢_v ⥤ₑ 𝒢_e.
Not formalized (open)
  • The converse direction of Remark 1.1.1.1 (a connected anabelioid is a Galois category): Mathlib has no transport of GaloisCategory along an equivalence of categories.
  • The recovery of G up to inner automorphism as Aut(β*) (page 9), the uniqueness of fundamental functors up to isomorphism (page 9), independence of π₁ of the basepoint (Remark 1.1.2.2), and Proposition 1.1.4. These are reconstruction and uniqueness results and are not stated.
  • Anabelioids that are not connected, Example 1.1.3, and the rest of The Geometry of Anabelioids.
  • From Semi-graphs of Anabelioids Section 2: morphisms of semi-graphs of anabelioids (called "evident" on page 22), semi-graphs of anabelioids of injective type (π₁-monomorphisms), the category B(𝒢), the groups Π_𝔾, Π_v, Π_b, Remark 2.4.2 and its corrected form, and everything after Definition 2.1.
Public declarations

IUT.Prerequisites.FiniteGSets.{u,abbrev

abbrev FiniteGSets.{u, w} (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Type (max u (w + 1)) :=
  @ContAction FintypeCat.{w} _ _ _ _ _
    FintypeCatDiscrete.instHasForget₂FintypeCatFunObjFiniteTopCatContinuousMapCarrier G _ _

The category B(G) of finite sets with continuous action of a profinite group G (The Geometry of Anabelioids, page 9), as Mathlib's category of finite sets with the discrete topology and continuous G-action. The discrete topology on finite types is Mathlib's scoped instance of the namespace FintypeCatDiscrete, named explicitly here instead of opening that namespace.

IUT.Prerequisites.finiteGSets_galoisCategory.{u,theorem

theorem finiteGSets_galoisCategory.{u, w} (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    GaloisCategory (FiniteGSets.{u, w} G) :=
  inferInstance

/-- A connected anabelioid (*The Geometry of Anabelioids*, Definition 1.1.1): a category
equivalent to `B(G)` for some profinite group `G`. -/
def IsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, u₁, v₁} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] : Prop :=
  ∃ G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}, Nonempty (X ≌ FiniteGSets.{u, w} G)

/-- `B(G)` is a connected anabelioid. -/
theorem finiteGSets_isConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    IsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} (FiniteGSets.{u, w} G) :=
  ⟨G, ⟨CategoryTheory.Equivalence.refl⟩⟩

/-- Every Galois category in the sense of Mathlib is a connected anabelioid: one direction of
Remark 1.1.1.1 of *The Geometry of Anabelioids*. The profinite group is the automorphism group of
a fiber functor, and the equivalence is Mathlib's `PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction`. -/
theorem isConnectedAnabelioid_of_galoisCategory.{u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{u₂} C]
    [GaloisCategory C] : IsConnectedAnabelioid.{max u₁ u₂, u₂} C :=
  ⟨ProfiniteGrp.of (Aut (GaloisCategory.getFiberFunctor C)),
    ⟨(PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction (GaloisCategory.getFiberFunctor C)).asEquivalence⟩⟩

/-- A morphism `X → Y` of connected anabelioids (*The Geometry of Anabelioids*,
Definition 1.1.2 (i)): an exact functor `Y ⥤ X`, that is, one preserving finite limits and finite
colimits. -/
abbrev AnabelioidMorphism.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] (Y : Type u₂)
    [Category.{v₂} Y] :=
  Y ⥤ₑ X

/-- An isomorphism of connected anabelioids (Definition 1.1.2 (i)): a morphism whose functor in
the opposite direction is an equivalence of categories. -/
def AnabelioidMorphism.IsIsomorphism.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} {X : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} X] {Y : Type u₂}
    [Category.{v₂} Y] (φ : AnabelioidMorphism X Y) : Prop :=
  φ.obj.IsEquivalence

/-- A basepoint of a connected anabelioid `X` (Definition 1.1.2 (ii)): a morphism from the
category of finite sets to `X`, that is, an exact functor `X ⥤ FintypeCat`. -/
abbrev AnabelioidBasepoint.{w, u₁, v₁} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] :=
  AnabelioidMorphism FintypeCat.{w} X

/-- The fundamental group `π₁(X, β) = Aut(β)` of a connected anabelioid with a basepoint
(Definition 1.1.2 (ii)): the automorphisms of the functor underlying `β`. -/
abbrev basepointFundamentalGroup.{w, u₁, v₁} {X : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} X]
    (β : AnabelioidBasepoint.{w, u₁, v₁} X) : Type (max u₁ w) :=
  Aut β.obj

/-- The full subcategory of connected objects, with Mathlib's notion of a connected object of a
Galois category (`PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected`). -/
abbrev connectedObjectSubcategory.{u₁, v₁} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] : Type _ :=
  ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory fun A : X => PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected A

/-- A connected anabelioid, bundled: a category together with the fact that it is a connected
anabelioid. -/
structure ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, u₁, v₁} where
  /-- The underlying category. -/
  underlyingCat : Cat.{v₁, u₁}
  /-- It is equivalent to some `B(G)`. -/
  isConnectedAnabelioid : IsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} underlyingCat

/-- A semi-graph of (connected) anabelioids (*Semi-graphs of Anabelioids*, Definition 2.1): a
semi-graph `𝔾`, a connected anabelioid `𝒢_v` for each vertex `v`, a connected anabelioid `𝒢_e`
for each edge `e`, and for each branch `b` of `e` abutting to a vertex `v` a morphism of
anabelioids `b_* : 𝒢_e → 𝒢_v`, that is, an exact functor `𝒢_v ⥤ 𝒢_e`. -/
structure SemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, u₁, v₁, u₃} (𝔾 : SemiGraph.{u₃}) where
  /-- The constituent anabelioid at a vertex. -/
  vertexAnabelioid : 𝔾.Vertex → ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, u₁, v₁}
  /-- The constituent anabelioid at an edge. -/
  edgeAnabelioid : 𝔾.Edge → ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, u₁, v₁}
  /-- The morphism `b_* : 𝒢_e → 𝒢_v` for a branch `b` of `e` abutting to `v`. -/
  branchMorphism : ∀ (b : 𝔾.Branch) (v : 𝔾.Vertex), 𝔾.coincidence b = some v →
    AnabelioidMorphism (edgeAnabelioid (𝔾.edgeOf b)).underlyingCat
      (vertexAnabelioid v).underlyingCat

/-- `B(G)` as a bundled connected anabelioid. -/
def finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, max u (w + 1), w} where
  underlyingCat := Cat.of (FiniteGSets.{u, w} G)
  isConnectedAnabelioid := finiteGSets_isConnectedAnabelioid G

/-- Nonvacuity of Definition 2.1: on any semi-graph, the constant semi-graph of anabelioids with
every constituent anabelioid `B(G)` and every branch morphism the identity functor. -/
def constantSemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, u₃} (𝔾 : SemiGraph.{u₃}) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    SemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, max u (w + 1), w, u₃} 𝔾 where
  vertexAnabelioid := fun _ => finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} G
  edgeAnabelioid := fun _ => finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} G
  branchMorphism := fun _ _ _ =>
    ⟨𝟭 _, (exactFunctor_iff _).2 ⟨Limits.PreservesLimitsOfSize.preservesFiniteLimits.{0, 0} _,
      Limits.PreservesColimitsOfSize.preservesFiniteColimits.{0, 0} _⟩⟩

end IUT.Prerequisites

B(G) is a Galois category in the sense of Mathlib (The Geometry of Anabelioids, page 9, "a rather special kind of topos called a Galois category"). The proof is Mathlib's.

abbrev AnabelioidMorphism.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] (Y : Type u₂)
    [Category.{v₂} Y] :=
  Y ⥤ₑ X

A morphism X → Y of connected anabelioids (The Geometry of Anabelioids, Definition 1.1.2 (i)): an exact functor Y ⥤ X, that is, one preserving finite limits and finite colimits.

IUT.Prerequisites.AnabelioidMorphism.IsIsomorphism.{u₁,def

def AnabelioidMorphism.IsIsomorphism.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} {X : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} X] {Y : Type u₂}
    [Category.{v₂} Y] (φ : AnabelioidMorphism X Y) : Prop :=
  φ.obj.IsEquivalence

An isomorphism of connected anabelioids (Definition 1.1.2 (i)): a morphism whose functor in the opposite direction is an equivalence of categories.

IUT.Prerequisites.AnabelioidBasepoint.{w,abbrev

abbrev AnabelioidBasepoint.{w, u₁, v₁} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] :=
  AnabelioidMorphism FintypeCat.{w} X

A basepoint of a connected anabelioid X (Definition 1.1.2 (ii)): a morphism from the category of finite sets to X, that is, an exact functor X ⥤ FintypeCat.

IUT.Prerequisites.basepointFundamentalGroup.{w,abbrev

abbrev basepointFundamentalGroup.{w, u₁, v₁} {X : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} X]
    (β : AnabelioidBasepoint.{w, u₁, v₁} X) : Type (max u₁ w) :=
  Aut β.obj

The fundamental group π₁(X, β) = Aut(β) of a connected anabelioid with a basepoint (Definition 1.1.2 (ii)): the automorphisms of the functor underlying β.

IUT.Prerequisites.connectedObjectSubcategory.{u₁,abbrev

abbrev connectedObjectSubcategory.{u₁, v₁} (X : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} X] : Type _ :=
  ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory fun A : X => PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected A

The full subcategory of connected objects, with Mathlib's notion of a connected object of a Galois category (PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected).

IUT.Prerequisites.ConnectedAnabelioid.{u,structure

structure ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, u₁, v₁} where

A connected anabelioid, bundled: a category together with the fact that it is a connected anabelioid.

IUT.Prerequisites.SemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u,structure

structure SemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, u₁, v₁, u₃} (𝔾 : SemiGraph.{u₃}) where

A semi-graph of (connected) anabelioids (Semi-graphs of Anabelioids, Definition 2.1): a semi-graph 𝔾, a connected anabelioid 𝒢_v for each vertex v, a connected anabelioid 𝒢_e for each edge e, and for each branch b of e abutting to a vertex v a morphism of anabelioids b_* : 𝒢_e → 𝒢_v, that is, an exact functor 𝒢_v ⥤ 𝒢_e.

IUT.Prerequisites.finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u,def

def finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    ConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w, max u (w + 1), w} where
  underlyingCat := Cat.of (FiniteGSets.{u, w} G)
  isConnectedAnabelioid := finiteGSets_isConnectedAnabelioid G

B(G) as a bundled connected anabelioid.

IUT.Prerequisites.constantSemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u,def

def constantSemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, u₃} (𝔾 : SemiGraph.{u₃}) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) :
    SemiGraphOfAnabelioids.{u, w, max u (w + 1), w, u₃} 𝔾 where
  vertexAnabelioid := fun _ => finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} G
  edgeAnabelioid := fun _ => finiteGSetsConnectedAnabelioid.{u, w} G
  branchMorphism := fun _ _ _ =>
    ⟨𝟭 _, (exactFunctor_iff _).2 ⟨Limits.PreservesLimitsOfSize.preservesFiniteLimits.{0, 0} _,
      Limits.PreservesColimitsOfSize.preservesFiniteColimits.{0, 0} _⟩⟩

Nonvacuity of Definition 2.1: on any semi-graph, the constant semi-graph of anabelioids with every constituent anabelioid B(G) and every branch morphism the identity functor.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid

IUT/Prerequisites/Frobenioid.lean

Frobenioids: monoids, elementary Frobenioids, Definitions 1.1 to 1.3 (partial)

Module documentation

Source: Shinichi Mochizuki, The Geometry of Frobenioids I: The General Theory, Section 0 ("Notations and Conventions", pages 10 to 16) and Section 1 (Definitions 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, Remarks 1.1.1 and 1.2.1, pages 19 to 25, and Proposition 1.5, page 27), with the author's Comments on "The Geometry of Frobenioids I" (January 2024). Pages read for this file: 10 to 25 and 27 of the paper and pages 1 to 6 of the comments (text); pages checked against rendered images: 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 19 to 25 and 27 of the paper and pages 1 and 6 of the comments. Every definition below was compared with the rendered page it cites.

Errata applied (numbering of the comments): item 30 (in Definition 1.1 (i) "of characteristic type" is automatic) is proved as isCharacteristicTypeMonoid_of_isIntegralMonoid; the definition IsPreDivisorialMonoid keeps all three conditions of the page, and isPreDivisorialMonoid_iff shows the third redundant. Item 3 (quotation marks around Φ^pf in Definition 1.1 (ii)) is typographical. Items 4, 13 (monoprime monoids, ordering of {ℤ, ℚ, ℝ}) and 28 (FSMFF-type) concern notions not formalized here. No other item touches pages 10 to 25.

This file is a prerequisite for the Frobenioid-theoretic data of IUT I (Examples 3.2 to 3.5, Definitions 3.6 and 4.1); it does not formalize any statement of IUT I.

Formalized
  • Section 0, page 11 and 12: sharp, integral, saturated, torsion-free, perfect monoids; the characteristic M^char = M / M^± (characteristicCon, MonoidCharacteristic); characteristic type; characteristically injective morphisms; the relations ≤, ≼; irreducible and primary elements. The groupification M^gp is Mathlib's Grothendieck group, whose construction is the one of page 11.
  • Section 0, pages 14 and 15: fiberwise-surjective arrows, FSM-morphisms, totally epimorphic categories. "Connected" (page 16) is read as Mathlib's IsConnected (nonempty and connected by zigzags).
  • Definition 1.1 (i): pre-divisorial, group-like, divisorial monoids, non-dilating endomorphisms. Group-like, divisorial and non-dilating are defined on the page only under the pre-divisorial hypothesis, which is therefore part of each definition.
  • Definition 1.1 (ii): monoids on a category (IsMonoidOn, with "isomorphism of monoids" read as a bijective morphism) and divisorial monoids on a category.
  • Definition 1.1 (iii): the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_Φ of a functor Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat: objects, morphisms (φ_D, Z_φ, n_φ), the composition (ψ_D ∘ φ_D, φ_D^*(Z_ψ) + n_ψ · Z_φ, n_ψ · n_φ), identities, and the three category laws as theorems (elemFrobCompose_identity_left, elemFrobCompose_identity_right, elemFrobCompose_assoc); the category structure elemFrobCategory and the projection functor to D. The construction does not use conditions (a), (b) of a monoid on D, so it is stated for every functor. The elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_M of a monoid (elemFrobMonoid) and the noncommutativity of the standard Frobenioid 𝔽 = 𝔽_{ℤ≥0}.
  • Definition 1.1 (iv) and Remark 1.1.1: functors C → 𝔽_Φ, the pre-Frobenioid hypotheses, and Base, Div, deg_Fr with their behavior under composition, proved from functoriality.
  • Definition 1.2 (i) to (iii) completely, and from (iv) the Frobenius-ample, Frobenius-trivial and isotropic objects and isotropic hulls. Remark 1.2.1, third implication.
  • Definition 1.3: clauses (i) (a), (i) (b), (ii), (iii) (a) to (c), (iv), (v), (vi), (vii), one definition each, and their conjunction with the pre-Frobenioid hypotheses, PartialFrobenioidConditions.
  • An inhabitant of PartialFrobenioidConditions: the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_ℕ over the one-object, one-morphism category Discrete PUnit, with its identity functor (natPoint_partialFrobenioidConditions), each clause proved separately. Proposition 1.5 (i) (page 27) asserts that 𝔽_Φ, with the natural functor 𝔽_Φ → 𝔽_{Φ^char}, is a Frobenioid whenever Φ is a pre-divisorial monoid on a connected, totally epimorphic category D. The example meets these hypotheses: the constant monoid ℕ is divisorial, and Discrete PUnit is connected and totally epimorphic. Since ℕ is sharp, Φ^char = Φ, so the natural functor is the identity functor used here.
Not formalized
  • Definition 1.3 (i) (c) (the functor (C^pl-bk)_A → D_{A_D} is an equivalence) and (iii) (d) (the functors from the categories of co-angular pre-steps under and over A to Order(Φ(A)) and its opposite are equivalences). They need category structures on slices of non-full subcategories, which would have to be built as new categories. Hence PartialFrobenioidConditions is not the definition of a Frobenioid, and no declaration here is called a Frobenioid.
  • The perfection M^pf (only the predicate "perfect" is defined), primes Prime(M), bounded subsets and suprema, and the objects of Definition 1.2 (iv) other than those listed above; Definition 1.2 (v) (types of pre-Frobenioids).
  • That the example satisfies the omitted clauses (i) (c) and (iii) (d), which Proposition 1.5 asserts, is not proved, since those clauses are not stated.
Conventions
  • Monoids are written additively, as on page 11, and ℕ≥1 is ℕ+.
  • Mathlib writes composition in diagrammatic order: the paper's ψ ∘ φ is φ ≫ ψ.
  • The library registers no instances, so the category structure of 𝔽_Φ is the plain definition elemFrobCategory, passed explicitly where it is needed; functors C → 𝔽_Φ are FrobFunctor C Φ.
  • "Isomorphism class of a Frobenius-trivial object maps to every isomorphism class" in Definition 1.3 (i) (a) is stated as: for every object X of D there is a Frobenius-trivial A with Base(A) ≅ X. The pull-back condition of Definition 1.2 (ii) is stated objectwise (an isomorphism of presheaves of sets is an objectwise bijection).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.toGroupificationabbrev

noncomputable abbrev toGroupification : M →+ Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup M :=
  Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup.of

The natural homomorphism M → M^gp to the groupification, realized by Mathlib's Grothendieck group (the localization of M at all of M; its elements are classes of pairs (a, b) with (a₁, b₁) ∼ (a₂, b₂) when a₁ + b₂ + c = b₁ + a₂ + c for some c, as on page 11).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsSharpMonoiddef

def IsSharpMonoid : Prop := ∀ u : AddUnits M, u = 0

M is sharp (page 11): its group of invertible elements M^± is zero.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsIntegralMonoiddef

def IsIntegralMonoid : Prop := Function.Injective (toGroupification M)

M is integral (page 11): the natural map M → M^gp is injective.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsSaturatedMonoiddef

def IsSaturatedMonoid : Prop :=
  ∀ a : Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup M,
    (∃ n : ℕ+, (n : ℕ) • a ∈ Set.range (toGroupification M)) →
      a ∈ Set.range (toGroupification M)

M is saturated (page 11): every a ∈ M^gp such that n · a lies in the image of M for some n ∈ ℕ≥1 lies in the image of M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsTorsionFreeMonoiddef

def IsTorsionFreeMonoid : Prop := ∀ (a : M) (n : ℕ+), (n : ℕ) • a = 0 → a = 0

M is torsion-free (page 11): M has no torsion elements. Reading: a torsion element is a nonzero a with n · a = 0 for some n ∈ ℕ≥1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPerfectMonoiddef

def IsPerfectMonoid : Prop := ∀ n : ℕ+, Function.Bijective fun a : M => (n : ℕ) • a

M is perfect (page 11): multiplication by every element of ℕ≥1 is bijective on M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.characteristicCondef

def characteristicCon : AddCon M where
  r a b := ∃ u : AddUnits M, a + (u : M) = b
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun a => ⟨0, by simp⟩,
     fun {a b} ⟨u, h⟩ => ⟨-u, by rw [← h, add_assoc, AddUnits.add_neg, add_zero]⟩,
     fun {a b c} ⟨u, h⟩ ⟨w, k⟩ => ⟨u + w, by rw [← k, ← h, AddUnits.val_add, add_assoc]⟩⟩
  add' := by
    rintro a b c d ⟨u, h⟩ ⟨w, k⟩
    refine ⟨u + w, ?_⟩
    rw [← h, ← k, AddUnits.val_add]
    abel

The congruence on M whose quotient is the characteristic M^char = M / M^± (page 11): a ∼ b when a + u = b for some invertible u.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.MonoidCharacteristicabbrev

abbrev MonoidCharacteristic : Type _ := (characteristicCon M).Quotient

The characteristic M^char = M / M^± of M (page 11), as the quotient monoid of characteristicCon.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsCharacteristicTypeMonoiddef

def IsCharacteristicTypeMonoid : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : M, characteristicCon M a b → ∃! u : AddUnits M, a + (u : M) = b

M is of characteristic type (page 11): the fibers of M ↠ M^char are torsors over M^±. Reading: M^± acts on each fiber by addition; the action is transitive by the definition of the quotient, and the torsor condition asks that it be free, so for a, b in one fiber there is exactly one invertible u with a + u = b.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isCharacteristicTypeMonoid_of_isIntegralMonoidtheorem

theorem isCharacteristicTypeMonoid_of_isIntegralMonoid {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
  (h : IsIntegralMonoid M) : IsCharacteristicTypeMonoid M

Erratum 30 of the comments on the paper: "of characteristic type" is automatic in Definition 1.1 (i). Here: an integral monoid is of characteristic type.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPreDivisorialMonoiddef

def IsPreDivisorialMonoid : Prop :=
  IsIntegralMonoid M ∧ IsSaturatedMonoid M ∧ IsCharacteristicTypeMonoid M

Definition 1.1 (i), page 19: M is pre-divisorial if it is integral, saturated and of characteristic type. All three conditions of the page are kept; by isCharacteristicTypeMonoid_of_isIntegralMonoid the third is redundant (erratum 30).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isPreDivisorialMonoid_ifftheorem

theorem isPreDivisorialMonoid_iff :
  IsPreDivisorialMonoid M ↔ IsIntegralMonoid M ∧ IsSaturatedMonoid M

Pre-divisorial is equivalent to integral and saturated (erratum 30).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsGroupLikeMonoiddef

def IsGroupLikeMonoid : Prop :=
  IsPreDivisorialMonoid M ∧ ∀ x : MonoidCharacteristic M, x = 0

Definition 1.1 (i), page 19: a pre-divisorial M is group-like if M^char is zero. The page defines the term only for pre-divisorial M, so that hypothesis is part of the definition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsDivisorialMonoiddef

def IsDivisorialMonoid : Prop := IsPreDivisorialMonoid M ∧ IsSharpMonoid M

Definition 1.1 (i), page 19: a pre-divisorial M is divisorial if it is sharp. The pre-divisorial hypothesis of the page is part of the definition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.MonoidDividesdef

def MonoidDivides (a b : M) : Prop := ∃ c : M, a + c = b

The relation a ≤ b of page 12: a + c = b for some c ∈ M. The page introduces it for sharp, integral, saturated M; it is defined here for every commutative monoid.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.MonoidPrecedesdef

def MonoidPrecedes (a b : M) : Prop := ∃ n : ℕ+, MonoidDivides a ((n : ℕ) • b)

The relation a ≼ b of page 12: a ≤ n · b for some n ∈ ℕ≥1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsIrreducibleElemdef

def IsIrreducibleElem (a : M) : Prop := a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ b c : M, a = b + c → b = 0 ∨ c = 0

An irreducible element (page 12): a ≠ 0, and a = b + c implies b = 0 or c = 0.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPrimaryElemdef

def IsPrimaryElem (a : M) : Prop :=
  a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ b : M, MonoidPrecedes b a → b ≠ 0 → MonoidPrecedes a b

A primary element (page 12): a ≠ 0, and for every b ≠ 0 with b ≼ a, a ≼ b.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.characteristicMapdef

def characteristicMap (f : M →+ N) : MonoidCharacteristic M →+ MonoidCharacteristic N :=
  (characteristicCon M).lift ((characteristicCon N).mk'.comp f) <| by
    rintro a b ⟨u, rfl⟩
    rw [AddCon.ker_rel, AddMonoidHom.comp_apply, AddMonoidHom.comp_apply, map_add]
    exact (AddCon.eq _).2 ⟨AddUnits.map f u, rfl⟩

The morphism M^char → N^char induced by a morphism f : M → N of commutative monoids.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.characteristicMap_mktheorem

theorem characteristicMap_mk (f : M →+ N) (a : M) :
  characteristicMap f ((characteristicCon M).mk' a) = (characteristicCon N).mk' (f a)

The induced map on characteristics sends the class of a to the class of f(a).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsCharInjectivedef

def IsCharInjective (f : M →+ N) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Injective (characteristicMap f)

A morphism f : M → N is characteristically injective (page 11) if f is injective and the induced morphism M^char → N^char is injective.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsNonDilatingdef

def IsNonDilating (α : M →+ M) : Prop :=
  IsPreDivisorialMonoid M ∧
    ((∀ a : MonoidCharacteristic M, IsPrimaryElem a → MonoidPrecedes (characteristicMap α a) a) →
      characteristicMap α = AddMonoidHom.id _)

Definition 1.1 (i), page 19: an endomorphism α of a pre-divisorial M is non-dilating if α^char is the identity of M^char whenever α^char(a) ≼ a for every primary a ∈ M^char. The pre-divisorial hypothesis of the page is part of the definition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isIntegralMonoid_of_isCancelAddtheorem

theorem isIntegralMonoid_of_isCancelAdd (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [IsCancelAdd M] :
  IsIntegralMonoid M

A cancellative commutative monoid is integral (via Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup.of_injective).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.exists_eq_sub_toGroupificationtheorem

theorem exists_eq_sub_toGroupification {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
  (x : Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup M) :
  ∃ p q : M, x = toGroupification M p - toGroupification M q

Every element of M^gp is a difference of two elements of the image of M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isSaturatedMonoid_of_addCommGrouptheorem

theorem isSaturatedMonoid_of_addCommGroup (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] :
  IsSaturatedMonoid M

A commutative group is saturated: M → M^gp is onto.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isSharpMonoid_of_canonicallyOrderedAddtheorem

theorem isSharpMonoid_of_canonicallyOrderedAdd (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [PartialOrder M]
  [CanonicallyOrderedAdd M] : IsSharpMonoid M

A sharp-type criterion: a canonically ordered commutative monoid is sharp.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isSaturatedMonoid_of_linearOrdertheorem

theorem isSaturatedMonoid_of_linearOrder (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [LinearOrder M]
  [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid M] [CanonicallyOrderedAdd M] : IsSaturatedMonoid M

A linearly and canonically ordered cancellative commutative monoid is saturated. This covers ℕ, ℚ≥0 and ℝ≥0.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isDivisorialMonoid_of_linearOrdertheorem

theorem isDivisorialMonoid_of_linearOrder (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [LinearOrder M]
  [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid M] [CanonicallyOrderedAdd M] : IsDivisorialMonoid M

A cancellative, linearly and canonically ordered commutative monoid is divisorial.

theorem nat_isDivisorialMonoid : IsDivisorialMonoid ℕ

ℕ = ℤ≥0 under addition is divisorial.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.nnrat_isDivisorialMonoidtheorem

theorem nnrat_isDivisorialMonoid : IsDivisorialMonoid ℚ≥0

ℚ≥0 under addition is divisorial.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.nnreal_isDivisorialMonoidtheorem

theorem nnreal_isDivisorialMonoid : IsDivisorialMonoid NNReal

ℝ≥0 under addition is divisorial.

theorem nat_not_isPerfectMonoid : ¬ IsPerfectMonoid ℕ

ℕ is not perfect: 2 · a = 1 has no solution.

theorem nnrat_isPerfectMonoid : IsPerfectMonoid ℚ≥0

ℚ≥0 is perfect.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.nnreal_isPerfectMonoidtheorem

theorem nnreal_isPerfectMonoid : IsPerfectMonoid NNReal

ℝ≥0 is perfect.

theorem nat_isTorsionFreeMonoid : IsTorsionFreeMonoid ℕ

ℕ is torsion-free.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.zmod2_not_isTorsionFreeMonoidtheorem

theorem zmod2_not_isTorsionFreeMonoid : ¬ IsTorsionFreeMonoid (ZMod 2)

ZMod 2 is not torsion-free.

theorem int_isGroupLikeMonoid : IsGroupLikeMonoid ℤ

ℤ is pre-divisorial and group-like: its characteristic is zero.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.int_not_isSharpMonoidtheorem

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.withTopNat_not_isIntegralMonoidtheorem

theorem withTopNat_not_isIntegralMonoid : ¬ IsIntegralMonoid (WithTop ℕ)

WithTop ℕ is not integral: 0 + ⊤ = 1 + ⊤ and M^gp is a group.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.withTopInt_not_isCharacteristicTypeMonoidtheorem

theorem withTopInt_not_isCharacteristicTypeMonoid :
  ¬ IsCharacteristicTypeMonoid (WithTop ℤ)

WithTop ℤ is not of characteristic type: the units 0 and 1 act equally on ⊤.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsFiberwiseSurjectivedef

def IsFiberwiseSurjective {B A : C} (β : B ⟶ A) : Prop :=
  ∀ (E : C) (γ : E ⟶ A), ∃ (F : C) (δB : F ⟶ B) (δE : F ⟶ E), δB ≫ β = δE ≫ γ

An arrow β : B → A is fiberwise-surjective (page 14) if for every arrow γ : E → A there are arrows δ_B : F → B, δ_E : F → E with β ∘ δ_B = γ ∘ δ_E.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsFSMMorphismdef

def IsFSMMorphism {B A : C} (β : B ⟶ A) : Prop := IsFiberwiseSurjective β ∧ Mono β

An FSM-morphism (page 14): a fiberwise-surjective monomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsTotallyEpimorphicCatdef

def IsTotallyEpimorphicCat (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y), Epi f

A totally epimorphic category (page 15): every morphism is an epimorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsMonoidOndef

def IsMonoidOn (Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat.{w}) : Prop :=
  (∀ {B A : D} (α : B ⟶ A), IsCharInjective (Φ.map α.op).hom) ∧
    ∀ {B A : D} (α : B ⟶ A), IsFSMMorphism α → Function.Bijective (Φ.map α.op).hom

Definition 1.1 (ii), page 19: a contravariant functor Φ : D → Mon (here Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat) is a *monoid on D* if (a) every induced α^* : Φ(A) → Φ(B), for α : B → A, is characteristically injective, and (b) α^* is an isomorphism of monoids (here: bijective) whenever α is an FSM-morphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsDivisorialMonoidOndef

def IsDivisorialMonoidOn (Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat.{w}) : Prop :=
  IsMonoidOn Φ ∧ ∀ A : D, IsDivisorialMonoid (Φ.obj (op A))

Definition 1.1 (ii): Φ is divisorial if every Φ(A) is divisorial.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.characteristicMap_idtheorem

theorem characteristicMap_id {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] :
  characteristicMap (AddMonoidHom.id M) = AddMonoidHom.id _

Characteristic map of the identity.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.constNat_isDivisorialMonoidOntheorem

theorem constNat_isDivisorialMonoidOn :
  IsDivisorialMonoidOn
    ((Functor.const (Discrete PUnit.{1})ᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommMonCat.of ℕ))

The constant functor with value ℕ on a category in which every morphism is an identity (here Discrete PUnit) is a divisorial monoid on that category: Definition 1.1 (ii) is nonvacuous.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.ElemFrobObjdef

def ElemFrobObj (_Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat.{w}) : Type u := D

The objects of 𝔽_Φ: the objects of D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.ElemFrobHomabbrev

abbrev ElemFrobHom (A B : D) : Type (max v w) := (A ⟶ B) × Φ.obj (op A) × ℕ+

A morphism A → B of 𝔽_Φ: a triple (φ_D, Z_φ, n_φ) with φ_D : A_D → B_D in D, Z_φ ∈ Φ(A_D) and n_φ ∈ ℕ≥1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemBasedef

def elemBase {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) : A ⟶ B := φ.1

The projection Base(φ) = φ_D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemDivdef

def elemDiv {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) : Φ.obj (op A) := φ.2.1

The zero divisor Div(φ) = Z_φ ∈ Φ(A_D).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemDegdef

def elemDeg {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) : ℕ+ := φ.2.2

The Frobenius degree deg_Fr(φ) = n_φ ∈ ℕ≥1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobIdentitydef

def elemFrobIdentity (A : D) : ElemFrobHom Φ A A := (𝟙 A, 0, 1)

The identity of A in 𝔽_Φ: (id, 0, 1).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobComposedef

def elemFrobCompose {A B C : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) (ψ : ElemFrobHom Φ B C) :
    ElemFrobHom Φ A C :=
  (φ.1 ≫ ψ.1, (Φ.map φ.1.op).hom ψ.2.1 + (ψ.2.2 : ℕ) • φ.2.1, ψ.2.2 * φ.2.2)

Composition in 𝔽_Φ (page 20). For φ = (φ_D, Z_φ, n_φ) : A → B and ψ = (ψ_D, Z_ψ, n_ψ) : B → C, the composite ψ ∘ φ (written elemFrobCompose φ ψ, in diagrammatic order) is (ψ_D ∘ φ_D, φ_D^*(Z_ψ) + n_ψ · Z_φ, n_ψ · n_φ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobCompose_identity_lefttheorem

theorem elemFrobCompose_identity_left {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) :
  elemFrobCompose (elemFrobIdentity Φ A) φ = φ

Left identity law of 𝔽_Φ: φ ∘ id = φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobCompose_identity_righttheorem

theorem elemFrobCompose_identity_right {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) :
  elemFrobCompose φ (elemFrobIdentity Φ B) = φ

Right identity law of 𝔽_Φ: id ∘ φ = φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobCompose_assoctheorem

theorem elemFrobCompose_assoc {A B C E : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) (ψ : ElemFrobHom Φ B C)
  (χ : ElemFrobHom Φ C E) :
  elemFrobCompose (elemFrobCompose φ ψ) χ = elemFrobCompose φ (elemFrobCompose ψ χ)

Associativity of the composition of 𝔽_Φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemBase_composetheorem

theorem elemBase_compose {A B C : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) (ψ : ElemFrobHom Φ B C) :
  elemBase (elemFrobCompose φ ψ) = elemBase φ ≫ elemBase ψ

In 𝔽_Φ: Base(ψ ∘ φ) = Base(ψ) ∘ Base(φ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemDiv_composetheorem

theorem elemDiv_compose {A B C : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) (ψ : ElemFrobHom Φ B C) :
  elemDiv (elemFrobCompose φ ψ) =
    (Φ.map (elemBase φ).op).hom (elemDiv ψ) + (elemDeg ψ : ℕ) • elemDiv φ

In 𝔽_Φ: Div(ψ ∘ φ) = Base(φ)^*(Div(ψ)) + deg_Fr(ψ) · Div(φ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemDeg_composetheorem

theorem elemDeg_compose {A B C : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) (ψ : ElemFrobHom Φ B C) :
  elemDeg (elemFrobCompose φ ψ) = elemDeg ψ * elemDeg φ

In 𝔽_Φ the Frobenius degree is multiplicative: deg_Fr(ψ ∘ φ) = deg_Fr(ψ) · deg_Fr(φ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobCategorydef

@[reducible] def elemFrobCategory : Category.{max v w} (ElemFrobObj Φ) where
  Hom A B := ElemFrobHom Φ A B
  id A := elemFrobIdentity Φ A
  comp φ ψ := elemFrobCompose φ ψ
  id_comp := elemFrobCompose_identity_left
  comp_id := elemFrobCompose_identity_right
  assoc := elemFrobCompose_assoc

The category structure of the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_Φ (Definition 1.1 (iii)). It is a plain definition, not a registered instance, because the library declares no instances; the three laws are the theorems elemFrobCompose_identity_left, elemFrobCompose_identity_right and elemFrobCompose_assoc about the concrete composition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobProjectiondef

def elemFrobProjection : @Functor (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) D _ :=
  letI := elemFrobCategory Φ
  { obj := fun A => (A : D)
    map := fun φ => elemBase φ
    map_id := fun _ => rfl
    map_comp := fun _ _ => rfl }

The natural projection functor 𝔽_Φ → D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.ElemFrobMonoidCarrierabbrev

abbrev ElemFrobMonoidCarrier : Type _ := M × ℕ+

The underlying set M × ℕ≥1 of the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_M associated to M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobMuldef

def elemFrobMul (x y : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M :=
  (x.1 + (x.2 : ℕ) • y.1, x.2 * y.2)

The product of 𝔽_M (page 20): (a₁, n₁) · (a₂, n₂) = (a₁ + n₁ · a₂, n₁ · n₂). It agrees with the composition of 𝔽_Φ for the one-object case, (a₁, n₁) · (a₂, n₂) being the composite ψ ∘ φ with ψ = (a₁, n₁), φ = (a₂, n₂) and φ_D^* the identity.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobMul_assoctheorem

theorem elemFrobMul_assoc (x y z : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) :
  elemFrobMul (elemFrobMul x y) z = elemFrobMul x (elemFrobMul y z)

Associativity of the product of 𝔽_M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobMul_unit_lefttheorem

theorem elemFrobMul_unit_left (x : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) :
  elemFrobMul ((0, 1) : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) x = x

(0, 1) is a left unit of 𝔽_M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobMul_unit_righttheorem

theorem elemFrobMul_unit_right (x : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) :
  elemFrobMul x ((0, 1) : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) = x

(0, 1) is a right unit of 𝔽_M.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobMonoiddef

@[reducible] def elemFrobMonoid : Monoid (ElemFrobMonoidCarrier M) where
  mul := elemFrobMul
  one := ((0 : M), (1 : ℕ+))
  mul_assoc := elemFrobMul_assoc
  one_mul := elemFrobMul_unit_left
  mul_one := elemFrobMul_unit_right

The monoid 𝔽_M (page 20), as a plain definition (no instance is registered).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.standardFrobenioid_mul_not_commtheorem

theorem standardFrobenioid_mul_not_comm :
  elemFrobMul ((1, 1) : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier ℕ) (0, 2) = (1, 2) ∧
    elemFrobMul ((0, 2) : ElemFrobMonoidCarrier ℕ) (1, 1) = (2, 2)

The standard Frobenioid 𝔽 = 𝔽_{ℤ≥0} (page 20) is not commutative: (1, 1) · (0, 2) = (1, 2) while (0, 2) · (1, 1) = (2, 2).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobFunctorabbrev

abbrev FrobFunctor (C : Type u') [Category.{v'} C] (Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat.{w}) :=
  @Functor C _ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ)

A functor C → 𝔽_Φ, with the category structure elemFrobCategory Φ on the target.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPreFrobenioidStructuredef

def IsPreFrobenioidStructure (_P : FrobFunctor C Φ) : Prop :=
  IsDivisorialMonoidOn Φ ∧ IsConnected C ∧ IsConnected D ∧ IsTotallyEpimorphicCat C ∧
    IsTotallyEpimorphicCat D

Definition 1.1 (iv), page 20: a functor C → 𝔽_Φ is a pre-Frobenioid structure on C when Φ is a divisorial monoid on D and C, D are connected, totally epimorphic categories. Reading of "connected" (page 16: the graph of the category is connected): Mathlib's IsConnected, which also asks the category to be nonempty.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobObjdef

def frobObj (X : C) : D := @Functor.obj C _ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) P X

Base(X) ∈ Ob(D) for an object X of C.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobImagedef

def frobImage {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ElemFrobHom Φ (frobObj P X) (frobObj P Y) :=
  letI := elemFrobCategory Φ
  P.map f

The morphism P(f) of 𝔽_Φ, as a triple.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobImage_composetheorem

theorem frobImage_compose {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  frobImage P (f ≫ g) = elemFrobCompose (frobImage P f) (frobImage P g)

Functoriality: the image of a composite is the composite in 𝔽_Φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobImage_identitytheorem

theorem frobImage_identity (X : C) : frobImage P (𝟙 X) = elemFrobIdentity Φ (frobObj P X)

Functoriality: the image of an identity is the identity of 𝔽_Φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobBasedef

def frobBase {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : frobObj P X ⟶ frobObj P Y := elemBase (frobImage P f)

Base(f), the projection of f to D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDivdef

def frobDiv {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Φ.obj (op (frobObj P X)) := elemDiv (frobImage P f)

Div(f) ∈ Φ(Base(X)), the zero divisor of f : X → Y.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDegdef

def frobDeg {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ℕ+ := elemDeg (frobImage P f)

deg_Fr(f) ∈ ℕ≥1, the Frobenius degree of f.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobBase_composetheorem

theorem frobBase_compose {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  frobBase P (f ≫ g) = frobBase P f ≫ frobBase P g

Remark 1.1.1, page 21: Base(φ ∘ ψ) = Base(φ) ∘ Base(ψ) (here ψ ≫ φ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDiv_composetheorem

theorem frobDiv_compose {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  frobDiv P (f ≫ g) =
    (Φ.map (frobBase P f).op).hom (frobDiv P g) + ((frobDeg P g : ℕ)) • frobDiv P f

Remark 1.1.1, page 21: Div(φ ∘ ψ) = Base(ψ)^*(Div(φ)) + deg_Fr(φ) · Div(ψ), with ψ = f, φ = g.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDeg_composetheorem

theorem frobDeg_compose {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  frobDeg P (f ≫ g) = frobDeg P g * frobDeg P f

Remark 1.1.1, page 21: deg_Fr(φ ∘ ψ) = deg_Fr(φ) · deg_Fr(ψ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDeg_identitytheorem

theorem frobDeg_identity (X : C) : frobDeg P (𝟙 X) = 1

An identity has Frobenius degree 1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDiv_identitytheorem

theorem frobDiv_identity (X : C) : frobDiv P (𝟙 X) = 0

An identity has zero divisor 0.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobBase_identitytheorem

theorem frobBase_identity (X : C) : frobBase P (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (frobObj P X)

The base of an identity is an identity.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.elemFrobIdentityFunctordef

def elemFrobIdentityFunctor (Φ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommMonCat.{w}) :
    @FrobFunctor D _ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) Φ :=
  @Functor.id (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ)

𝔽_Φ itself, through its identity functor, as a functor to 𝔽_Φ; the notions of Definitions 1.2 and 1.3 thus apply to morphisms of 𝔽_Φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDeg_elemFrobIdentityFunctortheorem

theorem frobDeg_elemFrobIdentityFunctor {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) :
  @frobDeg D _ Φ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) (elemFrobIdentityFunctor Φ) A B φ =
    elemDeg φ

For 𝔽_Φ through its identity functor, deg_Fr is the third component of the triple.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDiv_elemFrobIdentityFunctortheorem

theorem frobDiv_elemFrobIdentityFunctor {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) :
  @frobDiv D _ Φ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) (elemFrobIdentityFunctor Φ) A B φ =
    elemDiv φ

For 𝔽_Φ through its identity functor, Div is the second component of the triple.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobBase_elemFrobIdentityFunctortheorem

theorem frobBase_elemFrobIdentityFunctor {A B : D} (φ : ElemFrobHom Φ A B) :
  @frobBase D _ Φ (ElemFrobObj Φ) (elemFrobCategory Φ) (elemFrobIdentityFunctor Φ) A B φ =
    elemBase φ

For 𝔽_Φ through its identity functor, Base is the first component of the triple.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsLinearMordef

def IsLinearMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := frobDeg P f = 1

Definition 1.2 (i): f is linear if deg_Fr(f) = 1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsIsometricMordef

def IsIsometricMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := frobDiv P f = 0

Definition 1.2 (i): f is isometric (an isometry) if Div(f) = 0.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.AreMetricallyEquivalentdef

def AreMetricallyEquivalent {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := frobDiv P f = frobDiv P g

Definition 1.2 (i): co-objective f, g are metrically equivalent if Div(f) = Div(g).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsBaseIsoMordef

def IsBaseIsoMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsIso (frobBase P f)

Definition 1.2 (ii): f is a base-isomorphism if Base(f) is an isomorphism of D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsBaseFSMMordef

def IsBaseFSMMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsFSMMorphism (frobBase P f)

Definition 1.2 (ii): f is a base-FSM-morphism if Base(f) is an FSM-morphism of D.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.AreBaseIsomorphicdef

def AreBaseIsomorphic (X Y : C) : Prop := Nonempty (frobObj P X ≅ frobObj P Y)

Definition 1.2 (ii): two objects are base-isomorphic if their images in D are isomorphic.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPullBackMordef

def IsPullBackMor {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : C, Function.Bijective fun g : T ⟶ A =>
    (⟨(g ≫ f, frobBase P g), by simp only [frobBase_compose]⟩ :
      {p : (T ⟶ B) × (frobObj P T ⟶ frobObj P A) // frobBase P p.1 = p.2 ≫ frobBase P f})

Definition 1.2 (ii): f : A → B is a pull-back morphism if the natural transformation Hom_C(-, A) → Hom_C(-, B) ×_{Hom_D(-, B_D)|_C} Hom_D(-, A_D)|_C induced by f is an isomorphism. Stated pointwise: for every object T of C, the map sending g : T → A to the pair (f ∘ g, Base(g)) is a bijection onto the pairs (h, k) with Base(h) = Base(f) ∘ k.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.AreBaseEquivalentdef

def AreBaseEquivalent {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := frobBase P f = frobBase P g

Definition 1.2 (ii): co-objective f, g are base-equivalent if Base(f) = Base(g).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.AreDivEquivalentdef

def AreDivEquivalent {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  Φ.map (frobBase P f).op = Φ.map (frobBase P g).op

Definition 1.2 (ii): co-objective f, g are Div-equivalent if Φ(f) = Φ(g), read as equality of the induced morphisms Φ(Base(f)), Φ(Base(g)) : Φ(Y_D) → Φ(X_D).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsBaseIdentityEndodef

def IsBaseIdentityEndo {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : Prop := AreBaseEquivalent P f (𝟙 X)

Definition 1.2 (ii): a base-identity endomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsDivIdentityEndodef

def IsDivIdentityEndo {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : Prop := AreDivEquivalent P f (𝟙 X)

Definition 1.2 (ii): a Div-identity endomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.unitTriangleEndosdef

def unitTriangleEndos (X : C) : Set (X ⟶ X) :=
  {f | IsBaseIdentityEndo P f ∧ IsLinearMor P f}

Definition 1.2 (ii): O^▷(X) ⊆ End_C(X), the base-identity linear endomorphisms.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.unitTimesAutosdef

def unitTimesAutos (X : C) : Set (X ⟶ X) :=
  {f | f ∈ unitTriangleEndos P X ∧ IsIso f}

Definition 1.2 (ii): O^×(X) ⊆ Aut_C(X), the base-identity linear automorphisms (as the endomorphisms in O^▷(X) that are isomorphisms).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPreStepdef

def IsPreStep {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsLinearMor P f ∧ IsBaseIsoMor P f

Definition 1.2 (iii): a pre-step is a linear base-isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsStepMordef

def IsStepMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsPreStep P f ∧ ¬ IsIso f

Definition 1.2 (iii): a step is a pre-step that is not an isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPrimaryPreStepdef

def IsPrimaryPreStep {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  IsPreStep P f ∧ IsPrimaryElem (frobDiv P f)

Definition 1.2 (iii): a primary pre-step: a pre-step whose zero divisor is a primary element of Φ(X).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsCoAngulardef

def IsCoAngular {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B) : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : C) (γ : A ⟶ X) (β : X ⟶ Y) (α : Y ⟶ B), γ ≫ β ≫ α = φ →
    IsLinearMor P α → IsIsometricMor P β → IsPreStep P β →
      (IsBaseIsoMor P α ∨ IsBaseIsoMor P γ) → IsIso β

Definition 1.2 (iii): φ is co-angular if for every factorization φ = α ∘ β ∘ γ with α linear, β an isometric pre-step, and α or γ a base-isomorphism, β is an isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsLBInvertibledef

def IsLBInvertible {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsCoAngular P f ∧ IsIsometricMor P f

Definition 1.2 (iii): LB-invertible: co-angular and isometric.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsFrobeniusTypeMordef

def IsFrobeniusTypeMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := IsLBInvertible P f ∧ IsBaseIsoMor P f

Definition 1.2 (iii): a morphism of Frobenius type: an LB-invertible base-isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsPrimeFrobeniusMordef

def IsPrimeFrobeniusMor {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  IsFrobeniusTypeMor P f ∧ (frobDeg P f : ℕ).Prime

Definition 1.2 (iii): a prime-Frobenius morphism: of Frobenius type with prime Frobenius degree.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsFrobeniusAmpleObjdef

def IsFrobeniusAmpleObj (X : C) : Prop := ∀ n : ℕ+, ∃ f : X ⟶ X, frobDeg P f = n

Definition 1.2 (iv): a Frobenius-ample object admits an endomorphism of every Frobenius degree n ∈ ℕ≥1.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsFrobeniusTrivialObjdef

def IsFrobeniusTrivialObj (X : C) : Prop :=
  ∃ ζ : ℕ+ →* End X, (∀ n, frobDeg P ((ζ n).asHom) = n) ∧
    ∀ n, IsBaseIdentityEndo P ((ζ n).asHom) ∧
      IsFrobeniusTypeMor P ((ζ n).asHom)

Definition 1.2 (iv): a Frobenius-trivial object X admits a monoid homomorphism ζ : ℕ≥1 → End_C(X) with (a) deg_Fr ∘ ζ = id and (b) every ζ(n) a base-identity endomorphism of Frobenius type. (ℕ≥1 is commutative, so the composition convention of End X does not matter.)

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsIsotropicObjdef

def IsIsotropicObj (X : C) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsIsometricMor P f → IsPreStep P f → IsIso f

Definition 1.2 (iv): an isotropic object: every isometric pre-step out of it is an isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsIsotropicHulldef

def IsIsotropicHull {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B) : Prop :=
  IsIsometricMor P φ ∧ IsPreStep P φ ∧ IsIsotropicObj P B ∧
    ∀ (E : C) (γ : A ⟶ E), IsIsotropicObj P E → ∃! β : B ⟶ E, φ ≫ β = γ

Definition 1.2 (iv): φ : A → B is an isotropic hull of A if φ is an isometric pre-step, B is isotropic, and every γ : A → E with E isotropic factors uniquely as γ = β ∘ φ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsLinearMor.composetheorem

theorem IsLinearMor.compose {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (hf : IsLinearMor P f)
  (hg : IsLinearMor P g) : IsLinearMor P (f ≫ g)

Linear morphisms are closed under composition (from Remark 1.1.1).

  (hg : IsPreStep P g) : IsPreStep P (f ≫ g)

Pre-steps are closed under composition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.isPreStep_identitytheorem

theorem isPreStep_identity (X : C) : IsPreStep P (𝟙 X) ∧ IsIsometricMor P (𝟙 X)

Identities are pre-steps and isometric.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.frobDeg_powtheorem

theorem frobDeg_pow {X : C} (f : End X) (n : ℕ) :
  frobDeg P (f ^ n).asHom = frobDeg P f.asHom ^ n

The Frobenius degree of the n-fold composite of an endomorphism f is deg_Fr(f)^n.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsBaseIdentityEndo.isDivIdentityEndotheorem

theorem IsBaseIdentityEndo.isDivIdentityEndo {X : C} {f : X ⟶ X}
  (h : IsBaseIdentityEndo P f) : IsDivIdentityEndo P f

Remark 1.2.1, page 24: a base-identity endomorphism is a Div-identity endomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIAdef

def FrobCondIA : Prop :=
  ∀ X : D, ∃ A : C, IsFrobeniusTrivialObj P A ∧ Nonempty (frobObj P A ≅ X)

Definition 1.3 (i) (a): every isomorphism class of D is the image of the isomorphism class of a Frobenius-trivial object of C.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIBdef

def FrobCondIB : Prop :=
  ∀ (A B : C) (α : frobObj P A ≅ frobObj P B), ∃ (E : C) (φ : E ⟶ A) (ψ : E ⟶ B),
    IsPreStep P φ ∧ IsPreStep P ψ ∧ frobBase P φ ≫ α.hom = frobBase P ψ

Definition 1.3 (i) (b): for every isomorphism α : A_D ≅ B_D there are pre-steps φ : E → A, ψ : E → B with α = Base(ψ) ∘ Base(φ)⁻¹, stated without the inverse as α ∘ Base(φ) = Base(ψ).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIIdef

def FrobCondII : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : C) (n : ℕ+), ∃ (B : C) (φ : A ⟶ B), IsFrobeniusTypeMor P φ ∧ frobDeg P φ = n ∧
    ∀ (E : C) (ψ : A ⟶ E), IsFrobeniusTypeMor P ψ → frobDeg P ψ = n →
      ∃ β : B ≅ E, φ ≫ β.hom = ψ

Definition 1.3 (ii): for every A and n ∈ ℕ≥1 there is a morphism of Frobenius type φ : A → B of degree n, and every other ψ : A → E of Frobenius type and degree n is β ∘ φ for an isomorphism β : B ≅ E.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIIIAdef

def FrobCondIIIA : Prop :=
  ∀ {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), IsCoAngular P f → IsCoAngular P g →
    IsCoAngular P (f ≫ g)

Definition 1.3 (iii) (a): co-angular morphisms are closed under composition.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIIIBdef

def FrobCondIIIB : Prop :=
  ∀ {A' A : C} (f : A' ⟶ A), IsCoAngular P f → IsPreStep P f → ∀ g : A' ⟶ A, IsCoAngular P g

Definition 1.3 (iii) (b): if A' → A is a co-angular pre-step, then every morphism A' → A is co-angular.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.IsInducedUnitBijectiondef

def IsInducedUnitBijection {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (e : unitTriangleEndos P A ≃ unitTriangleEndos P B) : Prop :=
  (∀ α : unitTriangleEndos P A, φ ≫ (e α).1 = α.1 ≫ φ) ∧
    ∀ α α' α'' : unitTriangleEndos P A, α.1 ≫ α'.1 = α''.1 →
      (e α).1 ≫ (e α').1 = (e α'').1

A bijection e : O^▷(A) ≅ O^▷(B) is induced by φ : A → B (Definition 1.3 (iii) (c)) if it is multiplicative and e(α) ∘ φ = φ ∘ α for every α ∈ O^▷(A).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIIICdef

def FrobCondIIIC : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B), IsCoAngular P φ → IsPreStep P φ →
    (∃ e, IsInducedUnitBijection P φ e) ∧
      ∀ (φ' : A ⟶ B), IsCoAngular P φ' → IsPreStep P φ' → AreBaseEquivalent P φ φ' →
        ∀ e e', IsInducedUnitBijection P φ e → IsInducedUnitBijection P φ' e' → e = e'

Definition 1.3 (iii) (c): every co-angular pre-step φ : A → B induces a bijection of monoids O^▷(A) ≅ O^▷(B), and the induced bijection depends only on Base(φ). The bracketed uniqueness of the page is included (take φ' = φ); it holds automatically when C is totally epimorphic.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIVAdef

def FrobCondIVA : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B),
    (∃ (X Y : C) (γ : A ⟶ X) (β : X ⟶ Y) (α : Y ⟶ B), γ ≫ β ≫ α = φ ∧
      IsPullBackMor P α ∧ IsPreStep P β ∧ IsFrobeniusTypeMor P γ) ∧
    ∀ (X Y X' Y' : C) (γ : A ⟶ X) (β : X ⟶ Y) (α : Y ⟶ B) (γ' : A ⟶ X') (β' : X' ⟶ Y')
      (α' : Y' ⟶ B),
      γ ≫ β ≫ α = φ → IsPullBackMor P α → IsPreStep P β → IsFrobeniusTypeMor P γ →
      γ' ≫ β' ≫ α' = φ → IsPullBackMor P α' → IsPreStep P β' → IsFrobeniusTypeMor P γ' →
      ∃ (δ : Y' ≅ Y) (ε : X' ≅ X), α' = δ.hom ≫ α ∧ β' = ε.hom ≫ β ≫ δ.inv ∧
        γ' = γ ≫ ε.inv

Definition 1.3 (iv) (a): every φ : A → B factors as φ = α ∘ β ∘ γ with α a pull-back morphism, β a pre-step and γ of Frobenius type, uniquely up to replacing (α, β, γ) by (α ∘ δ, δ⁻¹ ∘ β ∘ ε, ε⁻¹ ∘ γ) for isomorphisms δ, ε.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondIVBdef

def FrobCondIVB : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B), IsPullBackMor P f → IsLBInvertible P f ∧ IsLinearMor P f

Definition 1.3 (iv) (b): every pull-back morphism is LB-invertible and linear.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVAdef

def FrobCondVA : Prop := ∀ {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B), IsPreStep P f → Mono f

Definition 1.3 (v) (a): every pre-step is a monomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.HasUniqueTwoFactorizationdef

def HasUniqueTwoFactorization {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B) (Sα Sβ : ∀ {X Y : C}, (X ⟶ Y) → Prop) :
    Prop :=
  (∃ (X : C) (β : A ⟶ X) (α : X ⟶ B), β ≫ α = φ ∧ Sα α ∧ Sβ β) ∧
    ∀ (X X' : C) (β : A ⟶ X) (α : X ⟶ B) (β' : A ⟶ X') (α' : X' ⟶ B),
      β ≫ α = φ → Sα α → Sβ β → β' ≫ α' = φ → Sα α' → Sβ β' →
        ∃ γ : X' ≅ X, α' = γ.hom ≫ α ∧ β' = β ≫ γ.inv

The factorization pattern of Definition 1.3 (v) (b) and (c): φ = α ∘ β with α in the class Sα and β in the class Sβ, unique up to replacing (α, β) by (α ∘ γ, γ⁻¹ ∘ β) for an isomorphism γ.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVBdef

def FrobCondVB : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B), IsPreStep P φ →
    HasUniqueTwoFactorization φ (fun f => IsIsometricMor P f ∧ IsPreStep P f)
      (fun f => IsCoAngular P f ∧ IsPreStep P f)

Definition 1.3 (v) (b): every pre-step factors as an isometric pre-step after a co-angular pre-step, uniquely up to isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVCdef

def FrobCondVC : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (φ : A ⟶ B), IsPreStep P φ →
    HasUniqueTwoFactorization φ (fun f => IsCoAngular P f ∧ IsPreStep P f)
      (fun f => IsIsometricMor P f ∧ IsPreStep P f)

Definition 1.3 (v) (c): every pre-step factors as a co-angular pre-step after an isometric pre-step, uniquely up to isomorphism.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVIdef

def FrobCondVI : Prop :=
  ∀ {A B : C} (φ ψ : A ⟶ B), AreBaseEquivalent P φ ψ → AreMetricallyEquivalent P φ ψ →
    IsCoAngular P φ → IsPreStep P φ → IsCoAngular P ψ → IsPreStep P ψ →
      ∃ α ∈ unitTimesAutos P B, φ = ψ ≫ α

Definition 1.3 (vi): base-equivalent, metrically equivalent co-angular pre-steps φ, ψ : A → B satisfy φ = α ∘ ψ for some α ∈ O^×(B).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVIIAdef

def FrobCondVIIA : Prop := ∀ A : C, ∃ (B : C) (φ : A ⟶ B), IsIsotropicHull P φ

Definition 1.3 (vii) (a): every object has an isotropic hull.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.FrobCondVIIBdef

def FrobCondVIIB : Prop :=
  ∀ {A E : C} (_f : A ⟶ E), IsIsotropicObj P A → IsIsotropicObj P E

Definition 1.3 (vii) (b): the codomain of a morphism out of an isotropic object is isotropic.

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.PartialFrobenioidConditionsdef

def PartialFrobenioidConditions : Prop :=
  IsPreFrobenioidStructure P ∧ FrobCondIA P ∧ FrobCondIB P ∧ FrobCondII P ∧
    FrobCondIIIA P ∧ FrobCondIIIB P ∧ FrobCondIIIC P ∧ FrobCondIVA P ∧ FrobCondIVB P ∧
    FrobCondVA P ∧ FrobCondVB P ∧ FrobCondVC P ∧ FrobCondVI P ∧ FrobCondVIIA P ∧
    FrobCondVIIB P

The conditions of Definition 1.3 (pages 24 and 25) that are stated in this file, together with the pre-Frobenioid hypotheses of Definition 1.1 (iv). This is not the definition of a Frobenioid: clauses (i) (c) and (iii) (d) are omitted (see the module docstring). Every clause that is included has a verified example: all fifteen conjuncts hold for the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_ℕ over Discrete PUnit (natPoint_partialFrobenioidConditions).

IUT.Prerequisites.Frobenioid.natPoint_partialFrobenioidConditionstheorem

    (ElemFrobObj natPointMonoid) (elemFrobCategory natPointMonoid) natPointFrobFunctor

PartialFrobenioidConditions holds for the elementary Frobenioid 𝔽_ℕ over Discrete PUnit with its identity functor, so the stated clauses are jointly satisfiable. Proposition 1.5 (i) (page 27) asserts that 𝔽_Φ, with the natural functor 𝔽_Φ → 𝔽_{Φ^char}, is a Frobenioid for a pre-divisorial monoid Φ on a connected, totally epimorphic category; here Φ is divisorial (sharp), so Φ^char = Φ and the natural functor is the identity.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog

IUT/Prerequisites/PadicLog.lean

The p-adic logarithm on ℚ_p and the log-shell of ℚ_p

Module documentation

Sources:

  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Definition 1.1, PDF pages 23 and 24 (rendered and read): for a nonarchimedean v, the pre-log-shell is the image under the p_v-adic logarithm of the Galois-invariant units, and the log-shell is the pre-log-shell multiplied by (p_v^*)⁻¹, with p_v^* = p_v for odd p_v and p_v^* = p_v ^ 2 for p_v = 2 (page 24, citing [AbsTopIII], Definition 5.4 (iii)).
  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Proposition 1.2 (v), PDF pages 31 and 32 (rendered and read): at nonarchimedean v the log-shell is compact, contains the invariants of the integers of the codomain, and contains the image of the invariant units.
  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.2 (i), PDF pages 10 and 11 (rendered and read; page 9, read, fixes the notation R_i, ord, p ^ λ of Proposition 1.1 used there): for a finite extension k_i of ℚ_p with ramification index e_i, p ^ (a_i) R_i ⊆ log_p (R_i^×) ⊆ p ^ (- b_i) R_i, with equalities when p > 2 and e_i ≤ p - 2; the proof cites [Kobl], page 81.

Pages read for this file: IUT III pages 23, 24, 31 and 32; IUT IV pages 9, 10 and 11. Pages checked against rendered images: the same.

This file is a prerequisite for log-shells over ℚ_p only. Finite extensions of ℚ_p, tensor products of rings of integers, and the Frobenioid-theoretic setting of IUT III are not treated here; the logarithm on a finite extension of ℚ_p is in IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Logarithm.lean. It does not formalize IUT III Definition 1.1, IUT III Proposition 1.2 or IUT IV Proposition 1.2; it proves, for the base field k = ℚ_p (so e = 1, R = ℤ_p), the facts about the logarithm on which they rest.

Contents
  • padicLogOnePlus p x = ∑_{n ≥ 1} (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n, which agrees with Mathlib's NormedSpace.log (1 + x) (padicLogOnePlus_eq_normedSpace_log) and converges for ‖x‖ < 1 (padicLogSeries_summable). Outside the open unit disc the value is a junk value.
  • ‖log (1 + x)‖ = ‖x‖ for ‖x‖ ≤ 1 / p* (padicLogOnePlus_norm_eq), that is ‖x‖ ≤ 1 / p for odd p and ‖x‖ ≤ 1 / 4 for p = 2.
  • The homomorphism property log ((1 + x) (1 + y)) = log (1 + x) + log (1 + y) on the whole open unit disc (padicLogOnePlus_add_add_mul), proved by re-expanding the series around x as a norm-summable double series and summing it in both orders.
  • The logarithm of a unit, padicLogUnit p u = (p - 1)⁻¹ log (u ^ (p - 1)), which agrees with log u on 1 + p ℤ_p (padicLogUnit_one_add), and its image log (ℤ_p^×) = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ 1 / p*} (padicLogUnit_range), that is p ℤ_p for odd p and 4 ℤ_2 for p = 2. Surjectivity is proved by the contraction mapping principle.
  • The log-shell padicLogShell p = (p*)⁻¹ · log (ℤ_p^×) and its computation padicLogShell p = ℤ_p (padicLogShell_eq_range_coe), with the three properties of IUT III Proposition 1.2 (v) at nonarchimedean v in this case: compactness (padicLogShell_isCompact), ℤ_p ⊆ I (padicInt_subset_padicLogShell) and log (ℤ_p^×) ⊆ I (padicLogUnit_range_subset_padicLogShell).
Interpretation choices, recorded
  • The "Galois-invariant units" of IUT III page 24 are taken to be ℤ_p^× for the base field ℚ_p (the invariants of the units of the ring of integers of an algebraic closure under the absolute Galois group of ℚ_p); this identification is not formalized here.
  • The papers write log_p without fixing the extension to all units on the pages read. The extension (p - 1)⁻¹ log (u ^ (p - 1)) used here is the standard one; for p = 2 it is log u itself. Since log is a homomorphism on 1 + p ℤ_p (padicLogOnePlus_add_add_mul), this extension is a homomorphism on ℤ_p^× (padicLogUnit_mul), and it is the unique homomorphic extension into the torsion-free group ℚ_p; that uniqueness statement is not formalized here.
  • For k = ℚ_p, the constants of IUT IV Proposition 1.2 are a = 1, b = -1 for p > 2 and a = 2, b = 0 for p = 2 (computed from the displays on page 10). The theorem padicLogUnit_range gives the equality log (ℤ_p^×) = p ℤ_p asserted there for p > 2 and, for p = 2, the sharper log (ℤ_2^×) = 4 ℤ_2, which implies the two inclusions 4 ℤ_2 ⊆ log (ℤ_2^×) ⊆ ℤ_2.
  • Some secondary sources write the log-shell as (2p)⁻¹ log (O_k^×). For p = 2 this is (p*)⁻¹; for odd p, 2p and p* = p differ by the unit 2, so the set is the same. Only the (p*)⁻¹ form of page 24 is defined; padicLogShell_eq_two_mul proves the two forms equal.
Public declarations
variable {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime]

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogSeriesdef

noncomputable def padicLogSeries (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (x : ℚ_[p]) (n : ℕ) : ℚ_[p] :=
  (-1) ^ (n + 1) / n * x ^ n

The n-th term (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n of the logarithm series; the 0-th term is 0 because 1 / 0 = 0.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogOnePlusdef

noncomputable def padicLogOnePlus (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (x : ℚ_[p]) : ℚ_[p] :=
  ∑' n : ℕ, padicLogSeries p x n

log (1 + x) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n; meaningful for ‖x‖ < 1, where the series converges (padicLogSeries_summable), and a junk value otherwise.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogOnePlus_eq_normedSpace_logtheorem

theorem padicLogOnePlus_eq_normedSpace_log (x : ℚ_[p]) :
  padicLogOnePlus p x = NormedSpace.log (1 + x)

Agreement with Mathlib's NormedSpace.log.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLog_exists_norm_inv_natCasttheorem

theorem padicLog_exists_norm_inv_natCast {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
  ∃ e : ℕ, p ^ e ∣ n ∧ ‖((n : ℚ_[p]))⁻¹‖ = (p : ℝ) ^ e

For n ≠ 0, ‖1 / n‖ = p ^ e for some e with p ^ e ∣ n.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLog_norm_inv_natCast_letheorem

‖1 / n‖ ≤ n in ℚ_p.

theorem padicLogSeries_norm_le (x : ℚ_[p]) (n : ℕ) :
  ‖padicLogSeries p x n‖ ≤ n * ‖x‖ ^ n

‖x ^ n / n‖ ≤ n ‖x‖ ^ n.

The logarithm series converges on the open unit disc.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogOnePlus_zerotheorem

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogPStardef

def padicLogPStar (p : ℕ) : ℕ := if p = 2 then p ^ 2 else p

p* of IUT III page 24: p for odd p and p ^ 2 = 4 for p = 2.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLog_aux_lt_three_powtheorem

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLog_pow_mul_le_pStar_powtheorem

Key arithmetic: for n ≥ 2 and p ^ e ∣ n, p ^ e * p ≤ (p*) ^ (n - 1).

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogSeries_norm_le_of_two_letheorem

theorem padicLogSeries_norm_le_of_two_le {x : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ (padicLogPStar p : ℝ)⁻¹)

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogOnePlus_eq_add_tailtheorem

theorem padicLogOnePlus_eq_add_tail {x : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) :
  padicLogOnePlus p x = x + ∑' n : ℕ, padicLogSeries p x (n + 2)

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogOnePlus_norm_eqtheorem

theorem padicLogOnePlus_norm_eq {x : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ (padicLogPStar p : ℝ)⁻¹) :

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogDoubledef

noncomputable def padicLogDouble (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (x w : ℚ_[p]) (nk : ℕ × ℕ) : ℚ_[p] :=
  (-1) ^ (nk.1 + 1) / nk.1 * (nk.1.choose nk.2) * x ^ (nk.1 - nk.2) * w ^ nk.2

The double family used to re-expand log (1 + x + w) around x.

theorem padicLogDouble_summable {x w : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) (hw : ‖w‖ < 1) :
  Summable (padicLogDouble p x w)

The double family is norm-summable for ‖x‖, ‖w‖ < 1.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogDouble_hasSum_fsttheorem

theorem padicLogDouble_hasSum_fst (x w : ℚ_[p]) (n : ℕ) :
  HasSum (fun k => padicLogDouble p x w (n, k)) (padicLogSeries p (x + w) n)

Summing the double family over k first gives the series of log (1 + (x + w)).

theorem padicLogDouble_hasSum_snd_succ {x : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) (w : ℚ_[p]) (j : ℕ) :
  HasSum (fun n => padicLogDouble p x w (n, j + 1))
    ((-1) ^ (j + 2) / (j + 1 : ℕ) * (w / (1 + x)) ^ (j + 1))

  padicLogOnePlus p (x + y + x * y) = padicLogOnePlus p x + padicLogOnePlus p y

theorem padicLogOnePlus_sub_sub_norm_le {a b : ℚ_[p]} (ha : ‖a‖ ≤ (padicLogPStar p : ℝ)⁻¹)

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogUnitdef

noncomputable def padicLogUnit (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (u : ℚ_[p]) : ℚ_[p] :=
  ((p - 1 : ℕ) : ℚ_[p])⁻¹ * padicLogOnePlus p (u ^ (p - 1) - 1)

The p-adic logarithm of a unit u of ℤ_p, as (p - 1)⁻¹ log (u ^ (p - 1)), where log is the series padicLogOnePlus at u ^ (p - 1) - 1. Meaningful for ‖u‖ = 1.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogUnit_one_addtheorem

theorem padicLogUnit_one_add {x : ℚ_[p]} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) :
  padicLogUnit p (1 + x) = padicLogOnePlus p x

On 1 + x with ‖x‖ < 1, the logarithm of units agrees with the series log (1 + x).

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogShelldef

noncomputable def padicLogShell (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Set ℚ_[p] :=
  (fun z => ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℚ_[p])⁻¹ * z) ''
    Set.range (fun u : ℤ_[p]ˣ => padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p]))

The log-shell of ℚ_p in the sense of IUT III Definition 1.1, page 24, for the base field ℚ_p: (p*)⁻¹ · log (ℤ_p^×).

  (fun z => c⁻¹ * z) '' Set.range (fun u : ℤ_[p]ˣ => padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p])) =
    {y : ℚ_[p] | ‖y‖ ≤ 1}

The log-shell of ℚ_p is the closed unit ball, that is ℤ_p.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume

IUT/Prerequisites/PadicVolume.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm, IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Comparison

Haar measure and normalized log-volume on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces

Module documentation

Sources:

  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.4 (i), page 13: the log-volumes of [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7, on finite extensions of ℚ_p "may be suitably normalized [i.e., by dividing by the degree of the finite extension] so as to yield a notion of log-volume μ^log(−) defined on compact open subsets of finite extensions of ℚ_p contained in ℚ̄_p, valued in ℝ, and normalized so that μ^log(R_i) = 0, μ^log(p · R_i) = −log(p)"; on tensor products, which "decompose, naturally, as direct sums of finitely many finite extensions of ℚ_p", one obtains a log-volume "defined on compact open subsets of such tensor products, valued in ℝ, and normalized so that μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0, μ^log(p · (R_E)^∼) = −log(p)". Proposition 1.4 (ii) to (iv), pages 13 and 14, and the proof on page 14 (which uses μ^log(R_I) ≤ μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0 and the additivity of μ^log over tensor products).
  • IUT IV, Proposition 1.1, page 9 (R_E = ⊗_{i ∈ E} R_i over ℤ_p, and (−)^∼ the normalization of the reduced ring in its ring of fractions), and Proposition 1.2, pages 10 and 11 (the constants a_i, b_i and the inclusions (i) to (iv)).
  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Proposition 3.9 (i), pages 115 and 116: the p_v-adic log-volume on each direct summand, normalized so that the integral structures have log-volume zero and "multiplication of an element of 𝔐(−) by p_v corresponds to adding the quantity −log(p_v)" (the packet-normalization). Remark 3.1.1 (ii), (iii), pages 94 and 95: the normalized weights, and the warning that weighted sums of log-volumes do not in general arise as a positive multiple of the logarithm of a measure.

Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14; IUT III pages 94, 95, 115 and 116. Pages checked against rendered images: the same.

What is proved
  1. Scaling of Haar measure. For a finite-dimensional normed ℚ_p-vector space V of dimension d and any additive Haar measure μ on V: μ (c • A) = ‖c‖ ^ d · μ A for every c ≠ 0 in ℚ_p and every set A (padicVol_measure_smul). The proof computes the distributive Haar character of ℚ_p^× (MeasureTheory.distribHaarChar) on one box {x | ∀ i, ‖x_i‖ ≤ 1} in coordinates: the box is the disjoint union of p ^ d translates of p times itself (padicVolBox_measure_one).
  2. Normalized log-volume. padicMuLog p μ Λ A = log (μ A / μ Λ) / d, real valued, normalized at a set Λ. It does not depend on the Haar measure (padicMuLog_haar_indep), nor on a change of coordinates by a continuous linear automorphism (padicMuLog_image_equiv). Laws: μ^log(Λ) = 0 (padicMuLog_self), translation invariance (padicMuLog_vadd), monotonicity (padicMuLog_mono), μ^log(c • A) = μ^log(A) + log ‖c‖ (padicMuLog_smul), hence μ^log(p ^ n • A) = μ^log(A) − n log p (padicMuLog_p_zpow_smul). The EReal form padicMuLogE is monotone on all sets (padicMuLogE_mono), agrees with padicMuLog on sets of positive finite measure (padicMuLogE_eq), and is a region log-volume for the interface of IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Comparison (padicRegionComparison).
  3. *A finite extension K of ℚ_p* (a normed field that is a finite-dimensional normed ℚ_p-algebra; R is the closed unit ball, as in IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm): μ^log(R) = 0 and μ^log(p · R) = −log p with the normalization of IUT IV page 13 (padicMuLog_unitBall, padicMuLog_p_smul_unitBall); μ (x • A) = ‖x‖ ^ d · μ A for x ∈ K^× with ‖x‖ ^ m = p ^ (−n) for some m ≥ 1 (padicVol_field_measure_smul); for a uniformizer π (‖π‖ ^ e = 1 / p), the closed ball of radius ‖π‖ ^ k has log-volume −(k / e) log p (padicMuLog_ball_uniformizer). From IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i) as proved in Logarithm.lean: −a · log p ≤ μ^log(log_p(R^×)) ≤ b · log p (padicMuLog_logUnit_bounds) and the corresponding bounds for the log-shell I = (p*)⁻¹ · log_p(R^×), shifted by log p* (padicMuLog_logShell_bounds).
  4. Tensor packets. For a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space W without topology (for example K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂), padicPacketMuLog is the normalized log-volume computed in the coordinates of Module.finBasis; by padicMuLog_image_equiv any other linear coordinates give the same value (padicPacketMuLog_coord_indep). Laws: padicPacketMuLog_self, padicPacketMuLog_p_zpow_smul (μ^log(p ^ n • A) = μ^log(A) − n log p for any Λ, A of positive finite measure), and padicVol_finrank_tensor (dim (K₁ ⊗ K₂) = dim K₁ · dim K₂, the degree by which the log-volume of the packet is divided). For two finite extensions the lattice R_E (padicPacketIntegers, the additive span of x ⊗ y with x, y integral over ℤ_p) and (R_E)^∼ (padicPacketNormalization, the elements of K₁ ⊗ K₂ integral over ℤ_p) are defined, and R_E ⊆ (R_E)^∼ is proved (padicPacketIntegers_subset).
  5. *Nonvacuity on ℚ_p* (d = 1): for the Haar measure normalized on ℤ_p, μ(ℤ_p) = 1 (padicVol_padic_unitBall), μ(p ^ n ℤ_p) = p ^ (−n) (padicVol_padic_p_zpow), the log-shell of ℚ_p of IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog has measure 1 (padicVol_padicLogShell) and normalized log-volume 0 (padicMuLog_padicLogShell), and the hypotheses hval, hπ of step 3 hold together for K = ℚ_p, e = 1, π = p (padicMuLog_logUnit_bounds_padic).
Interpretation choices
  • The normalization. IUT IV page 13 fixes μ^log on a finite extension k_i by the two values μ^log(R_i) = 0 and μ^log(p · R_i) = −log p, "dividing by the degree". With μ a Haar measure on k_i and d = [k_i : ℚ_p], the function log (μ A / μ R_i) / d has both values (padicMuLog_unitBall, padicMuLog_p_smul_unitBall); that it is the only function of the form α log μ + β with them is elementary and not formalized. The paper's μ^log is the log-volume of [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7, which is not read here; that it is of this form is an interpretation, not a quotation.
  • The ring of integers. As in Logarithm.lean, R_i is modeled by the closed unit ball of a norm extending the p-adic norm, p ^ λ · R_i by the closed ball of radius p ^ (−λ), and the ramification index by a positive integer e with ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ 1 / p on the open unit disc (hval). A uniformizer is an element π with ‖π‖ ^ e = 1 / p (hπ). Both are standing properties of a finite extension with its ramification index, not claims of the papers; their derivation from integralClosure ℤ_p k_i and Ideal.ramificationIdx is not formalized.
  • Real values. padicMuLog is real valued with Lean's Real.log 0 = 0; it is meaningful on sets of positive finite measure (the compact open sets of page 13), and every law below that needs it assumes it. The value padicMuLog_self holds for every Λ, so it carries content only when 0 < μ Λ < ∞.
  • Tensor packets. Page 13 obtains the log-volume on ⊗ k_i from the decomposition into a direct sum of fields without saying how the summands are weighted. Here the packet log-volume is log (μ A / μ Λ) / D for one Haar measure μ on the D-dimensional space ⊗ k_i, which has the two normalizing values of page 13 whenever 0 < μ Λ < ∞. On a product region with respect to the decomposition it should be the sum of the log-volumes of the factors weighted by [K_j : ℚ_p] / D (not formalized; the decomposition itself is not formalized); other weightings are possible (IUT III Remark 3.1.1 (iii), page 95), and this one is a choice.
  • *Normalization of R_E.* Page 9 defines (R_E)^∼ as the normalization of the reduced ring R_E in its ring of fractions. Here padicPacketNormalization is the set of elements of K₁ ⊗ K₂ integral over ℤ_p. The two agree because the ring of fractions of R_E is K₁ ⊗ K₂ and R_E is integral over ℤ_p; neither fact is formalized.
Not proved
  • That padicPacketNormalization (that is (R_E)^∼) is compact and open in K₁ ⊗ K₂, so has positive finite Haar measure; without it the normalization μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0, μ^log(p · (R_E)^∼) = −log p of page 13 is only an instance of the general laws for sets of positive finite measure. Its finiteness needs that K₁ ⊗ K₂ is reduced (a product of fields), its openness that it contains a lattice.
  • The general index formula μ(Λ') = [Λ : Λ']⁻¹ μ(Λ) for sublattices; only the case Λ' = p Λ of a coordinate box is proved (padicVolBox_measure_one).
  • IUT IV Proposition 1.1 (p ^ 𝔡 · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ R_I), hence Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (iv).
  • The additivity used on page 14, μ^log(⊗ A_i) = ∑ μ^log(A_i) + μ^log(R_I): it needs the index formula for tensor products of lattices, or the determinant formula for Haar measure over ℚ_p (Mathlib has the latter only over ℝ).
  • IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (ii), the exact value −(1/e_i + m_i/(e_i f_i)) log p: it needs the residue field, the torsion of R_i^×, and Haar measure on the unit group. The bounds of padicMuLog_logUnit_bounds come from Proposition 1.2 (i) only and are weaker.
  • The identification of the closed unit ball with integralClosure ℤ_p k_i and of π, e with a uniformizer and the ramification index, and μ (x • A) = ‖x‖ ^ d μ A for every x ∈ K^× without the hypothesis on a power of ‖x‖.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume.padicVolBox_measure_onetheorem

theorem padicVolBox_measure_one :
  μ (padicVolBox p V 1) =
    (p : ENNReal) ^ Module.finrank ℚ_[p] V * μ (padicVolBox p V (p : ℝ)⁻¹)

The counting step. The unit box is the disjoint union of the p ^ d translates k + p · box (k ∈ {0, …, p - 1} ^ d in coordinates), so its measure is p ^ d times that of box (1 / p).

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume.padicVol_measure_smultheorem

theorem padicVol_measure_smul {c : ℚ_[p]} (hc : c ≠ 0) (A : Set V) :
  μ (c • A) = ((‖c‖₊ ^ Module.finrank ℚ_[p] V : NNReal) : ENNReal) * μ A

**Scaling of Haar measure by a scalar of ℚ_p.** For every additive Haar measure μ on a d-dimensional normed ℚ_p-vector space, every c ≠ 0 in ℚ_p and every set A, μ (c • A) = ‖c‖ ^ d · μ A.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume.padicMuLogdef

noncomputable def padicMuLog (Λ A : Set V) : ℝ :=
  Real.log ((μ A).toReal / (μ Λ).toReal) / (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] V : ℝ)

The normalized log-volume μ^log(A) = log (μ A / μ Λ) / d, d = dim_{ℚ_p} V, normalized at Λ: the normalization "by dividing by the degree" of IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (i), page 13. Real valued, with Lean's Real.log 0 = 0; it is meaningful when μ A and μ Λ are positive and finite.

The EReal form ENNReal.log ((μ A / μ Λ) ^ (1 / d)) of the normalized log-volume. It is defined and monotone on all sets (padicMuLogE_mono), with −∞ on null sets.

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume.padicVol_field_measure_smultheorem

theorem padicVol_field_measure_smul {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) {n : ℤ}

**Scaling of Haar measure by an element of K.** If x ≠ 0 and ‖x‖ ^ m = p ^ (−n) for some m ≥ 1 and n ∈ ℤ (true for every nonzero element of a finite extension of ℚ_p, whose value group is p ^ (ℤ / e); here a hypothesis on x), then μ (x • A) = ‖x‖ ^ d · μ A, d = [K : ℚ_p].

IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume.padicMuLog_field_smultheorem

theorem padicMuLog_field_smul {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) {n : ℤ}
