IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.PilotLogVolumesstructure

structure PilotLogVolumes where

The two numbers that the statement of Corollary 3.12 defines, with the two properties that the statement attributes to them by definition: the value set ℝ ∪ {+∞} of − |log(Θ)|, and |log(q)| > 0. Nothing here is constructed from initial Θ-data.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Conclusiondef

def Conclusion : Prop :=
  v.negLogTheta ≠ ⊤ ∧ ((-v.absLogQ : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ v.negLogTheta

The conclusion of Corollary 3.12: − |log(Θ)| ∈ ℝ and − |log(Θ)| ≥ − |log(q)|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.ConstantFormdef

def ConstantForm : Prop :=
  ∀ C : ℝ, v.negLogTheta ≤ ((C * v.absLogQ : ℝ) : EReal) → -1 ≤ C

The reformulation after "i.e." in the statement: C_Θ ≥ −1 for any real number C_Θ such that − |log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ · |log(q)|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.constantForm_of_conclusiontheorem

theorem constantForm_of_conclusion (h : Conclusion v) : ConstantForm v

The conclusion implies the "i.e." form.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.conclusion_of_constantFormtheorem

theorem conclusion_of_constantForm (hfin : v.negLogTheta ≠ ⊤) (h : ConstantForm v) :
  Conclusion v

When − |log(Θ)| is finite, the "i.e." form implies the inequality.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.constantForm_of_toptheorem

theorem constantForm_of_top (h : v.negLogTheta = ⊤) : ConstantForm v

The "i.e." form alone does not give finiteness: it holds when − |log(Θ)| = +∞, because then no real C_Θ satisfies its hypothesis. So the "i.e." of the statement reformulates the inequality, and the assertion − |log(Θ)| ∈ ℝ is a separate claim.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.conclusion_iff_constantFormtheorem

theorem conclusion_iff_constantForm (hfin : v.negLogTheta ≠ ⊤) :
  Conclusion v ↔ ConstantForm v

With finiteness assumed, the conclusion and the "i.e." form are equivalent.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.inequality_of_nonnegtheorem

theorem inequality_of_nonneg (h : 0 ≤ v.negLogTheta) :
  ((-v.absLogQ : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ v.negLogTheta

The reduction at the start of the proof: "we may assume without loss of generality that − |log(Θ)| < 0", because − |log(Θ)| ≥ 0 gives − |log(Θ)| ≥ 0 > − |log(q)|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.possibleLogVolumesdef

def possibleLogVolumes : Set ℝ := {lam | (lam : EReal) ≤ v.negLogTheta}

The subset ℝ_{≤ −|log(Θ)|} = {λ ∈ ℝ | λ ≤ − |log(Θ)|} of Step (xi-d).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.stepXIf_inclusion_iff_inequalitytheorem

theorem stepXIf_inclusion_iff_inequality :
  -v.absLogQ ∈ possibleLogVolumes v ↔ ((-v.absLogQ : ℝ) : EReal) ≤ v.negLogTheta

Step (xi-f) at the level of numbers. The proof ends: "The inclusion − |log(q)| ∈ ℝ_{≤ −|log(Θ)|}, hence also the inequality − |log(q)| ≤ − |log(Θ)|, then follows formally." The second step is indeed formal: the inclusion and the inequality are the same proposition, by unfolding the definition of the subset. Consequently every bit of mathematical content of Step (xi) lies in establishing the inclusion, that is, in Steps (xi-a) to (xi-e) and the first sentence of (xi-f). No formalization that keeps only the two real numbers can express those steps: stated about numbers alone, the premise of the last step is the conclusion. A non-circular formalization must model the multiradial representation itself, with the properties (IPL) and (SHE) of Remark 3.11.1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.thm1_10_final_of_cor312theorem

theorem thm1_10_final_of_cor312 {l d D E Q : ℝ} (hl : 7 ≤ l) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hD : 0 ≤ D)
  (hE : 0 ≤ E)
  (hbound : v.negLogTheta ≤ ((constant l d D E Q v.absLogQ * v.absLogQ : ℝ) : EReal))
  (hcor : Conclusion v) :
  1 / 6 * Q ≤ (1 + 20 * d / l) * D + 20 * E

Conditional derivation of the final inequality of IUT IV, Theorem 1.10. Hypotheses, each a statement about given real numbers: * hbound: − |log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ · |log(q)| for the constant C_Θ displayed in Theorem 1.10. This is the first assertion of Theorem 1.10 ("one may take the constant C_Θ to be ..."). * hcor: the conclusion of Corollary 3.12. * the side conditions 7 ≤ l, 1 ≤ d, 0 ≤ D, 0 ≤ E that the paper cites. Conclusion: (1/6)·log(𝔮) ≤ (1 + 20·d_mod/l)·(log 𝔡 + log 𝔣) + 20·(e*_mod·l + η_prm). The theorem is conditional. It does not show that the objects of the paper satisfy hbound or hcor; it shows that nothing else is used in passing from them to the final inequality.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.PacketHull

IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/PacketHull.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.VolumeBridge, IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado

IUT III, Remark 3.9.5 (i), (ii): the holomorphic hull on a finite product of p-adic fields

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Remark 3.9.5 (i), (ii), page 127 (the remark begins at the foot of page 126; (iii) and (iv) follow on page 128). Pages read for this file: 126, 127 and 128. Pages checked against rendered images: 126, 127 and 128.

What the page says

Remark 3.9.5 (i), page 127, in the situation of Proposition 3.9 (i): let U ⊆ ℐ^ℚ(−) be a subset that contains a relatively compact subset whose log-volume is finite (that is, > −∞). If U is relatively compact, its holomorphic hull is "the smallest subset of the form λ · 𝒪" that contains U, where 𝒪 is the integral structure and λ ∈ ℐ^ℚ(−) is an element each of whose components, relative to the decomposition of ℐ^ℚ(−) as a direct sum of fields, is nonzero. If U is not relatively compact, its holomorphic hull is ℐ^ℚ(−) itself. "One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined [under the conditions stated]." Remark 3.9.5 (ii) writes ℙ for the direct product regions, ℍ = {H ⊊ ℐ^ℚ(−) | H is a hull} (proper subsets), observes ℍ ⊆ ℙ, and characterizes the map φ : ℙ → ℍ by (P1), (P2), (P3) (IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.IsHullMap).

What this file is and is not

This file does not treat tensor packets. It works on a finite product V = Π s, L s of normed fields in place of the direct sum of fields of the page; the isomorphism of a tensor packet with such a product (IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.volBridge_tensor_equiv_pi for two factors) is not applied here, and the archimedean case is not treated. The integral structure is 𝒪 = {x | ∀ s, ‖x s‖ ≤ 1} (pktHullIntegers), the product of the closed unit balls; for a finite extension of ℚ_p with its spectral norm the closed unit ball is the ring of integers (pktHullIntegers_eq_pi_integralClosure).

  • pktHullPrincipal c = c • 𝒪 for c : Π s, (L s)ˣ (the sets λ · 𝒪), equal to the box {x | ∀ s, ‖x s‖ ≤ ‖c s‖} (pktHull_mem_principal); pktHullForms is the family of them.
  • pktHull U is ⋂ {H ∈ pktHullForms | U ⊆ H} when closure U is compact, and univ otherwise. Where the page's smallest set exists, it is this intersection; the definition does not presuppose that it exists.
  • Existence of the smallest set (pktHull_isLeast): under a discreteness hypothesis on the value group (pktHullDiscrete, proved for every finite extension of ℚ_p with its spectral norm in pktHullDiscrete_spectral and for ℚ_p in pktHullDiscrete_padic), for every relatively compact U none of whose coordinate projections is zero (pktHullNondeg), pktHull U is the least set of the form λ · 𝒪 containing U, with λ_s a point of the projection of U of largest norm (pktHull_eq_principal). The page's condition (a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume) implies the nondegeneracy: a set of positive product measure is not contained in a coordinate hyperplane (pktHullNondeg_of_measure). For finite extensions of ℚ_p with Haar measure the two together give pktHull_isLeast_spectral.
  • Excluded cases. For U that is not relatively compact, pktHull U = univ, by definition, as on the page; in particular for every unbounded U (pktHull_of_not_isBounded), and relatively compact is the same as bounded for finite extensions of ℚ_p (pktHull_relCompact_iff). For a bounded U with a zero coordinate projection, which the page's condition excludes, there may be no smallest set: for U = {0} there is none (pktHull_not_exists_isLeast_zero). The value of pktHull there is a convention.
  • Properties (for all subsets, unless stated): U ⊆ pktHull U (pktHull_extensive), monotone (pktHull_mono), idempotent for proper discretely valued factors (pktHull_idem), and pktHull (g • U) = g • pktHull U for every unit g of V, that is, every element of the product of the groups L_s^× (pktHull_smul). With 𝓟 the relatively compact sets with nonzero projections and 𝓗 = pktHullForms, pktHull satisfies IsHullMap 𝓟 𝓗 (pktHull_isHullMap). On all subsets it does not, because pktHull univ = univ is not of the form λ · 𝒪, in accordance with H ⊊ ℐ^ℚ(−) on page 127 (pktHull_not_isHullMap_univ). The paper's ℙ (direct product regions, Remark 3.1.1 (iii)) is not modeled; the domain 𝓟 here is a choice.
  • Log-volume (pktHull_muLog_principal): for finite extensions L_s of ℚ_p of degrees d_s, any Haar measures μ_s and the product measure, the normalized log-volume padicMuLog (normalized at 𝒪, divided by D = Σ d_s) is μ^log(λ · 𝒪) = (Σ_s d_s log ‖λ_s‖) / D, a weighted sum with weights d_s / D that come from Measure.pi and the scaling law μ_s(y • A) = ‖y‖ ^ d_s μ_s(A). Hence the log-volume of a hull (pktHull_muLog_hull). These are the Haar weights of the whole product, not the normalized weights of IUT III Remark 3.1.1 (ii); in the reading of WeightedPacket.lean, wPkt_weight_eq_haar_iff shows that the two weight systems coincide for every tuple of places if and only if [K_v : (F_mod)_v] is the same at all places over p (for nonempty label and place sets and positive degrees).
  • Comparison with the coordinatewise hull IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado.dhHull (polydisc of the coordinate suprema of norms). On relatively compact sets they agree for discretely valued factors (pktHull_eq_dhHull), whether or not a projection is zero. On ℚ_p × ℤ_p ⊆ ℚ_p² they differ (pktHull_dhHull_padic_test): the page's definition gives ℚ_p² (the set is not relatively compact), the polydisc construction gives ℚ_p × ℤ_p itself (radii ∞ and 1). This is a difference between two definitions on an unbounded set.
  • Unions. ⋃ i, pktHull (U i) ⊆ pktHull (⋃ i, U i) (pktHull_iUnion_subset); the inclusion is strict for U₀ = {(1, p)}, U₁ = {(p, 1)} in ℚ_p², where (1, 1) lies in the hull of the union and in neither hull (pktHull_union_strict_padic). This matters because Corollary 3.12 takes the hull of the union of the possible images.
Interpretation choices
  1. Relatively compact is IsCompact (closure U) in the product topology.
  2. Finite log-volume. The page asks for a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume. Here it is read as a subset of positive (outer) product Haar measure; only its consequence, that no coordinate projection of U is zero, is used, and the theorems are stated under that weaker hypothesis where possible.
  3. *The domain of φ.* (P1) to (P3) are checked on 𝓟 above, not on the paper's direct product regions.
Not proved
  • Nothing about tensor packets, ℐ^ℚ(−) itself, log-shells, or the archimedean places.
  • Remark 3.9.5 (iii), (iv) (the sets Φ(P), Ξ(P) of page 128).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullDiscretedef

def pktHullDiscrete (K : Type*) [NormedField K] : Prop :=
  ∃ ϖ : K, 0 < ‖ϖ‖ ∧ ‖ϖ‖ < 1 ∧ ∀ x : K, x ≠ 0 → ∃ k : ℤ, ‖x‖ = ‖ϖ‖ ^ k

The value group of a normed field K is discrete: there is ϖ with 0 < ‖ϖ‖ < 1 such that every nonzero x has ‖x‖ = ‖ϖ‖ ^ k for an integer k. For a finite extension of ℚ_p with its spectral norm this is pktHullDiscrete_spectral.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_exists_smalltheorem

theorem pktHull_exists_small (hK : pktHullDiscrete K) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ c : K, c ≠ 0 ∧ ‖c‖ < ε

Elements of arbitrarily small nonzero norm.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_exists_largetheorem

theorem pktHull_exists_large (hK : pktHullDiscrete K) (B : ℝ) :
  ∃ c : K, c ≠ 0 ∧ B ≤ ‖c‖

Elements of arbitrarily large norm.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_exists_maxtheorem

theorem pktHull_exists_max (hK : pktHullDiscrete K) {S : Set K} {B : ℝ}
  (hB : ∀ y ∈ S, ‖y‖ ≤ B) {x₀ : K} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ S) (h0 : x₀ ≠ 0) :
  ∃ x ∈ S, x ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ y ∈ S, ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖

The largest norm is attained on a set S of a discretely valued field whose norms are bounded and which contains a nonzero element.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullIntegersdef

def pktHullIntegers : Set (∀ s, L s) := {x | ∀ s, ‖x s‖ ≤ 1}

The integral structure 𝒪 = Π s, 𝒪_{L_s}, modeled as the product of the closed unit balls.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullPrincipaldef

def pktHullPrincipal (c : ∀ s, (L s)ˣ) : Set (∀ s, L s) :=
  (fun s => ((c s : (L s)ˣ) : L s)) • pktHullIntegers

The set λ · 𝒪 of Remark 3.9.5 (i), page 127, for λ with every component nonzero (an element of Π s, L_s^×).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullFormsdef

def pktHullForms : Set (Set (∀ s, L s)) := Set.range (pktHullPrincipal (L := L))

The family of the sets λ · 𝒪, the candidate hulls.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullNondegdef

def pktHullNondeg (U : Set (∀ s, L s)) : Prop := ∀ s, ∃ x ∈ U, x s ≠ 0

No coordinate projection of U is zero.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHulldef

noncomputable def pktHull (U : Set (∀ s, L s)) : Set (∀ s, L s) :=
  if IsCompact (closure U) then ⋂₀ {H | H ∈ pktHullForms ∧ U ⊆ H} else Set.univ

The holomorphic hull of Remark 3.9.5 (i), page 127: for relatively compact U, the intersection of the sets λ · 𝒪 containing U (the smallest one when it exists, pktHull_isLeast); for U not relatively compact, the whole space.

theorem pktHull_mem_principal {c : ∀ s, (L s)ˣ} {x : ∀ s, L s} :

λ · 𝒪 is the box {x | ∀ s, ‖x s‖ ≤ ‖λ_s‖}.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullPrincipal_onetheorem

theorem pktHullPrincipal_one : pktHullPrincipal (1 : ∀ s, (L s)ˣ) = pktHullIntegers

𝒪 itself is of the form λ · 𝒪, with λ = 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullPrincipal_eq_pitheorem

theorem pktHull_of_relCompact {U : Set (∀ s, L s)} (h : IsCompact (closure U)) :

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_mem_sInter_ifftheorem

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_eq_principaltheorem

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_isLeasttheorem

  IsLeast {H | U ⊆ H ∧ H ∈ pktHullForms} (pktHull U)

**Remark 3.9.5 (i), page 127: the hull is the smallest set of the form λ · 𝒪 containing U**, for relatively compact U none of whose coordinate projections is zero, over discretely valued fields.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_not_exists_isLeast_zerotheorem

Agreement with the coordinatewise hull of IUT.Applications.DupuyHilado: on relatively compact sets, over discretely valued fields, pktHull U is the polydisc of the coordinate suprema of norms, whether or not a projection is zero.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_subset_of_formtheorem

theorem pktHull_subset_of_form [∀ s, ProperSpace (L s)] {U H : Set (∀ s, L s)}
  (hH : H ∈ pktHullForms) (hUH : U ⊆ H) : pktHull U ⊆ H

For proper factors, the hull of U lies in every λ · 𝒪 that contains U.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_idemtheorem

theorem pktHull_idem [∀ s, ProperSpace (L s)] (U : Set (∀ s, L s)) :
  pktHull (pktHull U) = pktHull U

Idempotence (all subsets, proper factors): pktHull (pktHull U) = pktHull U.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullDomaindef

def pktHullDomain : Set (Set (∀ s, L s)) := {U | IsCompact (closure U) ∧ pktHullNondeg U}

The domain on which (P1) to (P3) are checked: relatively compact sets with nonzero coordinate projections. A choice; the paper's ℙ is the set of direct product regions.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_isHullMaptheorem

theorem pktHull_isHullMap [∀ s, ProperSpace (L s)] :
  IsHullMap (pktHullDomain (L := L)) pktHullForms pktHull

Remark 3.9.5 (ii), page 127, for this hull: with 𝓗 the sets λ · 𝒪 and 𝓟 the relatively compact sets with nonzero projections, pktHull maps 𝓟 into 𝓗 and satisfies (P1), (P2), (P3), and 𝓗 ⊆ 𝓟; proper, discretely valued factors.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_not_isHullMap_univtheorem

theorem pktHull_not_isHullMap_univ [Nonempty ι] :
  ¬ IsHullMap (Set.univ : Set (Set (∀ s, L s))) pktHullForms pktHull

On all subsets (P1) to (P3) fail: univ would have to be mapped to a set of the form λ · 𝒪, but pktHull univ = univ is not of that form. Page 127 requires hulls to be proper subsets (H ⊊ ℐ^ℚ(−)).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullNondeg_of_measuretheorem

theorem pktHullNondeg_of_measure (μ : ∀ s, Measure (L s)) [∀ s, SigmaFinite (μ s)]
  (h0 : ∀ s, μ s {0} = 0) {U : Set (∀ s, L s)} (hU : Measure.pi μ U ≠ 0) :
  pktHullNondeg U

Positive measure implies nonzero projections: if the product of measures with no mass at 0 gives U positive (outer) measure, then no coordinate projection of U is zero.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_measure_principaltheorem

theorem pktHull_measure_principal (d : ι → ℕ) (μ : ∀ s, Measure (L s))
  [∀ s, SigmaFinite (μ s)]
  (hsc : ∀ s (y : L s), y ≠ 0 → ∀ A : Set (L s),
    μ s (y • A) = ((‖y‖₊ ^ d s : NNReal) : ENNReal) * μ s A)
  (c : ∀ s, (L s)ˣ) :
  Measure.pi μ (pktHullPrincipal c) =
    ∏ s, ((‖(c s : L s)‖₊ ^ d s : NNReal) : ENNReal) * μ s {y | ‖y‖ ≤ 1}

**Haar measure of λ · 𝒪**: under the scaling law μ_s(y • A) = ‖y‖ ^ d_s μ_s(A), the product measure of λ · 𝒪 is ∏_s ‖λ_s‖ ^ d_s μ_s(𝒪_s).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullDiscrete_padictheorem

theorem pktHullDiscrete_padic : pktHullDiscrete ℚ_[p]

**ℚ_p is discretely valued**, with ϖ = p.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullDiscrete_spectraltheorem

theorem pktHullDiscrete_spectral (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra ℚ_[p] K]
  [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K] [Algebra ℤ_[p] K] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K] :
  letI

**A finite extension of ℚ_p with its spectral norm is discretely valued** (from the uniformizer of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.padicBridge_uniformizer).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_haar_singleton_zerotheorem

theorem pktHull_haar_singleton_zero (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra ℚ_[p] K]
  [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K] [Algebra ℤ_[p] K] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K] :
  letI

For a finite extension with its spectral norm and any Haar measure, {0} is a null set.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHullIntegers_eq_pi_integralClosuretheorem

theorem pktHullIntegers_eq_pi_integralClosure :
  letI : ∀ s, NormedField (L s)

The integral structure 𝒪 = Π s, 𝒪_{L_s} is the product of the rings of integers integralClosure ℤ_p L_s.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_isLeast_spectraltheorem

theorem pktHull_isLeast_spectral :
  letI : ∀ s, NormedField (L s)

**Remark 3.9.5 (i), page 127, for a finite product of finite extensions of ℚ_p**: for every additive Haar measure on each factor and every relatively compact U containing a subset of positive product measure, pktHull U is the smallest set of the form λ · 𝒪 containing U.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_isHullMap_spectraltheorem

theorem pktHull_isHullMap_spectral :
  letI : ∀ s, NormedField (L s)

**(P1) to (P3) for finite extensions of ℚ_p**, on relatively compact sets with nonzero projections.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_muLog_principaltheorem

theorem pktHull_muLog_principal :
  letI : ∀ s, NormedField (L s)

**Log-volume of λ · 𝒪**: for finite extensions L_s of ℚ_p of degrees d_s, Haar measures μ_s and the product measure on V = Π s, L s (of dimension D = Σ d_s), the normalized log-volume padicMuLog normalized at 𝒪 is μ^log(λ · 𝒪) = (Σ_s d_s log ‖λ_s‖) / D: the average of the log ‖λ_s‖ with weights d_s / D.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_muLog_hulltheorem

theorem pktHull_muLog_hull :
  letI : ∀ s, NormedField (L s)

Log-volume of the hull: for relatively compact U with nonzero projections, with x_s ∈ U a point whose s-th coordinate has the largest norm, μ^log(pktHull U) = (Σ_s d_s log ‖(x_s)_s‖) / D.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_dhHull_padic_testtheorem

theorem pktHull_dhHull_padic_test :
  let U : Set (Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) := {x | ‖x 1‖ ≤ 1}
  pktHull (L := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) U = Set.univ ∧
    dhPolyRadius (X := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) U 0 = ⊤ ∧
    dhPolyRadius (X := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) U 1 = 1 ∧
    dhHull (X := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) U = U ∧ U ≠ Set.univ

**ℚ_p × ℤ_p in ℚ_p²: the two definitions differ.** For U = {x | ‖x₁‖ ≤ 1}, the hull of page 127 is the whole space ℚ_p², because U is not relatively compact; the polydisc hull dhHull of the coordinate suprema of norms has radii ∞ and 1 and is U itself, which is not the whole space. A difference between two definitions on an unbounded set.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.pktHull_union_strict_padictheorem

theorem pktHull_union_strict_padic :
  let v : Fin 2 → ℚ_[p] := ![1, (p : ℚ_[p])]
  let w : Fin 2 → ℚ_[p] := ![(p : ℚ_[p]), 1]
  (fun _ => 1 : Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) ∈ pktHull (L := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) ({v} ∪ {w}) ∧
    (fun _ => 1 : Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) ∉ pktHull (L := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) {v} ∧
    (fun _ => 1 : Fin 2 → ℚ_[p]) ∉ pktHull (L := fun _ : Fin 2 => ℚ_[p]) {w}

The hull of a union can be strictly larger than the union of the hulls: in ℚ_p², for v = (1, p) and w = (p, 1), the point (1, 1) lies in pktHull ({v} ∪ {w}) but in neither pktHull {v} nor pktHull {w}.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Places

IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/Places.lean · imports IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Comparison

IUT III, Corollary 3.12: the sum over places in the interface of the final comparison

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Remark 3.1.1 (ii) to (iv), pages 94 to 97; Proposition 3.9 (i) to (iii), pages 115 to 117; the statement of Corollary 3.12 and the opening of its proof, pages 173 to 175; Step (xi-d), page 183. Pages read for this file: 94 to 97, 115 to 120, 173 to 175, 181 to 183. Pages checked against rendered images: 94 to 97, 116, 117, 173 to 175, 181, 183. Pages 115, 118, 119 and 120 were read in text only; no formula of this file is taken from them.

What this file is and is not

This file is not a formalization of Corollary 3.12, nor of Proposition 3.9 (iii). It adds one feature to the interface of Comparison.lean: the passage from local log-volumes, one for each place, to a global log-volume. As in Comparison.lean, no region is constructed from initial Θ-data, Hodge theaters, the log-theta-lattice or the multiradial representation of Theorem 3.11; every region and every measure is an input. The comparison of the q-pilot region with the hull of the union of the possible images remains an unproved hypothesis, now placewise (PlacewiseContainment) or global (GlobalLogVolumeComparison); nothing here gives evidence for or against it.

What the pages say
  • Proposition 3.9 (iii), page 117 (rendered): on the families indexed by v_Q ∈ 𝕍_ℚ whose components have zero log-volume for all but finitely many v_Q, adding the local log-volumes of (i) ("all but finitely many of which are zero!") gives a global log-volume with values in ℝ.
  • Proposition 3.9 (i), pages 115 and 116 (page 116 rendered): the local log-volumes are defined on nonempty compact open subsets (nonarchimedean) or compact closures of nonempty open subsets (archimedean), with values in ℝ, and are determined by the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), (iii), (iv).
  • Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94 (rendered): the portion corresponding to K_v gets the weight [K_v : (F_mod)_v]⁻¹; a direct sum over the v above v_Q gets the normalized weight 1 / ([K_v : (F_mod)_v] · ∑_{w | v_Q} [(F_mod)_w : ℚ_{v_Q}]), and tensor products over A get the analogous products. Remark 3.1.1 (iv), page 97 (rendered): for a direct product region ∏_v S_v, (1/N_E) · μ^log_E(S) = ∑_{v ∈ V} (1/N_v) · μ^log_v(S_v).
What is typed
  • PlaceWeights P: a positive real weight at each place of an index type P. Two readings are covered. If P is 𝕍_ℚ, page 117 adds the local log-volumes with weight 1 (unitPlaceWeights), the weights of Remark 3.1.1 being already inside each local log-volume. If P is a set of places v lying over 𝕍_ℚ, the weight at v is a normalized weight of Remark 3.1.1 (ii) or the 1/N_v of (iv). Positivity is the one regularity field; each displayed weight on page 94 is the reciprocal of a positive number.
  • LogVolumeAlmostAllZero μ R: the condition of page 117, "zero log-volume for all but finitely many" places, for a family of regions R v with measures μ v.
  • globalLogVolume w μ R = ∑ᶠ v, w v · log μ_v (R v), with value in EReal.
  • Monotonicity under placewise containment (globalLogVolume_mono), finiteness when every local term is finite (globalLogVolume_ne_bot, globalLogVolume_ne_top), and the bridge to Conclusion (conclusion_of_placewiseContainment).
  • Examples on two places, built from IntervalExample.setting of Comparison.lean: one where every hypothesis of the bridge holds, one where every structural hypothesis holds and the global comparison and the conclusion fail, and one where the global comparison holds while the placewise comparison fails at one place.
The values −∞ and +∞

The paper's local log-volumes are real (page 116: values in ℝ on 𝔐(−)), so the paper's hypotheses exclude ±∞ at every place, and the sum of page 117 is a finite sum of real numbers. Here a local log-volume is log of an arbitrary measure (logVolume of Comparison.lean), so it can be −∞ (measure zero) or +∞ (infinite measure). In EReal, Mathlib's convention is ⊥ + ⊤ = ⊥ (EReal.bot_add): a sum containing both −∞ and +∞ is −∞. Nothing below depends on that case being meaningful:

  • globalLogVolume_mono holds in EReal with no finiteness hypothesis, because addition on EReal is monotone in each argument whatever the convention for ⊥ + ⊤;
  • finiteness of the global value is proved only from finiteness of each local term;
  • the bridge assumes every q-pilot component has positive measure and every hull component has positive finite measure, so the case ⊥ + ⊤ does not arise on either side.

If the support condition LogVolumeAlmostAllZero fails, ∑ᶠ returns 0 by Mathlib's convention; every theorem that uses the sum assumes the support condition, so that value is never used.

Interpretation choices
  1. Which places. The index type P and the weights are arbitrary; the reading of page 117 (P = 𝕍_ℚ, weight 1) is the instance unitPlaceWeights. Remark 3.1.1 (iii), page 95, warns that weighted sums of log-volumes are not in general the logarithm of one measure; here only weighted sums of logarithms of measures, one measure per place, are formed, and no product measure is used. The local log-volume is the measure instance logVolume of Comparison.lean; the abstract RegionComparison there is not used here, and the normalization of the local log-volumes (Proposition 3.9 (i), pages 115 and 116) is not modeled.
  2. Placewise containment. Page 174 writes the regions n,◦U and n,◦Ū as collections indexed by (j, v_Q) with j ∈ |𝔽_l| and v_Q ∈ 𝕍_ℚ, and their inclusions componentwise. PlacewiseContainment is that componentwise inclusion over the places. Step (xi-f), page 184, asserts only the global numerical inequality; example_global_not_placewise shows that the global inequality does not imply the placewise one.
  3. Labels and places together. The procession-normalization (average over labels, see LabelAverage.lean) and the sum over places are typed separately. For finitely many labels and places of finite support the two operations commute; that is not stated here.
What is still omitted
  • No construction from initial Θ-data; the comparison is a hypothesis.
  • Finiteness of the global value needs the support condition for the hull family; page 175 argues finiteness from "the [easily verified] compactness" of the 1,◦U_{j,v_Q}, which gives finiteness at each place but not the support condition; not formalized.
  • Tensor packets, the identification of the two sides through the Θ^{×μ}_{LGP}-link and the permutation symmetry (Steps (xi-a), (xi-b), pages 181 and 182), and the determinant and tensor power normalization of Step (xi-d), page 183.
  • The invariance of the global log-volume under multiplication by elements of (M_MOD)_α and its equality with an arithmetic degree (page 117).
Public declarations
variable {P : Type*} {X : P → Type*} [∀ v, MeasurableSpace (X v)]
variable {P : Type*} {X : P → Type*} [∀ v, MeasurableSpace (X v)] {ι : P → Type*}

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.PlaceWeightsstructure

structure PlaceWeights (P : Type*) where

A positive real weight at each place (Remark 3.1.1 (ii), (iv), pages 94 and 97; weight 1 at each v_Q in the sum of Proposition 3.9 (iii), page 117).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.unitPlaceWeightsdef

def unitPlaceWeights (P : Type*) : PlaceWeights P := ⟨fun _ => 1, fun _ => one_pos⟩

The weights of Proposition 3.9 (iii), page 117: the local log-volumes at the various v_Q ∈ 𝕍_ℚ are added, each with weight 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.LogVolumeAlmostAllZerodef

def LogVolumeAlmostAllZero (μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v)) (R : ∀ v, Set (X v)) : Prop :=
  {v | logVolume (μ v) (R v) ≠ 0}.Finite

The condition of Proposition 3.9 (iii), page 117: the family has zero log-volume at all but finitely many places.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.weightedLocalLogVolumedef

noncomputable def weightedLocalLogVolume (w : PlaceWeights P) (μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v))
    (R : ∀ v, Set (X v)) (v : P) : EReal :=
  ((w.placeWeight v : ℝ) : EReal) * logVolume (μ v) (R v)

The weighted local log-volume w_v · log μ_v (R_v) at a place.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolumedef

noncomputable def globalLogVolume (w : PlaceWeights P) (μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v))
    (R : ∀ v, Set (X v)) : EReal :=
  ∑ᶠ v, weightedLocalLogVolume w μ R v

The global log-volume ∑_v w_v · log μ_v (R_v) (Proposition 3.9 (iii), page 117), as a finite sum. It is meaningful under LogVolumeAlmostAllZero; otherwise ∑ᶠ returns 0.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.hasFiniteSupport_weightedLocalLogVolumetheorem

theorem hasFiniteSupport_weightedLocalLogVolume (w : PlaceWeights P) {μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v)}
  {R : ∀ v, Set (X v)} (h : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero μ R) :
  Function.HasFiniteSupport (weightedLocalLogVolume w μ R)

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolume_monotheorem

theorem globalLogVolume_mono (w : PlaceWeights P) (μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v))
  {R R' : ∀ v, Set (X v)} (hR : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero μ R)
  (hR' : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero μ R') (h : ∀ v, R v ⊆ R' v) :
  globalLogVolume w μ R ≤ globalLogVolume w μ R'

Monotonicity. Placewise containment of two families, both of zero log-volume at all but finitely many places, gives the inequality of the global log-volumes. No finiteness is needed.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolume_ne_bottheorem

theorem globalLogVolume_ne_bot (w : PlaceWeights P) {μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v)}
  {R : ∀ v, Set (X v)} (h : ∀ v, logVolume (μ v) (R v) ≠ ⊥) :
  globalLogVolume w μ R ≠ ⊥

If no local log-volume is −∞, the global log-volume is not −∞.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolume_ne_toptheorem

theorem globalLogVolume_ne_top (w : PlaceWeights P) {μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v)}
  {R : ∀ v, Set (X v)} (h : ∀ v, logVolume (μ v) (R v) ≠ ⊤) :
  globalLogVolume w μ R ≠ ⊤

If no local log-volume is +∞, the global log-volume is not +∞.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolume_finitetheorem

theorem globalLogVolume_finite (w : PlaceWeights P) {μ : ∀ v, Measure (X v)}
  {R : ∀ v, Set (X v)} (h0 : ∀ v, μ v (R v) ≠ 0) (htop : ∀ v, μ v (R v) ≠ ⊤) :
  globalLogVolume w μ R ≠ ⊥ ∧ globalLogVolume w μ R ≠ ⊤

Finiteness: if every local log-volume is finite (0 < μ_v (R_v) < ∞ at each place), the global log-volume is a real number.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalQLogVolumedef

noncomputable def globalQLogVolume : EReal :=
  globalLogVolume w (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).qPilot

The global log-volume of the q-pilot family: − |log(q)| summed over places.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalThetaLogVolumedef

noncomputable def globalThetaLogVolume : EReal :=
  globalLogVolume w (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).hullOfUnion

The global log-volume of the family of hulls of unions: − |log(Θ)| summed over places.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.PlacewiseContainmentdef

def PlacewiseContainment : Prop := ∀ v, (S v).Containment

Region form of the comparison over places: at every place, the q-pilot region lies in the hull of the union of the possible images (componentwise inclusion, page 174). Not proved here; see ComparisonSetting.Containment.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.GlobalLogVolumeComparisondef

def GlobalLogVolumeComparison : Prop := globalQLogVolume S w ≤ globalThetaLogVolume S w

Numerical form of the comparison for the global log-volumes: − |log(q)| ≤ − |log(Θ)| (Step (xi-f), page 184). Not proved here.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalLogVolumeComparison_of_placewiseContainmenttheorem

theorem globalLogVolumeComparison_of_placewiseContainment
  (hqs : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).qPilot)
  (hΘs : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).hullOfUnion)

Placewise containment gives the global comparison, provided both families satisfy the support condition of page 117.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.globalPilotLogVolumesdef

noncomputable def globalPilotLogVolumes (hq0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).qPilot ≠ 0)
    (hneg : globalQLogVolume S w < 0) (hΘ0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0) :
    PilotLogVolumes :=
  PilotLogVolumes.ofLogVolumes (globalQLogVolume S w) (globalThetaLogVolume S w)
    (globalLogVolume_ne_bot w fun v => (logVolume_eq_bot_iff _ _).not.mpr (hq0 v)) hneg
    (globalLogVolume_ne_bot w fun v => (logVolume_eq_bot_iff _ _).not.mpr (hΘ0 v))

The two numbers of Corollary 3.12 from the global log-volumes. Hypotheses: every q-pilot component and every hull component has positive measure (no local term is −∞), and the global q-side log-volume is negative (|log(q)| > 0, page 174).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.conclusion_globalPilotLogVolumes_ifftheorem

theorem conclusion_globalPilotLogVolumes_iff (hq0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).qPilot ≠ 0)
  (hneg : globalQLogVolume S w < 0) (hΘ0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0) :
  Conclusion (globalPilotLogVolumes S w hq0 hneg hΘ0) ↔
    globalThetaLogVolume S w ≠ ⊤ ∧ GlobalLogVolumeComparison S w

For the global numbers, the conclusion of Corollary 3.12 is finiteness of the global Θ-side log-volume together with GlobalLogVolumeComparison.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.conclusion_of_placewiseContainmenttheorem

theorem conclusion_of_placewiseContainment (hq0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).qPilot ≠ 0)
  (hneg : globalQLogVolume S w < 0) (hΘ0 : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0)
  (hfin : ∀ v, (S v).μ (S v).hullOfUnion ≠ ⊤)
  (hqs : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).qPilot)
  (hΘs : LogVolumeAlmostAllZero (fun v => (S v).μ) fun v => (S v).hullOfUnion)
  (hcont : PlacewiseContainment S) : Conclusion (globalPilotLogVolumes S w hq0 hneg hΘ0)

Bridge over places (conditional). Placewise containment of the q-pilot regions in the hulls of the unions, finiteness of each hull, and the support condition of page 117 for both families give the conclusion of Corollary 3.12 for the global numbers. Conditional on hcont (Theorem 3.11 and Steps (i) to (xi); the text asserts only the global numerical form, Step (xi-f), page 184), on hfin (page 175, compactness; not formalized) and on hΘs (the support condition for the hulls; not argued on the pages read).

  GlobalLogVolumeComparison (settings (qPair a b))
    (unitPlaceWeights Bool) ↔ a * b ≤ 1 / 4

The global comparison for q-pilot regions [0, a], [0, b] holds exactly when a · b ≤ 1/4.

theorem hullOfUnion_volume_ne_zero (q : Bool → Set ℝ) (v : Bool) :
  (settings q v).μ (settings q v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.TwoPlaceExample.hullOfUnion_volume_ne_toptheorem

theorem hullOfUnion_volume_ne_top (q : Bool → Set ℝ) (v : Bool) :
  (settings q v).μ (settings q v).hullOfUnion ≠ ⊤

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.TwoPlaceExample.qPair_volume_ne_zerotheorem

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.TwoPlaceExample.example_global_conclusiontheorem

theorem example_global_conclusion :
  ∃ (hq0 : ∀ v, (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2)) v).μ
      (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2)) v).qPilot ≠ 0)
    (hneg : globalQLogVolume (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2))) (unitPlaceWeights Bool) < 0)
    (hΘ0 : ∀ v, (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2)) v).μ
      (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2)) v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0),
    Conclusion (globalPilotLogVolumes (settings (qPair (1 / 2) (1 / 2)))
      (unitPlaceWeights Bool) hq0 hneg hΘ0)

Nonvacuity (a). With q-pilot region [0, 1/2] at both places, every hypothesis of conclusion_of_placewiseContainment holds, so the conclusion of Corollary 3.12 holds for the global numbers.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.TwoPlaceExample.example_global_comparison_failstheorem

theorem example_global_comparison_fails :
  ∃ (hq0 : ∀ v, (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).μ
      (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).qPilot ≠ 0)
    (hneg : globalQLogVolume (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4))) (unitPlaceWeights Bool) < 0)
    (hΘ0 : ∀ v, (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).μ
      (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).hullOfUnion ≠ 0),
    (∀ v, (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).μ
      (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)) v).hullOfUnion ≠ ⊤) ∧
    ¬ GlobalLogVolumeComparison (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4))) (unitPlaceWeights Bool) ∧
    ¬ Conclusion (globalPilotLogVolumes (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (3 / 4)))
      (unitPlaceWeights Bool) hq0 hneg hΘ0)

Nonvacuity (b). With q-pilot region [0, 3/4] at both places, every structural hypothesis holds (positive measures, finite hulls, the support condition, negative global q-side log-volume), but the global comparison fails, and so does the conclusion of Corollary 3.12 for the global numbers.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.TwoPlaceExample.example_global_not_placewisetheorem

theorem example_global_not_placewise :
  GlobalLogVolumeComparison (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (1 / 8))) (unitPlaceWeights Bool) ∧
    ¬ (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (1 / 8)) false).LogVolumeComparison ∧
    ¬ PlacewiseContainment (settings (qPair (3 / 4) (1 / 8)))

The global inequality does not imply the placewise one. With q-pilot regions [0, 3/4] at place false and [0, 1/8] at place true, the global comparison holds (3/4 · 1/8 ≤ 1/4) while the placewise comparison fails at place false: the deficit at one place is compensated at the other.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.UpperSemiCompatibility

IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/UpperSemiCompatibility.lean · imports IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.Indeterminacy, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm

IUT III, upper semi-compatibility and the indeterminacy (Ind3)

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III: Remark 1.1.1 (i), page 28; Proposition 1.2 (v), (vi), pages 31 and 32; Remark 1.2.2 (i), (iii), pages 36 and 37; Proposition 3.5 (ii), pages 104 to 106; Theorem 3.11 (i), (ii), pages 154 to 156 and 158; Remark 3.11.1, pages 160, 161 and 166; proof of Corollary 3.12, Steps (iv) to (x), pages 177 to 181. Pages read for this file: 28, 29, 31, 32, 36, 37, 103 to 106, 154 to 156, 158, 160, 161, 166, 177 to 181. Pages checked against rendered images: all of these.

What this file is and is not

This file is not a formalization of Proposition 3.5, Theorem 3.11 or Corollary 3.12. It proves the local nonarchimedean inclusions behind "upper semi-compatibility" in one local field (the normed-field model of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm, and ℚ_p), and it types (Ind3) by one faithful reading as a family of regions inside a container, combined with the orbit of Indeterminacy.lean. No region is constructed from Hodge theaters, Kummer isomorphisms or the log-theta-lattice. The results bound the log-volume of the hull of the possible images from above (the direction of Step (x), page 181); they say nothing about the comparison of the q-pilot region with that hull, which remains an unproved hypothesis of Comparison.lean.

What the pages say
  • Remark 1.1.1 (i), page 28: the log-links "that appear in such iterates are to be understood as being defined only on the [local] units" in their domains.
  • Proposition 1.2 (v), pages 31 and 32: at v ∈ 𝕍^non the log-shell is compact (a_non), contains the submonoid of Π_v-invariants of Ψ_{log(F_v)} (b_non), and contains the image of the Π_v-invariants of Ψ^×_{F_v} (c_non).
  • Remark 1.2.2 (i), page 36: concretely I_k = (p*)⁻¹ · log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k, and (b_non), (c_non) are the inclusions O_k^▷ = O_k \ {0} ⊆ O_k ⊆ I_k and log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ I_k.
  • Remark 1.2.2 (iii), page 37: the coric log-shells contain "not only the images, via the Kummer isomorphisms", of the O^▷, "but also the images, via the composite of the Kummer isomorphisms with the various iterates" of the log-link, "of the portions of the various O^▷ ... on which these iterates are defined"; this is called "upper semi-commutativity".
  • Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a), pages 104 and 105: for v_ℚ ∈ 𝕍_ℚ^non the module I(𝕊^±_{j+1} F(n,∘𝔇_≻)_{v_ℚ}) "contains the images" of the Galois invariants of the groups of units (Ψ_cns(n,m 𝔉_≻)_{|t|})^×_v, via both (1) the tensor product over |t| of the Kummer isomorphisms and (2) the tensor product over |t| of their pre-composite "with the m'-th iterates ... of the log-links, for m' ≥ 1". Part (b), page 105, at archimedean places, is a statement about closed balls and surjections onto units; part (c) concerns bad places.
  • (Ind3), Theorem 3.11 (ii), page 156: "as one varies m ∈ ℤ, the isomorphisms of (a) are 'upper semi-compatible', relative to the log-links of the n-th column ..., in a sense that involves certain natural inclusions '⊆' at v_ℚ ∈ 𝕍_ℚ^non and certain natural surjections '↠' at v_ℚ ∈ 𝕍_ℚ^arc", with details in Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a), (b). The next sentence: the isomorphisms of (a) are "[precisely!] compatible" with the respective log-volumes as m varies.
  • Step (iv), page 177: vertical coricity is available "only at the cost of admitting the 'indeterminacy' constituted by the upper semi-compatibility of (Ind3)". Step (v), page 177: the mono-analytic log-shells serve as "multiradial mono-analytic containers". Step (x), page 181: the procession-normalized log-volumes are invariant under (Ind1), (Ind2) and convert (Ind3) into an inequality "[from above]".
What is proved on real objects (part 1)

logUnitIterateRegion start units log is the sequence S 0 = start, S (n + 1) = log '' (S n ∩ units): the n-th iterate of the log-link, defined only on units as Remark 1.1.1 (i) says, applied to start. For start ⊆ O (the units of Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a) or the O^▷ of Remark 1.2.2 (iii)), every S n lies in the log-shell:

  • extLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegion: in a complete, locally compact normed ℚ_p-algebra field K (the model of finite extensions of ℚ_p in Logarithm.lean), with O the closed unit ball, units the unit sphere and log = extLogUnit;
  • padicLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegion: the same over ℚ_p with padicLogUnit and padicLogShell p = ℤ_p.

This is Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a) and Remark 1.2.2 (iii) for one tensor factor (j = 0, |t| = 0), with the Kummer isomorphisms taken to be identities and every level m of the column identified with the same field. It rests on (b_non) and (c_non) only: S 0 ⊆ O ⊆ I and S (n + 1) ⊆ log(O^×) ⊆ I (logUnitIterateRegion_succ_subset). Not covered: tensor products over |t| and the Galois invariants in them, Kummer isomorphisms and vertical coricity, part (b) (archimedean surjections), part (c) (bad places).

Over ℚ_p the chain is explicit: S 1 = log(ℤ_p^×) = {‖z‖ ≤ 1 / p*} (padic_logUnitIterateRegion_one), which is strictly smaller than the container ℤ_p (padic_logUnitIterateRegion_one_ssubset), and S n = ∅ for n ≥ 2 (padic_logUnitIterateRegion_add_two), because log(ℤ_p^×) contains no unit. Over a ramified finite extension the image log(O^×) can meet the units, so the chain need not stop; that is not computed here.

The typed (Ind3) (part 2): one faithful reading

VerticalRegionFamily X ι is data only: a container (the log-shell in the nonarchimedean reading) and regions indexed by a vertical coordinate ι (the paper varies m ∈ ℤ; the iterate family above is indexed by m' ∈ ℕ). UpperSemiCompatible is the named proposition that every region lies in the container; it is proved for the iterate families (padicIterateFamily, extIterateFamily) and is a hypothesis elsewhere. The possible image under (Ind3) is the hull of columnUnion. Theorems: the hull of the union bounds every member; under UpperSemiCompatible and with the container a hull, the hull of the union lies in the container and its log-volume is at most that of the container, for any region log-volume monotone into the hull domain (the condition logVol_mono of RegionComparison).

Combination with (Ind1), (Ind2): for an IndeterminacyOrbit O, the joint possible images are a • R_m (jointColumnImage). Without further hypotheses their union lies in the orbit union of the container (jointColumnUnion_subset_containerOrbit), so the log-volume of its hull is at most that of the hull of the container's orbit. Under ContainerStable (every element of ind1 and of ind2 maps the container onto itself), that orbit union is the container. Measure preservation by ind1, ind2 (the abstract form of the invariance of Step (x)) gives the bound logVolume (a • R_m) ≤ logVolume container for every member (logVolume_jointColumnImage_le_shellContainer): (Ind3) becomes an inequality from above.

Stability is a hypothesis. Proposition 1.2 (vi), page 32, asserts that the Ism-orbit of isomorphisms of mono-analytic log-shells is compatible with "the respective log-shells", which is the nonarchimedean (Ind2) of page 154 acting on one factor; it is not proved here. No page read for this file asserts that the automorphisms of the procession (Ind1) preserve the log-shell of the tensor packet.

Alternatives not chosen. (i) The upward closure {Y | ∃ a, a • base ⊑ Y} for a relation ⊑ (mentioned in Indeterminacy.lean); (ii) a relation between regions at consecutive m (R_m ⊆ R_{m+1}), which the pages do not assert: they assert containment of every image in one coric container; (iii) at archimedean places, a surjection from a closed ball onto the units (Proposition 3.5 (ii) (b)), which is not a containment and is not modeled; (iv) indexing by ℤ with a translation symmetry (page 106), not modeled.

Examples (part 3)
  • padic_iUnion_nonzeroIntegers: with start = O^▷ = ℤ_p \ {0} (Remark 1.2.2), the union of the chain is the container ℤ_p, for every p.
  • padic_two_iUnion_units_ssubset: with start the units (Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a)) and p = 2, the union ℤ_2^× ∪ 4ℤ_2 is strictly smaller than the container ℤ_2 (it misses 2).
  • On ℝ with the interval hull of Comparison.lean: a family whose union is strictly smaller than the container while the hull of the union equals it (example_gap_union), and one whose hull is strictly smaller than the container (example_hull_ssubset).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.logUnitIterateRegiondef

def logUnitIterateRegion (start units : Set K) (log : K → K) : ℕ → Set K
  | 0 => start
  | n + 1 => log '' (logUnitIterateRegion start units log n ∩ units)

The regions along a vertical line: S 0 = start and S (n + 1) = log '' (S n ∩ units), the (n + 1)-th iterate of the log-link applied to the part of start on which it is defined (the log-link is defined only on units, Remark 1.1.1 (i), page 28).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.logUnitIterateRegion_succ_subsettheorem

theorem logUnitIterateRegion_succ_subset (start units : Set K) (log : K → K) (n : ℕ) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start units log (n + 1) ⊆ log '' units

Every iterate of positive order lies in the image of the units (the pre-log-shell).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.logUnitIterateRegion_subset_oftheorem

theorem logUnitIterateRegion_subset_of {start units I : Set K} {log : K → K}
  (hstart : start ⊆ I) (hlog : log '' units ⊆ I) :
  ∀ n, logUnitIterateRegion start units log n ⊆ I

If start and the image of the units lie in I, every iterate lies in I.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.extLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegiontheorem

theorem extLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegion [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K]
  {start : Set K} (hstart : start ⊆ {x | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}) (n : ℕ) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} extLogUnit n ⊆ extLogShell p K

Upper semi-compatibility, one factor, finite extension model. In a complete, locally compact normed ℚ_p-algebra field K, for any start in the closed unit ball O, every iterate of extLogUnit on the unit sphere applied to start lies in the log-shell extLogShell p K. From (b_non) O ⊆ I (extLogShell_unitBall_subset) and (c_non) log(O^×) ⊆ I (extLogUnit_image_subset_extLogShell); Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a), pages 104 and 105, for j = 0 with identity Kummer maps.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padicLogUnit_image_unitSpheretheorem

theorem padicLogUnit_image_unitSphere :
  padicLogUnit p '' {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} =
    Set.range (fun u : ℤ_[p]ˣ => padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p]))

The image of the unit sphere of ℚ_p under padicLogUnit is log(ℤ_p^×).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padicLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegiontheorem

theorem padicLogShell_contains_logUnitIterateRegion {start : Set ℚ_[p]}
  (hstart : start ⊆ {x | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}) (n : ℕ) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p) n ⊆ padicLogShell p

**Upper semi-compatibility, one factor, over ℚ_p.** For any start ⊆ ℤ_p, every iterate of padicLogUnit on the units applied to start lies in the log-shell padicLogShell p.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_logUnitIterateRegion_onetheorem

theorem padic_logUnitIterateRegion_one {start : Set ℚ_[p]}
  (h : {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ start) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p) 1 =
    {z : ℚ_[p] | ‖z‖ ≤ ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹}

The first iterate over ℚ_p: if start contains the units, S 1 = log(ℤ_p^×), the closed ball of radius 1 / p*.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_logUnitIterateRegion_succ_inter_unitSpheretheorem

theorem padic_logUnitIterateRegion_succ_inter_unitSphere (start : Set ℚ_[p]) (k : ℕ) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p) (k + 1) ∩
    {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} = ∅

Over ℚ_p no iterate of positive order contains a unit: log(ℤ_p^×) has norm ≤ 1 / p* < 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_logUnitIterateRegion_add_twotheorem

theorem padic_logUnitIterateRegion_add_two (start : Set ℚ_[p]) (k : ℕ) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p) (k + 2) = ∅

Over ℚ_p the chain stops: S n = ∅ for n ≥ 2.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_logUnitIterateRegion_one_ssubsettheorem

theorem padic_logUnitIterateRegion_one_ssubset {start : Set ℚ_[p]}
  (h : {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ start) :
  logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p) 1 ⊂ padicLogShell p

The container is strictly larger than the first image: log(ℤ_p^×) ⊊ ℤ_p (1 is missing).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamilystructure

structure VerticalRegionFamily (X ι : Type*) where

One faithful reading of the (Ind3) data (page 156): a container (the log-shell, the "multiradial mono-analytic container" of Step (v), page 177) and regions indexed by a vertical coordinate. Data only; containment is the separate proposition UpperSemiCompatible.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.UpperSemiCompatibledef

def UpperSemiCompatible : Prop := ∀ m, F.columnRegion m ⊆ F.shellContainer

Upper semi-compatibility in the nonarchimedean reading: every region lies in the container (Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a), pages 104 and 105). A proposition about the family, proved for the iterate families of part 1 and a hypothesis elsewhere.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.columnUniondef

def columnUnion : Set X := ⋃ m, F.columnRegion m

The union of the regions along the vertical line.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.columnUnion_subset_shellContainertheorem

theorem columnUnion_subset_shellContainer (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) :
  F.columnUnion ⊆ F.shellContainer

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.columnRegion_subset_hull_columnUniontheorem

theorem columnRegion_subset_hull_columnUnion (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull)
  (hU : F.columnUnion ∈ hullDomain) (m : ι) : F.columnRegion m ⊆ hull F.columnUnion

Every region lies in the hull of the union, by (P2).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.hull_columnUnion_subset_shellContainertheorem

theorem hull_columnUnion_subset_shellContainer (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull)
  (hU : F.columnUnion ∈ hullDomain) (hC : F.shellContainer ∈ hulls)
  (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) : hull F.columnUnion ⊆ F.shellContainer

If the family is upper semi-compatible and the container is a hull, the hull of the union lies in the container, by (P3) and (P1).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.logVol_columnRegion_le_hulltheorem

theorem logVol_columnRegion_le_hull (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull)
  (logVol : Set X → EReal) (hmono : ∀ S T : Set X, S ⊆ T → T ∈ hullDomain → logVol S ≤ logVol T)
  (hU : F.columnUnion ∈ hullDomain) (m : ι) :
  logVol (F.columnRegion m) ≤ logVol (hull F.columnUnion)

For a region log-volume monotone into the hull domain, every region has log-volume at most that of the hull of the union.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalRegionFamily.logVol_hull_columnUnion_le_shellContainertheorem

theorem logVol_hull_columnUnion_le_shellContainer (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull)
  (logVol : Set X → EReal) (hmono : ∀ S T : Set X, S ⊆ T → T ∈ hullDomain → logVol S ≤ logVol T)
  (hU : F.columnUnion ∈ hullDomain) (hC : F.shellContainer ∈ hulls)
  (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) : logVol (hull F.columnUnion) ≤ logVol F.shellContainer

The container bounds the possible image. Under upper semi-compatibility, with the container a hull, the log-volume of the hull of the union is at most that of the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.containerOrbitdef

def containerOrbit : IndeterminacyOrbit X A := { O with baseRegion := F.shellContainer }

The orbit of the container under the same (Ind1), (Ind2).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.jointColumnImagedef

def jointColumnImage (g : O.jointGroup) (m : ι) : Set X := (g : A) • F.columnRegion m

The possible image indexed by an element of the joint group of (Ind1), (Ind2) and a vertical coordinate (Ind3).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.jointColumnUniondef

def jointColumnUnion : Set X := ⋃ (g : O.jointGroup) (m : ι), O.jointColumnImage F g m

The union of all possible images under (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.jointColumnUnion_subset_containerOrbittheorem

theorem jointColumnUnion_subset_containerOrbit (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) :
  O.jointColumnUnion F ⊆ (O.containerOrbit F).orbitUnion

Under upper semi-compatibility, the union of all possible images lies in the orbit union of the container. No stability of the container is needed.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.ContainerStabledef

def ContainerStable : Prop :=
  (∀ a ∈ O.ind1, a • F.shellContainer = F.shellContainer) ∧
    ∀ a ∈ O.ind2, a • F.shellContainer = F.shellContainer

Stability of the container under (Ind1) and (Ind2): every element of ind1 and every element of ind2 maps the container onto itself. A hypothesis; see the module docstring for what the pages say about it.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.orbitUnion_containerOrbit_eqtheorem

theorem orbitUnion_containerOrbit_eq (hs : O.ContainerStable F) :
  (O.containerOrbit F).orbitUnion = F.shellContainer

Under stability, the orbit union of the container is the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.jointColumnImage_subset_hulltheorem

theorem jointColumnImage_subset_hull (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull)
  (hJ : O.jointColumnUnion F ∈ hullDomain) (g : O.jointGroup) (m : ι) :
  O.jointColumnImage F g m ⊆ hull (O.jointColumnUnion F)

Every joint possible image lies in the hull of the union of all of them, by (P2).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.logVol_hull_jointColumnUnion_le_hull_containerOrbittheorem

theorem logVol_hull_jointColumnUnion_le_hull_containerOrbit
  (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull) (logVol : Set X → EReal)
  (hmono : ∀ S T : Set X, S ⊆ T → T ∈ hullDomain → logVol S ≤ logVol T)
  (hJ : O.jointColumnUnion F ∈ hullDomain) (hO : (O.containerOrbit F).orbitUnion ∈ hullDomain)
  (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) :
  logVol (hull (O.jointColumnUnion F)) ≤ logVol (hull (O.containerOrbit F).orbitUnion)

(Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3) together, without stability. Under upper semi-compatibility, the log-volume of the hull of the union of all possible images is at most the log-volume of the hull of the orbit union of the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.logVol_hull_jointColumnUnion_le_shellContainertheorem

theorem logVol_hull_jointColumnUnion_le_shellContainer
  (isHull : IsHullMap hullDomain hulls hull) (logVol : Set X → EReal)
  (hmono : ∀ S T : Set X, S ⊆ T → T ∈ hullDomain → logVol S ≤ logVol T)
  (hJ : O.jointColumnUnion F ∈ hullDomain) (hC : F.shellContainer ∈ hulls)
  (hs : O.ContainerStable F) (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible) :
  logVol (hull (O.jointColumnUnion F)) ≤ logVol F.shellContainer

(Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3) together, with stability. If moreover the container is a hull and is stable under (Ind1) and (Ind2), the log-volume of the hull of the union of all possible images is at most the log-volume of the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.IndeterminacyOrbit.logVolume_jointColumnImage_le_shellContainertheorem

theorem logVolume_jointColumnImage_le_shellContainer [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X)
  (h1 : ∀ a ∈ O.ind1, ∀ S : Set X, μ (a • S) = μ S)
  (h2 : ∀ a ∈ O.ind2, ∀ S : Set X, μ (a • S) = μ S) (h : F.UpperSemiCompatible)
  (g : O.jointGroup) (m : ι) :
  logVolume μ (O.jointColumnImage F g m) ≤ logVolume μ F.shellContainer

(Ind3) as an inequality from above. If every element of ind1 and of ind2 preserves μ (the abstract form of the invariance asserted in Step (x), page 181, a hypothesis) and the family is upper semi-compatible, every joint possible image has log-volume at most that of the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padicIterateFamilydef

noncomputable def padicIterateFamily (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (start : Set ℚ_[p]) :
    VerticalRegionFamily ℚ_[p] ℕ :=
  ⟨padicLogShell p, logUnitIterateRegion start {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} (padicLogUnit p)⟩

The iterate family over ℚ_p: container padicLogShell p, regions the iterates of part 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padicIterateFamily_upperSemiCompatibletheorem

theorem padicIterateFamily_upperSemiCompatible (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {start : Set ℚ_[p]}
  (hstart : start ⊆ {x | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}) : (padicIterateFamily p start).UpperSemiCompatible

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.extIterateFamilydef

noncomputable def extIterateFamily (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [NormedField K] (start : Set K) :
    VerticalRegionFamily K ℕ :=
  ⟨extLogShell p K, logUnitIterateRegion start {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} extLogUnit⟩

The iterate family in the finite extension model: container extLogShell p K.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.extIterateFamily_upperSemiCompatibletheorem

theorem extIterateFamily_upperSemiCompatible (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {K : Type*} [NormedField K]
  [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[p] K] [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] {start : Set K}
  (hstart : start ⊆ {x | ‖x‖ ≤ 1}) : (extIterateFamily p K start).UpperSemiCompatible

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padicNonzeroIntegersdef

def padicNonzeroIntegers (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Set ℚ_[p] := {x | x ≠ 0 ∧ ‖x‖ ≤ 1}

O^▷ = ℤ_p \ {0} of Remark 1.2.2 (i), page 36, as a subset of ℚ_p.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_iUnion_nonzeroIntegerstheorem

theorem padic_iUnion_nonzeroIntegers (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
  (padicIterateFamily p (padicNonzeroIntegers p)).columnUnion =
    (padicIterateFamily p (padicNonzeroIntegers p)).shellContainer

Union equal to the container. Starting from O^▷ (Remark 1.2.2 (iii)), the union of the chain over ℚ_p is the container ℤ_p: S 0 = ℤ_p \ {0} and 0 ∈ S 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.padic_two_iUnion_units_ssubsettheorem

theorem padic_two_iUnion_units_ssubset :
  (padicIterateFamily 2 {u : ℚ_[2] | ‖u‖ = 1}).columnUnion ⊂
    (padicIterateFamily 2 {u : ℚ_[2] | ‖u‖ = 1}).shellContainer

Union strictly smaller than the container. Starting from the units (Proposition 3.5 (ii) (a)) with p = 2, the union ℤ_2^× ∪ 4ℤ_2 of the chain misses 2 ∈ ℤ_2.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalExample.gapFamilydef

noncomputable def gapFamily (c : Set ℝ) : VerticalRegionFamily ℝ Bool := ⟨c, intervalImage⟩

The regions [0, 1/8] and [3/8, 1/2] of IntervalExample.intervalImage, with container c.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalExample.gapFamily_upperSemiCompatibletheorem

theorem gapFamily_upperSemiCompatible {c : Set ℝ} (hc : Icc 0 (1 / 2) ⊆ c) :
  (gapFamily c).UpperSemiCompatible

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalExample.example_gap_uniontheorem

theorem example_gap_union :
  (gapFamily (Icc 0 (1 / 2))).columnUnion ⊂ (gapFamily (Icc 0 (1 / 2))).shellContainer ∧
    hull (gapFamily (Icc 0 (1 / 2))).columnUnion = (gapFamily (Icc 0 (1 / 2))).shellContainer

Union strictly smaller, hull equal. With container [0, 1/2], the union misses 1/4, while the interval hull of the union is the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.VerticalExample.example_hull_ssubsettheorem

theorem example_hull_ssubset :
  (gapFamily (Icc 0 1)).UpperSemiCompatible ∧
    hull (gapFamily (Icc 0 1)).columnUnion ⊂ (gapFamily (Icc 0 1)).shellContainer

Hull strictly smaller. With container [0, 1], the family is upper semi-compatible and the hull [0, 1/2] of the union is strictly smaller than the container.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.WeightedPacket

IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/WeightedPacket.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Packets, IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.LabelAverage

IUT III, Remark 3.1.1 and Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii): weighted log-volumes on tensor packets

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Remark 3.1.1 (i) to (iv), pages 93 to 97; Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii), pages 115 to 117; Remark 3.9.5 (i), (ii), page 127. Pages read for this file: 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 115, 116, 117 and 127. Pages checked against rendered images: all of them; the displays of page 94 and the normalization sentence of page 115 also at a higher resolution.

What the pages print
  • Page 94, Remark 3.1.1 (ii). For v ∈ 𝕍 the log-volume on the portion of 𝔩𝔬𝔤(^α ℱ_v) corresponding to K_v is considered "relative to the weight [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1}"; for direct sums over all v ∈ 𝕍 over a given v_ℚ, "the normalized weight" 1 / ([K_v : (F_mod)_v] · (Σ_{𝕍_mod ∋ w | v_ℚ} [(F_mod)_w : ℚ_{v_ℚ}])), "normalized so that multiplication by p_{v_ℚ} affects log-volumes by addition or subtraction [...] of the quantity log(p_{v_ℚ})". For the tensor product of the K_{v_α}, α ∈ A, the weight 1 / Π_{α ∈ A} [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}], and for direct sums over all choices of {v_α}_{α ∈ A} the normalized weight 1 / ((Π_{α ∈ A} [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}]) · {Σ_{{w_α}_{α ∈ A}} (Π_{α ∈ A} [(F_mod)_{w_α} : ℚ_{v_ℚ}])}), "where the sum is over all collections {w_α}_{α ∈ A} of [not necessarily distinct!] elements w_α ∈ 𝕍_mod lying over v_ℚ".
  • Page 93, Proposition 3.1 (i), (ii), and page 94, Remark 3.1.1 (i): the ind-topological ring 𝔩𝔬𝔤(^A ℱ_{v_ℚ}) is an inductive limit of direct sums of fields, and the integral structures are copies of 𝒪_{k̄}.
  • Page 95, Remark 3.1.1 (iii): "such weighted sums of log-volumes do not, in general, arise as some positive real multiple of the [natural] logarithm of a 'volume' or 'measure' in the usual sense of measure theory"; they are clear on a "direct product region" (a direct product of compact subsets of positive measure in each of the direct summands), and "may be computed for, say, arbitrary Borel sets" by the construction of (iv), with V = Π_{α ∈ A} 𝕍_{v_ℚ} and (page 96) N_v = Π_{α ∈ A} [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}]; "the result of multiplying the [natural] logarithm of the '𝓔-weighted measure μ_𝓔(−)' of (iv) by a suitable normalization factor [i.e., a suitable positive real number] yields the weighted sums of log-volumes".
  • Pages 96 and 97, Remark 3.1.1 (iv): E = Π_{v'} E_{v'}, E_{≠v} = Π_{v' ≠ v} E_{v'}, W = ⨿_{v'} E_{≠v'} × {v'}, M_{E*V} ≅ M_W, S_E = {Π_{e ∈ E} S} ∩ M_{E*V}, and for a direct product region S = Π_v S_v: (1/N_𝓔) · μ^log_𝓔(S) = Σ_{v ∈ V} (1/N_v) · μ^log_v(S_v), N_𝓔 = Π_{v ∈ V} N_v.
  • Page 115, Proposition 3.9 (i): the log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_ℚ}, μ^log_{A,v_ℚ}, μ^log_{A,α,v} on nonempty compact open subsets, determined by the p_{v_ℚ}-adic log-volume on each direct summand field "together with the discussion of normalized weights in Remark 3.1.1, (ii), (iii), (iv)", such that the integral structures have log-volume zero, and "normalized so that multiplication of an element of 𝔐(−) by p_v corresponds to adding the quantity −log(p_v)": the packet-normalization. Page 116: the archimedean analogue (radial log-volumes; multiplication by e adds 1 = log(e)); μ^log_{A,v_ℚ} is invariant under permutations of A; for a procession, the log-volumes are normalized "by taking the average, over the various capsules under consideration": the procession-normalization. Proposition 3.9 (ii), pages 116 and 117: the same on the mono-analytic log-shells, and the average of the packet-normalized log-volumes gives procession-normalized log-volumes.
  • Page 127, Remark 3.9.5 (i), (ii): for a subset that contains a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume, the holomorphic hull λ · 𝒪 of the subset, when it is relatively compact, is a direct product region (ℍ ⊆ ℙ), so its packet-normalized log-volume is a weighted sum of the kind computed here; see PacketHull.lean for the hull on a product of fields.
What is formalized

Weights (plain inputs e(v) = [K_v : (F_mod)_v], f(v) = [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}], a finite set V of places over v_ℚ, a finite label set A; tuples are t : A → V, and A = Fin (j + 1) gives V^{j+1}). wPktWeight is the normalized weight of page 94 exactly as printed; wPktDenom_eq_pow: its denominator sum is (Σ_v f(v)) ^ |A|. wPkt_weight_dim_sum: Σ_t w_t · dim_t = 1, with dim_t = Π_α e(v_α) f(v_α) the dimension of the summand; the weights themselves sum to (Σ_v 1/e(v)) ^ |A| / (Σ_v f(v)) ^ |A| (wPkt_weight_sum), which is 1/2 for one place with e = 2, f = 1 and one label (wPkt_weight_sum_example).

Real packets. Fields F v (the role of (F_mod)_v) and K v (the role of K_v), finite over ℚ_p, with K v a finite extension of F v; e, f are their degrees (wPktE, wPktF), and [K_v : ℚ_p] = e(v) f(v) is the tower law (wPkt_finrank_tower). The summand of t is the packet ⊗_α K_{v_α} (PiTensorProduct over ℚ_p). wPktSummandLogVol is its unnormalized log-volume L_t (logarithm of a Haar measure, zero on the integral elements; it is dim_t times padicPacketMuLog). wPktLogVol is the weighted sum Σ_t w_t · L_t(X_t) on a direct product region Π_t X_t.

  • Tests (wPkt_logVol_integral, wPkt_logVol_zpow_smul, wPkt_logVol_integral_zpow): the integral structure has log-volume 0; multiplying every component by p ^ n subtracts exactly n log p.
  • Double division (wPkt_doubleDivision_zpow_smul): the page's weights applied to log-volumes already divided by the dimension shift by −n (Σ_t w_t) log p, which differs from −n log p in general. So, in general, only the unnormalized L_t give the printed normalization with the printed weights (the other reading passes when Σ_t w_t = 1); the pages do not state which is meant.

Comparison with the Haar normalization of the whole packet (scope: model_test in the records). For a ℚ_p-algebra isomorphism G from a finite ℚ_p-algebra W onto Π_t ⊗_α K_{v_α} (the decomposition of Proposition 3.1 (i); an input here), the log-volume of W normalized by its dimension (padicPacketMuLog, as in Packets.lean) is Σ_t (1/dim W) · L_t(X_t) with dim W = (Σ_v e(v) f(v)) ^ |A| (wPkt_haar_region; the general form for summands that are packets is wPkt_muLog_pi_region). In terms of the per-dimension log-volumes L_t / dim_t of Packets.lean, the Haar weights are dim_t / dim W, the page's are w_t · dim_t = Π_α f(v_α) / (Σ_v f(v)) ^ |A|. The result:

  • wPkt_weight_eq_haar_mul: w_t = (1/dim W) · Π_α (ē / e(v_α)), with ē = Σ_v e(v) f(v) / Σ_v f(v).
  • wPkt_weight_eq_haar_iff: in the reading of this module, for nonempty label and place sets and positive degrees, the two normalizations have the same weights for every tuple if and only if [K_v : (F_mod)_v] is the same at all places over p; then the two log-volumes agree on every direct product region (wPkt_logVol_eq_haar_of_const). In general they differ by Σ_t (w_t − 1/dim W) · L_t(X_t) (wPkt_logVol_sub_haar).
  • Both normalizations pass both tests (both weight systems give total 1 against dim_t), so the tests do not determine the weights. wPkt_scaled_integral and wPkt_coeff_example: for e = (1, 2), f = (1, 1), one label and the region p · 𝒪 on the first summand, 𝒪 on the second, the coefficients of −log p are 1/2 (page) and 1/3 (Haar).

Procession-normalization (wPktProcAvg, wPktProcLogVol): the average over a finite nonempty set J of capsules, the capsule j with its own label set L j, of the packet-normalized log-volumes; the two tests hold (wPkt_procLogVol_integral, wPkt_procLogVol_zpow_smul). The abstract layer is an instance: on real values equalWeightAverage of Comparison.lean is wPktProcAvg (wPktProcAvg_eq_equalWeightAverage), and labelAverage of LabelAverage.lean is wPktProcAvg over 𝔽_l^⋇ (wPktProcAvg_eq_labelAverage). The abstract layer takes the per-label values as free inputs; here they are the weighted log-volumes of real packets.

Remark 3.1.1 (iv) (wPktEMeasure, wPkt_EMeasure_log): the 𝓔-weighted measure, defined on all subsets of M_V through M_W (the page's homeomorphism M_{E*V} ≅ M_W is used as the definition of the measure space), and the display of page 97 on direct product regions, for any finite V, nonempty finite E_v and σ-finite measures.

The warning of page 95, made precise in a model (scope: model_test): wPkt_warning_forces_equal, wPkt_warning_iff: on ℝ × ℝ with Lebesgue measure on each factor and positive weights a, b, there are a measure ν on ℝ × ℝ and c > 0 with c · log ν(S₁ × S₂) = a log vol(S₁) + b log vol(S₂) for all direct product regions if and only if a = b. The regions used are [0, 1/4] × [0, 1], [1/2, 3/4] × [0, 1] and their union (itself a direct product region), and the same with the factors exchanged. This concerns measures on the product space itself; the 𝓔-weighted measure of (iv) lives on M_W, and its logarithm, scaled by 1/N_𝓔, does give the weighted sum (wPkt_EMeasure_log).

Interpretation choices
  1. The places of 𝕍 over v_ℚ and of 𝕍_mod over v_ℚ are identified (the natural bijection of page 94); V stands for both.
  2. The log-volume on a summand that the weights multiply is the unnormalized one (natural logarithm of a Haar measure, zero on the integral elements). Under this reading the page's normalization sentence holds for all degrees (wPkt_weight_dim_sum); under the other reading (log-volumes divided by the dimension of the summand) it fails in general, though it holds when Σ_t w_t = 1 (wPkt_doubleDivision_zpow_smul). The pages do not decide between the two.
  3. The summands are the packets ⊗_α K_{v_α} over ℚ_p, not their decompositions into fields; the log-volume of a packet is additive over its fields (packet_muLog_pi_region), so nothing changes on regions that are products over the fields as well.
  4. Page 115 writes p_v (with v underlined) where page 94 writes p_{v_ℚ}; both are the residue characteristic p.
Not proved
  • The decomposition ⊗_α (Π_v K_v) ≅ Π_t ⊗_α K_{v_α} (Proposition 3.1 (i) for finite levels): it is an input G of the comparison theorems.
  • The inductive limits of Proposition 3.1 (the algebraic closures k̄, 𝒪_{k̄}): only finite levels K_v are treated.
  • Weighted log-volumes of regions that are not direct product regions, other than through the 𝓔-weighted measure; that μ_𝓔 restricted to direct product regions is the page's choice of extension, and the "suitable normalization factor" of page 96 between (1/N_𝓔) μ^log_𝓔 and the normalized weights (it is the constant 1 / Σ_{{w_α}} Π_α [(F_mod)_{w_α} : ℚ_{v_ℚ}], which the pages do not display).
  • Archimedean places: the weights are the same formula (page 94, with v_ℚ ∈ 𝕍_ℚ^arc), and the arithmetic of wPktWeight applies to any positive degrees; the radial log-volume, the normalization by e of page 116 and the archimedean summands are not formalized.
  • Proposition 3.9 (ii) on mono-analytic log-shells, (iii) and (iv); the sizes of the capsules of a procession (Proposition 3.4, not read for this file): the label sets L j are inputs.
  • Nothing here computes either side of Corollary 3.12: all regions are inputs.
