IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktDenomdef

def wPktDenom (f : V → ℕ) (A : Type) [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] : ℕ :=
  ∑ w : A → V, ∏ α, f (w α)

The sum Σ_{w : A → V} Π_{α ∈ A} f(w_α) in the denominator of the normalized weight of page 94, over all collections {w_α}_{α ∈ A} of not necessarily distinct places over v_ℚ; f(w) = [(F_mod)_w : ℚ_{v_ℚ}].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktWeightdef

noncomputable def wPktWeight (e f : V → ℕ) (t : A → V) : ℝ :=
  1 / ((∏ α, (e (t α) : ℝ)) * (wPktDenom f A : ℝ))

The normalized weight of page 94 of the tuple t = {v_α}_{α ∈ A}: 1 / ((Π_α [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}]) · Σ_{{w_α}} Π_α [(F_mod)_{w_α} : ℚ_{v_ℚ}]), with e(v) = [K_v : (F_mod)_v] and f(v) = [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktDimdef

def wPktDim (e f : V → ℕ) (t : A → V) : ℕ :=
  ∏ α, e (t α) * f (t α)

The dimension over ℚ_{v_ℚ} of the summand ⊗_α K_{v_α} of the tuple t: Π_α [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}] · [(F_mod)_{v_α} : ℚ_{v_ℚ}].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktDenom_eq_powtheorem

theorem wPktDenom_eq_pow (f : V → ℕ) : wPktDenom f A = (∑ v, f v) ^ Fintype.card A

The denominator is a power: Σ_{w : A → V} Π_α f(w_α) = (Σ_v f(v)) ^ |A|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktDenom_postheorem

theorem wPktDenom_pos [Nonempty V] {f : V → ℕ} (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) : 0 < wPktDenom f A

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_weight_dim_sumtheorem

theorem wPkt_weight_dim_sum [Nonempty V] {e f : V → ℕ} (he : ∀ v, 0 < e v)
  (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) :
  ∑ t : A → V, wPktWeight e f t * (wPktDim e f t : ℝ) = 1

The weights times the dimensions sum to one: Σ_t w_t · dim_t = 1. This is the normalization that makes multiplication by p subtract exactly log p from the weighted sum of unnormalized log-volumes (wPkt_logVol_zpow_smul).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_weight_sumtheorem

theorem wPkt_weight_sum (e f : V → ℕ) :
  ∑ t : A → V, wPktWeight e f t =
    (∑ v, (e v : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ Fintype.card A / ((∑ v, f v : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card A

The weights alone do not sum to one: Σ_t w_t = (Σ_v 1/e(v)) ^ |A| / (Σ_v f(v)) ^ |A|. A weighted sum of log-volumes that are already divided by the dimension (the normalization of padicPacketMuLog) shifts under multiplication by p by −(Σ_t w_t) log p (wPkt_doubleDivision_zpow_smul), which differs from −log p in general (wPkt_weight_sum_example).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_weight_sum_exampletheorem

theorem wPkt_weight_sum_example :
  ∑ t : Unit → Unit, wPktWeight (fun _ => 2) (fun _ => 1) t = 1 / 2

The double-division test, numerically: one place with [K_v : (F_mod)_v] = 2, [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_p] = 1, and one label. The weights sum to 1/2, not 1.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktHaarCoeffdef

noncomputable def wPktHaarCoeff (e f : V → ℕ) (A : Type) [Fintype A] : ℝ :=
  1 / ((∑ v, e v * f v : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ Fintype.card A

The coefficient of the unnormalized log-volume of each summand in the log-volume of the whole packet normalized by its dimension (packet_muLog_pi_region, wPkt_haar_region): 1 / dim = 1 / (Σ_v [K_v : (F_mod)_v] · [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_p]) ^ |A|, the same for every tuple.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_dim_sumtheorem

theorem wPkt_dim_sum (e f : V → ℕ) :
  ∑ t : A → V, wPktDim e f t = (∑ v, e v * f v) ^ Fintype.card A

The dimension of the whole packet: Σ_t dim_t = (Σ_v e(v) f(v)) ^ |A|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktMeanDegdef

noncomputable def wPktMeanDeg (e f : V → ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((∑ v, e v * f v : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((∑ v, f v : ℕ) : ℝ)

The f-weighted mean ē = (Σ_v e(v) f(v)) / (Σ_v f(v)) of the local degrees [K_v : (F_mod)_v].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_weight_eq_haar_multheorem

theorem wPkt_weight_eq_haar_mul [Nonempty V] {e f : V → ℕ} (he : ∀ v, 0 < e v)
  (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) (t : A → V) :
  wPktWeight e f t = wPktHaarCoeff e f A * ∏ α, (wPktMeanDeg e f / (e (t α) : ℝ))

The page's weight is the Haar coefficient times an explicit factor: w_t = (1 / dim) · Π_α (ē / [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}]).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_weight_eq_haar_ifftheorem

theorem wPkt_weight_eq_haar_iff [Nonempty V] [Nonempty A] {e f : V → ℕ} (he : ∀ v, 0 < e v)
  (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) :
  (∀ t : A → V, wPktWeight e f t = wPktHaarCoeff e f A) ↔ ∀ v v', e v = e v'

When the two normalizations agree: for at least one label (nonempty A and V, positive degrees), the page's weights equal the Haar coefficient 1 / dim for every tuple if and only if the local degree [K_v : (F_mod)_v] is the same at all places over p. This compares the two weight systems in the reading of this module (choice 2 of the module docstring).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktEdef

noncomputable def wPktE (v : V) : ℕ := Module.finrank (F v) (K v)

e(v) = [K_v : (F_mod)_v], the local degree of the field K v over the field F v.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktFdef

noncomputable def wPktF (v : V) : ℕ := Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (F v)

f(v) = [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_p].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_finrank_towertheorem

theorem wPkt_finrank_tower (v : V) :
  Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (K v) = wPktE F K v * wPktF p F v

The tower law [K_v : ℚ_p] = [K_v : (F_mod)_v] · [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_p].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktE_postheorem

theorem wPktE_pos (v : V) : 0 < wPktE F K v

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktF_postheorem

theorem wPktF_pos (v : V) : 0 < wPktF p F v

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktSummandabbrev

abbrev wPktSummand (t : A → V) : Type := PiTensorProduct ℚ_[p] (fun α => K (t α))

The summand ⊗_{α ∈ A} K_{v_α} of the tuple t = {v_α} (tensor product over ℚ_p).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_summand_finranktheorem

theorem wPkt_summand_finrank (t : A → V) :
  Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t) = wPktDim (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t

dim_{ℚ_p} ⊗_α K_{v_α} = Π_α [K_{v_α} : (F_mod)_{v_α}] [(F_mod)_{v_α} : ℚ_p].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktSummandLogVoldef

noncomputable def wPktSummandLogVol (t : A → V) (X : Set (wPktSummand p K t)) : ℝ :=
  (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t) : ℝ) *
    padicPacketMuLog p (wPktSummand p K t) (μ t) (packetNormalizationSet p _) X

The unnormalized log-volume L_t on the summand of the tuple t: the logarithm of a Haar measure, normalized so that the integral elements (R_E)^∼ have log-volume 0 (multiplication by p subtracts dim_t · log p). It is dim_t times padicPacketMuLog, which divides by the dimension.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktLogVoldef

noncomputable def wPktLogVol (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ t, wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t * wPktSummandLogVol p K μ t (X t)

**The packet-normalized log-volume of a direct product region Π_t X_t** (Remark 3.1.1 (ii), (iii); Proposition 3.9 (i)): Σ_t w_t · L_t(X_t) with the normalized weights of page 94.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_logVol_integraltheorem

theorem wPkt_logVol_integral :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ (fun t => packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) = 0

Test 1: the integral structure Π_t (R_E)^∼_t has packet-normalized log-volume 0.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_summand_integraltheorem

theorem wPkt_summand_integral (t : A → V) :
  μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun ''
      packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) ≠ 0 ∧
    μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun ''
      packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) ≠ ⊤ ∧
    ∀ n : ℤ, padicPacketMuLog p (wPktSummand p K t) (μ t)
      (packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t))
      (((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) =
        -(n * Real.log p)

The integral elements of a summand have positive finite Haar measure, and μ^log(p ^ n · (R_E)^∼) = −n log p (IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (i), Packets.lean).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_summandLogVol_zpow_smultheorem

theorem wPkt_summandLogVol_zpow_smul (t : A → V) {X : Set (wPktSummand p K t)}
  (hX0 : μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X) ≠ 0)
  (hX : μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X) ≠ ⊤) (n : ℤ) :
  wPktSummandLogVol p K μ t (((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • X) =
    wPktSummandLogVol p K μ t X -
      n * Real.log p * (wPktDim (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t : ℝ)

The scaling law of L_t.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_logVol_zpow_smultheorem

theorem wPkt_logVol_zpow_smul [Nonempty V] (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ ⊤)
  (n : ℤ) :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ (fun t => ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • X t) =
    wPktLogVol p F K μ X - n * Real.log p

Test 2: multiplying every component of a direct product region (of positive finite measures) by p ^ n subtracts exactly n · log p from the packet-normalized log-volume (Proposition 3.9 (i), page 115, for n = 1).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_logVol_integral_zpowtheorem

theorem wPkt_logVol_integral_zpow [Nonempty V] (n : ℤ) :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ (fun t => ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) •
    packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) = -(n * Real.log p)

Test 2 on the integral structure: Π_t p ^ n · (R_E)^∼_t has packet-normalized log-volume −n log p; for n = 1 this is the normalization printed on page 115.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_doubleDivision_zpow_smultheorem

theorem wPkt_doubleDivision_zpow_smul (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ ⊤)
  (n : ℤ) :
  ∑ t, wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t *
      padicPacketMuLog p (wPktSummand p K t) (μ t) (packetNormalizationSet p _)
        (((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • X t) =
    ∑ t, wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t *
      padicPacketMuLog p (wPktSummand p K t) (μ t) (packetNormalizationSet p _) (X t) -
      n * Real.log p * ∑ t : A → V, wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t

The double-division test on real packets: if the page's weights are applied to the log-volumes padicPacketMuLog that are already divided by the dimension, multiplication by p ^ n shifts the weighted sum by −n (Σ_t w_t) log p, and Σ_t w_t ≠ 1 in general (wPkt_weight_sum, wPkt_weight_sum_example).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_muLog_pi_regiontheorem

theorem wPkt_muLog_pi_region {J : Type*} [Fintype J] (B : J → Type*) [∀ j, CommRing (B j)]
  [∀ j, Algebra ℚ_[p] (B j)] [∀ j, FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] (B j)]
  (hU : ∀ j, Algebra.FormallyUnramified ℚ_[p] (B j)) (hN : ∀ j, Nontrivial (B j))
  (G : W ≃ₐ[ℚ_[p]] Π j, B j)
  [∀ j, MeasurableSpace (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (B j)) → ℚ_[p])]
  [∀ j, BorelSpace (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (B j)) → ℚ_[p])]
  (μ : ∀ j, Measure (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (B j)) → ℚ_[p]))
  [∀ j, (μ j).IsAddHaarMeasure] (S : ∀ j, Set (B j))
  (hS0 : ∀ j, μ j ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (B j)).equivFun '' S j) ≠ 0)
  (hS : ∀ j, μ j ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (B j)).equivFun '' S j) ≠ ⊤) :
  padicPacketMuLog p W ν (packetNormalizationSet p W) (G ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi S) =
    ∑ j, ((Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (B j) : ℝ) / Module.finrank ℚ_[p] W) *
      padicPacketMuLog p (B j) (μ j) (packetNormalizationSet p (B j)) (S j)

Product regions in a decomposition into formally unramified summands: for a ℚ_p-algebra isomorphism G : W ≃ Π_j B_j onto a finite product of finite formally unramified ℚ_p-algebras (not necessarily fields) and sets S_j of positive finite measure, μ^log_W(G⁻¹(Π_j S_j)) = Σ_j (dim B_j / dim W) · μ^log_j(S_j), each normalized at its integral elements. This is packet_muLog_pi_region with summands that are packets instead of fields.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_haar_regiontheorem

theorem wPkt_haar_region (G : W ≃ₐ[ℚ_[p]] Π t : A → V, wPktSummand p K t)
  (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ ⊤) :
  padicPacketMuLog p W ν (packetNormalizationSet p W) (G ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi X) =
    ∑ t, wPktHaarCoeff (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) A * wPktSummandLogVol p K μ t (X t)

The Haar normalization on the whole packet in terms of the summands: for a ℚ_p-algebra isomorphism G from W (the whole packet) onto Π_t ⊗_α K_{v_α} (the decomposition of Proposition 3.1 (i), taken here as an input) and a direct product region Π_t X_t, the log-volume of W normalized by its dimension is Σ_t (1 / dim W) · L_t(X_t), with dim W = (Σ_v [K_v : ℚ_p]) ^ |A|.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_logVol_sub_haartheorem

theorem wPkt_logVol_sub_haar (G : W ≃ₐ[ℚ_[p]] Π t : A → V, wPktSummand p K t)
  (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ ⊤) :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ X - padicPacketMuLog p W ν (packetNormalizationSet p W)
      (G ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi X) =
    ∑ t, (wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t - wPktHaarCoeff (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) A) *
      wPktSummandLogVol p K μ t (X t)

The page's weighted sum against the Haar normalization: on a direct product region the difference is Σ_t (w_t − 1/dim W) · L_t(X_t); when [K_v : (F_mod)_v] is the same at all places the two coincide (wPkt_weight_eq_haar_iff). Both sides are taken in the reading of this module (choice 2 of the module docstring).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_logVol_eq_haar_of_consttheorem

theorem wPkt_logVol_eq_haar_of_const [Nonempty V] (hc : ∀ v v', wPktE F K v = wPktE F K v')
  (G : W ≃ₐ[ℚ_[p]] Π t : A → V, wPktSummand p K t)
  (X : ∀ t : A → V, Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ t, μ t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X t) ≠ ⊤) :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ X =
    padicPacketMuLog p W ν (packetNormalizationSet p W) (G ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi X)

Equal local degrees: if [K_v : (F_mod)_v] does not depend on v, the packet-normalized log-volume wPktLogVol of a direct product region (the page's weights, in the reading of this module) equals the log-volume of the whole packet normalized by its dimension.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_scaled_integraltheorem

theorem wPkt_scaled_integral (k : (A → V) → ℤ) (G : W ≃ₐ[ℚ_[p]] Π t : A → V, wPktSummand p K t) :
  wPktLogVol p F K μ (fun t => ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ k t) •
      packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) =
    -(Real.log p * ∑ t, wPktWeight (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t * k t *
      (wPktDim (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t : ℝ)) ∧
  padicPacketMuLog p W ν (packetNormalizationSet p W) (G ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi (fun t =>
      ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ k t) • packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t))) =
    -(Real.log p * ∑ t, wPktHaarCoeff (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) A * k t *
      (wPktDim (wPktE F K) (wPktF p F) t : ℝ))

**The regions Π_t p ^ {k_t} · (R_E)^∼_t**: the page's normalization gives −log p · Σ_t w_t k_t dim_t and the Haar normalization −log p · Σ_t k_t dim_t / dim W. Both satisfy the two tests (k constant); they differ in general (wPkt_coeff_example).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_coeff_exampletheorem

theorem wPkt_coeff_example :
  ∑ t : Unit → Bool, wPktWeight (fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else 1) (fun _ => 1) t *
      ((if t () then 0 else 1 : ℤ) : ℝ) *
      (wPktDim (fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else 1) (fun _ => 1) t : ℝ) = 1 / 2 ∧
  ∑ t : Unit → Bool, wPktHaarCoeff (fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else 1) (fun _ => 1) Unit *
      ((if t () then 0 else 1 : ℤ) : ℝ) *
      (wPktDim (fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else 1) (fun _ => 1) t : ℝ) = 1 / 3

The two normalizations differ, numerically: two places over p with [K_v : (F_mod)_v] = 1, 2 and [(F_mod)_v : ℚ_p] = 1, 1, one label, and the region p · (R_E)^∼ on the first summand, (R_E)^∼ on the second (k = 1, 0). The coefficient of −log p is 1/2 for the page's weights and 1/3 for the Haar normalization (wPkt_scaled_integral).

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcAvgdef

noncomputable def wPktProcAvg (v : J → ℝ) : ℝ := (Fintype.card J : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j, v j

The average (1/|J|) Σ_j v_j over the capsules of a procession (Proposition 3.9 (i), page 116: "which we normalize by taking the average, over the various capsules").

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcAvg_consttheorem

theorem wPktProcAvg_const [Nonempty J] (c : ℝ) : wPktProcAvg (fun _ : J => c) = c

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcAvg_subtheorem

theorem wPktProcAvg_sub [Nonempty J] (v : J → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
  wPktProcAvg (fun j => v j - c) = wPktProcAvg v - c

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcAvg_eq_equalWeightAveragetheorem

theorem wPktProcAvg_eq_equalWeightAverage (v : J → ℝ) :
  ((wPktProcAvg v : ℝ) : EReal) = equalWeightAverage (fun j => (v j : EReal))

The abstract layer's average is this one: on real values, equalWeightAverage of Comparison.lean is the procession average.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcAvg_eq_labelAveragetheorem

theorem wPktProcAvg_eq_labelAverage {l : ℕ} (hl : Odd l) [Fintype (NonzeroLabel l)]
  (v : NonzeroLabel l → ℝ) :
  ((wPktProcAvg v : ℝ) : EReal) = labelAverage l (fun j => (v j : EReal))

**The label average of LabelAverage.lean is this one** over 𝔽_l^⋇.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktProcLogVoldef

noncomputable def wPktProcLogVol (X : ∀ j (t : L j → V), Set (wPktSummand p K t)) : ℝ :=
  wPktProcAvg (fun j => wPktLogVol p F K (μ j) (X j))

The procession-normalized log-volume (Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii), page 116): the average over the capsules j ∈ J of the packet-normalized log-volumes, the capsule j having label set L j.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_procLogVol_integraltheorem

theorem wPkt_procLogVol_integral :
  wPktProcLogVol p F K μ (fun _ t => packetNormalizationSet p (wPktSummand p K t)) = 0

Test 1 for the procession: the integral structures have procession-normalized log-volume 0.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_procLogVol_zpow_smultheorem

theorem wPkt_procLogVol_zpow_smul [Nonempty J] [Nonempty V]
  (X : ∀ j (t : L j → V), Set (wPktSummand p K t))
  (hX0 : ∀ j t, μ j t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X j t) ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ j t, μ j t ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (wPktSummand p K t)).equivFun '' X j t) ≠ ⊤)
  (n : ℤ) :
  wPktProcLogVol p F K μ (fun j t => ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • X j t) =
    wPktProcLogVol p F K μ X - n * Real.log p

Test 2 for the procession: multiplying every component of every capsule's region by p ^ n subtracts exactly n · log p.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktENeabbrev

abbrev wPktENe (v : V) : Type := ∀ v' : {v' : V // v' ≠ v}, E v'

E_{≠v} = Π_{v' ≠ v} E_{v'}.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktWIdxabbrev

abbrev wPktWIdx : Type := Σ v : V, wPktENe E v

W = ⨿_{v ∈ V} E_{≠v} × {v}, as a sigma type over V.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPktEMeasuredef

noncomputable def wPktEMeasure (S : Set (∀ v, M v)) : ENNReal :=
  Measure.pi (fun w : wPktWIdx E => μ w.1)
    {m | ∀ e : ∀ v, E v, (fun v => m ⟨v, fun v' => e v'⟩) ∈ S}

**The 𝓔-weighted measure of page 97**: μ_𝓔(S) is the product measure on M_W = Π_{w ∈ W} M_{π(w)} of the set of m such that, for every e ∈ E, the point (m_{(e_{≠v}, v)})_{v ∈ V} lies in S. Under the homeomorphism M_{E*V} ≅ M_W of page 96 this set is S_E = {Π_{e ∈ E} S} ∩ M_{E*V}.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_ESet_pitheorem

theorem wPkt_ESet_pi (hE : ∀ v, Nonempty (E v)) (S : ∀ v, Set (M v)) :
  {m : ∀ w : wPktWIdx E, M w.1 |
      ∀ e : ∀ v, E v, (fun v => m ⟨v, fun v' => e v'⟩) ∈ Set.univ.pi S} =
    Set.univ.pi (fun w : wPktWIdx E => S w.1)

For a direct product S = Π_v S_v and nonempty E_v, the set defining μ_𝓔(S) is the product Π_{w ∈ W} S_{π(w)}.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_EMeasure_logtheorem

theorem wPkt_EMeasure_log (hE : ∀ v, Nonempty (E v)) (S : ∀ v, Set (M v))
  (hS0 : ∀ v, μ v (S v) ≠ 0) (hS : ∀ v, μ v (S v) ≠ ⊤) :
  (1 / (∏ v, (Fintype.card (E v) : ℝ))) *
      Real.log (wPktEMeasure E μ (Set.univ.pi S)).toReal =
    ∑ v, (1 / (Fintype.card (E v) : ℝ)) * Real.log (μ v (S v)).toReal

The display of page 97: for a direct product region S = Π_v S_v with 0 < μ_v(S_v) < ∞ and nonempty E_v of cardinality N_v, (1/N_𝓔) · log μ_𝓔(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v) · log μ_v(S_v), where N_𝓔 = Π_v N_v.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_split_forcestheorem

theorem wPkt_split_forces (a c xP xQ xU : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hxP : 0 ≤ xP) (hxQ : 0 ≤ xQ)
  (hU : xU = xP + xQ) (h1 : c * Real.log xP = a * Real.log (1 / 4))
  (h2 : c * Real.log xQ = a * Real.log (1 / 4)) (h3 : c * Real.log xU = a * Real.log (1 / 2)) :
  a = c

An elementary step: if x_U = x_P + x_Q and c log x_P = c log x_Q = a log(1/4), c log x_U = a log(1/2) with a > 0, then a = c.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_model_factstheorem

theorem wPkt_model_facts :
  IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 4)) ∧ IsCompact (Icc (1 / 2 : ℝ) (3 / 4)) ∧
    IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 4) ∪ Icc (1 / 2) (3 / 4)) ∧ IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧
    (volume (Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 4))).toReal = 1 / 4 ∧
    (volume (Icc (1 / 2 : ℝ) (3 / 4))).toReal = 1 / 4 ∧
    (volume (Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 4) ∪ Icc (1 / 2) (3 / 4))).toReal = 1 / 2 ∧
    (volume (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)).toReal = 1 ∧
    Disjoint (Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 / 4)) (Icc (1 / 2) (3 / 4))

The three intervals of the model: P = [0, 1/4], Q = [1/2, 3/4], I = [0, 1].

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_warning_forces_equaltheorem

theorem wPkt_warning_forces_equal {a b c : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (ν : Measure (ℝ × ℝ))
  (h : ∀ S₁ S₂ : Set ℝ, IsCompact S₁ → IsCompact S₂ → volume S₁ ≠ 0 → volume S₂ ≠ 0 →
    c * Real.log (ν (S₁ ×ˢ S₂)).toReal =
      a * Real.log (volume S₁).toReal + b * Real.log (volume S₂).toReal) :
  a = c ∧ b = c

The warning of page 95, in a model: on M_1 × M_2 = ℝ × ℝ with Lebesgue measure on each factor, let a, b > 0 be weights. If some measure ν on ℝ × ℝ and some real c satisfy c · log ν(S₁ × S₂) = a · log vol(S₁) + b · log vol(S₂) for all direct product regions (compact S₁, S₂ of positive measure), then a = c = b. So for unequal weights the weighted sum of log-volumes is not a multiple of the logarithm of any measure on the product.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_equal_weights_measuretheorem

theorem wPkt_equal_weights_measure (a : ℝ) (S₁ S₂ : Set ℝ) (h₁ : IsCompact S₁)
  (h₂ : IsCompact S₂) (h₁0 : volume S₁ ≠ 0) (h₂0 : volume S₂ ≠ 0) :
  a * Real.log (volume (S₁ ×ˢ S₂)).toReal =
    a * Real.log (volume S₁).toReal + a * Real.log (volume S₂).toReal

Equal weights do arise from a measure: with ν the product Lebesgue measure and c = a, a · log ν(S₁ × S₂) = a · log vol(S₁) + a · log vol(S₂) for all compact S₁, S₂ of positive measure.

IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.wPkt_warning_ifftheorem

theorem wPkt_warning_iff {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) :
  (∃ (ν : Measure (ℝ × ℝ)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c ∧
    ∀ S₁ S₂ : Set ℝ, IsCompact S₁ → IsCompact S₂ → volume S₁ ≠ 0 → volume S₂ ≠ 0 →
      c * Real.log (ν (S₁ ×ˢ S₂)).toReal =
        a * Real.log (volume S₁).toReal + b * Real.log (volume S₂).toReal) ↔ a = b

The model statement in both directions: for positive weights a, b, a measure ν on ℝ × ℝ and a constant c > 0 with c · log ν(S₁ × S₂) = a log vol(S₁) + b log vol(S₂) on all direct product regions exist if and only if a = b.

IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.HullOperator

IUT/PaperIII/Remark3_9_5/HullOperator.lean

IUT III, Remark 3.9.5 (ii): the order-theoretic characterization of the hull map

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Remark 3.9.5, (i), (ii), pages 126 to 128. Pages 126 to 145 (all of Remark 3.9.5) were read from the extracted text; page 127, which carries the displays of (i) and (ii), was checked against a rendered image.

What the paper says

Remark 3.9.5 (i) defines the holomorphic hull of a suitable subset U of a tensor packet ℐ^ℚ(−) as the smallest subset of the form λ · 𝒪 containing U. Remark 3.9.5 (ii) writes ℙ for the set of direct product regions and ℍ ⊆ ℙ for the set of hulls, and asserts that forming the hull is a map φ : ℙ → ℍ that "may be characterized uniquely" by

  • (P1) φ(H) = H for every H ∈ ℍ;
  • (P2) P ⊆ φ(P) for every P ∈ ℙ;
  • (P3) φ(P₁) ⊆ φ(P₂) whenever P₁ ⊆ P₂ in ℙ.

It then says that, since any intersection of elements of ℍ which is itself of finite log-volume necessarily determines an element of ℍ (the qualifier "of finite log-volume" applies to the intersection, not to the members intersected), it "follows formally" from (P1), (P2), (P3) that φ(P) is the intersection of all H ∈ ℍ containing P.

What this file is and is not

This file is not a formalization of holomorphic hulls or of Remark 3.9.5. Tensor packets, log-shells and direct product regions are not formalized. It checks the order-theoretic part of Remark 3.9.5 (ii) for arbitrary families 𝓗 ⊆ 𝓟 of subsets of an arbitrary type:

  • IsHullMap.eq_sInter: (P1), (P2), (P3), together with ℍ ⊆ ℙ and φ(ℙ) ⊆ ℍ (the two other clauses of IsHullMap, both stated on page 127), force φ(P) = ⋂ {H ∈ 𝓗 | P ⊆ H}. The intersection hypothesis quoted by the paper is not needed for this formula.
  • IsHullMap.unique: hence at most one map satisfies (P1), (P2), (P3); this is the paper's "characterized uniquely".
  • isHullMap_sInter: if for each P ∈ 𝓟 the intersection of the members of 𝓗 containing P lies in 𝓗, then that intersection defines a map satisfying (P1), (P2), (P3). This is the role of the intersection hypothesis: it gives existence, not the formula.

The paper's closure claim (an intersection of hulls that has finite log-volume is a hull) is replaced by the plain hypothesis hcl of isHullMap_sInter: for each P ∈ 𝓟 the intersection of the members of 𝓗 containing P lies in 𝓗. That hypothesis is a statement about the given families only; no log-volume occurs in this file, and the finite-volume condition of the paper is not modeled.

Public declarations
variable {X : Type*}
variable {𝓟 𝓗 : Set (Set X)} {φ : Set X → Set X}

IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.IsHullMapstructure

structure IsHullMap (𝓟 𝓗 : Set (Set X)) (φ : Set X → Set X) : Prop where

A map φ on subsets of X satisfies the conditions of Remark 3.9.5 (ii) relative to the families 𝓟 (playing the role of direct product regions) and 𝓗 (playing the role of hulls): it sends 𝓟 into 𝓗, and satisfies (P1), (P2), (P3).

IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.IsHullMap.eq_sIntertheorem

theorem eq_sInter (h : IsHullMap 𝓟 𝓗 φ) {P : Set X} (hP : P ∈ 𝓟) :
  φ P = ⋂₀ {H | H ∈ 𝓗 ∧ P ⊆ H}

The clauses of IsHullMap (ℍ ⊆ ℙ, φ(ℙ) ⊆ ℍ, (P1), (P2), (P3)) force φ(P) = ⋂ {H ∈ ℍ | P ⊆ H}, with no hypothesis on intersections.

IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.IsHullMap.uniquetheorem

theorem unique {ψ : Set X → Set X} (hφ : IsHullMap 𝓟 𝓗 φ) (hψ : IsHullMap 𝓟 𝓗 ψ)
  {P : Set X} (hP : P ∈ 𝓟) : φ P = ψ P

At most one map satisfies the conditions of Remark 3.9.5 (ii) on ℙ.

IUT.PaperIII.Remark3_9_5.isHullMap_sIntertheorem

theorem isHullMap_sInter {𝓟 𝓗 : Set (Set X)} (hsub : 𝓗 ⊆ 𝓟)
  (hcl : ∀ P ∈ 𝓟, ⋂₀ {H | H ∈ 𝓗 ∧ P ⊆ H} ∈ 𝓗) :
  IsHullMap 𝓟 𝓗 (fun P => ⋂₀ {H | H ∈ 𝓗 ∧ P ⊆ H})

Existence: if ℍ ⊆ ℙ and, for each P ∈ ℙ, the intersection of the members of ℍ containing P lies in ℍ, then P ↦ ⋂ {H ∈ ℍ | P ⊆ H} satisfies (P1), (P2), (P3).

IUT IV

Log-volume computations and set-theoretic foundations.

IUT.PaperIV.ArithmeticDivisor

IUT/PaperIV/ArithmeticDivisor.lean

IUT IV, Definition 1.9 (i): arithmetic divisors on a number field

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Definition 1.9, pages 21 and 22 of the April 2020 manuscript, which recalls notation from [GenEll], §1.

For a number field F, the set 𝕍(F) of valuations is the disjoint union of the nonarchimedean ones and the archimedean ones. An ℝ-arithmetic divisor is a finite formal sum ∑ c_v · v with real coefficients. The degree map sends a nonarchimedean v to log(q_v), with q_v the cardinality of the residue field, and an archimedean v to 1.

Interpretation choices, recorded
  • Nonarchimedean valuations are represented by the nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F)), archimedean ones by NumberField.InfinitePlace F. A pair of complex conjugate embeddings is one valuation.
  • The archimedean weight is 1 for real and complex places alike, exactly as in the display of Definition 1.9 (i). Other conventions weight a complex place by 2.
  • The pull-back 𝔞|_K to a finite extension, defined "in the evident fashion", and the identity deg(𝔞|_K) = deg(𝔞) for the normalized degree are formalized in IUT/PaperIV/DegreePullback.lean, in one reading of that phrase. Part (ii) of the definition is not formalized here.
Public declarations
variable (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F]
variable {F}

IUT.PaperIV.Valuationsabbrev

abbrev Valuations : Type _ :=
  IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F) ⊕ InfinitePlace F

The set 𝕍(F) of valuations of F: nonarchimedean ones on the left, archimedean ones on the right.

IUT.PaperIV.ADivabbrev

abbrev ADiv : Type _ := Valuations F →₀ ℝ

The group ADiv_ℝ(F) of ℝ-arithmetic divisors: finite formal real combinations of valuations.

IUT.PaperIV.degWeightdef

noncomputable def degWeight : Valuations F → ℝ
  | .inl v => Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)
  | .inr _ => 1

The weight of a valuation in the degree map: log(q_v) at a nonarchimedean valuation, where q_v is the cardinality of the residue field, and 1 at an archimedean one.

IUT.PaperIV.degWeight_nonnegtheorem

theorem degWeight_nonneg (v : Valuations F) : 0 ≤ degWeight v

IUT.PaperIV.ADiv.suppdef

def ADiv.supp (a : ADiv F) : Finset (Valuations F) := a.support

The support Supp(𝔞): the valuations with nonzero coefficient.

IUT.PaperIV.ADiv.Effectivedef

def ADiv.Effective (a : ADiv F) : Prop := ∀ v, 0 ≤ a v

An arithmetic divisor is effective when all its coefficients are ≥ 0.

IUT.PaperIV.degFdef

noncomputable def degF : ADiv F →+ ℝ :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom fun v => AddMonoidHom.mulLeft (degWeight v)

The degree map deg_F : ADiv_ℝ(F) → ℝ, a homomorphism of groups.

IUT.PaperIV.degF_singletheorem

theorem degF_single (v : Valuations F) (c : ℝ) :
  degF (Finsupp.single v c) = degWeight v * c

IUT.PaperIV.degF_applytheorem

theorem degF_apply (a : ADiv F) : degF a = a.sum fun v c => degWeight v * c

IUT.PaperIV.degF_nonnegtheorem

theorem degF_nonneg {a : ADiv F} (h : a.Effective) : 0 ≤ degF a

An effective arithmetic divisor has nonnegative degree.

IUT.PaperIV.normalizedDegdef

noncomputable def normalizedDeg (a : ADiv F) : ℝ := degF a / Module.finrank ℚ F

The normalized degree deg(𝔞) = deg_F(𝔞) / [F : ℚ].

IUT.PaperIV.normalizedDeg_addtheorem

theorem normalizedDeg_add (a b : ADiv F) :
  normalizedDeg (a + b) = normalizedDeg a + normalizedDeg b

IUT.PaperIV.normalizedDeg_nonnegtheorem

theorem normalizedDeg_nonneg {a : ADiv F} (h : a.Effective) : 0 ≤ normalizedDeg a

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.Arithmetic

IUT/PaperIV/Corollary2_2/Arithmetic.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.Theorem1_10.ElementaryFacts, IUT.PaperIV.Proposition2_1

IUT IV, Corollary 2.2: the real arithmetic of (C1), (C2) and of the proof

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Corollary 2.2 and its proof, pages 41 to 48 of the April 2020 manuscript, read from the extracted text and from the rendered pages 42 to 48; every display formalized here was checked against the renders.

This file is not a formalization of Corollary 2.2. The corollary constructs initial Θ-data from a point of a compactly bounded subset of the λ-line and applies Theorem 1.10; that uses the theory of elliptic curves, [GenEll] (Lemma 3.5, Proposition 3.4, Lemma 3.1, Proposition 1.4), [CanLift] and [IUTchI], none of which is formalized. Every arithmetic fact about the curve is a hypothesis here; what is checked is the real arithmetic of the proof:

  • the bound on θ_A (thetaA_chain) and the choice of l in (P1) (P1_upper, P1_lower, P1_l_ge_seven, P1_bound), which is condition (C1);
  • the boundedness arguments behind (P4) and (P5) (P4_bound, P5_bound) and the chain h^{1/2}·log(l) ≤ 16·δ^{1/4}·h^{3/4} (sqrt_mul_log_l);
  • the application of Theorem 1.10 (apply_theorem_1_10), the comparison of log(𝔮^{∤2}) with log(𝔮) (q_not2_step), the constant (15δ)² (fifteen_delta_step) and the assembly of the bound (1/6)·h ≤ (1 + ε_E/5)·D + (2/5)·ε_E·(1/6)·h + C_K/2 (assembly);
  • the lower bound ε_E ≥ 5·δ·h^{-1/2} (epsE_ge) and the real-power estimate showing that ε < ε_E bounds h (h_lt_of_eps_lt_epsE), with the explicit constant H_unif (h_bound_Hunif);
  • the final step (1/6)·h ≤ (1 + ε_E)·D + C_K for 0 < ε_E ≤ 1 (final_step), which is the inequality (C2) after D ≤ log-diff_X(x_E) + log-cond_D(x_E) (C2_of_final).

Notation: s = h^{1/2} with h = s² = log(𝔮^∀); L = log(2δh); D = log(𝔡^{F_tpd}) + log(𝔣^{F_tpd}); Q = log(𝔮), Q2 = log(𝔮^{∤2}).

Public declarations

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.thetaA_chaintheorem

theorem thetaA_chain {θ s δ L ξ : ℝ} (hδ : 2 ≤ δ) (hL : 1 ≤ L) (hξ : 0 ≤ ξ) (hs : ξ ≤ s)
  (h : θ ≤ 2 * s + δ * s + 2 * δ * s * L) :
  θ ≤ 4 * δ * s * L ∧ θ ≤ -ξ + 5 * δ * s * L

**The bound on θ_A** (page 45). If θ_A ≤ 2s + δs + 2δsL (the contributions of (S1), (S3), (S2)), δ ≥ 2, L ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ ξ ≤ s, then θ_A ≤ 4δ·s·L ≤ -ξ + 5δ·s·L.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.S1_boundtheorem

theorem S1_bound {ξ s : ℝ} (hs : ξ ≤ s) (hξ : 0 ≤ ξ)
  (hθ : ∀ x : ℝ, ξ ≤ x → Chebyshev.theta x ≤ 4 / 3 * x) : Chebyshev.theta s ≤ 2 * s

The contribution of (S1): with ξ ≤ s and θ(x) ≤ (4/3)·x for x ≥ ξ, θ(s) ≤ 2s.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P1_uppertheorem

theorem P1_upper {l θ ξ δ s L : ℝ} (hl : l ≤ 2 * (θ + ξ)) (hθ : θ ≤ -ξ + 5 * δ * s * L) :
  l ≤ 10 * δ * s * L

(P1), upper bound. If l ≤ 2(θ_A + ξ) (Proposition 2.1 (ii)) and θ_A ≤ -ξ + 5δ·s·L, then l ≤ 10δ·s·L.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P1_lowertheorem

theorem P1_lower {A : Finset ℕ} {l : ℕ} {s : ℝ} (hS1 : ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → (p : ℝ) ≤ s → p ∈ A)
  (hl : l.Prime) (hlA : l ∉ A) : s < l

(P1), lower bound. If every prime ≤ s lies in A (condition (S1)) and the prime l does not, then s < l.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P1_l_ge_seventheorem

theorem P1_l_ge_seven {l : ℕ} {s : ℝ} (hl : l.Prime) (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hsl : s < l) : 7 ≤ l

**l ≥ 7.** Theorem 1.10 in its final form requires l ≥ 7. The paper notes on page 22 that l ≠ 5 follows from [IUTchI] Definition 3.1 (c), since the 5-torsion points are rational over F. Independently, since 5 ≤ s < l (with s = h^{1/2}) and l is prime, l ≥ 7.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P1_boundtheorem

theorem P1_bound {δ s : ℝ} (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
  10 * δ * s * Real.log (2 * δ * s ^ 2) ≤ 20 * δ ^ 2 * (s ^ 2) ^ 2

(P1), parenthetical bound. 10δ·s·log(2δh) ≤ 20·δ²·h² for h = s², s ≥ 1, δ ≥ 1; uses Proposition 2.1 (i).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P4_boundtheorem

theorem P4_bound {l Q T : ℝ} (hl : 5 ≤ l) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
  (h : (l - 2) / 24 * Q ≤ 2 * Real.log l + T) : Q ≤ 48 * (1 + T)

(P4), boundedness. (l-2)/24·Q ≤ 2·log(l) + T with l ≥ 5 and T ≥ 0 implies Q ≤ 48·(1 + T); the paper uses 1 ≤ 2·log(l) ≤ 48·(l-2)/24.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.sqrt_mul_log_ltheorem

theorem sqrt_mul_log_l {a b l : ℝ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hl0 : 0 < l)
  (hl : l ≤ 20 * (a ^ 4) ^ 2 * (b ^ 4) ^ 2) :
  b ^ 2 * Real.log l ≤ 16 * a * b ^ 3

**The chain h^{1/2}·log(l) ≤ 16·δ^{1/4}·h^{3/4}** (pages 45 and 46), written with δ = a⁴, h = b⁴ (so h^{1/2} = b²). Uses (P1) l ≤ 20δ²h², 20 ≤ 5², 5 ≤ 2⁴ and Proposition 2.1 (i).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.sqrt_mul_log_l_stepstheorem

theorem sqrt_mul_log_l_steps {a b : ℝ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) :
  Real.log (20 * (a ^ 4) ^ 2 * (b ^ 4) ^ 2) ≤ 2 * Real.log (5 * a ^ 4 * b ^ 4) ∧
    Real.log (5 * a ^ 4 * b ^ 4) ≤ 4 * Real.log (2 * a * b)

The paper's intermediate steps of the same chain: log(20δ²h²) ≤ 2·log(5δh) and log(5δh) ≤ 4·log(2·δ^{1/4}·h^{1/4}), with δ = a⁴, h = b⁴.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.P5_boundtheorem

theorem P5_bound {b B c : ℝ} (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (h : b ^ 4 ≤ B + c * b ^ 3) :
  b ≤ B + c

(P5), boundedness. If h ≤ B + c·h^{3/4} with h ≥ 1 and B, c ≥ 0, then h is bounded; written with h = b⁴: b⁴ ≤ B + c·b³ and b ≥ 1 imply b ≤ B + c.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.apply_theorem_1_10theorem

theorem apply_theorem_1_10 {Q D d dstar l E η δ s L : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hD : 0 ≤ D)
  (hd : 0 ≤ d) (hdd : 20 * d ≤ dstar) (hdδ : dstar ≤ δ) (hsl : s ≤ l)
  (hl : l ≤ 10 * δ * s * L) (hE : E ≤ dstar * l + η)
  (h : 1 / 6 * Q ≤ (1 + 20 * d / l) * D + 20 * E) :

Applying Theorem 1.10 (page 46). From the final inequality of Theorem 1.10 with E ≤ d*_mod·l + η_prm (Remark 1.10.7 (i): e*_mod ≤ d*_mod), 20·d_mod ≤ d*_mod ≤ δ, s ≤ l ≤ 10δ·s·L and D ≥ 0: (1/6)·Q ≤ (1 + δ/s)·D + 200·δ²·s·L + 20·η_prm.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.q_not2_steptheorem

theorem q_not2_step {Q Q2 s l δ h : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) (hh : 1 ≤ h)
  (h1 : 1 / 6 * Q2 - 1 / 6 * Q ≤ 1 / 6 * (s * Real.log l))

**The comparison of log(𝔮^{∤2}) with log(𝔮)** (page 47). Given (1/6)·Q2 - (1/6)·Q ≤ (1/6)·s·log(l) (from (P3)) and s·log(l) ≤ 2·s·log(5δh), with δ, h ≥ 1 and 5 ≤ 2³: (1/6)·Q2 - (1/6)·Q ≤ s·log(2δh).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.fifteen_delta_steptheorem

theorem fifteen_delta_step {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) :
  200 * δ ^ 2 + 1 ≤ (15 * δ) ^ 2 ∧ (15 * δ) ^ 2 ≤ 1 / 6 * (2 / 5) * (60 * δ) ^ 2

**The constant (15δ)²** (page 47): 200·δ² + 1 ≤ (15δ)² ≤ (1/6)·(2/5)·(60δ)² for δ ≥ 1; the second inequality is the paper's "6·5 ≤ 2·4²".

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.assemblytheorem

theorem assembly {Q Q2 D s δ L η B εE : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
  (hD : 0 ≤ D)
  (hB : 1 / 6 * s ^ 2 - 1 / 6 * Q2 ≤ B)
  (hq2 : 1 / 6 * Q2 - 1 / 6 * Q ≤ s * L)
  (hthm : 1 / 6 * Q ≤ (1 + δ / s) * D + 200 * δ ^ 2 * s * L + 20 * η)
  (hεE : εE = (60 * δ) ^ 2 * s⁻¹ * L) (hδε : δ / s ≤ εE / 5) :

**Assembly of the bound on (1/6)·h** (page 47). With (1/6)·h - (1/6)·Q2 ≤ B (the bounded discrepancy B_K of assertion (i)), the two preceding steps, C = 40·η + 2·B, h = s², ε_E = (60δ)²·s⁻¹·L, and δ/s ≤ ε_E/5: (1/6)·h ≤ (1 + ε_E/5)·D + (2/5)·ε_E·(1/6)·h + C/2.

theorem epsE_ge {δ s L : ℝ} (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) (hL : 1 ≤ L) (hs : 0 < s) :
  5 * δ * s⁻¹ ≤ (60 * δ) ^ 2 * s⁻¹ * L

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.eps_star_estimatestheorem

theorem eps_star_estimates {εd : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < εd) (h1 : εd ≤ 1) :
  1 / (1 / 2 - εd / 16) ≤ 3 ∧ (2 + εd / 16) / (1 / 2 - εd / 16) ≤ 4 + εd ∧ 4 + εd ≤ 5

The two estimates of page 47 for ε*_d = ε_d/16: 1/(1/2 - ε*_d) = 16/(8 - ε_d) ≤ 3 and (2 + ε*_d)/(1/2 - ε*_d) = (32 + ε_d)/(8 - ε_d) ≤ 4 + ε_d ≤ 5, for 0 < ε_d ≤ 1.

theorem h_lt_of_eps_lt_epsE {h δ εd ε : ℝ} (hh : 1 ≤ h) (hδ : 1 ≤ δ) (hεd0 : 0 < εd)

theorem h_bound_Hunif {d εd ε : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hεd0 : 0 < εd) (hεd1 : εd ≤ 1)

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.PrimeSelection

IUT/PaperIV/Corollary2_2/PrimeSelection.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.Arithmetic

IUT IV, Corollary 2.2: the choice of the prime l

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, the proof of Corollary 2.2, pages 44 and 45 of the April 2020 manuscript (the choice of l, conditions (P1), (P2), (P3)), with Proposition 2.1 on page 40 for ξ_prm and the prime estimate. Pages read for this file: 40, 43, 44, 45, 46; all of them were checked against rendered images, and every display used here was transcribed from the render.

This file is not a formalization of Corollary 2.2. On the page, h = log(𝔮^∀) is attached to an elliptic curve E_F over a number field F; h_v is the local height of E_F at the nonarchimedean place v (zero at places of good reduction), p_v the residue characteristic, and δ a bound on [F : ℚ] from properties (E3), (E4), (E5) of the proof of Theorem 1.10. Here all of these are plain numbers: a finite index type V of places, a prime p v, a natural number hv v, a positive natural f v for each v, a natural n (for [F : ℚ]) and a real δ, with

h = (1/n)·∑_v hv v · f v · log(p v) (page 44, the definition of h).

What is checked is the arithmetic of pages 44 and 45: under the printed numerical hypotheses h^{1/2} ≥ ξ_prm ≥ 5, [F : ℚ] ≤ δ and δ ≥ 2, the set A of primes that (S1) are ≤ h^{1/2}, (S2) divide a nonzero h_v, or (S3) equal p_v for some v with h_v ≥ h^{1/2} has θ_A ≤ -ξ_prm + 5δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh), so that Proposition 2.1 (ii) gives a prime l ∉ A with

  • (P1) (5 ≤) h^{1/2} ≤ l ≤ 10δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh) (≤ 20·δ²·h²);
  • (P2) l divides no nonzero h_v;
  • (P3) if l = p_v, then h_v < h^{1/2}.

The page bounds the (S2) part only through the primes dividing some h_v ≥ h^{1/2}; that the remaining primes of (S2) lie in (S1) is left implicit on the page and is proved here (primeSel_A_subset). Proposition 2.1 (ii) is used through Proposition2_1.lean; no further prime number estimate is needed.

Main results: primeSel_exists_prime_of (for any ξ ≥ 5 with the two bounds of Proposition 2.1 (ii)) and primeSel_exists_prime (with the ξ_prm provided by Proposition2_1.exists_xi_prm). Nonvacuity: primeSel_hypotheses_satisfiable.

Not proved: nothing that the page proves in this passage is left out. Not addressed: the link of the numbers h, h_v, p_v, f_v, n, δ with an elliptic curve, and the enlargement of the exceptional set that makes h^{1/2} ≥ ξ_prm hold (page 44, via [GenEll] Proposition 1.4 (iv)).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelHeightdef

noncomputable def primeSelHeight {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p hv f : V → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 / (n : ℝ) * ∑ v, (hv v : ℝ) * f v * Real.log (p v)

The quantity h = (1/[F:ℚ])·∑_v h_v·f_v·log(p_v) of page 44, for numerical data.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelS1def

noncomputable def primeSelS1 (s : ℝ) : Finset ℕ := {q ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊s⌋₊ | q.Prime}

(S1): the primes ≤ s, written as in the definition of Chebyshev.theta.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelS2def

def primeSelS2 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (hv : V → ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  univ.biUnion fun v => (hv v).primeFactors

(S2): the primes dividing some nonzero h_v (primeFactors 0 = ∅).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelBigdef

noncomputable def primeSelBig {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (hv : V → ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Finset V :=

The places with h_v ≥ s.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelS3def

noncomputable def primeSelS3 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p hv : V → ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Finset ℕ :=

(S3): the primes equal to p_v for some v with h_v ≥ s.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelAdef

noncomputable def primeSelA {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p hv : V → ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Finset ℕ :=

The set A of page 44: primes in (S1), (S2) or (S3), with s = h^{1/2}.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSelS2bigdef

noncomputable def primeSelS2big {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (hv : V → ℕ) (s : ℝ) : Finset ℕ :=

The part of (S2) that the page estimates: primes dividing some h_v ≥ s.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_sum_union_letheorem

theorem primeSel_sum_union_le (A B : Finset ℕ) {g : ℕ → ℝ} (hg : ∀ q, 0 ≤ g q) :
  ∑ q ∈ A ∪ B, g q ≤ ∑ q ∈ A, g q + ∑ q ∈ B, g q

A sum of nonnegative terms over a union is at most the sum of the two sums.

A sum of nonnegative terms over a biUnion is at most the double sum.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_sum_log_primeFactors_letheorem

  ∑ q ∈ m.primeFactors, Real.log q ≤ Real.log m

∑_{q ∣ m} log(q) ≤ log(m) for m ≠ 0, the sum over the distinct prime factors.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_term_nonnegtheorem

theorem primeSel_term_nonneg {V : Type*} {p hv f : V → ℕ} (v : V) :

Each term h_v·f_v·log(p_v) is nonnegative.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_sum_eqtheorem

[F:ℚ]·h = ∑_v h_v·f_v·log(p_v) for [F:ℚ] ≠ 0.

n ≠ 0 as soon as h > 0 (with n = 0, the formula gives h = 0).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_S3_sum_letheorem

theorem primeSel_S3_sum_le {δ : ℝ} (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) (hnδ : (n : ℝ) ≤ δ)
  (hh : 0 < primeSelHeight p hv f n) :
  ∑ v ∈ primeSelBig hv (Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)), Real.log (p v)
    ≤ δ * Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)

First chain of page 44. With s = h^{1/2} and [F:ℚ] ≤ δ: δ·h^{1/2} ≥ [F:ℚ]·h^{1/2} = ∑_v h^{-1/2}·h_v·f_v·log(p_v) ≥ ∑_{h_v ≥ h^{1/2}} log(p_v).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_S2_sum_letheorem

theorem primeSel_S2_sum_le {δ : ℝ} (hp : ∀ v, (p v).Prime) (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v)

  ∑ v ∈ primeSelBig hv (Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)), Real.log (hv v)

        * Real.log (2 * δ * primeSelHeight p hv f n)

Second chain of page 44. With s = h^{1/2}, [F:ℚ] ≤ δ, 1 ≤ δ and h^{1/2} ≥ 1: 2δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh) ≥ ∑_{h_v ≠ 0} 2·h^{-1/2}·log(2·h_v·f_v·log(p_v))·h_v·f_v·log(p_v) ≥ ∑_{h_v ≥ h^{1/2}} log(h_v), using 2·log(p_v) ≥ log(4) ≥ 1 (property (E6)).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_A_subsettheorem

theorem primeSel_A_subset {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p hv : V → ℕ) (s : ℝ) :
  primeSelA p hv s ⊆ primeSelS1 s ∪ primeSelS2big hv s ∪ primeSelS3 p hv s

The bridge left implicit on page 44: a prime dividing a nonzero h_v < s is ≤ s, hence in (S1); so A ⊆ (S1) ∪ (S2 restricted to h_v ≥ s) ∪ (S3).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_thetaA_letheorem

theorem primeSel_thetaA_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {p hv f : V → ℕ} {n : ℕ} {δ ξ : ℝ}
  (hp : ∀ v, (p v).Prime) (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) (hnδ : (n : ℝ) ≤ δ) (hδ : 1 ≤ δ)
  (hξ1 : 1 ≤ ξ) (hθ : ∀ x : ℝ, ξ ≤ x → Chebyshev.theta x ≤ 4 / 3 * x)
  (hh : 0 < primeSelHeight p hv f n) (hs : ξ ≤ Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)) :
  Proposition2_1.thetaA (primeSelA p hv (Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)))
    ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n) + δ * Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)
      + 2 * δ * Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)
        * Real.log (2 * δ * primeSelHeight p hv f n)

**The bound on θ_A, first line of page 45.** Under the hypotheses of page 44 (s = h^{1/2} with ξ ≤ s and θ(x) ≤ (4/3)·x for x ≥ ξ ≥ 1, [F:ℚ] ≤ δ, 1 ≤ δ): θ_A ≤ 2·h^{1/2} + δ·h^{1/2} + 2δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh), the three terms bounding (S1), (S3), (S2).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_exists_prime_oftheorem

theorem primeSel_exists_prime_of {ξ : ℝ} (hξ5 : 5 ≤ ξ)
  (hθ : ∀ x : ℝ, ξ ≤ x → 2 / 3 * x ≤ Chebyshev.theta x ∧ Chebyshev.theta x ≤ 4 / 3 * x)
  {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p hv f : V → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (δ h : ℝ)
  (hp : ∀ v, (p v).Prime) (hf : ∀ v, 0 < f v) (hh : h = primeSelHeight p hv f n)
  (hξh : ξ ≤ Real.sqrt h) (hnδ : (n : ℝ) ≤ δ) (hδ : 2 ≤ δ) :
  ∃ l : ℕ, l.Prime ∧
    (5 ≤ Real.sqrt h ∧ Real.sqrt h ≤ l ∧
      (l : ℝ) ≤ 10 * δ * Real.sqrt h * Real.log (2 * δ * h) ∧
      10 * δ * Real.sqrt h * Real.log (2 * δ * h) ≤ 20 * δ ^ 2 * h ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ v, hv v ≠ 0 → ¬ l ∣ hv v) ∧
    (∀ v, l = p v → (hv v : ℝ) < Real.sqrt h)

**The choice of the prime l** (pages 44 and 45), for any ξ ≥ 5 satisfying the two bounds of Proposition 2.1 (ii). Data: places V, primes p_v, naturals h_v, positive naturals f_v, a natural n (for [F:ℚ]), a real δ, and h given by the formula of page 44. Hypotheses as printed: h^{1/2} ≥ ξ_prm (≥ 5), [F:ℚ] ≤ δ, δ ≥ 2. Conclusion: a prime l with (P1) 5 ≤ h^{1/2} ≤ l ≤ 10δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh) ≤ 20·δ²·h², (P2) l divides no nonzero h_v, and (P3) l = p_v implies h_v < h^{1/2}.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_exists_primetheorem

theorem primeSel_exists_prime :
  ∃ ξ : ℝ, 5 ≤ ξ ∧
    (∀ x : ℝ, ξ ≤ x → 2 / 3 * x ≤ Chebyshev.theta x ∧ Chebyshev.theta x ≤ 4 / 3 * x) ∧
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (p hv f : V → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (δ h : ℝ),
      (∀ v, (p v).Prime) → (∀ v, 0 < f v) → h = primeSelHeight p hv f n →
      ξ ≤ Real.sqrt h → (n : ℝ) ≤ δ → 2 ≤ δ →
      ∃ l : ℕ, l.Prime ∧
        (5 ≤ Real.sqrt h ∧ Real.sqrt h ≤ l ∧
          (l : ℝ) ≤ 10 * δ * Real.sqrt h * Real.log (2 * δ * h) ∧
          10 * δ * Real.sqrt h * Real.log (2 * δ * h) ≤ 20 * δ ^ 2 * h ^ 2) ∧
        (∀ v, hv v ≠ 0 → ¬ l ∣ hv v) ∧
        (∀ v, l = p v → (hv v : ℝ) < Real.sqrt h)

**The choice of the prime l**, with the ξ_prm of Proposition 2.1 (ii): there is ξ_prm ≥ 5 with (2/3)·x ≤ θ(x) ≤ (4/3)·x for x ≥ ξ_prm such that for all data as in primeSel_exists_prime_of with h^{1/2} ≥ ξ_prm, [F:ℚ] ≤ δ and δ ≥ 2, there is a prime l satisfying (P1), (P2), (P3).

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_2.primeSel_hypotheses_satisfiabletheorem

theorem primeSel_hypotheses_satisfiable (ξ : ℝ) :
  ∃ (p hv f : Unit → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ), (∀ v, (p v).Prime) ∧ (∀ v, 0 < f v) ∧
    (n : ℝ) ≤ δ ∧ 2 ≤ δ ∧ ξ ≤ Real.sqrt (primeSelHeight p hv f n)

Nonvacuity. For every real ξ there are data satisfying all hypotheses of primeSel_exists_prime_of: one place with p = 2, f = 1, [F:ℚ] = 1, δ = 2 and h_v = N for N large.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3

IUT/PaperIV/Corollary2_3.lean

IUT IV, Corollary 2.3: the bounded discrepancy logic of the proof

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Corollary 2.3, its proof, and Remark 2.3.1 (ii), pages 54 and 55 of the April 2020 manuscript, read from the extracted text and from the rendered pages 54 and 55. The bounded discrepancy relations are those of [GenEll], Definition 1.2 (ii), with the correction of Remark 2.3.1 (ii): α ≲ β on F means that there is a constant C with α(x) - β(x) ≤ C for all x ∈ F.

This file is not a formalization of Corollary 2.3. The proof of the corollary has two parts:

  1. By [GenEll], Theorem 2.1 ((ii) implies (i)), it suffices to prove the inequality ht_{ω_X(D)} ≲ (1 + ε)·(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on K_V ∩ U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d} for the λ-line X = ℙ¹, D = {0, 1, ∞} and a compactly bounded K_V as in Corollary 2.2. That reduction is an external theorem and is not formalized here.
  2. On K_V ∩ U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d}, the inequality follows from Corollary 2.2 (i), (ii) (condition (C2)) and (iii). This file checks only the logical form of that step, as an abstract lemma about real functions on an arbitrary set S (cor2_3_on_KV): an equality of bounded discrepancy classes, a bound outside a finite exceptional set, a bound on a further function outside that set and a nonnegativity condition give an inequality of bounded discrepancy classes on all of S.

Nothing here refers to curves, divisors, points of bounded degree, heights, log-differents or log-conductors: these are arbitrary real functions on an arbitrary type, and the lemma holds for every S, including S = ∅. It says nothing about K_V unless the hypotheses are established for the actual functions, which requires Corollary 2.2 and is not done here. Corollary 2.3 itself is not stated in Lean; the form to which its proof reduces it (page 55) is stated as an open proposition in IUT/Applications/CompactlyBounded.lean (iutIVCor2_3ReducedFormStatement).

Public declarations
variable {α : Type*}

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDledef

def BDle (S : Set α) (f g : α → ℝ) : Prop := ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ S, f x - g x ≤ C

f ≲ g on S ([GenEll], Definition 1.2 (ii), as corrected by IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1 (ii)): there is a constant C with f(x) - g(x) ≤ C for every x ∈ S.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDeqdef

def BDeq (S : Set α) (f g : α → ℝ) : Prop := ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ S, |f x - g x| ≤ C

f ≈ g on S: there is a constant C with |f(x) - g(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ S.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDeq.letheorem

theorem BDeq.le {S : Set α} {f g : α → ℝ} (h : BDeq S f g) : BDle S f g

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDle.transtheorem

theorem BDle.trans {S : Set α} {f g k : α → ℝ} (h1 : BDle S f g) (h2 : BDle S g k) :
  BDle S f k

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDle_of_finite_exceptionstheorem

theorem BDle_of_finite_exceptions {S : Set α} (Exc : Finset α) {f g : α → ℝ} (C : ℝ)
  (h : ∀ x ∈ S, x ∉ Exc → f x - g x ≤ C) : BDle S f g

A bound that holds outside a finite exceptional set gives an inequality of bounded discrepancy classes on the whole set.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.cor2_3_on_KVtheorem

theorem cor2_3_on_KV {S : Set α} (Exc : Finset α) {ht H Λ εE : α → ℝ} {ε CK : ℝ}
  (hi : BDeq S ht (fun x => 1 / 6 * H x))
  (hC2 : ∀ x ∈ S, x ∉ Exc → 1 / 6 * H x ≤ (1 + εE x) * Λ x + CK)
  (hiii : ∀ x ∈ S, x ∉ Exc → εE x ≤ ε)
  (hΛ : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Λ x) :
  BDle S ht (fun x => (1 + ε) * Λ x)

**Abstract form of the step of the proof of Corollary 2.3 on K_V ∩ U_X(ℚ̄)^{≤d}** (page 55). This is a lemma about arbitrary real functions on an arbitrary set S; it holds for every S, so it carries information about K_V only once its hypotheses are proved for the actual functions. In the intended application S is the set of points, ht the height ht_{ω_X(D)}, H the function log(𝔮^∀), Λ the function log-diff_X + log-cond_D, and εE the invariant ε_E of Corollary 2.2 (ii). Assume: * (Corollary 2.2 (i)) ht ≈ (1/6)·H on S; * (Corollary 2.2 (ii), (C2)) (1/6)·H(x) ≤ (1 + ε_E(x))·Λ(x) + C_K for x ∈ S outside a finite set Exc; * (Corollary 2.2 (iii)) ε_E(x) ≤ ε for x ∈ S outside Exc; * Λ ≥ 0 on S (log-differents and log-conductors are degrees of effective divisors). Then ht ≲ (1 + ε)·Λ on S.

IUT.PaperIV.Corollary2_3.BDle_mono_epstheorem

theorem BDle_mono_eps {S : Set α} {ht Λ : α → ℝ} {ε ε' : ℝ} (hεε' : ε ≤ ε')
  (hΛ : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Λ x) (h : BDle S ht (fun x => (1 + ε) * Λ x)) :
  BDle S ht (fun x => (1 + ε') * Λ x)

Corollary 2.2 (iii) is stated for ε ≤ 1. For ε > 1 the inequality follows from the case ε = 1, since Λ ≥ 0; this monotonicity is the following statement.

IUT.PaperIV.Definition1_9

IUT/PaperIV/Definition1_9.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.ArithmeticDivisor

IUT IV, Definition 1.9 (ii): the degree deg_E of an arithmetic divisor relative to a set

Module documentation

of valuations

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Definition 1.9, pages 21 and 22 of the April 2020 manuscript, read from the extracted text and from the rendered pages 21 and 22 (with a magnified crop of the display of (ii)).

Definition 1.9 (ii) of the paper: for a nonempty set E ⊆ 𝕍(F) of valuations lying over a single valuation v_ℚ of ℚ, and an arithmetic divisor 𝔞 on F, write 𝔞_E for the portion of 𝔞 supported in E and set

deg_E(𝔞) = deg(𝔞_E) / ∑_{v ∈ E} [F_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}].

The paper then states that deg_{E|K}(𝔞|_K) = deg_E(𝔞) for a finite extension K of F, where E|K is the set of valuations of K over E; part (i) states the analogous invariance deg(𝔞|_K) = deg(𝔞) of the normalized degree.

Interpretation of the numerator. In the render of page 22 the line under deg(𝔞_E) is the fraction bar, so the numerator is the degree deg_F of Definition 1.9 (i), not the normalized degree; this file uses degF in the numerator.

Domain. degE is defined only on PlaceSet F, the finite sets E that are nonempty and whose elements all lie over one place of ℚ (LiesOverOnePlace). Interpretation choice: the place of ℚ below a valuation is encoded by placeBelow as some p, with p the residue characteristic ringChar (𝓞 F ⧸ 𝔭), for a finite place 𝔭, and as none for an archimedean place.

What is formalized: the domain (placeBelow, LiesOverOnePlace, PlaceSet), the definition (degE), the local degree [F_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}] (localDeg, as e_v·f_v at finite places and as InfinitePlace.mult at infinite places), basic properties (degE_add, degE_nonneg), the identification deg_E(𝔞) = deg(𝔞_E) (normalized degree) under the hypothesis that the local degrees over E sum to [F : ℚ] (degE_eq_normalizedDeg), and its unconditional instance for the set of all archimedean valuations (degE_arc_eq_normalizedDeg).

What is not formalized here: the set E|K and the invariance deg_{E|K}(𝔞|_K) = deg_E(𝔞) of (ii). The pull-back 𝔞|_K along a finite extension and the invariance deg(𝔞|_K) = deg(𝔞) of (i) are in IUT/PaperIV/DegreePullback.lean, for one reading of "the evident fashion"; the fact that the local degrees over all valuations above one finite v_ℚ sum to [F : ℚ] (fundamental identity) is used there, through Mathlib's Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank, and is not proved in this file.

IUT.PaperIV.localDegdef

noncomputable def localDeg : Valuations F → ℕ
  | .inl v => v.asIdeal.ramificationIdx ℤ * v.asIdeal.inertiaDeg ℤ
  | .inr w => w.mult

The local degree [F_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}]: e_v·f_v at a finite place (ramification index times inertia degree of the prime of 𝓞 F over ℤ), and 1 or 2 at an infinite place.

IUT.PaperIV.placeBelowdef

noncomputable def placeBelow : Valuations F → Option ℕ
  | .inl v => some (ringChar (𝓞 F ⧸ v.asIdeal))
  | .inr _ => none

The place of ℚ below a valuation of F: some p for a finite place 𝔭, where p is the residue characteristic of 𝔭, and none for an archimedean place.

IUT.PaperIV.LiesOverOnePlacedef

def LiesOverOnePlace (E : Finset (Valuations F)) : Prop :=
  E.Nonempty ∧ ∃ vQ : Option ℕ, ∀ v ∈ E, placeBelow v = vQ

The domain condition of Definition 1.9 (ii): E is nonempty and all its elements lie over one place v_ℚ of ℚ.

IUT.PaperIV.PlaceSetabbrev

abbrev PlaceSet : Type _ := {E : Finset (Valuations F) // LiesOverOnePlace E}

The finite sets of valuations on which Definition 1.9 (ii) defines deg_E.

IUT.PaperIV.ADiv.restrictdef

noncomputable def ADiv.restrict (E : Finset (Valuations F)) (a : ADiv F) : ADiv F :=
  a.filter (· ∈ E)

𝔞_E, the portion of 𝔞 supported in E.

IUT.PaperIV.degEdef

noncomputable def degE (E : PlaceSet F) (a : ADiv F) : ℝ :=
  degF (ADiv.restrict E.1 a) / ∑ v ∈ E.1, (localDeg v : ℝ)

Definition 1.9 (ii), with the unnormalized degree in the numerator (see the module docstring): for E a nonempty set of valuations over one place of ℚ, deg_E(𝔞) = deg_F(𝔞_E) / ∑_{v ∈ E} [F_v : ℚ_{v_ℚ}].

IUT.PaperIV.ADiv.restrict_addtheorem

theorem ADiv.restrict_add (E : Finset (Valuations F)) (a b : ADiv F) :
  ADiv.restrict E (a + b) = ADiv.restrict E a + ADiv.restrict E b

IUT.PaperIV.degE_addtheorem

theorem degE_add (E : PlaceSet F) (a b : ADiv F) :
  degE E (a + b) = degE E a + degE E b

IUT.PaperIV.ADiv.restrict_effectivetheorem

theorem ADiv.restrict_effective {E : Finset (Valuations F)} {a : ADiv F} (h : a.Effective) :

IUT.PaperIV.degE_nonnegtheorem

theorem degE_nonneg {E : PlaceSet F} {a : ADiv F} (h : a.Effective) :
