IUT.PaperIV.degE_eq_normalizedDegtheorem

theorem degE_eq_normalizedDeg {E : PlaceSet F} (a : ADiv F)
  (hE : ∑ v ∈ E.1, (localDeg v : ℝ) = Module.finrank ℚ F) :
  degE E a = normalizedDeg (ADiv.restrict E.1 a)

If the local degrees over E sum to [F : ℚ], then deg_E(𝔞) is the normalized degree of 𝔞_E. The hypothesis holds when E is the set of all valuations over one v_ℚ; this file proves that only for the archimedean place (sum_localDeg_arc).

IUT.PaperIV.arcValuationsdef

noncomputable def arcValuations (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    Finset (Valuations F) :=
  Finset.univ.map ⟨Sum.inr, Sum.inr_injective⟩

The set of all archimedean valuations, i.e. the valuations over the archimedean place of ℚ.

IUT.PaperIV.sum_localDeg_arctheorem

theorem sum_localDeg_arc :
  ∑ v ∈ arcValuations F, (localDeg v : ℝ) = Module.finrank ℚ F

The local degrees [F_w : ℝ] over all archimedean w sum to [F : ℚ].

IUT.PaperIV.arcPlaceSetdef

noncomputable def arcPlaceSet (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] : PlaceSet F :=
  ⟨arcValuations F, by
    refine ⟨?_, none, ?_⟩
    · rw [arcValuations, Finset.map_nonempty]; exact Finset.univ_nonempty
    · intro v hv
      rw [arcValuations, Finset.mem_map] at hv
      obtain ⟨w, -, rfl⟩ := hv
      rfl⟩

The set of all archimedean valuations, as an element of PlaceSet F: it is nonempty and all its elements lie over the archimedean place of ℚ.

IUT.PaperIV.degE_arc_eq_normalizedDegtheorem

theorem degE_arc_eq_normalizedDeg (a : ADiv F) :
  degE (arcPlaceSet F) a = normalizedDeg (ADiv.restrict (arcValuations F) a)

Unconditional instance. For E the set of all archimedean valuations, deg_E(𝔞) = deg(𝔞_E).

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback

IUT/PaperIV/DegreePullback.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.Definition1_9, IUT.Applications.VojtaNumberField

IUT IV, Definition 1.9 (i): pull-back of arithmetic divisors and invariance of the

Module documentation

normalized degree

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Definition 1.9 (pages 21 and 22), the definitions of log(𝔡^{F□}) and log(𝔣^{F□}) in the statement of Theorem 1.10 (pages 22 and 23) and Step (ii) of the proof of Theorem 1.10 (page 24); Mochizuki, Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position ([GenEll]), §1 (pages 3 and 4: arithmetic divisors, principal arithmetic divisors, the degree deg_F, the normalized degree and its invariance under finite extension for arithmetic line bundles), Definition 1.5 (page 8), Propositions 1.6 and 1.7 with the proof of 1.7 (pages 9 and 10). Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 21 to 24; [GenEll] pages 3, 4, 8, 9 and 10. Pages checked against rendered images: all of these.

The conventions, and which sentences fix them
  • IUT IV page 21: the degree deg_F sends a nonarchimedean v to log(q_v) and an archimedean v to 1; page 22: deg = deg_F/[F : ℚ], and "Thus, for any finite extension K of F, we have deg(𝔞|_K) = deg(𝔞)", where deg(𝔞|_K) is the normalized degree of "the pull-back 𝔞|_K ∈ ADiv_ℝ(K) [defined in the evident fashion] of 𝔞 to K". The page prints no formula for the pull-back and no principal divisor.
  • [GenEll] page 4 prints the principal arithmetic divisor ADiv(f) = ∑_{v non} ord_v(f)·v - ∑_{v arc} [F_v : ℝ]·log(|f|_v)·v, the same degree map (weight 1 at every archimedean place), and the isomorphism ADiv(F)/APrc(F) ≅ APic(Spec 𝒪_F), under which it states deg_K(𝓛|_{Spec 𝒪_K}) = deg_F(𝓛) (normalized) for arithmetic line bundles. This display fixes the archimedean coefficient convention: the factor [F_v : ℝ] sits in the coefficient, not in the weight. With it the degree of a principal divisor is zero (degPb_degF_principal); no coefficient convention at complex places has to be invented.
  • The pull-back of divisors is not printed on either page. This file defines it as the pull-back that matches the pull-back of arithmetic line bundles: at a finite place w | v the coefficient is multiplied by the ramification index e(w|v), and at an archimedean place w | v by the local degree [L_w : K_v] (1 or 2; 2 exactly for a complex w over a real v). This choice is derived, not quoted. Two checks that it is the evident one: degPb_pullback_principal proves that it sends the principal divisor of x ∈ K^× to the principal divisor of x in L (both as printed on [GenEll] page 4), and the coefficient formulas degPbPullback_apply_inl, degPbPullback_apply_inr state it place by place. The identification with the pull-back of arithmetic line bundles through ADiv/APrc ≅ APic is not formalized. [GenEll] takes integer coefficients at finite places; IUT IV takes real ones; the definitions here use real coefficients throughout.
What is proved
  • degPbPullback (an additive map ADiv(K) → ADiv(L)), with the coefficient formulas.
  • degPb_degF_pullback: deg_L(𝔞|_L) = [L : K]·deg_K(𝔞), from ∑_{w | v} e(w|v) f(w|v) = [L : K] and q_w = q_v^{f(w|v)} at finite places and from ∑_{w | v} [L_w : K_v] = [L : K] at archimedean places (Mathlib's Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank, Ideal.absNorm_pow_inertiaDeg, InfinitePlace.sum_inertiaDeg_eq_finrank). These are the content; the definition does not build them in.
  • degPb_normalizedDeg_pullback: **the invariance deg(𝔞|_L) = deg(𝔞) of Definition 1.9 (i)**.
  • degPbPrincipal, degPb_degF_principal: the principal divisor of [GenEll] page 4 has degree zero (Mathlib's product formula NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one), and degPb_pullback_principal.
  • degPb_logDiffNF_tower: log-diff_L = log-diff_K + (1/[L : ℚ])·log N(𝔇_{L/K}), with logDiffNF of IUT.VojtaNumberField (Mathlib's natAbs_discr_eq_absNorm_differentIdeal_mul_natAbs_discr_pow).
  • degPb_logDiff_add_cond_le: for a finite set S of primes of K and the reduced divisor of L supported on the primes over S, log-diff_K + log-cond_K ≤ log-diff_L + log-cond_L (normalized degrees). This is the shape of the first inequality of Step (ii) on page 24, log(𝔡^{F_tpd}) + log(𝔣^{F_tpd}) ≤ log(𝔡^F) + log(𝔣^F), where the conductor 𝔣 of page 23 is the reduced divisor with the support of 𝔮, and the support of 𝔮 over F is the set of places over the support over F_tpd. The paper derives the inequality from Proposition 1.3 (i); here the input is Mathlib's bound w^{e(w|v) - 1} ∣ 𝔇_{L/K}.
  • degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_finite, degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_iff, degPb_logDiffNF_add_logCondNF_le: for y ∈ K off the boundary (y ≠ 0, y ≠ 1), the conductor is finite and log-diff_K + log-cond_K(y) ≤ log-diff_L + log-cond_L(y) with logCondNF of IUT.VojtaNumberField (the conductor of a point of ℙ¹ \ {0, 1, ∞}).
Not proved
  • The invariance deg_{E|K}(𝔞|_K) = deg_E(𝔞) of Definition 1.9 (ii).
  • The isomorphism ADiv/APrc ≅ APic of [GenEll] page 4 and the pull-back of arithmetic line bundles.
  • The inequality of Step (ii) for the paper's own objects: the divisor 𝔮 of q-parameters of the elliptic curve and the fields F_tpd ⊆ F of Theorem 1.10 are not defined here; only the inequality for an arbitrary reduced conductor pulled back from the smaller field is proved. The second inequality of Step (ii) (the bound by log(2^{11}·3^3·5^2)) and the bounds on log(𝔡^K) are not treated.
  • [GenEll] Proposition 1.7 (log-conductor and log-different along a finite covering of curves) is a different statement; it is not formalized.
Public declarations
variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] (L : Type*) [Field L] [NumberField L]

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPrimeOfdef

def degPbPrimeOf (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L)) :
    HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L) where
  asIdeal := q.1
  isPrime := q.2.1
  ne_bot := by
    have := q.2.2
    exact Ideal.ne_bot_of_liesOver_of_ne_bot v.ne_bot q.1

The height one prime of 𝓞 L given by a prime ideal of 𝓞 L lying over the prime v of 𝓞 K.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbSingledef

noncomputable def degPbSingle : Valuations K → ADiv L
  | .inl v => ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L),
      Finsupp.single (.inl (degPbPrimeOf L v q)) (q.1.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ)
  | .inr v => ∑ w ∈ (v.placesOver L).toFinset, Finsupp.single (.inr w) (v.inertiaDeg w : ℝ)

The pull-back to L of the arithmetic divisor 1 · v of K: at a finite place v the sum of e(w|v) · w over the primes w of 𝓞 L over v; at an archimedean place v the sum of [L_w : K_v] · w over the archimedean places w of L over v, where [L_w : K_v] is Mathlib's InfinitePlace.inertiaDeg, the degree of the completion L_w over K_v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPullbackdef

noncomputable def degPbPullback : ADiv K →+ ADiv L :=
  Finsupp.liftAddHom fun v => (smulAddHom ℝ (ADiv L)).flip (degPbSingle L v)

The pull-back 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞|_L of arithmetic divisors along K ⊆ L, extended additively from degPbSingle. Its coefficients are computed in degPbPullback_apply_inl and degPbPullback_apply_inr.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPullback_singletheorem

theorem degPbPullback_single (v : Valuations K) (c : ℝ) :
  degPbPullback L (Finsupp.single v c) = c • degPbSingle L v

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbSingle_inl_apply_inltheorem

theorem degPbSingle_inl_apply_inl (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))
  (w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L)) :
  degPbSingle L (.inl v) (.inl w) =
    if v = HeightOneSpectrum.under (𝓞 K) w then (w.asIdeal.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ)
    else 0

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbSingle_inr_apply_inltheorem

theorem degPbSingle_inr_apply_inl (v : InfinitePlace K) (w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L)) :
  degPbSingle L (.inr v) (.inl w) = 0

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbSingle_inl_apply_inrtheorem

theorem degPbSingle_inl_apply_inr (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (w : InfinitePlace L) :
  degPbSingle L (.inl v) (.inr w) = 0

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_liesOver_ifftheorem

theorem degPb_liesOver_iff (v : InfinitePlace K) (w : InfinitePlace L) :
  w.LiesOver v ↔ v = w.comap (algebraMap K L)

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbSingle_inr_apply_inrtheorem

theorem degPbSingle_inr_apply_inr (v : InfinitePlace K) (w : InfinitePlace L) :
  degPbSingle L (.inr v) (.inr w) =
    if v = w.comap (algebraMap K L) then (v.inertiaDeg w : ℝ) else 0

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPullback_apply_inltheorem

theorem degPbPullback_apply_inl (a : ADiv K) (w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L)) :
  degPbPullback L a (.inl w) =
    (w.asIdeal.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ) * a (.inl (HeightOneSpectrum.under (𝓞 K) w))

The coefficient of the pull-back at a finite place. For a prime w of 𝓞 L over the prime v = w ∩ 𝓞 K, the coefficient of 𝔞|_L at w is e(w|v) times the coefficient of 𝔞 at v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPullback_apply_inrtheorem

theorem degPbPullback_apply_inr (a : ADiv K) (w : InfinitePlace L) :
  degPbPullback L a (.inr w) =
    ((w.comap (algebraMap K L)).inertiaDeg w : ℝ) * a (.inr (w.comap (algebraMap K L)))

The coefficient of the pull-back at an archimedean place. For an archimedean place w of L over the place v of K below it, the coefficient of 𝔞|_L at w is [L_w : K_v] times the coefficient of 𝔞 at v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_degF_smultheorem

theorem degPb_degF_smul {F : Type*} [Field F] [NumberField F] (c : ℝ) (x : ADiv F) :
  degF (c • x) = c * degF x

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_finrank_inttheorem

theorem degPb_finrank_int : Module.finrank (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) = Module.finrank K L

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_degF_single_inltheorem

theorem degPb_degF_single_inl (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  degF (degPbSingle L (.inl v)) = Module.finrank K L * degWeight (.inl v : Valuations K)

The degrees of the places of L over a finite place v of K, weighted by the ramification indices, add up to [L : K]·log q_v: ∑_{w | v} e(w|v)·log q_w = [L : K]·log q_v, from ∑_{w | v} e(w|v) f(w|v) = [L : K] and q_w = q_v^{f(w|v)}.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_degF_single_inrtheorem

theorem degPb_degF_single_inr (v : InfinitePlace K) :
  degF (degPbSingle L (.inr v)) = Module.finrank K L * degWeight (.inr v : Valuations K)

The local degrees [L_w : K_v] over an archimedean place v of K add up to [L : K].

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_degF_pullbacktheorem

theorem degPb_degF_pullback (a : ADiv K) :
  degF (degPbPullback L a) = Module.finrank K L * degF a

deg_L(𝔞|_L) = [L : K]·deg_K(𝔞).

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_normalizedDeg_pullbacktheorem

theorem degPb_normalizedDeg_pullback (a : ADiv K) :
  normalizedDeg (degPbPullback L a) = normalizedDeg a

Invariance of the normalized degree under pull-back (IUT IV, Definition 1.9 (i), page 22): deg(𝔞|_L) = deg(𝔞).

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_sum_ramificationIdx_logtheorem

theorem degPb_sum_ramificationIdx_log (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L),
      (q.1.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ) * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm q.1) =
    Module.finrank K L * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)

The fiber identity behind the invariance at a finite place, in the form used below: ∑_{w | v} e(w|v)·log q_w = [L : K]·log q_v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_logDiffNF_towertheorem

theorem degPb_logDiffNF_tower :
  logDiffNF L = logDiffNF K +
    Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (differentIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L))) / Module.finrank ℚ L

The transitivity formula for the log-different: log-diff_L = log-diff_K + (1/[L : ℚ])·log N(𝔇_{L/K}), where 𝔇_{L/K} is the relative different ideal of 𝓞 L over 𝓞 K. From Mathlib's |d_L| = N(𝔇_{L/K})·|d_K|^{[L : K]}.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_sum_ramification_sub_one_letheorem

theorem degPb_sum_ramification_sub_one_le (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) :
  ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L),
      ((q.1.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) : ℝ) - 1) * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm q.1) ≤
    Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (differentIdeal (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)))

For the primes w of 𝓞 L over the primes of a finite set S of primes of 𝓞 K, ∑ (e(w|v) - 1)·log q_w ≤ log N(𝔇_{L/K}): the ideal ∏ w^{e(w|v) - 1} divides the relative different.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_logDiff_add_cond_letheorem

theorem degPb_logDiff_add_cond_le (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) :
  logDiffNF K + (∑ v ∈ S, Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)) / Module.finrank ℚ K ≤
    logDiffNF L + (∑ v ∈ S, ∑ q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L),
      Real.log (Ideal.absNorm q.1)) / Module.finrank ℚ L

**Monotonicity of log-different plus log-conductor, for a conductor pulled back from K.** For a finite set S of primes of 𝓞 K, with normalized degree (1/[K : ℚ])∑_{v ∈ S} log q_v, and the reduced divisor of L supported on the primes over S, with normalized degree (1/[L : ℚ])∑_{v ∈ S} ∑_{w | v} log q_w: log-diff_K + log-cond_K ≤ log-diff_L + log-cond_L. The relative different 𝔇_{L/K}, which is divisible by w^{e(w|v) - 1}, compensates the loss ∑ (e(w|v) - 1)·log q_w of the reduced conductor.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_under_primeOftheorem

theorem degPb_under_primeOf (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (q : v.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L)) :
  HeightOneSpectrum.under (𝓞 K) (degPbPrimeOf L v q) = v

The prime of 𝓞 K below degPbPrimeOf L v q is v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_primeOf_injectivetheorem

theorem degPb_primeOf_injective (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  Function.Injective (degPbPrimeOf L v)

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_pow_eq_one_ifftheorem

theorem degPb_pow_eq_one_iff {a : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
  a ^ n = 1 ↔ a = 1

A valuation of ℤᵐ⁰ whose n-th power is 1, for n ≠ 0, is 1.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_ifftheorem

theorem degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_iff (w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L)) (y : K) :
  MeetsBoundaryAt L w (algebraMap K L y) ↔
    MeetsBoundaryAt K (HeightOneSpectrum.under (𝓞 K) w) y

The conductor pulls back. A point y ∈ K of ℙ¹ meets {0, 1, ∞} at a prime w of 𝓞 L exactly when it meets it at the prime of 𝓞 K below w: the valuations satisfy v_w(y) = e(w|v)·v_v(y).

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_card_quottheorem

theorem degPb_card_quot {F : Type*} [Field F] [NumberField F] (I : Ideal (𝓞 F)) :
  (Nat.card (𝓞 F ⧸ I) : ℝ) = Ideal.absNorm I

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_valuation_ne_one_finitetheorem

theorem degPb_valuation_ne_one_finite {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
  {v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | v.valuation K x ≠ 1}.Finite

For x ≠ 0, v(x) ≠ 1 for only finitely many primes v of 𝓞 K.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_finitetheorem

theorem degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_finite {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1) :
  {v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | MeetsBoundaryAt K v y}.Finite

**The conductor of a point of ℙ¹ \ {0, 1, ∞} is finite**: for y ∉ {0, 1} only finitely many primes of 𝓞 K meet the boundary at y.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_logDiffNF_add_logCondNF_letheorem

theorem degPb_logDiffNF_add_logCondNF_le {y : K} (hy0 : y ≠ 0) (hy1 : y ≠ 1) :
  logDiffNF K + logCondNF K y ≤ logDiffNF L + logCondNF L (algebraMap K L y)

**Monotonicity of log-diff + log-cond for a point of ℙ¹ \ {0, 1, ∞}.** For a finite extension L of K and y ∈ K off the boundary (y ≠ 0, y ≠ 1; y ≠ ∞ holds since y ∈ K): log-diff_K + log-cond_K(y) ≤ log-diff_L + log-cond_L(y), in the normalization of IUT.VojtaNumberField (both evaluated at the field given, not at the minimal field of definition of y). The hypotheses make the conductor finite (degPb_meetsBoundaryAt_finite), so both log-conductors are finite sums.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbOrddef

noncomputable def degPbOrd (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) (x : K) : ℤ :=
  -WithZero.log (v.valuation K x)

ord_v(x), the order of x ∈ K at the prime v of 𝓞 K, normalized so that a generator of the maximal ideal of the localization at v has order 1. Mathlib's v-adic valuation of x is exp(-ord_v(x)), so ord_v(x) = -log(v(x)) with WithZero.log.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbOrd_finitetheorem

theorem degPbOrd_finite {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
  {v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) | degPbOrd v x ≠ 0}.Finite

For x ≠ 0, ord_v(x) ≠ 0 for only finitely many v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPrincipalCoeffdef

noncomputable def degPbPrincipalCoeff (x : K) : Valuations K → ℝ
  | .inl v => (degPbOrd v x : ℝ)
  | .inr w => -((w.mult : ℝ) * Real.log (w x))

The coefficients of the principal arithmetic divisor of x: ord_v(x) at a finite place and -[K_v : ℝ]·log|x|_v at an archimedean place v, with [K_v : ℝ] = InfinitePlace.mult v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPrincipalCoeff_support_finitetheorem

theorem degPbPrincipalCoeff_support_finite {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
  (Function.support (degPbPrincipalCoeff x)).Finite

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPbPrincipaldef

noncomputable def degPbPrincipal (x : Kˣ) : ADiv K :=
  Finsupp.ofSupportFinite (degPbPrincipalCoeff (x : K))
    (degPbPrincipalCoeff_support_finite x.ne_zero)

The principal arithmetic divisor of x ∈ K^×, as printed in [GenEll], page 4: ADiv(x) = ∑_{v finite} ord_v(x)·v - ∑_{v archimedean} [K_v : ℝ]·log(|x|_v)·v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_log_finitePlacetheorem

theorem degPb_log_finitePlace {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  Real.log (FinitePlace.mk v x) = -(degPbOrd v x : ℝ) * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal)

The v-adic absolute value of x ≠ 0 (the finite place attached to v) is q_v^{-ord_v(x)}, so its logarithm is -ord_v(x)·log q_v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_finitePlace_postheorem

theorem degPb_finitePlace_pos {x : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) :
  0 < FinitePlace.mk v x

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_degF_principaltheorem

theorem degPb_degF_principal (x : Kˣ) : degF (degPbPrincipal x) = 0

The degree of a principal arithmetic divisor is zero (the product formula), in the convention of [GenEll] page 4: weight log q_v at a finite place, weight 1 at an archimedean place, coefficient -[K_v : ℝ]·log|x|_v at an archimedean place.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_ord_algebraMaptheorem

theorem degPb_ord_algebraMap (w : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 L)) (x : K) :
  degPbOrd w (algebraMap K L x) =
    w.asIdeal.ramificationIdx (𝓞 K) * degPbOrd (HeightOneSpectrum.under (𝓞 K) w) x

ord_w(x) = e(w|v)·ord_v(x) for x ∈ K and a prime w of 𝓞 L over v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_mult_mul_inertiaDegtheorem

theorem degPb_mult_mul_inertiaDeg (w : InfinitePlace L) :
  (w.comap (algebraMap K L)).mult * (w.comap (algebraMap K L)).inertiaDeg w = w.mult

[K_v : ℝ]·[L_w : K_v] = [L_w : ℝ] for an archimedean place w of L over v.

IUT.PaperIV.DegreePullback.degPb_pullback_principaltheorem

theorem degPb_pullback_principal (x : Kˣ) :
  degPbPullback L (degPbPrincipal x) =
    degPbPrincipal (Units.map (algebraMap K L).toMonoidHom x)

The pull-back of a principal divisor is the principal divisor of the image: ADiv(x)|_L = ADiv(x) for x ∈ K^× viewed in L^×. This checks the multipliers of degPbPullback against the principal divisors of [GenEll] page 4, independently of the degree.

IUT.PaperIV.FreyReduction

IUT/PaperIV/FreyReduction.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LegendreFrey

Reduction of the Frey curve of a triple at the odd primes

Module documentation

Sources.

  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Corollary 2.2 and the beginning of its proof (pages 41 to 43). Page 41 regards X = ℙ¹_ℚ minus {0, 1, ∞} as the λ-line of the Legendre form y² = x(x - 1)(x - λ), and Corollary 2.2 (i) introduces log(q^∀) and log(q^{∤2}), the normalized degrees of the arithmetic divisors cut out by the q-parameters of an elliptic curve over a number field at all nonarchimedean primes, respectively at those not dividing 2. Page 42 uses that E_F has stable reduction at every nonarchimedean prime of F, and condition (C2) and page 43 use log-cond_D(x_E) and log(f^{F_tpd}).
  • Silverman's standard facts on minimal models and reduction types, as encoded in Mathlib's Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Reduction.lean.

Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 41 to 43. Pages checked against rendered images: IUT IV pages 41 to 43.

What is and is not taken from the paper. The pages read do not mention a triple, the Frey curve, its reduction at odd primes, or the relation v(q) = -v(j). They use the q-parameters and the conductor of curves over number fields. This file checks the classical arithmetic that lies behind these invariants for the rational points of the λ-line coming from coprime triples a + b = c, through the Frey curve y² = x(x - a)(x + b) (a quadratic twist of the Legendre curve, IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_variableChange_legendre). The Legendre model at λ itself is not treated here: minimality, the reduction type and the discriminant change under a quadratic twist (a twist ramified at an odd prime turns multiplicative into additive reduction), and only the j-invariant is shared by the two curves.

What this file proves. Let a + b = c be positive and coprime, p an odd prime, and W the Frey model IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve a b base changed from ℤ to ℚ_[p]. Valuations are those of Mathlib's reduction API for the discrete valuation ring ℤ_[p], with values in ℤᵐ⁰ (multiplicative: the additive valuation n corresponds to exp (-n)).

  1. A general minimality criterion over any discrete valuation ring: an integral Weierstrass equation whose Δ or c₄ is a unit is minimal (freyRed_isMinimal_of_val); two minimal equations related by a change of variables have discriminants of equal valuation (freyRed_val_Δ_eq_of_isMinimal).
  2. W is integral and minimal at p (freyRedModel_isMinimal).
  3. HasGoodReduction ℤ_[p] W ↔ ¬ p ∣ abc and HasMultiplicativeReduction ℤ_[p] W ↔ p ∣ abc; the reduction is never additive.
  4. v(Δ) = exp (-2 v_p(abc)), also for every minimal model of W, and, when p ∣ abc, v(j) = exp (2 v_p(abc)), that is v_p(j) = -2 v_p(abc). Here v_p is Mathlib's multiplicity p on natural numbers (equal to padicValNat p by Nat.padicValNat_def).
  5. The set of odd primes at which W has multiplicative reduction is the set of odd prime factors of abc, and twice the product of these primes is Challenge.rad (abc) (abc is always even).
  6. At p = 2: W over ℤ_[2] has neither good nor multiplicative reduction in Mathlib's sense (both Δ and c₄ are divisible by 16), and for the triple 3 + 16 = 19 the model is not minimal at 2 (an explicit change of variables with u = 2 keeps it integral).

Not proved.

  • The relation v(q) = -v(j) between the Tate parameter and the j-invariant at a prime of multiplicative reduction: it needs Tate uniformization, and Mathlib has no Tate curve and no q-parameter.
  • The conductor exponent: Mathlib defines no conductor of an elliptic curve. Item 5 is stated with HasMultiplicativeReduction and Challenge.rad instead; the statement "the conductor exponent at an odd prime of multiplicative reduction is 1" is not formalized.
  • The minimal model, the minimal discriminant and the reduction type at 2 for a general triple; only the single non-minimal example above is proved.
  • Anything over a number field other than ℚ, the stable reduction of E_F over F, and every assertion of Corollary 2.2.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRed_isMinimal_of_valtheorem

theorem freyRed_isMinimal_of_val (W : WeierstrassCurve K) [IsIntegral R W]
  (h : (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal R).valuation K W.Δ = 1 ∨
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal R).valuation K W.c₄ = 1) :
  IsMinimal R W

Minimality criterion. Over the fraction field K of a discrete valuation ring R, an integral Weierstrass equation whose discriminant or whose c₄ has valuation 1 (is a unit of R) is minimal in the sense of WeierstrassCurve.IsMinimal. If v(c₄) = 1, a change of variables with u of positive valuation would make c₄' = u⁻⁴ c₄ non-integral; if v(Δ) = 1, no integral model has a discriminant of larger multiplicative valuation.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRed_val_Δ_eq_of_isMinimaltheorem

theorem freyRed_val_Δ_eq_of_isMinimal (W : WeierstrassCurve K) (C : VariableChange K)
  [hW : IsMinimal R W] [hCW : IsMinimal R (C • W)] :
  (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal R).valuation K (C • W).Δ =
    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal R).valuation K W.Δ

Two minimal Weierstrass equations related by a change of variables have discriminants of the same valuation.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedValabbrev

noncomputable abbrev freyRedVal (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    Valuation ℚ_[p] (WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
  (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]).valuation ℚ_[p]

The valuation of ℚ_[p] used by Mathlib's reduction API for the discrete valuation ring ℤ_[p]: the adic valuation of its maximal ideal, with values in ℤᵐ⁰.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedVal_natCast_eq_one_ifftheorem

theorem freyRedVal_natCast_eq_one_iff (n : ℕ) : freyRedVal p (n : ℚ_[p]) = 1 ↔ ¬ p ∣ n

A natural number has valuation 1 in ℚ_[p] exactly when p does not divide it.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedVal_ptheorem

theorem freyRedVal_p : freyRedVal p (p : ℚ_[p]) = WithZero.exp (-1 : ℤ)

The prime p is a uniformizer: its valuation is exp (-1).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedVal_natCasttheorem

theorem freyRedVal_natCast (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
  freyRedVal p (n : ℚ_[p]) = WithZero.exp (-(multiplicity p n : ℤ))

The valuation of a nonzero natural number in ℚ_[p] is exp (-v_p(n)).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModeldef

noncomputable def freyRedModel (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (a b : ℕ) : WeierstrassCurve ℚ_[p] :=
  (freyCurve (a : ℤ) b).map (Int.castRingHom ℚ_[p])

The Frey curve y² = x(x - a)(x + b) of a pair of natural numbers, as the base change to ℚ_[p] of the integral model IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve (a : ℤ) b over ℤ.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_isIntegraltheorem

theorem freyRedModel_isIntegral (a b : ℕ) : IsIntegral ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b)

The Frey model over ℚ_[p] is integral over ℤ_[p]: it is the base change of the Frey model over ℤ_[p].

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_Δtheorem

theorem freyRedModel_Δ {a b c : ℕ} (h : a + b = c) :
  (freyRedModel p a b).Δ = ((16 * (a * b * c) ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℚ_[p])

The discriminant of the Frey model is the natural number 16 (abc)².

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_c₄theorem

theorem freyRedModel_c₄ (a b : ℕ) :
  (freyRedModel p a b).c₄ = ((16 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) : ℕ) : ℚ_[p])

The invariant c₄ of the Frey model is the natural number 16 (a² + ab + b²).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_val_Δ_eq_one_ifftheorem

theorem freyRedModel_val_Δ_eq_one_iff {a b c : ℕ} (h : a + b = c) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
  freyRedVal p (freyRedModel p a b).Δ = 1 ↔ ¬ p ∣ a * b * c

At an odd prime, the discriminant of the Frey model has valuation 1 exactly when p does not divide abc.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_val_c₄_eq_onetheorem

theorem freyRedModel_val_c₄_eq_one {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hd : p ∣ a * b * c) : freyRedVal p (freyRedModel p a b).c₄ = 1

For a coprime pair, at an odd prime dividing abc, the invariant c₄ of the Frey model is a unit of ℤ_[p].

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_isMinimaltheorem

theorem freyRedModel_isMinimal {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : IsMinimal ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b)

Minimality at odd primes. For a coprime pair a + b = c and an odd prime p, the Frey model is a minimal Weierstrass equation over ℤ_[p]: if p ∤ abc its discriminant is a unit; if p ∣ abc its c₄ is a unit.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_hasGoodReduction_ifftheorem

theorem freyRedModel_hasGoodReduction_iff {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : HasGoodReduction ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b) ↔ ¬ p ∣ a * b * c

Good reduction. For a coprime pair a + b = c and an odd prime p, the Frey model has good reduction at p (in the sense of WeierstrassCurve.HasGoodReduction) exactly when p does not divide abc.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_hasMultiplicativeReduction_ifftheorem

theorem freyRedModel_hasMultiplicativeReduction_iff {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
  HasMultiplicativeReduction ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b) ↔ p ∣ a * b * c

Multiplicative reduction. For a coprime pair a + b = c and an odd prime p, the Frey model has multiplicative reduction at p (in the sense of WeierstrassCurve.HasMultiplicativeReduction) exactly when p divides abc.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_not_hasAdditiveReductiontheorem

theorem freyRedModel_not_hasAdditiveReduction {a b c : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) : ¬ HasAdditiveReduction ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b)

The reduction of the Frey model at an odd prime is never additive.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_val_Δtheorem

theorem freyRedModel_val_Δ {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c)
  (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
  freyRedVal p (freyRedModel p a b).Δ =
    WithZero.exp (-(2 * multiplicity p (a * b * c) : ℤ))

Valuation of the discriminant. For positive a, b with a + b = c and an odd prime p, the discriminant of the Frey model has valuation exp (-2 v_p(abc)): additively, v_p(Δ) = 2 v_p(abc).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_val_minimal_Δtheorem

theorem freyRedModel_val_minimal_Δ {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (C : VariableChange ℚ_[p])
  [IsMinimal ℤ_[p] (C • freyRedModel p a b)] :
  freyRedVal p (C • freyRedModel p a b).Δ =
    WithZero.exp (-(2 * multiplicity p (a * b * c) : ℤ))

Valuation of the minimal discriminant. For a coprime pair of positive numbers a + b = c and an odd prime p, every minimal Weierstrass equation over ℤ_[p] isomorphic to the Frey model (by a change of variables over ℚ_[p]) has discriminant of valuation exp (-2 v_p(abc)).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_isElliptictheorem

theorem freyRedModel_isElliptic {a b : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) :
  (freyRedModel p a b).IsElliptic

For positive a, b, the Frey model over ℚ_[p] is an elliptic curve.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_val_jtheorem

theorem freyRedModel_val_j {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hd : p ∣ a * b * c) [(freyRedModel p a b).IsElliptic] :
  freyRedVal p (freyRedModel p a b).j =
    WithZero.exp ((2 * multiplicity p (a * b * c) : ℕ) : ℤ)

**Valuation of j.** For a coprime pair of positive numbers a + b = c and an odd prime p dividing abc, the j-invariant of the Frey model has valuation exp (2 v_p(abc)): additively, v_p(j) = -2 v_p(abc). (The ellipticity instance is supplied by freyRedModel_isElliptic.)

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedOddMultPrimedef

def freyRedOddMultPrime (a b p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ hp : p.Prime, p ≠ 2 ∧
    letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
    HasMultiplicativeReduction ℤ_[p] (freyRedModel p a b)

The prime p is odd and the Frey model of (a, b) has multiplicative reduction at p, in the sense of WeierstrassCurve.HasMultiplicativeReduction over ℤ_[p].

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedOddMultPrime_ifftheorem

theorem freyRedOddMultPrime_iff {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) (p : ℕ) :
  freyRedOddMultPrime a b p ↔ p ∈ (a * b * c).primeFactors ∧ p ≠ 2

For a coprime pair of positive numbers a + b = c, the odd primes of multiplicative reduction of the Frey model are the odd prime factors of abc.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRed_two_dvdtheorem

theorem freyRed_two_dvd {a b c : ℕ} (h : a + b = c) : 2 ∣ a * b * c

For a coprime pair a + b = c, the product abc is even.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRed_oddMultPrimes_radtheorem

theorem freyRed_oddMultPrimes_rad {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) :
  {p | freyRedOddMultPrime a b p} = ↑((a * b * c).primeFactors.erase 2) ∧
    2 * ∏ p ∈ (a * b * c).primeFactors.erase 2, p = Challenge.rad (a * b * c)

The odd part of the radical. For a coprime pair of positive numbers a + b = c, the set of odd primes at which the Frey model has multiplicative reduction is the set of odd prime factors of abc, and twice the product of these primes is rad(abc).

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_two_not_good_not_multtheorem

theorem freyRedModel_two_not_good_not_mult {a b c : ℕ} (h : a + b = c) :
  ¬ HasGoodReduction ℤ_[2] (freyRedModel 2 a b) ∧
    ¬ HasMultiplicativeReduction ℤ_[2] (freyRedModel 2 a b)

At the prime 2, the Frey model (an integral equation over ℤ_[2], minimal or not) is neither of good nor of multiplicative reduction in the sense of Mathlib: both Δ = 16(abc)² and c₄ = 16(a² + ab + b²) lie in the maximal ideal.

IUT.FreyReduction.freyRedModel_two_not_isMinimaltheorem

theorem freyRedModel_two_not_isMinimal : ¬ IsMinimal ℤ_[2] (freyRedModel 2 3 16)

**The model is not minimal at 2 in general.** For the coprime triple 3 + 16 = 19, the Frey model y² = x(x - 3)(x + 16) is not a minimal Weierstrass equation over ℤ_[2]: the change of variables x = 4x', y = 8y' + 4x' (u = 2, r = t = 0, s = 1) carries it to the integral equation y'² + x'y' = x'³ + 3x'² - 3x', whose discriminant is 2⁻¹²Δ.

IUT.PaperIV.LegendreFrey

IUT/PaperIV/LegendreFrey.lean · imports IUT.Applications.ABCSpecialization

The Legendre curve, the Frey curve of a triple, and the j-invariant on the λ-line

Module documentation

Sources.

  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Proposition 1.8 (vi) (statement on page 19, proof on pages 20 and 21), which descends an elliptic curve with rational 2-torsion to a curve in Legendre form after a possibly trivial quadratic twist; Theorem 1.10 (page 22), which uses the model in Legendre form over the tripodal field; Corollary 2.2 (page 41), which regards X = ℙ¹_ℚ minus {0, 1, ∞} as the λ-line of the Legendre form y² = x(x - 1)(x - λ) with its classifying morphism to the moduli stack of elliptic curves; the proof of Corollary 2.2 (i) (page 43), which uses that the pullback to X of the divisor at infinity of the compactified moduli stack has degree 6 to get the equality of bounded discrepancy classes (1/6)·ht_∞ ≈ ht_{ω_X(D)}, and the proof of Corollary 2.2 (ii) (page 43), which excludes the points with one of "four possibilities for the j-invariant"; Corollary 2.3 and its proof (pages 54 and 55).
  • Mochizuki, Fesenko, Hoshi, Minamide, Porowski, Explicit estimates in inter-universal Teichmüller theory, Proposition 2.1 (page 21), which lists these four values: 2¹⁴·31³·5⁻³, 2²·73³·3⁻⁴, 2⁶·3³ = 1728 and 0.

Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 16 to 22, 41 to 43, 45, 54 to 56; Explicit estimates page 21. Pages checked against rendered images: IUT IV pages 18 to 22, 41 to 43, 45, 54 to 56; Explicit estimates page 21.

What is and is not taken from the papers. IUT IV does not print the formula for the j-invariant of the Legendre form, does not use the S₃-symmetry of the λ-line on the pages read (page 41 introduces the λ-line without it), and does not attach a point of the λ-line to an abc triple: the proof of Corollary 2.3 (pages 54 and 55) reduces to [GenEll], Theorem 2.1, and works with arbitrary points of a compactly bounded subset. The formulas below are computed here from Mathlib's definitions of WeierstrassCurve.Δ, WeierstrassCurve.c₄ and WeierstrassCurve.j, not transcribed. For a triple a + b = c this file uses the point λ = a / c of IUT.ABCSpecialization (the point used there to compare Corollary 2.3 with the abc conjecture); the Frey curve y² = x(x - a)(x + b) is the quadratic twist by a of the Legendre curve at λ = -b / a = 1 - c / a, which lies in the same S₃-orbit as a / c, so both normalizations give the same j-invariant (legendreJ_neg_div_eq).

What this file proves.

  1. legendreCurve t is y² = x(x - 1)(x - t) as a WeierstrassCurve; Δ = 16 t²(t - 1)², c₄ = 16(t² - t + 1); over a field with 2 ≠ 0 it is elliptic exactly when t ≠ 0, 1, and then its j is legendreJ t = 2⁸(t² - t + 1)³ / (t²(t - 1)²).
  2. legendreJ is invariant under t ↦ 1 - t and t ↦ t⁻¹ for every t (with Lean's convention x / 0 = 0 at t = 0, 1), hence on the orbit {t, 1 - t, t⁻¹, (1 - t)⁻¹, (t - 1)/t, t/(t - 1)}.
  3. freyCurve a b is y² = x(x - a)(x + b); Δ = 16 a²b²(a + b)², c₄ = 16(a² + ab + b²), j = 2⁸(a² + ab + b²)³ / (a²b²(a + b)²) = legendreJ (a / (a + b)); a change of variables with u² = a carries it to legendreCurve (-b / a).
  4. For positive coprime natural numbers a + b = c, with N = a² + ab + b²: N is odd and coprime to abc; the rational number j = legendreJ (a / c) has denominator dividing (abc)² and divisible by (abc)² / 2⁸, its numerator is divisible by N³ and divides 2⁸N³, and an odd prime divides its denominator exactly when it divides abc. For the integral Frey model over ℤ, an odd prime divides Δ exactly when it divides abc, and then it does not divide c₄. The statement fails at 2: the triple 1 + 1 = 2 gives j = 1728.
  5. The four special values: j = 1728 exactly at t ∈ {-1, 2, 1/2}; j = 2²·73³·3⁻⁴ exactly at t ∈ {9, -8, 9/8, -1/8, 8/9, 1/9} (the triple 1 + 8 = 9 gives this value); j = 2¹⁴·31³·5⁻³ exactly at the roots of three quadratics with discriminant 5·55², none rational; j = 0 exactly at the roots of t² - t + 1, none rational. Each statement assumes t ≠ 0, 1 and characteristic zero.
  6. Height comparison for triples: 6 h(λ) - log(64/27) ≤ h(j(λ)) ≤ 6 h(λ) + 8 log 2 for λ = a / c, with h = Height.logHeight₁. This is an explicit form, on the points of triples, of the degree-6 comparison behind (1/6)·ht_∞ ≈ ht_{ω_X(D)} (page 43); the identification of ht_∞ and ht_{ω_X(D)} with these Weil heights is not formalized. A uniform form over number fields is in IUT/Applications/HeightComparison.lean.

What Mathlib has and lacks. Mathlib has WeierstrassCurve with b₂ … b₈, c₄, c₆, Δ, IsElliptic, j, variable changes and their action, models with given j (ofJ), the isomorphism of curves with equal j over a separably closed field, and, over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring, integral and minimal models with HasGoodReduction, HasMultiplicativeReduction, HasAdditiveReduction and HasSplitMultiplicativeReduction. It lacks Tate curves, q-parameters, conductors and semistable reduction after extension. Minimality of the Frey model at odd primes, its multiplicative reduction at the odd primes dividing abc and the valuation of j there are proved in IUT/PaperIV/FreyReduction.lean, from the arithmetic of Δ and c₄ of item 4; the relation v(q) = -v(j) needs Tate curves and is not proved.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreCurvedef

def legendreCurve (t : R) : WeierstrassCurve R :=
  ⟨0, -(1 + t), 0, t, 0⟩

The Legendre curve y² = x(x - 1)(x - t) = x³ - (1 + t)x² + t x as a Weierstrass curve.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreCurve_disctheorem

theorem legendreCurve_disc (t : R) : (legendreCurve t).Δ = 16 * t ^ 2 * (t - 1) ^ 2

The discriminant of the Legendre curve is 16 t²(t - 1)².

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreCurve_c4theorem

theorem legendreCurve_c4 (t : R) : (legendreCurve t).c₄ = 16 * (t ^ 2 - t + 1)

The invariant c₄ of the Legendre curve is 16(t² - t + 1).

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurvedef

def freyCurve (a b : R) : WeierstrassCurve R :=
  ⟨0, b - a, 0, -(a * b), 0⟩

The Frey curve y² = x(x - a)(x + b) = x³ + (b - a)x² - ab x of a pair a, b.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_disctheorem

theorem freyCurve_disc (a b : R) :
  (freyCurve a b).Δ = 16 * a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 * (a + b) ^ 2

The discriminant of the Frey curve is 16 a²b²(a + b)².

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_c4theorem

theorem freyCurve_c4 (a b : R) : (freyCurve a b).c₄ = 16 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2)

The invariant c₄ of the Frey curve is 16(a² + ab + b²).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreCurve_isElliptic_ifftheorem

theorem legendreCurve_isElliptic_iff (h2 : (2 : K) ≠ 0) (t : K) :
  (legendreCurve t).IsElliptic ↔ t ≠ 0 ∧ t ≠ 1

Over a field with 2 ≠ 0, the Legendre curve is elliptic exactly when t ≠ 0 and t ≠ 1.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_isElliptic_ifftheorem

theorem freyCurve_isElliptic_iff (h2 : (2 : K) ≠ 0) (a b : K) :
  (freyCurve a b).IsElliptic ↔ a ≠ 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ a + b ≠ 0

Over a field with 2 ≠ 0, the Frey curve is elliptic exactly when a, b and a + b are nonzero.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJdef

noncomputable def legendreJ (t : K) : K :=
  2 ^ 8 * (t ^ 2 - t + 1) ^ 3 / (t ^ 2 * (t - 1) ^ 2)

The j-function of the λ-line, 2⁸(t² - t + 1)³ / (t²(t - 1)²). With Lean's convention x / 0 = 0 its value at t = 0 and t = 1 is 0; it is the j-invariant of the Legendre curve only for t ≠ 0, 1 (legendreCurve_jInv).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreCurve_jInvtheorem

theorem legendreCurve_jInv (t : K) [(legendreCurve t).IsElliptic] :
  (legendreCurve t).j = legendreJ t

The j-invariant of the Legendre curve, when it is elliptic, is legendreJ t.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_jInvtheorem

theorem freyCurve_jInv (a b : K) [(freyCurve a b).IsElliptic] :
  (freyCurve a b).j = 2 ^ 8 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3 / (a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 * (a + b) ^ 2)

The j-invariant of the Frey curve, when it is elliptic, is 2⁸(a² + ab + b²)³ / (a²b²(a + b)²).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_one_subtheorem

theorem legendreJ_one_sub (t : K) : legendreJ (1 - t) = legendreJ t

Invariance of the j-function under t ↦ 1 - t, for every t.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_invtheorem

theorem legendreJ_inv (t : K) : legendreJ t⁻¹ = legendreJ t

Invariance of the j-function under t ↦ t⁻¹, for every t.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_orbittheorem

theorem legendreJ_orbit (t : K) (h0 : t ≠ 0) :
  legendreJ (1 - t)⁻¹ = legendreJ t ∧ legendreJ ((t - 1) / t) = legendreJ t ∧
    legendreJ (t / (t - 1)) = legendreJ t

Invariance of the j-function on the orbit of t under the group generated by t ↦ 1 - t and t ↦ t⁻¹: the three remaining elements (1 - t)⁻¹, (t - 1)/t and t/(t - 1).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_div_addtheorem

theorem legendreJ_div_add (a b : K) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : a + b ≠ 0) :
  legendreJ (a / (a + b)) =
    2 ^ 8 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3 / (a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 * (a + b) ^ 2)

The value of the j-function at the point a / (a + b) of a pair.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_neg_div_eqtheorem

theorem legendreJ_neg_div_eq (a b : K) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
  legendreJ (-b / a) = legendreJ (a / (a + b))

The two normalizations -b / a and a / (a + b) of a pair give the same value of the j-function: -b / a = 1 - (a + b) / a and (a + b) / a = (a / (a + b))⁻¹.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_jInv_eq_legendreJtheorem

theorem freyCurve_jInv_eq_legendreJ (a b : K) [h : (freyCurve a b).IsElliptic] :
  (freyCurve a b).j = legendreJ (a / (a + b)) ∧ (freyCurve a b).j = legendreJ (-b / a)

The j-invariant of an elliptic Frey curve is the value of the j-function at a / (a + b), and also at -b / a.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_variableChange_legendretheorem

theorem freyCurve_variableChange_legendre (a b u : K) (hu : u ≠ 0) (h : u ^ 2 = a) :
  (⟨Units.mk0 u hu, 0, 0, 0⟩ : VariableChange K) • freyCurve a b = legendreCurve (-b / a)

The Frey curve is the quadratic twist by a of the Legendre curve at -b / a: if u² = a, the change of variables (x, y) ↦ (u² x', u³ y') carries freyCurve a b to legendreCurve (-b / a).

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyNorm_coprimetheorem

theorem freyNorm_coprime {a b : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) :
  (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2).Coprime (a * b * (a + b))

For coprime natural numbers a, b, the number a² + ab + b² is coprime to a b (a + b).

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyNorm_oddtheorem

theorem freyNorm_odd {a b : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) : Odd (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2)

For coprime natural numbers a, b, the number a² + ab + b² is odd.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_eqtheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_eq (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (h : a + b = c) :
  legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c) =
    ((2 ^ 8 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3 : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((a * b * c) ^ 2 : ℕ)

For a triple a + b = c of positive numbers, the j-function at a / c is 2⁸(a² + ab + b²)³ / (abc)².

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_num_dentheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_num_den (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) :
  ∃ k : ℕ, k ∣ 2 ^ 8 ∧ (a * b * c) ^ 2 = (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).den * k ∧
    (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).num.natAbs * k = 2 ^ 8 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3

The numerator and denominator of the j-invariant of a coprime triple, up to a common factor k: (abc)² = den · k and |num| · k = 2⁸(a² + ab + b²)³, with k ∣ 2⁸.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_den_dvdtheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_den_dvd (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) : (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).den ∣ (a * b * c) ^ 2

The denominator of the j-invariant of a coprime triple divides (abc)².

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_sq_dvdtheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_sq_dvd (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) : (a * b * c) ^ 2 ∣ 2 ^ 8 * (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).den

The denominator of the j-invariant of a coprime triple is at least (abc)² / 2⁸: (abc)² divides 2⁸ · den.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_numtheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_num (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b) (h : a + b = c) :
  (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3 ∣ (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).num.natAbs ∧
    (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).num.natAbs ∣ 2 ^ 8 * (a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2) ^ 3

The numerator of the j-invariant of a coprime triple is divisible by (a² + ab + b²)³ and divides 2⁸(a² + ab + b²)³.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_triple_prime_dvd_den_ifftheorem

theorem legendreJ_triple_prime_dvd_den_iff (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
  p ∣ (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)).den ↔ p ∣ a * b * c

An odd prime divides the denominator of the j-invariant of a coprime triple exactly when it divides abc.

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_prime_dvd_disc_ifftheorem

theorem freyCurve_prime_dvd_disc_iff {a b : ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) :
  (p : ℤ) ∣ (freyCurve (a : ℤ) b).Δ ↔ p ∣ a * b * (a + b)

For the integral Frey model over ℤ of a coprime pair of natural numbers, an odd prime divides the discriminant exactly when it divides ab(a + b).

IUT.LegendreFrey.freyCurve_prime_not_dvd_c4theorem

theorem freyCurve_prime_not_dvd_c4 {a b : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
  (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (hd : p ∣ a * b * (a + b)) : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ (freyCurve (a : ℤ) b).c₄

For the integral Frey model over ℤ of a coprime pair of natural numbers, an odd prime dividing ab(a + b) does not divide c₄.

IUT.LegendreFrey.logHeight₁_legendreJ_triple_letheorem

theorem logHeight₁_legendreJ_triple_le (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) :
  Height.logHeight₁ (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c)) ≤
    6 * Height.logHeight₁ ((a : ℚ) / c) + 8 * Real.log 2

Upper height bound. For a coprime triple a + b = c of positive numbers and λ = a / c, h(j(λ)) ≤ 6 h(λ) + 8 log 2, with h = Height.logHeight₁.

IUT.LegendreFrey.le_logHeight₁_legendreJ_tripletheorem

theorem le_logHeight₁_legendreJ_triple (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a.Coprime b)
  (h : a + b = c) :
  6 * Height.logHeight₁ ((a : ℚ) / c) - Real.log (64 / 27) ≤
    Height.logHeight₁ (legendreJ ((a : ℚ) / c))

Lower height bound. For a coprime triple a + b = c of positive numbers and λ = a / c, 6 h(λ) - log(64/27) ≤ h(j(λ)), with h = Height.logHeight₁.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_eq_1728_ifftheorem

theorem legendreJ_eq_1728_iff (t : K) (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : t ≠ 1) :
  legendreJ t = 2 ^ 6 * 3 ^ 3 ↔ t = -1 ∨ t = 2 ∨ t = 1 / 2

j = 2⁶·3³ = 1728 exactly at t ∈ {-1, 2, 1/2} (for t ≠ 0, 1).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_eq_73_ifftheorem

theorem legendreJ_eq_73_iff (t : K) (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : t ≠ 1) :
  legendreJ t = 2 ^ 2 * 73 ^ 3 / 3 ^ 4 ↔
    t = 9 ∨ t = -8 ∨ t = 9 / 8 ∨ t = -1 / 8 ∨ t = 8 / 9 ∨ t = 1 / 9

j = 2²·73³·3⁻⁴ exactly at t ∈ {9, -8, 9/8, -1/8, 8/9, 1/9} (for t ≠ 0, 1).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_eq_31_ifftheorem

theorem legendreJ_eq_31_iff (t : K) (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : t ≠ 1) :
  legendreJ t = 2 ^ 14 * 31 ^ 3 / 5 ^ 3 ↔
    t ^ 2 - 125 * t + 125 = 0 ∨ t ^ 2 + 123 * t + 1 = 0 ∨ 125 * t ^ 2 - 125 * t + 1 = 0

j = 2¹⁴·31³·5⁻³ exactly at the roots of t² - 125t + 125, t² + 123t + 1 and 125t² - 125t + 1 (for t ≠ 0, 1).

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_eq_zero_ifftheorem

theorem legendreJ_eq_zero_iff (t : K) (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : t ≠ 1) :
  legendreJ t = 0 ↔ t ^ 2 - t + 1 = 0

j = 0 exactly at the roots of t² - t + 1 (for t ≠ 0, 1).

theorem rat_sq_ne_five (s : ℚ) : s ^ 2 ≠ 5

No rational number squares to 5.

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_ne_31_rattheorem

theorem legendreJ_ne_31_rat (t : ℚ) (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : t ≠ 1) :

IUT.LegendreFrey.legendreJ_one_halftheorem

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Bridge

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Bridge.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic

IUT IV, Propositions 1.2 and 1.3: the closed unit ball of the spectral norm is the ring of integers

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Propositions 1.1 to 1.3, pages 9 to 12 of the April 2020 manuscript. Pages read for this file: 9, 10, 11 and 12. Pages checked against rendered images: 9, 10, 11 and 12 (the normalization ord(p) = 1, the ring of integers R_i of a finite extension k_i of ℚ_p and the order 𝔡_i of the different on page 9; the ramification index e_i, the constants a_i, b_i, the fractional ideals p ^ λ · R_i for λ ∈ (1 / e_i) ℤ and assertion (i) of Proposition 1.2 on page 10; the proof of Proposition 1.2 on page 11; Proposition 1.3 (i) on pages 11 and 12).

The gap closed here

Two earlier files model the paper's local objects in two different ways. IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic uses the ring of integers integralClosure ℤ_[p] L of a finite extension L of ℚ_[p], a prime P of it over p and Mathlib's Ideal.ramificationIdx. IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm uses the spectral norm ‖·‖ on L, the closed unit ball as ring of integers, the unit sphere as its units, and the ramification index only through the hypothesis hval : ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ 1 / p. This file proves that the two models agree, for a finite extension L of ℚ_[p] (a field with a finite-dimensional ℚ_[p]-algebra structure and a compatible ℤ_[p]-algebra structure) and its spectral norm spectralNorm ℚ_[p] L.

What is proved:

  1. padicBridge_norm_le_one_iff_isIntegral: ‖x‖ ≤ 1 if and only if x is integral over ℤ_[p]. The spectral norm of x is the spectral value of the minimal polynomial of x over ℚ_[p], which is at most one exactly when all coefficients lie in ℤ_[p] (spectralValue_le_one_iff); since ℤ_[p] is integrally closed, this holds exactly when x is integral (minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions', Polynomial.lifts_and_degree_eq_and_monic). Hence padicBridge_integralClosure_eq_unitBall: the closed unit ball is integralClosure ℤ_[p] L as a set.
  2. padicBridge_isUnit_iff, padicBridge_range_units_eq_unitSphere: the unit sphere is the image of the unit group of integralClosure ℤ_[p] L.
  3. The value group and the ramification index:
    • padicBridge_isLocalRing, padicBridge_isDiscreteValuationRing: the ring of integers is local with maximal ideal {‖x‖ < 1} (padicBridge_mem_maximalIdeal_iff), hence a discrete valuation ring;
    • padicBridge_maximalIdeal_liesOver, padicBridge_prime_eq_maximalIdeal: its maximal ideal lies over p, and it is the only prime ideal over p; so every statement of Padic.lean about a prime P over p is about this ideal, and differentOrder ℤ_[p] R P is the paper's 𝔡_i;
    • padicBridge_uniformizer: with e = P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p], there is a uniformizer ϖ with P = (ϖ), (p) = (ϖ) ^ e as ideals, ‖ϖ‖ ^ e = 1 / p, every nonzero x of L has ‖x‖ = ‖ϖ‖ ^ k for an integer k, and ‖x‖ ≤ ‖ϖ‖ when ‖x‖ < 1;
    • padicBridge_norm_range_units: the image of ‖·‖ on Lˣ is {p ^ (k / e) | k ∈ ℤ};
    • padicBridge_hval, padicBridge_ramificationIdx_le_of_hval: hval holds for e = P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p], and for no smaller natural number;
    • padicBridge_closedBall_eq_range_mul, padicBridge_exists_norm_eq_rpow: for λ ∈ (1 / e) ℤ the paper's fractional ideal p ^ λ · R, generated by an element of ord = λ, exists and equals the closed ball {‖z‖ ≤ p ^ (-λ)} used in Logarithm.lean; padicBridge_a_eq_int_div, padicBridge_b_eq_int_div: a_i and -b_i lie in (1 / e_i) ℤ.
  4. Corollaries without the hypothesis hval, for R = integralClosure ℤ_[p] L and e = P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]:
    • padicBridge_extLogUnit_image_bounds: IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i), p ^ a · R ⊆ log (R^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b) · R, with R^× the unit group of the integral closure and p ^ λ · R written as a closed ball;
    • padicBridge_extLogUnit_image_fractionalIdeal: the same with p ^ a · R and p ^ (-b) · R the fractional ideals y · R, z · R generated by elements y, z of norms p ^ (-a), p ^ b, which exist;
    • padicBridge_extLogUnit_image_eq_of_le: the equality log (R^×) = p ^ (1 / e) · R for p > 2 and e ≤ p - 2;
    • padicBridge_extLogShell_bounds: the bounds p* p ^ a · R ⊆ I ⊆ p* p ^ (-b) · R for the log-shell I of IUT III Definition 1.1;
    • padicBridge_log_bounds_and_differentOrder: Proposition 1.2 (i) together with 𝔡 ≥ (e - 1) / e (Proposition 1.3 (i) for k_0 = ℚ_p) and 𝔡 + a ≥ 1 (p > 2), 𝔡 + a ≥ 2 (p = 2), all with the same e and the same ideal P.

Not formalized here: the uniqueness of the norm on L (the spectral norm is used throughout; by Mathlib's spectralNorm_unique it is the only power-multiplicative algebra norm extending the p-adic norm, but no statement here uses another norm); Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (iv), which need the tensor products R_I of Proposition 1.1; the statements of Proposition 1.4, whose log-volumes are not formalized (its per-index arithmetic, Proposition1_4.a_add_b_le, takes only p and e and needs nothing from this file).

  (h : letI := spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] L
    ∀ x : L, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e' ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] ≤ e'

**No smaller exponent satisfies hval**: if ‖x‖ ^ e' ≤ 1 / p for every x with ‖x‖ < 1, then P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] ≤ e'. So the ramification index is the least natural number e for which the hypothesis hval of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm holds.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Different

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Different.lean

IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 (i): the lower bound for the order of the different

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Propositions 1.1 to 1.3, pages 9 to 12 of the April 2020 manuscript. Pages read for this file: 9 to 15. Pages checked against rendered images: 9, 10, 11 and 12 (the definition of 𝔡_i and the normalization of ord on page 9; the statement of Proposition 1.3 (i) on pages 11 and 12).

The statement of the paper

Page 9: ord is the p-adic valuation on \bar ℚ_p with ord(p) = 1; R_i is the ring of integers of a finite extension k_i of ℚ_p and 𝔡_i ∈ ℚ_{≥ 0} is the order ord of any generator of the different ideal of R_i over ℤ_p. Page 10: e_i is the ramification index of k_i over ℚ_p. Page 11: for a subfield ℚ_p ⊆ k_0 ⊆ k_i with ring of integers R_0, different order 𝔡_0 and ramification index e_0, and e_{i/0} = e_i/e_0, Proposition 1.3 (i) asserts 𝔡_i ≥ 𝔡_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i, with equality when k_i is tamely ramified over k_0 (page 12).

What is formalized, and the normalizations chosen

The setting is that of Mathlib's different ideal: a Dedekind domain A with fraction field K, a finite separable extension L/K, and the integral closure B of A in L; p is a nonzero maximal ideal of A and P a prime of B over p. With A = ℤ_p, K = ℚ_p, L = k_i this is the paper's setting (see IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic).

  • differentExponent A B P is the multiplicity of P in the different ideal 𝔇_{B/A} (Mathlib's differentIdeal), a natural number.
  • ramificationIdx is Mathlib's Ideal.ramificationIdx P A, the ramification index e of P over p.
  • differentOrder A B P = differentExponent A B P / e, a real number. This is the paper's normalization: if p is generated by an element ϖ with ord(ϖ) = 1 (for A = ℤ_p, the element p), then p·B_P = P^e·B_P, so a uniformizer of B_P has ord = 1/e, and a generator of 𝔇_{B/A}·B_P has ord = differentExponent/e. The paper writes ord of a generator of the different of R_i, which presupposes that this ideal is principal; it is when R_i is local, which holds for the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p. That locality is not proved here, so every statement below is made for every prime P over p; when P is the only one, differentOrder is the paper's 𝔡_i.

Proved, from Mathlib's pow_sub_one_dvd_differentIdeal_aux (P^{e-1} divides the different) and the transitivity of the different (differentIdeal_eq_differentIdeal_mul_differentIdeal):

  • ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_differentExponent: e - 1 ≤ differentExponent;
  • differentOrder_ge: (e - 1)/e ≤ differentOrder, i.e. Proposition 1.3 (i) for k_0 = ℚ_p (where 𝔡_0 = 0, e_0 = 1);
  • differentOrder_ge_tower: for a tower A ⊆ B ⊆ C of such rings (the paper's ℤ_p ⊆ R_0 ⊆ R_i) and primes P ⊆ C over P₀ ⊆ B over p, differentOrder A C P ≥ differentOrder A B P₀ + (e_{P/P₀} - 1)/e_{P/p}, which is the inequality of Proposition 1.3 (i) with e_{i/0} = e_{P/P₀} and e_i = e_{P/p} (e_{P/p} = e_{P₀/p}·e_{P/P₀} by Ideal.ramificationIdx_tower).

Not formalized in this file: the equality in the tamely ramified case (Mathlib, at the pinned version, has no statement computing the exact exponent of the different in the tame case; only the bound and the characterization P ∣ 𝔇 ↔ P ramified, dvd_differentIdeal_iff, are available), Proposition 1.3 (ii), and the uniqueness of P over p for ℤ_p. For k_0 = ℚ_p the tame equality is proved in IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Tame.lean and the uniqueness of P in IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Bridge.lean.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.DifferentBound

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/DifferentBound.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tower, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.UnitVolume

IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 (ii) for finite extensions of ℚ_p, and the bound for the different

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.3 and its proof, pages 11 and 12 of the April 2020 manuscript, and Remark 1.3.1 on page 13. Pages read for this file: 11, 12 and 13. Pages checked against rendered images: 11, 12 and 13 (the notation R_0, 𝔡_0, e_0, e_{i/0}, [k_i : k_0], n_i and the inequality of (i) on page 11; the tame equality of (i), assertion (ii) and its proof on page 12; Remark 1.3.1 on page 13). The setting, the normalization ord(p) = 1 and the notation are those of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tower.

The statement of the paper

Page 12, assertion (ii): "Suppose that k_i is a finite Galois extension of a subfield k_1 ⊆ k_i such that k_0 ⊆ k_1, and k_1 is tamely ramified over k_0. Then we have: 𝔡_i ≤ 𝔡_0 + n_i + 1/e_0", where (page 11) n_i is the nonnegative integer with [k_i : k_0]/p^{n_i} an integer prime to p. The proof on page 12 first replaces k_0 by an unramified extension of k_0 contained in k_i, so that k_i is totally ramified over k_0; for (ii) it inducts on n_i through Galois p-subextensions and computes the different of a Kummer extension x^p - ϖ_*. Remark 1.3.1 refers to [Ih], Lemma A, for similar estimates.

What is proved

The proof here is not the paper's induction. It rests on the classical upper bound for the different of an extension of local fields, v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e - 1 + v_P(e) with e = e_{L/K}. That bound is not printed in IUT IV; it is proved here from the trace, as follows.

  1. diffBound_differentExponent_lt (a local extension of Dedekind domains B/A, p ⊆ A maximal, P the prime of B): if the integer n = [L : K] generates P ^ m in B, then v_P(𝔇_{B/A}) < m + e. The trace of 1 is n, which does not lie in the ideal n·p, and (n·p) B = P ^ (m + e); Mathlib's not_dvd_differentIdeal_of_intTrace_notMem concludes.
  2. diffBound_exponent_le_finrank: for ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ L, v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p([L : K]) (diffBound_map_span_natCast: the integer n generates P ^ (e_L·v_p(n))). With [L : K] = e_{L/K} this is the classical bound in the totally ramified case, diffBound_exponent_le_of_totallyRamified.
  3. The classical bound in general, diffBound_exponent_le: v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}), in the exact form of the hypothesis of towerProp1_3ii_of_exponent_bound. As on page 12, the proof passes through an unramified subextension K₁ = K(a), where a is a root of unity of order N prime to p whose powers represent the nonzero residues of L (diffBound_exists_residue_root, by Hensel's lemma in the complete ring R_L). Then: K₁/K is unramified, since the derivative of the minimal polynomial of a at a divides N a ^ (N - 1), a unit, and lies in the different (diffBound_ramificationIdx_eq_one); [L : K₁] = e_{L/K₁}, since the residue field extension of L/K₁ is trivial (diffBound_finrank_eq_ramificationIdx); and diffBound_exponent_le_of_intermediate glues these by the transitivity of the different (towerDifferentExponent_eq).
  4. Proposition 1.3 (ii) for every finite L/K, with no Galois or tameness hypothesis: diffBound_prop1_3ii, from item 2 alone, since (e_{L/K} - 1)/e_L < 1/e_K. Consequently diffBound_towerProp1_3iiStatement proves towerProp1_3iiStatement (the form of page 12) for all its parameters.
  5. diffBound_prop1_3i: Proposition 1.3 (i) over a general base in one statement, the inequality together with the equality in the tame case.
Not proved
  • The paper's own route to (ii) (the induction on n_i, Galois p-subextensions and Kummer generators) is not formalized; the statement is proved by the different route above.
  • The equality case of the classical bound (for example ℚ_2(√2)/ℚ_2) is not checked here.

  letI

Reduction to the totally ramified case. Let ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ K₁ ⊆ L be finite extensions with K₁/K unramified at the primes over p (e_{K₁/K} = 1) and [L : K₁] = e_{L/K₁}. Then the classical bound v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}) holds. The proof: the different of K₁/K is trivial (the tame equality with e = 1), so transitivity gives v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) = v_P(𝔇_{L/K₁}) and e_{L/K₁} = e_{L/K}; then apply the totally ramified case.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_towerProp1_3iiStatementtheorem

theorem diffBound_towerProp1_3iiStatement : towerProp1_3iiStatement p K K₁ L

IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 (ii), as printed (page 12): towerProp1_3iiStatement holds for all finite extensions ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ K₁ ⊆ L. The Galois and tameness hypotheses are not used: the conclusion holds for every finite L/K (diffBound_prop1_3ii).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_exists_residue_roottheorem

theorem diffBound_exists_residue_root (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] :
  ∃ (a : integralClosure ℤ_[p] L) (N : ℕ), 0 < N ∧ ¬ p ∣ N ∧ a ^ N = 1 ∧
    ∀ y : integralClosure ℤ_[p] L, y ∈ P ∨ ∃ j : ℕ, y - a ^ j ∈ P

**Roots of unity of order prime to p represent the residue field.** For a finite extension L of ℚ_[p] and the prime P of R_L over p, there are a ∈ R_L and N > 0 with p ∤ N and a ^ N = 1 such that every element of R_L lies in P or is congruent modulo P to a power of a. In the proof (not in the statement, which only asserts existence), N + 1 is the cardinality of the residue field and a is the Hensel lift (Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing with unitVol_isAdicComplete) of a generator of the cyclic group of units of the residue field.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_ramificationIdx_eq_onetheorem

theorem diffBound_ramificationIdx_eq_one (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) [P₀.IsPrime]
  [P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L))
  [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  (ζ : integralClosure ℤ_[p] L) {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hpN : ¬ p ∣ N) (hζ : ζ ^ N = 1)
  (hgen : Algebra.adjoin K {(ζ : L)} = ⊤) :
  letI

**An extension generated by a root of unity of order prime to p is unramified.** If L is generated over K by an integer ζ with ζ ^ N = 1 and p ∤ N, then e_{L/K} = 1. The proof: the minimal polynomial g of ζ over R_K divides X ^ N - 1, so g'(ζ) divides N ζ ^ (N - 1), a unit; g'(ζ) lies in the different (Mathlib's aeval_derivative_mem_differentIdeal), so the different is trivial, and e_{L/K} - 1 ≤ v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) = 0.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_finrank_eq_ramificationIdxtheorem

theorem diffBound_finrank_eq_ramificationIdx (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K))
  [P₀.IsPrime] [P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  (hres : letI := towerAlgebra p K L
    ∀ y : integralClosure ℤ_[p] L, ∃ x : integralClosure ℤ_[p] K,
      y - algebraMap (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K) (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L) x ∈ P) :
  letI

**Residue degree one forces [L : K] = e_{L/K}.** If every element of R_L is congruent modulo P to an element of R_K (the residue field extension is trivial), then the degree [L : K] equals the ramification index e_{L/K} (the fundamental identity Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank, with one prime and inertia degree one).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_exponent_letheorem

theorem diffBound_exponent_le (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) [P₀.IsPrime]
  [P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L))
  [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] :
  letI

The classical upper bound for the different of a finite extension ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ L: v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}), where e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}) is the valuation at P of the integer e_{L/K}. This is exactly the hypothesis of towerProp1_3ii_of_exponent_bound. The proof: let a ∈ R_L be a root of unity of order N prime to p whose powers represent the nonzero residues (diffBound_exists_residue_root) and K₁ = K(a); then K₁/K is unramified (diffBound_ramificationIdx_eq_one), L/K₁ has trivial residue extension, so [L : K₁] = e_{L/K₁} (diffBound_finrank_eq_ramificationIdx), and diffBound_exponent_le_of_intermediate reduces to the totally ramified case.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.diffBound_prop1_3ii_of_classicaltheorem

theorem diffBound_prop1_3ii_of_classical (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) [P₀.IsPrime]
  [P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L))
  [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] :
  letI

Proposition 1.3 (ii) from the classical bound: the hypothesis of towerProp1_3ii_of_exponent_bound is discharged by diffBound_exponent_le.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Logarithm

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Logarithm.lean · imports IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog, IUT.PaperIV.Proposition1_2

The p-adic logarithm on a finite extension of ℚ_p; IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i)

Module documentation

Sources:

  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.2, pages 10 and 11, with the notation of Proposition 1.1 on page 9 (ord normalized by ord(p) = 1, R_i the ring of integers of a finite extension k_i of ℚ_p, p ^ λ · R_i the fractional ideal generated by an element of ord equal to λ). Page 10 defines, with e_i the ramification index of k_i over ℚ_p, a_i = (1 / e_i) ⌈e_i / (p - 2)⌉ for p > 2, a_i = 2 for p = 2, and b_i = ⌊log (p e_i / (p - 1)) / log p⌋ - 1 / e_i; assertion (i) is p ^ (a_i) · R_i ⊆ log_p (R_i^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b_i) · R_i, with equalities when p > 2 and e_i ≤ p - 2. The proof on page 11 derives (i) from a_i > 1 / (p - 1) and p ^ (b_i + 1 / e_i) / e_i > 1 / (p - 1) and the theory of the p-adic logarithm and exponential ([Kobl], page 81).
  • Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, Definition 1.1, page 24 (the log-shell is the pre-log-shell, the image under the logarithm of the Galois-invariant units, multiplied by (p*)⁻¹, with p* = p for odd p and p* = p ^ 2 for p = 2), and Proposition 1.2 (v), pages 31 and 32 ((a_non) compactness, (b_non) the log-shell contains the invariants of the integers, (c_non) it contains the image of the invariant units).

Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 9, 10 and 11; IUT III pages 24, 31 and 32. Pages checked against rendered images: the same.

The model of the paper's objects

K is a normed field that is a normed ℚ_p-algebra (so its norm extends the p-adic norm, ‖p‖ = 1 / p, and ord = -log_p ‖·‖); for the results on units it is also complete and locally compact (ProperSpace), which holds for every finite extension of ℚ_p (extLogUnit_image_bounds_of_finiteDimensional). For a finite extension L given only by the classes of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic (Field, Algebra ℚ_[p], FiniteDimensional), the norm is Mathlib's spectral norm (extLogUnit_image_bounds_spectralNorm, extLogUnit_lower_and_shell_spectralNorm). In this model:

  • R is the closed unit ball {‖x‖ ≤ 1}, R^× the unit sphere {‖x‖ = 1}, and p ^ λ · R the closed ball {‖z‖ ≤ p ^ (-λ)};
  • e is a positive integer such that every x with ‖x‖ < 1 has ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ 1 / p, that is ord(x) ≥ 1 / e on the maximal ideal (hypothesis hval). For the ramification index e_i this holds, since the value group of k_i is p ^ (ℤ / e_i). It is a standing property of the field, not a claim of the paper; the results below hold for every such e;
  • log on R^× is extLogUnit: log u = N⁻¹ log (u ^ N) where N > 0 is any exponent with ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1 (the value does not depend on N, extLogUnit_eq) and log (u ^ N) is the series. Such N exist on R^× by local compactness (extLog_exists_pow_near_one), and the least one is prime to p (extLog_find_not_dvd). The pages read do not say how log_p is extended from the principal units to R_i^×; this is the standard extension (for ℚ_p it agrees with IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogUnit, extLogUnit_padic), and it is a homomorphism (extLogUnit_mul, extLogUnit_pow).

Not formalized: the identification of the closed unit ball with the ring of integers integralClosure ℤ_[p] k_i used in IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic, of the unit sphere with its units, and of the least e satisfying hval with Ideal.ramificationIdx of that file; the uniqueness of the norm on k_i. The statements are therefore about the normed-field model above, not about the objects of Padic.lean.

Contents
  1. The series in K: extLogOnePlus x = ∑ (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n, convergent for ‖x‖ < 1 (extLogSeries_summable), equal to NormedSpace.log (1 + x) (extLogOnePlus_eq_normedSpace_log); the homomorphism property on the open unit disc (extLogOnePlus_add_add_mul, the double-series argument of PadicLog.lean); the isometry ‖log (1 + x)‖ = ‖x‖ on the disc p ‖x‖ ^ (p - 1) < 1 (extLogOnePlus_norm_eq), which is the open disc of radius p ^ (-1 / (p - 1)) (extLog_mul_pow_lt_one_iff). At the boundary p ‖x‖ ^ (p - 1) = 1 the p-th term has the norm of the first (extLogSeries_norm_eq_of_boundary), so the radius is exact for the termwise estimate; that the isometry itself fails at the boundary in a suitable ramified field (x = ζ_p - 1) is not formalized.
  2. In place of the exponential: on every closed ball of radius r with p r ^ (p - 1) < 1, x ↦ log (1 + x) is injective (extLogOnePlus_injOn, from the isometry of differences extLogOnePlus_norm_sub_eq) and maps the ball onto itself (extLogOnePlus_image_closedBall, surjectivity by the contraction mapping principle, extLogOnePlus_surjOn). The exponential series itself is not used.
  3. IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i) in the model above, with a = Proposition1_2.a p e and b = Proposition1_2.b p e (the constants of page 10, already in Proposition1_2.lean): p ^ a · R ⊆ log (R^×) (extLogUnit_image_lower, for every e ≥ 1, from Proposition1_2.a_gt), log (R^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b) · R (extLogUnit_image_upper, from Proposition1_2.rpow_b_gt and hval), both together (extLogUnit_image_bounds), the equality log (R^×) = p ^ (1 / e) · R for p > 2, e ≤ p - 2 (extLogUnit_image_eq_of_le, with Proposition1_2.a_b_of_le), the unramified case log (R^×) = p · R for p > 2 (extLogUnit_image_unramified), and consistency with the base field: for K = ℚ_p the image is padicLogUnit_range_of_ne_two's (extLogUnit_image_padic_of_ne_two).
  4. The log-shell extLogShell p K = (p*)⁻¹ · log (R^×) of IUT III Definition 1.1: it contains R (extLogShell_unitBall_subset, IUT III Proposition 1.2 (v) (b_non) in the model) and log (R^×) (extLogUnit_image_subset_extLogShell, (c_non)), and p* p ^ a · R ⊆ I ⊆ p* p ^ (-b) · R (extLogShell_bounds).

Not proved here: IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (iv) (tensor products R_I, their normalization, the automorphism φ, which rest on Proposition 1.1); the compactness (a_non) of the log-shell; the link to integralClosure and Ideal.ramificationIdx described above.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogSeriesdef

noncomputable def extLogSeries (x : K) (n : ℕ) : K :=
  (-1) ^ (n + 1) / n * x ^ n

The n-th term (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n of the logarithm series in a normed field K; the 0-th term is 0 because 1 / 0 = 0.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogOnePlusdef

noncomputable def extLogOnePlus (x : K) : K :=
  ∑' n : ℕ, extLogSeries x n

log (1 + x) = ∑_{n ≥ 1} (-1) ^ (n + 1) x ^ n / n in K; meaningful for ‖x‖ < 1 when K is a complete normed ℚ_p-algebra (extLogSeries_summable), and a junk value otherwise.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogOnePlus_zerotheorem

theorem extLogOnePlus_zero : extLogOnePlus (0 : K) = 0

log 1 = 0.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogDoubledef

noncomputable def extLogDouble (x w : K) (nk : ℕ × ℕ) : K :=
  (-1) ^ (nk.1 + 1) / nk.1 * (nk.1.choose nk.2) * x ^ (nk.1 - nk.2) * w ^ nk.2

The double family used to re-expand log (1 + x + w) around x.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogDouble_hasSum_fsttheorem

theorem extLogDouble_hasSum_fst (x w : K) (n : ℕ) :
  HasSum (fun k => extLogDouble x w (n, k)) (extLogSeries (x + w) n)

Summing the double family over k first gives the series of log (1 + (x + w)).
