Contraction estimate: for a, b in the closed ball of radius r, p r ^ (p - 1) < 1, ‖(a - b) - (log (1 + a) - log (1 + b))‖ ≤ max (p r ^ (p - 1)) r · ‖a - b‖.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogOnePlus_surjOntheorem

theorem extLogOnePlus_surjOn [CompleteSpace K] {r : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 ≤ r)
  (hpr : (p : ℝ) * r ^ (p - 1) < 1) {z : K} (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
  ∃ x : K, ‖x‖ ≤ r ∧ extLogOnePlus x = z

Surjectivity of x ↦ log (1 + x) onto the closed ball of radius r, for p r ^ (p - 1) < 1, by the contraction mapping principle.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogOnePlus_image_closedBalltheorem

theorem extLogOnePlus_image_closedBall [CompleteSpace K] {r : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 ≤ r)
  (hpr : (p : ℝ) * r ^ (p - 1) < 1) :
  extLogOnePlus '' {x : K | ‖x‖ ≤ r} = {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ r}

x ↦ log (1 + x) maps the closed ball of radius r onto itself when p r ^ (p - 1) < 1 (and is injective there, extLogOnePlus_injOn).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnitdef

noncomputable def extLogUnit {K : Type*} [NormedField K] (u : K) : K :=
  if h : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1 then
    ((Nat.find h : ℕ) : K)⁻¹ * extLogOnePlus (u ^ Nat.find h - 1)
  else 0

The logarithm of an element u of K some positive power of which lies in the open unit disc around 1: log u = N⁻¹ log (u ^ N) with N the least positive such exponent, where log (u ^ N) is the series extLogOnePlus (u ^ N - 1). The value does not depend on the choice of N (extLogUnit_eq), and on the units of a locally compact K such an N exists (extLog_exists_pow_near_one). Junk value 0 if there is no such N.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_auxtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_aux [CompleteSpace K] {u : K} {M N : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M)
  (hMu : ‖u ^ M - 1‖ < 1) (hN : 0 < N) (hNu : ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1) :
  (M : K)⁻¹ * extLogOnePlus (u ^ M - 1) = (N : K)⁻¹ * extLogOnePlus (u ^ N - 1)

N⁻¹ log (u ^ N) does not depend on the exponent N with ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_eqtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_eq [CompleteSpace K] {u : K} {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hu : ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1) :
  extLogUnit u = (N : K)⁻¹ * extLogOnePlus (u ^ N - 1)

log u = N⁻¹ log (u ^ N) for every N > 0 with ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_one_addtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_one_add [CompleteSpace K] {x : K} (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) :
  extLogUnit (1 + x) = extLogOnePlus x

On principal units, the logarithm of units is the series: log (1 + x) for ‖x‖ < 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_powtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_pow [CompleteSpace K] {u : K} {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hu : ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1)
  (m : ℕ) : extLogUnit (u ^ m) = m * extLogUnit u

log (u ^ m) = m log u.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_multheorem

theorem extLogUnit_mul [CompleteSpace K] {u v : K} {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hu : ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1)
  (hv : ‖v ^ N - 1‖ < 1) : extLogUnit (u * v) = extLogUnit u + extLogUnit v

log (u v) = log u + log v when u ^ N, v ^ N lie in the open disc around 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_norm_choose_letheorem

theorem extLog_norm_choose_le {k : ℕ} (hk0 : k ≠ 0) (hkp : k < p) :
  ‖((p.choose k : ℕ) : K)‖ ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹

‖binom(p, k)‖ ≤ 1 / p in K for 0 < k < p.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_norm_sub_one_lt_of_powtheorem

theorem extLog_norm_sub_one_lt_of_pow {y : K} (hy : ‖y‖ ≤ 1) (h : ‖y ^ p - 1‖ < 1) :
  ‖y - 1‖ < 1

Injectivity of Frobenius on the residue field, analytically: if ‖y‖ ≤ 1 and ‖y ^ p - 1‖ < 1, then ‖y - 1‖ < 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_find_not_dvdtheorem

theorem extLog_find_not_dvd {u : K} (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) (h : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1) :
  ¬ p ∣ Nat.find h

The least positive N with ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1 is prime to p, for ‖u‖ ≤ 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_exists_eqtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_exists_eq [CompleteSpace K] {u : K} (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1)
  (h : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1) :
  ∃ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 ∧ ‖extLogUnit u‖ = ‖extLogOnePlus x‖

For ‖u‖ ≤ 1 some power of which is a principal unit, ‖log u‖ = ‖log (1 + x)‖ for some x in the open unit disc (namely x = u ^ N - 1 with N prime to p).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_exists_pow_near_onetheorem

theorem extLog_exists_pow_near_one [ProperSpace K] {u : K} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) :
  ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ‖u ^ N - 1‖ < 1

In a locally compact (proper) normed field, every u with ‖u‖ = 1 has a positive power in the open disc around 1 (the residue field is finite).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_rpow_neg_a_mem_disctheorem

theorem extLog_rpow_neg_a_mem_disc {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  (p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)) ^ (p - 1) < 1

p ^ (-a) lies in the disc of the isometry: p (p ^ (-a)) ^ (p - 1) < 1, from a > 1 / (p - 1) (Proposition1_2.a_gt).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_lowertheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_lower [CompleteSpace K] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)} ⊆ extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1}

IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i), first inclusion: p ^ a · R ⊆ log (R^×), with R the closed unit ball, R^× the unit sphere, p ^ a · R = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ p ^ (-a)} and a = a_i of page 10. Valid for every e ≥ 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_b_factstheorem

theorem extLog_b_facts {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  ∃ c : ℕ, e < p ^ (c + 1) ∧
    (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p e) = (p : ℝ) ^ c * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / (e : ℝ)))

With c = ⌊log (p e / (p - 1)) / log p⌋ ≥ 0: e < p ^ (c + 1) (from Proposition1_2.rpow_b_gt) and p ^ b = p ^ c · p ^ (-1 / e).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogSeries_norm_le_uppertheorem

theorem extLogSeries_norm_le_upper {e c : ℕ} (he : e < p ^ (c + 1)) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ)
  (hρ1 : ρ ≤ 1) (hρe : ρ ^ e = (p : ℝ)⁻¹) {x : K} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ ρ) (n : ℕ) :
  ‖extLogSeries x n‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ c * ρ

The termwise estimate for the second inclusion: if e < p ^ (c + 1), 0 ≤ ρ ≤ 1, ρ ^ e = 1 / p and ‖x‖ ≤ ρ, then ‖x ^ n / n‖ ≤ p ^ c ρ for every n.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_uppertheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_upper [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hval : ∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p e)}

IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i), second inclusion: log (R^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b) · R, with p ^ (-b) · R = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ p ^ b} and b = b_i of page 10, for a locally compact K in which every element of the open unit disc has norm at most p ^ (-1 / e) (this holds when e is the ramification index: the value group is then p ^ (ℤ / e)).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_boundstheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_bounds [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hval : ∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)} ⊆ extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} ∧
    extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p e)}

IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i) (page 10), both inclusions p ^ (a_i) · R_i ⊆ log (R_i^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b_i) · R_i, for a complete, locally compact normed field K that is a normed ℚ_p-algebra, with R the closed unit ball, R^× the unit sphere, p ^ λ · R = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ p ^ (-λ)}, log on R^× the function extLogUnit, and e a positive integer such that the open unit disc lies in the closed disc of radius p ^ (-1 / e).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_eq_of_letheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_eq_of_le [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hp2 : 2 < p) (hep : e ≤ p - 2) (hval : ∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} = {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / (e : ℝ)))}

IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i), the equality case: for p > 2 and e ≤ p - 2, log (R^×) = p ^ (1 / e) · R = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ p ^ (-1 / e)} (here a_i = 1 / e_i = -b_i, Proposition1_2.a_b_of_le).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_unramifiedtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_unramified [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] (hp2 : 2 < p)
  (hval : ∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} = {z : K | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹}

The unramified case e = 1, p > 2: log (R^×) = p · R = {z | ‖z‖ ≤ 1 / p}.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_bounds_of_finiteDimensionaltheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_bounds_of_finiteDimensional {L : Type*} [NormedField L]
  [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[p] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] L] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hval : ∀ x : L, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  {z : L | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)} ⊆ extLogUnit '' {u : L | ‖u‖ = 1} ∧
    extLogUnit '' {u : L | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ {z : L | ‖z‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p e)}

The same inclusions for a finite extension L of ℚ_p carrying a norm that extends the p-adic norm (completeness and local compactness follow from finite dimensionality).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogOnePlus_padictheorem

theorem extLogOnePlus_padic (x : ℚ_[p]) : extLogOnePlus x = padicLogOnePlus p x

Over ℚ_p the series is that of IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_padictheorem

theorem extLogUnit_padic (u : ℤ_[p]ˣ) :
  extLogUnit ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p]) = padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p])

Over ℚ_p, on ℤ_p^×, the logarithm of units is padicLogUnit of IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_padic_disctheorem

theorem extLog_padic_disc (x : ℚ_[p]) (hx : ‖x‖ < 1) : ‖x‖ ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹

In ℚ_p the open unit disc lies in the closed disc of radius 1 / p (e = 1).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_padic_of_ne_twotheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_padic_of_ne_two (h2 : p ≠ 2) :
  extLogUnit '' {u : ℚ_[p] | ‖u‖ = 1} =
    Set.range (fun u : ℤ_[p]ˣ => padicLogUnit p ((u : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p]))

Consistency with the base field (a = 1, b = -1 for odd p): for K = ℚ_p the image log (R^×) given by extLogUnit_image_unramified is the image log (ℤ_p^×) of IUT.Prerequisites.PadicLog.padicLogUnit_range_of_ne_two.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogShelldef

noncomputable def extLogShell (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [NormedField K] : Set K :=
  (fun z => ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : K)⁻¹ * z) '' (extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1})

The log-shell of IUT III Definition 1.1 (page 24) for a normed field K: I = (p*)⁻¹ · log (R^×), with R^× the unit sphere and p* = p for odd p, p* = 4 for p = 2.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_norm_pStartheorem

theorem extLog_norm_pStar : ‖((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : K)‖ = ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹

‖p*‖ = 1 / p* in K.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogShell_mem_ifftheorem

theorem extLogShell_mem_iff {y : K} :
  y ∈ extLogShell p K ↔ ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : K) * y ∈ extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1}

y ∈ I if and only if p* y ∈ log (R^×).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLog_inv_pStar_le_rpow_neg_atheorem

theorem extLog_inv_pStar_le_rpow_neg_a {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)

1 / p* ≤ p ^ (-a): a ≤ 1 for odd p, and a = 2, p* = 4 for p = 2.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogShell_unitBall_subsettheorem

theorem extLogShell_unitBall_subset [CompleteSpace K] : {y : K | ‖y‖ ≤ 1} ⊆ extLogShell p K

IUT III Proposition 1.2 (v) (b_non) (page 32) for K: the log-shell contains the closed unit ball R.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_subset_extLogShelltheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_subset_extLogShell [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] :
  extLogUnit '' {u : K | ‖u‖ = 1} ⊆ extLogShell p K

IUT III Proposition 1.2 (v) (c_non) (page 32) for a locally compact K: the log-shell contains log (R^×).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogShell_boundstheorem

theorem extLogShell_bounds [CompleteSpace K] [ProperSpace K] {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hval : ∀ x : K, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  {y : K | ‖y‖ ≤ ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℝ) * (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p e)} ⊆
      extLogShell p K ∧
    extLogShell p K ⊆
      {y : K | ‖y‖ ≤ ((padicLogPStar p : ℕ) : ℝ) * (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p e)}

The bounds on the log-shell given by IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i): p* p ^ a · R ⊆ I ⊆ p* p ^ (-b) · R, written with closed balls of radii p* p ^ (-a) and p* p ^ b.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_image_bounds_spectralNormtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_image_bounds_spectralNorm {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
  (hval : letI := spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] L
    ∀ x : L, ‖x‖ < 1 → ‖x‖ ^ e ≤ (p : ℝ)⁻¹) :
  letI

IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (i) for a finite extension L of ℚ_p with its spectral norm: p ^ a · R ⊆ log (R^×) ⊆ p ^ (-b) · R in the closed-ball model, the second inclusion for every e ≥ 1 such that the open unit disc of L lies in the closed disc of radius p ^ (-1 / e).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.extLogUnit_lower_and_shell_spectralNormtheorem

theorem extLogUnit_lower_and_shell_spectralNorm {e : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) :
  letI

The first inclusion p ^ a · R ⊆ log (R^×) and IUT III Proposition 1.2 (v) (b_non), R ⊆ I, for a finite extension L of ℚ_p with its spectral norm, for every e ≥ 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Packets

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Packets.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.VolumeBridge

Tensor packets of finitely many finite extensions of ℚ_p and their normalized log-volume

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.1 (page 9), Proposition 1.2 (page 10), Proposition 1.4 (pages 13 and 14); Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory III, the parts of Proposition 3.1 and Remark 3.1.1 on pages 93 to 96, Proposition 3.9 (i) (pages 115 and 116). Pages read for this file: IUT IV pages 9, 10, 13 and 14; IUT III pages 93, 94, 95, 96, 115 and 116. Pages checked against rendered images: the same. Displays relied on:

  • IUT IV page 9: R_E = ⊗_{i ∈ E} R_i, "where the tensor product is over ℤ_p", and (−)^∼ "the normalization of the [reduced] ring in parentheses in its ring of fractions";
  • IUT IV page 10: log_p(R_E^×) = ⊗_{i ∈ E} log_p(R_i^×), again over ℤ_p;
  • IUT IV page 13, Proposition 1.4 (i): tensor products of finitely many finite extensions of ℚ_p over ℤ_p "decompose, naturally, as direct sums of finitely many finite extensions of ℚ_p", and the log-volume on them is "defined on compact open subsets of such tensor products, valued in ℝ, and normalized so that μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0, μ^log(p · (R_E)^∼) = −log(p), for any nonempty set E ⊆ I". No weights of the direct summands are printed;
  • IUT IV page 14, the first line of the computation proving (iii): μ^log(p ^ ⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋ · log_p(R_I^×)) ≤ (−λ + 𝔡_I + a_I + 1) · log(p) + μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)), and the next line, which writes μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) as ∑_{i ∈ I} μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) + μ^log(R_I): an unweighted sum over the tensor factors;
  • IUT III page 115, Proposition 3.9 (i): the log-volume on each direct summand p_v-adic field, "together with the discussion of normalized weights in Remark 3.1.1, (ii), (iii), (iv)", with the integral structures of log-volume zero and "multiplication of an element of 𝔐(−) by p_v corresponds to adding the quantity −log(p_v)" (the packet-normalization). The weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, are built from the global degrees [K_v : (F_mod)_v] and [(F_mod)_w : ℚ_{v_ℚ}]; they have no meaning for an abstract packet of local fields and are not formalized here.
The objects

K : ι → Type is a finite family of finite extensions of ℚ_[p], and the packet is Mathlib's PiTensorProduct ℚ_[p] K (written ⊗_i K_i below), not an iterated binary tensor product. The pages take the tensor product over ℤ_p; the packet here is the tensor product over ℚ_p, and the two are identified only for two factors (packet_tensor_zp_bijective). Most statements are proved for any finite-dimensional commutative ℚ_p-algebra W that is formally unramified over ℚ_p (a finite étale ℚ_p-algebra) and then hold for the packet by packet_formallyUnramified. (R_E)^∼ is packetNormalizationSet p W, the elements of W integral over ℤ_p; for W = K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ it is padicPacketNormalization (packetNormalizationSet_tensor). μ^log on W is the existing padicPacketMuLog, the logarithm of a Haar measure on the coordinate space of Module.finBasis divided by dim W and normalized at a set Λ; on a summand A_j it is the same construction with dim A_j.

What is proved
  1. Structure. packet_formallyUnramified: ⊗_i K_i is formally unramified over ℚ_p (two lifts agree on every K_i because K_i is separable, hence on the tensor product). packet_isReduced, packet_equiv_pi: it is reduced and isomorphic, as a ℚ_p-algebra, to a finite product of finite separable extensions of ℚ_p. packet_finrank: dim ⊗_i K_i = ∏_i dim K_i.
  2. *The normalization (R_E)^∼.* packet_normalization_eq_preimage: under any ℚ_p-algebra isomorphism e : W ≃ Π_j A_j, (R_E)^∼ is the preimage of the product of the sets of integral elements of the A_j (for fields, their rings of integers, the closed unit balls of the spectral norms, volBridge_padicVolIntegral_iff). packet_normalization_isCompact_isOpen: compact and open in coordinates. packet_muLog_normalization: positive finite Haar measure, μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0 and μ^log(p ^ n · (R_E)^∼) = −n log p for every n ∈ ℤ; this is Proposition 1.4 (i) for every finite E, on the tensor product over ℚ_p (packet_muLog_normalization_tensor on the packet).
  3. Lattice. packet_normalization_lattice: with ℤ_p acting through ℚ_p, (R_E)^∼ is the integral closure of ℤ_p in W, a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, and spans W over ℚ_p.
  4. *Tensor product over ℤ_p and over ℚ_p.* packet_tensor_zp_bijective: for K₁, K₂ with compatible ℤ_p- and ℚ_p-algebra structures, the natural map K₁ ⊗[ℤ_p] K₂ → K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂, x ⊗ y ↦ x ⊗ y, is bijective (ℚ_p is the fraction field of ℤ_p). packet_integers_span: the image padicPacketIntegers of R₁ ⊗[ℤ_p] R₂ spans K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ over ℚ_p.
  5. Direct summands. packet_muLog_pi_region: for a region that is a product Π_j S_j of sets of positive finite measure in the summands of a decomposition e : W ≃ Π_j A_j into fields, μ^log(Π_j S_j) = ∑_j ([A_j : ℚ_p] / dim W) · μ^log_j(S_j), with μ^log_j normalized at the integral elements of A_j. The weights [A_j : ℚ_p] / dim W are derived from the normalization by the dimension, not printed on the pages read. packet_muLog_transport computes μ^log in any linear coordinates.
  6. The step of page 14. packet_muLog_floor_smul_le: for A of positive finite measure and real x, μ^log(p ^ ⌊x⌋ · A) ≤ (−x + 1) log p + μ^log(A). With x = λ − 𝔡_I − a_I and A = log_p(R_I^×) this is the first inequality of the computation on page 14, provided log_p(R_I^×) has positive finite measure, which is not proved here.
Not proved
  • For more than two factors, that the tensor product over ℤ_p of the pages equals PiTensorProduct ℚ_[p] K; and R_E = ⊗_{i ∈ E} R_i itself for more than two factors.
  • The second line of the computation on page 14, μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) = ∑_i μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) + μ^log(R_I): an additivity over the tensor factors (not over the direct summands), which needs the index formula for tensor products of lattices; log_p(R_I^×) and R_I for more than two factors are not defined in Lean here.
  • That R_E has positive Haar measure for more than two factors; for two factors it is proved, with the step μ^log(R_I) ≤ μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0 of page 14, in TensorIndex.lean (tensorIdx_muLog_nonpos).
  • That (R_E)^∼ is the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions; here it is the integral closure of ℤ_p in the packet. For two factors it is proved in TensorIndex.lean (tensorIdx_isFractionRing).
  • The weighted log-volumes of IUT III Proposition 3.9 (i) with the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), which depend on global data. They are defined, with the weights as inputs, on direct product regions in IUT/PaperIII/Corollary312/WeightedPacket.lean.
  • IUT IV Proposition 1.1 and Proposition 1.4 (iii), (iv) for more than two factors, and the first inequality of 1.4 (iii) when some e_i > p − 2 (two factors otherwise: TensorDifferent.lean, TensorIndex.lean, TensorLogShell.lean; 1.4 (ii): UnitVolume.lean).

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Padic.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Different, IUT.PaperIV.Proposition1_4

IUT IV, Propositions 1.2 to 1.4: the different of a finite extension of ℚ_p

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Propositions 1.1 to 1.4, pages 9 to 14 of the April 2020 manuscript. Pages read for this file: 9 to 15. Pages checked against rendered images: 9 to 14 (the normalization ord(p) = 1 and the definition of 𝔡_i on page 9, the definitions of e_i, a_i, b_i on page 10, Proposition 1.3 (i) on pages 11 and 12, the inequalities 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ |I|, 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ 2|I| of Proposition 1.4 (iii) on page 13 with their proof on page 14).

This file specializes IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Different to the paper's objects: A = ℤ_p, K = ℚ_p, L = k_i a finite extension of ℚ_p, and R_i = integralClosure ℤ_p k_i its ring of integers. Here p is a prime number, ℤ_[p], ℚ_[p] are Mathlib's p-adic integers and numbers, and k_i is any field with a finite-dimensional ℚ_[p]-algebra structure (and the compatible ℤ_[p]-algebra structure). The ramification index e_i is that of a prime P of R_i over the maximal ideal pℤ_p, and 𝔡_i = differentOrder ℤ_[p] R_i P (exponent of P in the different divided by e_i); since p generates the maximal ideal of ℤ_p, this is the paper's normalization ord(p) = 1. The ring R_i has only one such prime P, but that is not proved here, so the statements hold for every prime P over p.

What is proved:

  • isDedekindDomain_ringOfIntegers_padic, isTorsionFree_ringOfIntegers_padic: R_i is a Dedekind domain, torsion free over ℤ_p (so the general results apply; this also shows that their hypotheses are satisfiable);
  • padic_differentOrder_ge: Proposition 1.3 (i) with k_0 = ℚ_p, i.e. 𝔡_i ≥ (e_i - 1)/e_i;
  • padic_differentOrder_add_a_ge: 𝔡_i + a_i ≥ 1 if p > 2 and 𝔡_i + a_i ≥ 2 if p = 2, with a_i = Proposition1_2.a p e_i the constant of page 10 evaluated at the actual p and e_i (the inequality Proposition1_2.d_add_a_ge with its hypothesis discharged);
  • padic_dI_add_aI_ge: for finitely many such extensions k_i (i ∈ I), the last sentence of Proposition 1.4 (iii), 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ |I| if p > 2 and 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ 2|I| if p = 2, with 𝔡_I = ∑ 𝔡_i and a_I = ∑ a_i (Proposition1_4.dI_add_aI_ge with its hypothesis discharged).

Not formalized in this file: the inclusions of Propositions 1.1 and 1.2 (tensor products of the R_i, their normalization, p-adic logarithms), the tame equality of Proposition 1.3 (i), Proposition 1.3 (ii), and the log-volumes of Proposition 1.4. Other files of this directory treat parts of them, each stating what it proves: Logarithm.lean and Bridge.lean (Proposition 1.2 (i)), Tame.lean (the tame equality for k_0 = ℚ_p) and VolumeBridge.lean (normalized log-volumes).

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Tame.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Bridge, IUT.PaperIV.Proposition1_3

IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 (i) for k_0 = ℚ_p: the tame equality and the wild inequality

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Propositions 1.1 and 1.3, pages 9 to 13 of the April 2020 manuscript. Pages read for this file: 8 to 13. Pages checked against rendered images: 8 to 13 (the normalization ord(p) = 1 and the definition of 𝔡_i on page 9; Proposition 1.1 on page 9; Proposition 1.3 (i), 𝔡_i ≥ 𝔡_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i with equality when k_i is tamely ramified over k_0, on pages 11 and 12; Proposition 1.3 (ii), 𝔡_i ≤ 𝔡_0 + n_i + 1/e_0, on page 12, with its proof on pages 12 and 13).

The objects are those of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Padic: L = k_i a finite extension of ℚ_[p], R = integralClosure ℤ_[p] L its ring of integers, P a prime of R over pℤ_p, e its ramification index, differentExponent ℤ_[p] R P the exponent of P in the different, and 𝔡 = differentOrder ℤ_[p] R P (that exponent divided by e, the normalization ord(p) = 1). Here k_0 = ℚ_p, so 𝔡_0 = 0, e_0 = 1 and e_{i/0} = e; k_i is tamely ramified over ℚ_p exactly when p does not divide e. The locality of R and the uniqueness of P come from IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Bridge.

What is proved:

  • trace_eq_add_of_exact, trace_quotient_eq_add_of_mul_exact: the trace of an endomorphism is additive along a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional vector spaces, and the trace over R ⧸ m of a quotient S ⧸ I splits along 0 → S ⧸ K → S ⧸ I → S ⧸ J → 0 (multiplication by an element);
  • map_maximalIdeal_eq_pow_padic: pR = P ^ e;
  • trace_quotient_pow_padic, intTrace_mk_eq_padic: the trace from R ⧸ P ^ n to 𝔽_p is n times the trace from R ⧸ P (1 ≤ n ≤ e), so the trace from R to ℤ_[p] is, modulo p, e times the residue field trace;
  • differentExponent_lt_of_intTrace_notMem_padic: an element whose trace is a unit of ℤ_[p] forces differentExponent < e;
  • differentExponent_eq_of_not_dvd_ramificationIdx_padic: the tame equality of Proposition 1.3 (i): if p ∤ e then differentExponent = e - 1; and differentOrder_eq_of_not_dvd_ramificationIdx_padic, the same as 𝔡 = (e - 1)/e;
  • ramificationIdx_le_differentExponent_of_dvd_padic: the wild inequality: if p ∣ e then differentExponent ≥ e; and one_le_differentOrder_of_dvd_ramificationIdx_padic, 𝔡 ≥ 1;
  • differentExponent_eq_ramificationIdx_sub_one_iff_padic: the equality of Proposition 1.3 (i) holds exactly in the tame case;
  • differentOrder_le_one_of_not_dvd_ramificationIdx_padic: Proposition 1.3 (ii) in its base case k_0 = ℚ_p, k_1 = k_i tame (n_i = 0): 𝔡 ≤ 1, through Proposition1_3.ii_base.

Not formalized here: Proposition 1.3 over a general base k_0, which is in Tower.lean ((i), and (ii) in the tame and n_i = 0 cases); Proposition 1.1, of which the first inclusion for two factors is in TensorDifferent.lean.

Let m be a maximal ideal of R, mapping into the ideals I, J, K of the R-algebra S, with I ≤ J, π * b ∈ I ↔ b ∈ K and v ∈ J ↔ ∃ b, v - π * b ∈ I. IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorDifferent

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/TensorDifferent.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Bridge, IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume

The different and the normalization of a tensor product of two rings of integers

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.1 (page 9) with its proof (pages 9 and 10), Proposition 1.2 (page 10) with its proof (page 11). Pages read for this file: 9, 10 and 11. Pages checked against rendered images: 9, 10 and 11. Displays relied on:

  • page 9: R_E = ⊗_{i ∈ E} R_i over ℤ_p, 𝔡_E = ∑_{i ∈ E} 𝔡_i, I* = I \ {*}, and p ^ (𝔡_{I*}) · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ R_I ⊆ (R_I)^∼, where (−)^∼ is "the normalization of the [reduced] ring in parentheses in its ring of fractions", 𝔡_i is the order of any generator of the different ideal of R_i over ℤ_p, and p ^ (𝔡_{I*}) may be taken to be a product of elements p ^ (𝔡_i) ∈ R_i, i ∈ I*. The exponent is 𝔡_{I*} itself; no floor or ceiling;
  • page 10: the proof reduces to |I| = 2, where "the desired inclusion follows immediately from the definition of the different ideal"; Proposition 1.2 (i) p ^ (a_i) · R_i ⊆ log_p(R_i^×);
  • page 11: the first display of the proof of Proposition 1.2 (ii), p ^ (𝔡_I + a_I) · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ ⊗_{i ∈ I} p ^ (a_i) · R_i (⊆ R_I), derived from Proposition 1.1.
The objects

K₁, K₂ are finite extensions of ℚ_[p]; R_i = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K_i. As in IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume, R_E = R₁ ⊗_{ℤ_p} R₂ is taken as its image in K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂, the additive span of the x ⊗ y with x, y integral over ℤ_p (padicPacketIntegers), and (R_E)^∼ is the set of elements of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ integral over ℤ_p (padicPacketNormalization); R_E ⊆ (R_E)^∼ is padicPacketIntegers_subset there and is not repeated here. The different is Mathlib's differentIdeal ℤ_[p] R₂. The page's p ^ (𝔡_2) is an element of order 𝔡_2, that is a generator of this ideal; the main theorem holds for every element of the ideal, which contains the generators. Two factors only, with * = 1 and I* = {2}; by symmetry of the argument the case I* = {1} is the same statement with the factors exchanged, which is not separately formalized.

What is proved
  • tensorDiff_trace_one_tmul: Tr_{(A ⊗_R M)/A}(1 ⊗ y) = Tr_{M/R}(y) for a finite free R-algebra M (from LinearMap.trace_baseChange).
  • tensorDiff_isIntegralElem_trace: the trace over a field F of an element of a finite F-algebra that is integral over R (through R → F) is integral over R. Mathlib's Algebra.isIntegral_trace asks for a field on top, and K₁ ⊗ K₂ is not one.
  • tensorDiff_mul_mem_packetIntegers: for δ in the different of R₂ over ℤ_p and z in (R_E)^∼, (1 ⊗ δ) · z ∈ R_E. Proof: with a ℤ_p-basis b of R₂, its trace dual basis b^∨ spans 𝔇^{-1} (Submodule.traceDual_span_of_basis, coeSubmodule_differentIdeal), so δ b_j^∨ ∈ R₂; the coordinate of z on 1 ⊗ b_j^∨ is Tr_{(K₁ ⊗ K₂)/K₁}(z (1 ⊗ b_j)), integral by the previous item.
  • tensorDiff_generator_mul_mem_packetIntegers: the same for a generator δ of the different.
  • tensorDiff_order_mul_mem_packetIntegers: the same for any y ∈ K₂ with ord(y) = 𝔡_2 (spectral norm p ^ (−𝔡_2), 𝔡_2 = differentOrder at a prime P over p), which is the page's p ^ (𝔡_{I*}) for I* = {2}: Proposition 1.1 for two factors as printed.
  • tensorDiff_mul_mem_logUnit_span: for u_i with ord(u_i) = a_i, (u₁ ⊗ u₂ δ) · (R_E)^∼ lies in the span of log_p(R₁^×) ⊗ log_p(R₂^×): the first display of page 11 for two factors (with 𝔡_{I*} in place of 𝔡_I; the page's form with 𝔡_I is not derived), followed by Proposition 1.2 (i) (padicBridge_extLogUnit_image_fractionalIdeal).
Not proved
  • That (R_E)^∼ is the normalization of R_E in its total ring of fractions: not proved here; it is proved in TensorIndex.lean (tensorIdx_isFractionRing).
  • More than two factors (the induction on |I| of page 10), and the identification of K₁ ⊗[ℤ_p] K₂ with K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂.
  • Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (iv) themselves: not proved here; they are proved for two factors in TensorLogShell.lean.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorDiff_trace_one_tmultheorem

theorem tensorDiff_trace_one_tmul {R A M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
  [CommRing M] [Algebra R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] (y : M) :
  Algebra.trace A (TensorProduct R A M) (TensorProduct.tmul R (1 : A) y) =
    algebraMap R A (Algebra.trace R M y)

The trace of a base change on a pure tensor: for a finite free R-algebra M and any commutative R-algebra A, the trace of 1 ⊗ y in the A-algebra A ⊗[R] M is the image of the trace of y in M over R.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorDiff_isIntegralElem_tracetheorem

theorem tensorDiff_isIntegralElem_trace {R F S : Type*} [CommRing R] [Field F] [CommRing S]
  [Algebra F S] [Module.Finite F S] (φ : R →+* F) {w : S}
  (hw : ((algebraMap F S).comp φ).IsIntegralElem w) :
  φ.IsIntegralElem (Algebra.trace F S w)

The trace of an integral element is integral, for a finite algebra S over a field F that need not be a field (Mathlib's Algebra.isIntegral_trace asks for a field): if w ∈ S is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in R (through a ring map φ : R → F), then so is Tr_{S/F}(w). The proof base changes to an algebraic closure of F, where the trace is the sum of the eigenvalues of the multiplication by w, each a root of the same polynomial.

    ‖u₁‖ = (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p (P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p])))
  (hu₂ : letI := spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] K₂;
    ‖u₂‖ = (p : ℝ) ^ (-Proposition1_2.a p (P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p])))
  {z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂} (hz : z ∈ padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂) :
  TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] u₁ (u₂ * δ) * z ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure
    {w | ∃ x y, x ∈ @extLogUnit K₁ (spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] K₁) '' Set.range
        (fun u : (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁)ˣ => ((u : integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁) : K₁)) ∧
      y ∈ @extLogUnit K₂ (spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] K₂) '' Set.range
        (fun u : (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₂)ˣ => ((u : integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₂) : K₂)) ∧
      w = TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] x y}

The first display of the proof of IUT IV Proposition 1.2 (ii), for two factors (page 11), combined with Proposition 1.2 (i): with R_i = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K_i, e_i the ramification index of a prime P_i of R_i over p, a_i the constant of page 10, any u_i ∈ K_i with ord(u_i) = a_i (that is ‖u_i‖ = p ^ (-a_i) for the spectral norm), and δ in the different of R₂ over ℤ_p: for every z of (R_E)^∼, (u₁ ⊗ u₂ δ) · z lies in the additive span of the x ⊗ y with x ∈ log_p(R₁^×) and y ∈ log_p(R₂^×), the image of log_p(R₁^×) ⊗_{ℤ_p} log_p(R₂^×) in K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂. The page multiplies by p ^ (𝔡_I + a_I); here only the different of the second factor is used (I* = {2}), which is stronger.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorIndex

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/TensorIndex.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Packets, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorDifferent, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tame

The integral tensor order R_E of two finite extensions of ℚ_p: index and log-volume

Module documentation

Sources: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.1 (page 9, proof on pages 9 and 10), Proposition 1.2 (pages 10 and 11; page 10 read), Proposition 1.4 (pages 13 and 14). Pages read for this file: 9, 10, 13 and 14. Pages checked against rendered images: 9, 10, 13 and 14. Displays relied on:

  • page 9: R_E = ⊗_{i ∈ E} R_i "where the tensor product is over ℤ_p", p ^ (𝔡_{I*}) · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ R_I ⊆ (R_I)^∼, where (−)^∼ is "the normalization of the [reduced] ring in parentheses in its ring of fractions", and 𝔡_i ∈ ℚ_{≥0} is the order of any generator of the different ideal of R_i over ℤ_p. The exponent printed is 𝔡_{I*}, with no ceiling;
  • page 10: the proof of Proposition 1.1 reduces to |I| = 2, where the inclusion "follows immediately from the definition of the different ideal";
  • page 13, Proposition 1.4 (i): the log-volume on compact open subsets of the tensor products, "normalized so that μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0, μ^log(p · (R_E)^∼) = −log(p)";
  • page 14, proof of Proposition 1.4 (iii): "by assertion (i), we have μ^log(R_I) ≤ μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0", and the term μ^log(R_I) in the second line of the computation, μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) = ∑_{i ∈ I} μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) + μ^log(R_I). The pages do not print a formula for μ^log(R_I); the index formula below is a fact about the normalized log-volume used here, not a quotation.
The objects

Two factors: K₁, K₂ are finite extensions of ℚ_[p] (fields with finite-dimensional ℚ_[p]-algebra structures). As in IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume, the tensor product is taken over ℚ_p (for fields it agrees with the one over ℤ_p, packet_tensor_zp_bijective), and:

  • R_E is tensorIdxRing, the subring of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ additively spanned by the x ⊗ y with x, y integral over ℤ_p (the image of R₁ ⊗_{ℤ_p} R₂); its carrier is padicPacketIntegers (tensorIdxRing_coe);
  • (R_E)^∼ is tensorIdxNormRing, the subring of elements integral over ℤ_p; its carrier is padicPacketNormalization;
  • μ^log is padicPacketMuLog, normalized at (R_E)^∼: the logarithm of the ratio of Haar measures in the coordinates of Module.finBasis, divided by D = dim_{ℚ_p}(K₁ ⊗ K₂). It does not depend on the coordinates (padicPacketMuLog_coord_indep) nor on the Haar measure;
  • 𝔡_i is differentOrder ℤ_[p] R_i P at the prime P of R_i = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K_i over p (the exponent of P in the different divided by the ramification index);
  • the index [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] is AddSubgroup.relIndex of the additive groups, that is the cardinality of (R_E)^∼ / R_E (0 when infinite, which is excluded by tensorIdx_relIndex_ne_zero).
What is proved
  1. *R_E as a lattice.* tensorIdxRing is a subring and a ℤ_p-submodule (tensorIdx_smul_mem), R_E ≤ (R_E)^∼ (tensorIdxRing_le). tensorIdx_pow_mem_differentIdeal, tensorIdx_pow_smul_mem: p ^ k lies in the different of R₂ as soon as k · e₂ ≥ n₂ (exponent of the different), hence p ^ k · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E; tensorIdx_ceil_smul_mem: in particular p ^ ⌈𝔡_2⌉ · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E, and tensorIdx_ceil_smul_mem_left: p ^ ⌈𝔡_1⌉ · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E (exchanging the factors). tensorIdx_coord_isOpen_isCompact: in the coordinates of Module.finBasis, R_E and (R_E)^∼ are open and compact (R_E is a subgroup containing the open set p ^ k · (R_E)^∼). tensorIdx_relIndex_ne_zero: (R_E)^∼ / R_E is finite.
  2. Measure and log-volume. tensorIdx_measure_eq_relIndex (general): for subgroups H ≤ N with N / H finite, μ N = [N : H] · μ H for a translation invariant measure. tensorIdx_measure: R_E has positive finite Haar measure and μ((R_E)^∼) = [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] · μ(R_E). tensorIdx_muLog_eq: the index formula μ^log(R_E) = −log [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] / D. tensorIdx_muLog_nonpos: μ^log(R_E) ≤ 0, the inequality μ^log(R_I) ≤ μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0 of page 14 for |I| = 2. tensorIdx_muLog_ge_of_pow, tensorIdx_muLog_bounds, tensorIdx_muLog_bounds_left: −⌈𝔡_i⌉ log p ≤ μ^log(R_E) and [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] ≤ p ^ (⌈𝔡_i⌉ · D) for i = 1, 2.
  3. Normalization. tensorIdx_isIntegralElem_iff: z is integral over R_E if and only if z ∈ (R_E)^∼. tensorIdx_exists_pow_smul_mem_ring: every z is r / p ^ n with r ∈ R_E. tensorIdx_isFractionRing: K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ is the total ring of fractions of R_E (IsFractionRing). Together: (R_E)^∼ is the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions, the definition of page 9.
  4. Equality case and an example. tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_one (and _left): if K₂ (or K₁) has ramification index 1, then R_E = (R_E)^∼; tensorIdx_muLog_eq_zero_of_eq: then the index is 1 and μ^log(R_E) = 0. tensorIdxEx_ne, tensorIdxEx_muLog_neg: for K₁ = K₂ = K with [K : ℚ_p] = 2 and π ∈ K, π ^ 2 = p (every prime p), p⁻¹ (π ⊗ π) is integral but not in R_E, so [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] ≥ 2 and μ^log(R_E) < 0; tensorIdxEx_exists: such K exists (ℚ_p[X] / (X ^ 2 − p)).
Not proved
  • The sharp bound μ^log(R_E) ≥ −𝔡_2 log p without the ceiling: it would follow from (1 ⊗ δ) · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E (tensorDiff_mul_mem_packetIntegers) and the scaling of Haar measure by the multiplication by 1 ⊗ δ, whose modulus is ‖N_{K₂/ℚ_p}(δ)‖ ^ [K₁ : ℚ_p]; Haar scaling by an element of a tensor product (a determinant formula over ℚ_p) is not available here.
  • The exact index in the example (it is p for p odd by a computation of the ring of integers of K ⊗ K ≅ K × K); only the lower bound 2 is proved.
  • More than two factors, and the identification of K₁ ⊗[ℤ_p] K₂ with K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ for more than two factors.
  • The additivity of page 14, μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) = ∑_i μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) + μ^log(R_I), is out of scope here. For two factors it would need: that the image L of log_p(R₁^×) ⊗_{ℤ_p} log_p(R₂^×) in K₁ ⊗ K₂ is a lattice and the index formula relating the generalized index of L relative to R_E to those of L_i = log_p(R_i^×) relative to R_i; that is, the multiplicativity of generalized indices under tensor products of ℤ_p-lattices, [R₁ ⊗ R₂ : L₁ ⊗ L₂] = [R₁ : L₁] ^ (dim K₂) · [R₂ : L₂] ^ (dim K₁) (true by elementary divisors, not formalized), together with the identification of the image of L₁ ⊗_{ℤ_p} L₂ with the lattice spanned by the x ⊗ y, x ∈ L₁, y ∈ L₂.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_mem_coset_ifftheorem

theorem tensorIdx_mem_coset_iff {H N : AddSubgroup V} (hHN : H ≤ N)
  (q : ↥N ⧸ H.addSubgroupOf N) (x : V) :
  x ∈ ((Quotient.out q : N) : V) +ᵥ (H : Set V) ↔
    ∃ hx : x ∈ N, (QuotientAddGroup.mk (⟨x, hx⟩ : N) : ↥N ⧸ H.addSubgroupOf N) = q

The coset q of H in N, translated back into V: x lies in out(q) + H if and only if x ∈ N and the class of x in N / H is q.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_measure_eq_relIndextheorem

theorem tensorIdx_measure_eq_relIndex [MeasurableSpace V] [MeasurableAdd V] (μ : Measure V)
  [μ.IsAddLeftInvariant] {H N : AddSubgroup V} (hHN : H ≤ N)
  [Finite (↥N ⧸ H.addSubgroupOf N)] (hH : MeasurableSet (H : Set V)) :
  μ (N : Set V) = (H.relIndex N : ENNReal) * μ (H : Set V)

Measure of a subgroup of finite relative index: for subgroups H ≤ N of V with N / H finite, H measurable and μ invariant under translations, μ N = [N : H] · μ H. N is the disjoint union of the [N : H] translates of H by representatives of N / H.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_finite_quotienttheorem

theorem tensorIdx_finite_quotient [TopologicalSpace V] [IsTopologicalAddGroup V]
  {H N : AddSubgroup V} (hHN : H ≤ N) (hH : IsOpen (H : Set V))
  (hN : IsCompact (N : Set V)) : Finite (↥N ⧸ H.addSubgroupOf N)

An open subgroup of a compact subgroup has finite index: for subgroups H ≤ N of a topological group V with H open and N compact, N / H is finite.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxPureMonoiddef

noncomputable def tensorIdxPureMonoid : Submonoid (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) where
  carrier := {z | ∃ x y, padicVolIntegral p x ∧ padicVolIntegral p y ∧
    z = TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] x y}
  one_mem' := ⟨1, 1, tensorIdx_integral_one p, tensorIdx_integral_one p, rfl⟩
  mul_mem' := by
    rintro _ _ ⟨x, y, hx, hy, rfl⟩ ⟨x', y', hx', hy', rfl⟩
    exact ⟨x * x', y * y', RingHom.IsIntegralElem.mul _ hx hx',
      RingHom.IsIntegralElem.mul _ hy hy', Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul _ _ _ _⟩

The pure tensors x ⊗ y with x, y integral over ℤ_p, a multiplicative submonoid of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂; its additive span is R_E = padicPacketIntegers.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxRingdef

noncomputable def tensorIdxRing : Subring (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) where
  toSubsemiring := (tensorIdxPureMonoid p K₁ K₂).subsemiringClosure
  neg_mem' {z} hz := by
    have hz' : z ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure
        ((tensorIdxPureMonoid p K₁ K₂ : Set (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂))) := by
      rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, ← Submonoid.subsemiringClosure_coe]
      exact hz
    show -z ∈ (tensorIdxPureMonoid p K₁ K₂).subsemiringClosure
    rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, Submonoid.subsemiringClosure_coe, SetLike.mem_coe]
    clear hz
    induction hz' using AddSubmonoid.closure_induction with
    | mem w hw =>
      obtain ⟨x, y, hx, hy, rfl⟩ := hw
      exact AddSubmonoid.subset_closure ⟨-x, y, RingHom.IsIntegralElem.neg _ hx, hy,
        (TensorProduct.neg_tmul x y).symm⟩
    | zero => rw [neg_zero]; exact zero_mem _
    | add a b _ _ ha hb => rw [neg_add]; exact add_mem ha hb

**R_E = R₁ ⊗_{ℤ_p} R₂ as a subring of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂**: the additive span of the x ⊗ y with x, y integral over ℤ_p. Its carrier is padicPacketIntegers (tensorIdxRing_coe).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxRing_coetheorem

theorem tensorIdxRing_coe :
  (tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂ : Set (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)) = padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂

The carrier of tensorIdxRing is padicPacketIntegers.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxNormRingdef

noncomputable def tensorIdxNormRing : Subring (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) where
  carrier := padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂
  mul_mem' ha hb := RingHom.IsIntegralElem.mul _ ha hb
  one_mem' := tensorIdx_integral_one p
  add_mem' ha hb := RingHom.IsIntegralElem.add _ ha hb
  zero_mem' := by
    show padicVolIntegral p (0 : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)
    unfold padicVolIntegral
    rw [← RingHom.map_zero ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).comp
      (algebraMap ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p]))]
    exact RingHom.isIntegralElem_map _
  neg_mem' ha := RingHom.IsIntegralElem.neg _ ha

**(R_E)^∼ as a subring of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂**: the elements integral over ℤ_p. Its carrier is padicPacketNormalization.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_measuretheorem

theorem tensorIdx_measure :
  μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun ''
      padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) ≠ 0 ∧
    μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun ''
      padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) ≠ ⊤ ∧
    μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun ''
      padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂) =
      ((tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup.relIndex
        (tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup : ENNReal) *
      μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun ''
        padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂)

Positive finite measure and the index formula for Haar measure: in coordinates, R_E has positive finite Haar measure and μ((R_E)^∼) = [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] · μ(R_E).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_eqtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_eq :
  padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂)
      (padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) =
    -Real.log ((tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup.relIndex
        (tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup) /
      Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)

The index formula for the log-volume: normalized so that μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0 (the normalization of IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (i), page 13), μ^log(R_E) = −log [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] / dim_{ℚ_p}(K₁ ⊗ K₂).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_nonpostheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_nonpos :
  padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂)
      (padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) ≤ 0

**μ^log(R_E) ≤ 0 = μ^log((R_E)^∼)**, the inequality used on IUT IV page 14 (for two factors).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_ge_of_powtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_ge_of_pow {k : ℕ}
  (hk : ∀ z ∈ tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂, ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ k) • z ∈ tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂) :
  -(k * Real.log p) ≤ padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ
      (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂) (padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) ∧
    (tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup.relIndex (tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup ≤
      p ^ (k * Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂))

**Lower bound from an inclusion p ^ k · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E**: μ^log(R_E) ≥ −k log p, and [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] ≤ p ^ (k · dim (K₁ ⊗ K₂)).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_isIntegralElem_ifftheorem

theorem tensorIdx_isIntegralElem_iff (z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) :
  (tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂).subtype.IsIntegralElem z ↔ z ∈ tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂

**Integral over R_E if and only if integral over ℤ_p**: an element z of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in R_E if and only if it lies in (R_E)^∼. So (R_E)^∼ is the integral closure of R_E in K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_exists_pow_smul_mem_ringtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_exists_pow_smul_mem_ring (z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) :
  ∃ n : ℕ, ((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ n) • z ∈ tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂

**Every element is r / p ^ n with r ∈ R_E**: for every z of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ some p ^ n • z lies in R_E.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_natCast_pow_memtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_natCast_pow_mem (n : ℕ) :
  ((p : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)) ^ n ∈ tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂

p ^ n (the image of the natural number) lies in R_E and is a unit of K₁ ⊗ K₂.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_isFractionRingtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_isFractionRing :
  IsFractionRing (tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂) (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)

**K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ is the total ring of fractions of R_E**: IsFractionRing R_E (K₁ ⊗ K₂). Nonzerodivisors of R_E are nonzerodivisors of K₁ ⊗ K₂ (multiply by a power of p), hence units (multiplication by them is an injective ℚ_p-linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space); every element is r / p ^ n. With tensorIdx_isIntegralElem_iff, (R_E)^∼ is the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions, the definition of page 9.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_onetheorem

theorem tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_one [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K₂] [Algebra ℤ_[p] K₂]
  [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K₂] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₂)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] (he : P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] = 1) :
  tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂ = tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂

**R_E = (R_E)^∼ when K₂ is unramified over ℚ_p**: if the prime P of R₂ = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₂ over p has ramification index 1, the different of R₂ is trivial (differentExponent = e − 1 = 0, the tame case of Proposition 1.3 (i)), and p ^ 0 · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_comm_memtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_comm_mem {z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₂ K₁} (hz : z ∈ tensorIdxRing p K₂ K₁) :
  Algebra.TensorProduct.comm ℚ_[p] K₂ K₁ z ∈ tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂

comm : K₂ ⊗ K₁ → K₁ ⊗ K₂ maps R_E of (K₂, K₁) into R_E of (K₁, K₂).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_comm_commtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_comm_comm (w : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) :
  Algebra.TensorProduct.comm ℚ_[p] K₂ K₁ (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂ w) = w

Exchanging the factors twice is the identity.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_ceil_smul_mem_lefttheorem

theorem tensorIdx_ceil_smul_mem_left [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K₁] [Algebra ℤ_[p] K₁]
  [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K₁] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  {z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂} (hz : z ∈ tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂) :
  letI

**p ^ ⌈𝔡_1⌉ · (R_E)^∼ ⊆ R_E**, the inclusion of Proposition 1.1 with * = 2, I* = {1}: the different of the first factor, by exchanging the factors.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_one_lefttheorem

theorem tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_one_left [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K₁]
  [Algebra ℤ_[p] K₁] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K₁] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁))
  [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  (he : P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] = 1) :
  tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂ = tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂

**R_E = (R_E)^∼ when K₁ is unramified over ℚ_p**, by exchanging the factors.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_boundstheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_bounds [Algebra ℤ_[p] K₂] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K₂]
  (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₂)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] :
  letI

**−⌈𝔡_2⌉ log p ≤ μ^log(R_E) ≤ 0**, and [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] ≤ p ^ (⌈𝔡_2⌉ · dim (K₁ ⊗ K₂)), with 𝔡_2 the order of the different of R₂ at the prime P over p.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_bounds_lefttheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_bounds_left [Algebra ℤ_[p] K₁] [IsScalarTower ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p] K₁]
  (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁)) [P.IsPrime]
  [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] :
  letI

The same with the first factor: −⌈𝔡_1⌉ log p ≤ μ^log(R_E) and [(R_E)^∼ : R_E] ≤ p ^ (⌈𝔡_1⌉ · dim (K₁ ⊗ K₂)).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdx_muLog_eq_zero_of_eqtheorem

theorem tensorIdx_muLog_eq_zero_of_eq (h : tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂ = tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂) :
  (tensorIdxRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup.relIndex (tensorIdxNormRing p K₁ K₂).toAddSubgroup = 1 ∧
    padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂)
      (padicPacketIntegers p K₁ K₂) = 0

The equality case for the log-volume: if R_E = (R_E)^∼ (for example when one factor is unramified, tensorIdx_eq_of_ramificationIdx_eq_one), the index is 1 and μ^log(R_E) = 0.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_not_sqtheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_not_sq (x : ℚ_[p]) : x ^ 2 ≠ (p : ℚ_[p])

p has no square root in ℚ_p.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_coeff_le_onetheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_coeff_le_one {π : K} (hπ : π ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ_[p] K p) {a b : ℚ_[p]}
  (h : padicVolIntegral p (algebraMap ℚ_[p] K a + algebraMap ℚ_[p] K b * π)) : ‖b‖ ≤ 1

**The π-coordinate of an integral element is integral**: if π ^ 2 = p in K and a + b π (with a, b ∈ ℚ_p) is integral over ℤ_p, then ‖b‖ ≤ 1. For the spectral norm, ‖a‖ ∈ p ^ ℤ and ‖b π‖ ∈ p ^ (ℤ + 1/2) differ unless both vanish, so ‖a + b π‖ = max ‖a‖ ‖b π‖ ≥ ‖b‖ p ^ (−1/2).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExBasisdef

noncomputable def tensorIdxExBasis : Module.Basis (Fin 2) ℚ_[p] K :=
  basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank
    (LinearIndependent.pair_iff.2 fun s t hst => by
      by_cases ht : t = 0
      · subst ht
        rw [zero_smul, add_zero, smul_eq_zero] at hst
        exact ⟨hst.resolve_right one_ne_zero, rfl⟩
      · exfalso
        have hπ' : π = algebraMap ℚ_[p] K (-s / t) := by
          rw [Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def, mul_one] at hst
          rw [map_div₀, map_neg, eq_div_iff ((map_ne_zero _).2 ht), mul_comm]
          exact (eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_right hst)
        rw [hπ', ← map_pow] at hπ
        exact tensorIdxEx_not_sq p _ ((algebraMap ℚ_[p] K).injective hπ))
    (by rw [Fintype.card_fin, hK])

1, π is a ℚ_p-basis of K.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExBasis_applytheorem

theorem tensorIdxExBasis_apply (i : Fin 2) :
  tensorIdxExBasis p hK hπ i = ![1, π] i

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExCoorddef

noncomputable def tensorIdxExCoord : K →ₗ[ℚ_[p]] ℚ_[p] := (tensorIdxExBasis p hK hπ).coord 1

The π-coordinate functional a + b π ↦ b.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExCoord_le_onetheorem

theorem tensorIdxExCoord_le_one {x : K} (hx : padicVolIntegral p x) :
  ‖tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ x‖ ≤ 1

The coordinate of an integral element is in ℤ_p.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_unit_mul_selftheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_unit_mul_self :
  ((p : ℚ_[p])⁻¹ • TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] π π) *
      ((p : ℚ_[p])⁻¹ • TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] π π) = (1 : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K)

u = p⁻¹ (π ⊗ π) satisfies u * u = 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_unit_memtheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_unit_mem :
  (p : ℚ_[p])⁻¹ • TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] π π ∈ tensorIdxNormRing p K K

u = p⁻¹ (π ⊗ π) lies in (R_E)^∼: it is a root of X ^ 2 − 1.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExFormdef

noncomputable def tensorIdxExForm : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K →ₗ[ℚ_[p]] ℚ_[p] :=
  TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.mul ℚ_[p] ℚ_[p]).compl₁₂ (tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ)
    (tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ))

The functional x ⊗ y ↦ b(x) b(y) on K ⊗ K, with b the π-coordinate.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExForm_tmultheorem

theorem tensorIdxExForm_tmul (x y : K) :
  tensorIdxExForm p hK hπ (TensorProduct.tmul ℚ_[p] x y) =
    tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ x * tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ y

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExForm_le_onetheorem

theorem tensorIdxExForm_le_one {z : TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K}
  (hz : z ∈ padicPacketIntegers p K K) : ‖tensorIdxExForm p hK hπ z‖ ≤ 1

The functional is ℤ_p-valued on R_E.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxExCoord_pitheorem

theorem tensorIdxExCoord_pi : tensorIdxExCoord p hK hπ π = 1

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_netheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_ne : tensorIdxRing p K K ≠ tensorIdxNormRing p K K

**R_E ≠ (R_E)^∼ for K₁ = K₂ = K, [K : ℚ_p] = 2, π ^ 2 = p** (any prime p): u = p⁻¹ (π ⊗ π) is integral (u ^ 2 = 1) but the functional x ⊗ y ↦ b(x) b(y), which is ℤ_p-valued on R_E, takes the value p⁻¹ at u.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_muLog_negtheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_muLog_neg
  [MeasurableSpace (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K)) → ℚ_[p])]
  [BorelSpace (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K)) → ℚ_[p])]
  (μ : Measure (Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K)) → ℚ_[p]))
  [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] :
  2 ≤ (tensorIdxRing p K K).toAddSubgroup.relIndex (tensorIdxNormRing p K K).toAddSubgroup ∧
    padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K K) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K K)
      (padicPacketIntegers p K K) < 0

**In the example the index is at least 2 and μ^log(R_E) < 0.**

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorIdxEx_existstheorem

theorem tensorIdxEx_exists (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
  ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra ℚ_[p] K) (_ : FiniteDimensional ℚ_[p] K),
    Module.finrank ℚ_[p] K = 2 ∧ ∃ π : K, π ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ_[p] K p

The example exists: there is a field K, finite-dimensional of degree 2 over ℚ_p, with an element π such that π ^ 2 = p (namely ℚ_p[X] / (X ^ 2 − p); X ^ 2 − p is irreducible since p is not a square in ℚ_p). So the hypotheses of tensorIdxEx_ne and tensorIdxEx_muLog_neg are satisfiable.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorLogShell

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/TensorLogShell.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorDifferent, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Packets, IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tame

IUT IV, Propositions 1.2 (ii) to (iv) and 1.4 (iii), (iv) for two tensor factors

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.2 (page 10) with its proof (page 11), Proposition 1.4 (page 13) with its proof (pages 13 and 14). Pages read for this file: 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15. Pages checked against rendered images: 10, 11, 13 and 14 (page 15, Proposition 1.5, is not used). Displays formalized, as printed:

  • page 10: log_p(R_E^×) = ⊗_{i ∈ E} log_p(R_i^×), "where the tensor product is over ℤ_p"; "For λ ∈ (1/e_i) · ℤ, we shall write p^λ · R_i for the fractional ideal of R_i generated by any element p^λ of k_i such that ord(p^λ) = λ"; φ is "an automorphism of the finite dimensional ℚ_p-vector space log_p(R_I^×) ⊗ ℚ_p that induces an automorphism of the submodule log_p(R_I^×)";
  • page 10, (ii): φ(p^λ · (R_I)^∼) ⊆ p^{⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋} · log_p(R_I^×) ⊆ p^{⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋ − b_I} · (R_I)^∼ "for any λ ∈ (1/e_i) · ℤ, i ∈ I"; "In particular, φ((R_I)^∼) ⊆ p^{−⌈𝔡_I + a_I⌉} · log_p(R_I^×) ⊆ p^{−⌈𝔡_I + a_I⌉ − b_I} · (R_I)^∼";
  • page 11, (iii): "Suppose that p > 2, and that e_i ≤ p − 2 for all i ∈ I. Then φ(p^λ · (R_I)^∼) ⊆ p^{λ − 𝔡_I − 1} · (R_I)^∼"; "In particular φ((R_I)^∼) ⊆ p^{−𝔡_I − 1} · (R_I)^∼";
  • page 11, (iv): "If p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i ∈ I, then φ((R_I)^∼) ⊆ (R_I)^∼";
  • page 11, proof: p^{𝔡_I + a_I} · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ ⊗_{i ∈ I} p^{a_i} · R_i (⊆ R_I = ⊗ R_i), then (i) on each factor; (iv) "follows from (ii)" with 𝔡_I = 0, a_I = −b_I ∈ ℤ;
  • page 13, (iii): for I* ⊆ I with p − 2 ≥ e_i (≥ 1) for i ∈ I \ I* and λ ∈ (1/e_{i†}) · ℤ, the inclusions of (ii) and the inequalities μ^log(p^{⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋} · log_p(R_I^×)) ≤ (−λ + 𝔡_I + 1 + 4 · |I*|/p) · log(p) and μ^log(p^{⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋ − b_I} · (R_I)^∼) ≤ (−λ + 𝔡_I + 1) · log(p) + ∑_{i ∈ I*} {3 + log(e_i)}; "Moreover, 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ |I| if p > 2; 𝔡_I + a_I ≥ 2 · |I| if p = 2";
  • page 13, (iv): "If p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i ∈ I, then φ((R_I)^∼) ⊆ (R_I)^∼, and μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0"; page 13, (i): the normalization μ^log((R_E)^∼) = 0.
The objects and interpretation choices

K₁, K₂ are finite extensions of ℚ_[p] and R_i = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K_i; two factors only, I = {1, 2}. As in IUT.Prerequisites.PadicVolume, R_I is the additive span of the x ⊗ y (x, y integral) in K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ and (R_I)^∼ is the set of elements integral over ℤ_p (padicPacketNormalization). ord is read through the spectral norm, ord(x) = λ ⟺ ‖x‖ = p ^ (−λ). e_i, 𝔡_i are the ramification index and differentOrder at a prime P_i of R_i over p (tensorLogDiffOrder); a_i, b_i are Proposition1_2.a, Proposition1_2.b at e_i; 𝔡_I = 𝔡_1 + 𝔡_2, a_I = a_1 + a_2, b_I = b_1 + b_2.

  • log_p(R_I^×) (tensorLogLattice) is the image in K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ of log_p(R_1^×) ⊗_{ℤ_p} log_p(R_2^×): the ℤ_p-span of the log_p(u₁) ⊗ log_p(u₂). Its ℚ_p-span is K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ (tensorLog_span_lattice), so φ is taken as a ℚ_p-linear automorphism of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ with φ(log_p(R_I^×)) = log_p(R_I^×) (the printed "induces an automorphism of the submodule").
  • p^μ · (R_I)^∼, for μ real, is (x ⊗ y) · (R_I)^∼ (tensorLogShift) for any x, y with ‖x‖ ‖y‖ = p ^ (−μ); it depends only on ‖x‖ ‖y‖ (tensorLogShift_subset both ways). The printed p^λ is an element of one k_i, that is x = p^λ, y = 1 or the reverse. The theorems hold for every real λ with such a representative; for λ ∈ (1/e_i) ℤ one exists (padicBridge_exists_norm_eq_rpow). Integer powers p ^ n · S are the scalar action of (p : ℚ_p) ^ n.
  • p^{k − b_I} · (R_I)^∼ is written p ^ k · ((z₁ ⊗ z₂) · (R_I)^∼) with ord(z_i) = −b_i.
  • μ^log is padicPacketMuLog with reference set (R_I)^∼, so μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0 holds by construction (padicPacketMuLog_self); tensorLog_normalization_measure shows the reference set has positive finite Haar measure.
What is proved
  • tensorLog_tmul_mem_normalization: x ⊗ y ∈ (R_I)^∼ when ‖x‖ ‖y‖ ≤ 1.
  • The two inclusions of page 11 around log_p(R_I^×): tensorLog_shift_subset_lattice (p^{𝔡_I + a_I} · (R_I)^∼ ⊆ log_p(R_I^×), through the first display tensorLog_shift_subset_integers and tensorLog_mul_integers_subset_lattice) and tensorLog_lattice_subset_shift (log_p(R_I^×) ⊆ p^{−b_I} · (R_I)^∼).
  • tensorLog_prop1_2_ii, tensorLog_prop1_2_ii_zero: Proposition 1.2 (ii) and its "in particular", for every φ as above.
  • tensorLog_prop1_2_iii, tensorLog_prop1_2_iii_zero: Proposition 1.2 (iii).
  • tensorLog_prop1_2_iv: Proposition 1.2 (iv).
  • tensorLog_muLog_shift: μ^log((x ⊗ y) · (R_I)^∼) = log(‖x‖ ‖y‖).
  • tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_shift: the second inequality of Proposition 1.4 (iii), for every I* as printed.
  • tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_lattice: the first inequality of Proposition 1.4 (iii) when p > 2 and e_1, e_2 ≤ p − 2 (every I*).
  • tensorLog_dI_add_aI_ge: the last sentence of Proposition 1.4 (iii).
  • tensorLog_prop1_4_iv: Proposition 1.4 (iv).
  • Nonvacuity for K₁ = K₂ = ℚ_p, p > 2: e = 1 (tensorLog_padic_ramificationIdx), log_p(ℤ_p^×) = p ℤ_p (tensorLog_padic_units), log_p(R_I^×) = p ^ 2 ℤ_p · (1 ⊗ 1) (tensorLog_padic_lattice), (R_I)^∼ = ℤ_p · (1 ⊗ 1) (tensorLog_padic_normalization), and tensorLog_padic_prop1_2_iv: φ = −id satisfies the hypothesis of (iv) and (iv) applies.
Not proved
  • The first inequality of Proposition 1.4 (iii) when some e_i > p − 2. The page 14 proof uses μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) = ∑_i μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) + μ^log(R_I) (additivity over the tensor factors) and μ^log(R_I) ≤ 0; the additivity is not formalized.
  • That log_p(R_1^×) ⊗_{ℤ_p} log_p(R_2^×) → K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ is injective, so that the image used here is the printed tensor product. The normalization property of (R_I)^∼ is proved for two factors in IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.TensorIndex (tensorIdx_isFractionRing).
  • More than two factors.

By tensorLogShift_subset it depends only on ‖x‖ ‖y‖; for λ ∈ (1 / e_1) ℤ the page's p ^ λ · (R_I)^∼ is tensorLogShift t 1 with ord(t) = λ (similarly in the second factor).

Let φ be a ℚ_p-linear automorphism of K₁ ⊗[ℚ_p] K₂ (the ℚ_p-span of log_p(R_I^×), tensorLog_span_lattice) that maps log_p(R_I^×) onto itself. theorem tensorLog_muLog_cocycle {Λ B A : Set (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)}
  (hΛ0 : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' Λ) ≠ 0)
  (hΛ : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' Λ) ≠ ⊤)
  (hB0 : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' B) ≠ 0)
  (hB : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' B) ≠ ⊤)
  (hA0 : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' A) ≠ 0)
  (hA : μ ((Module.finBasis ℚ_[p] (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂)).equivFun '' A) ≠ ⊤) :
  padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ Λ A =
    padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ Λ B +
      padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ B A

The cocycle relation μ^log(Λ, A) = μ^log(Λ, B) + μ^log(B, A) for sets of positive finite measure.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorLog_muLog_shifttheorem

theorem tensorLog_muLog_shift {x : K₁} {y : K₂} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) :
  letI

**The log-volume of p ^ μ · (R_I)^∼**: for nonzero x, y, μ^log((x ⊗ y) · (R_I)^∼) = log(‖x‖ ‖y‖), that is −μ log p when ‖x‖ ‖y‖ = p ^ (−μ). Proof: n μ^log((x ⊗ y)(R_I)^∼) = μ^log((x ⊗ y) ^ n (R_I)^∼) by the cocycle relation and the invariance under multiplication by a unit, and (x ⊗ y) ^ n = p ^ m (x' ⊗ y') with (x' ⊗ y') (R_I)^∼ = (R_I)^∼.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_shifttheorem

theorem tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_shift (Istar : Finset (Fin 2))
  (hIstar : ∀ i, i ∉ Istar →
    (![P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p], P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i ≤ p - 2)
  (lam : ℝ) {z₁ : K₁} {z₂ : K₂}
  (hz₁ : letI := spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] K₁
    ‖z₁‖ = (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p (P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p])))
  (hz₂ : letI := spectralNorm.normedField ℚ_[p] K₂
    ‖z₂‖ = (p : ℝ) ^ (Proposition1_2.b p (P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]))) :
  padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂)
      (((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ ⌊lam - (tensorLogDiffOrder p K₁ P₁ + tensorLogDiffOrder p K₂ P₂) -
        (Proposition1_2.a p (P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]) +
          Proposition1_2.a p (P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]))⌋) • tensorLogShift p K₁ K₂ z₁ z₂) ≤
    (-lam + (tensorLogDiffOrder p K₁ P₁ + tensorLogDiffOrder p K₂ P₂) + 1) * Real.log p +
      ∑ i ∈ Istar, (3 + Real.log
        (((![P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p], P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i : ℕ) : ℝ))

IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (iii), second inequality, for two factors (page 13, proof on page 14). Let I* ⊆ I = {1, 2} be such that e_i ≤ p − 2 for i ∉ I*. For every real λ and z_i with ord(z_i) = −b_i: μ^log(p ^ ⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋ · (p ^ (−b_I) · (R_I)^∼)) ≤ (−λ + 𝔡_I + 1) log p + ∑_{i ∈ I*} (3 + log e_i). The log-volume is the packet log-volume normalized by μ^log((R_I)^∼) = 0; the exact value μ^log(p ^ (−b_I) · (R_I)^∼) = b_I log p is tensorLog_muLog_shift, and the summation is Proposition1_4.iii_second.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_latticetheorem

theorem tensorLog_prop1_4_iii_lattice (hp2 : 2 < p) (he₁ : P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] ≤ p - 2)
  (he₂ : P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] ≤ p - 2) (Istar : Finset (Fin 2)) (lam : ℝ) :
  padicPacketMuLog p (TensorProduct ℚ_[p] K₁ K₂) μ (padicPacketNormalization p K₁ K₂)
      (((p : ℚ_[p]) ^ ⌊lam - (tensorLogDiffOrder p K₁ P₁ + tensorLogDiffOrder p K₂ P₂) -
        (Proposition1_2.a p (P₁.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]) +
          Proposition1_2.a p (P₂.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]))⌋) • tensorLogLattice p K₁ K₂) ≤
    (-lam + (tensorLogDiffOrder p K₁ P₁ + tensorLogDiffOrder p K₂ P₂) + 1 +
      4 * Istar.card / p) * Real.log p

**IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (iii), first inequality, for two factors, in the case e_1, e_2 ≤ p − 2** (page 13): if p > 2 and e_i ≤ p − 2 for i = 1, 2, then for every I* ⊆ I and real λ, μ^log(p ^ ⌊λ − 𝔡_I − a_I⌋ · log_p(R_I^×)) ≤ (−λ + 𝔡_I + 1 + 4 |I*| / p) log p. The proof bounds μ^log(log_p(R_I^×)) by μ^log(p ^ (−b_I) · (R_I)^∼) = b_I log p = −a_I log p instead of the additivity over the tensor factors used on page 14; for e_i > p − 2 that bound is too weak and the case is not covered.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tower

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/Tower.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tame

IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 over a general base field k_0

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.3 and its proof, pages 11 and 12 of the April 2020 manuscript, with the notation of Proposition 1.1 (page 9). Pages read for this file: 9, 11, 12 and 13. Pages checked against rendered images: 9, 11, 12 and 13 (the normalization ord(p) = 1 and the definition of the order 𝔡_i of the different on page 9; the notation R_0, 𝔡_0, e_0, e_{i/0} = e_i/e_0, [k_i : k_0], n_i and the inequality of (i) on page 11; the tame equality of (i), assertion (ii) and the proof on page 12; Remark 1.3.1 on page 13).

The statement of the paper

Page 11: for a subfield ℚ_p ⊆ k_0 ⊆ k_i, R_0 is the ring of integers of k_0, 𝔡_0 the order (ord, with ord(p) = 1) of a generator of the different of R_0 over ℤ_p, e_0 the ramification index of k_0 over ℚ_p, e_{i/0} = e_i/e_0, and n_i the nonnegative integer with [k_i : k_0]/p^{n_i} an integer prime to p. Then (i) 𝔡_i ≥ 𝔡_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/(e_{i/0}·e_0) = 𝔡_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i, with equality if k_i is tamely ramified over k_0 (page 12); (ii) if k_i is a finite Galois extension of a subfield k_1 with k_0 ⊆ k_1 and k_1 tamely ramified over k_0, then 𝔡_i ≤ 𝔡_0 + n_i + 1/e_0.

The objects

K = k_0 and L = k_i are fields with finite-dimensional ℚ_[p]-algebra structures, an algebra map K → L compatible with them, and compatible ℤ_[p]-algebra structures. R_K = integralClosure ℤ_[p] K and R_L = integralClosure ℤ_[p] L are the rings of integers; towerAlgebra is the inclusion R_K → R_L (a definition of the algebra map, used with letI). P₀ and P are primes of R_K and R_L over pℤ_p (each is the maximal ideal, by padicBridge_prime_eq_maximalIdeal; tower_liesOver shows that P lies over P₀). e_K = e_0 and e_L = e_i are the ramification indices of P₀ and P over pℤ_p, and e_{L/K} = e_{i/0} is that of P over P₀; towerRamificationIdx_eq_mul proves e_L = e_K·e_{L/K}, so the paper's e_i/e_0 is this relative index. 𝔡_K = differentOrder ℤ_[p] R_K P₀ and 𝔡_L = differentOrder ℤ_[p] R_L P (exponent of the different divided by the ramification index; the normalization ord(p) = 1 of page 9). The residue fields are finite, so L is tamely ramified over K exactly when p does not divide e_{L/K}; this is the reading of "tamely ramified" used below. n_i = multiplicity p [L : K].

What is proved

General local results (a Dedekind domain A, the integral closure B of A in a finite separable extension of Frac(A), B local, p ⊆ A maximal and nonzero, P the prime of B): tower_map_eq_pow (pB = P^e), tower_trace_quotient_pow, tower_intTrace_mk_eq (the trace to A ⧸ p is e times the residue trace), and tower_differentExponent_eq_of_ne_zero, the tame equality v_P(𝔇_{B/A}) = e - 1 when A ⧸ p is finite and e ≠ 0 in A ⧸ p. These adapt the argument of IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.Tame from the base ℤ_[p] to a general base.

For ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ L:

  1. Transitivity: towerRamificationIdx_eq_mul (e_L = e_K·e_{L/K}), towerDifferentExponent_eq (v_P(𝔇_{L/ℚ_p}) = v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) + e_{L/K}·v_{P₀}(𝔇_{K/ℚ_p})), and towerDifferentOrder_eq, 𝔡_L = 𝔡_K + 𝔡_{L/K}/e_K, where 𝔡_{L/K} = differentOrder R_K R_L P is the order of the relative different normalized by ord(π_K) = 1.
  2. Proposition 1.3 (i): towerProp1_3i_ge, 𝔡_L ≥ 𝔡_K + (e_{L/K} - 1)/e_L; the relative tame equality towerDifferentExponent_rel_eq_of_tame; and towerProp1_3i_eq_of_tame, 𝔡_L = 𝔡_K + (e_{L/K} - 1)/e_L when p ∤ e_{L/K}.
  3. Proposition 1.3 (ii), special cases: towerProp1_3ii_of_tame (L/K tame; this is the case k_1 = k_i, where the Galois hypothesis holds trivially), towerProp1_3ii_of_not_dvd_finrank (n_i = 0, the base case of the paper's induction, without the Galois hypothesis; it uses towerRamificationIdx_dvd_finrank, e_{L/K} ∣ [L : K]), and the conditional towerProp1_3ii_of_exponent_bound: (ii) for every finite L/K, with no Galois hypothesis, from the hypothesis v_P(𝔇_{L/K}) ≤ e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}). That hypothesis is the classical upper bound for the different of an extension of local fields; it is not in Mathlib at the pinned version, and it is proved in IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/DifferentBound.lean (diffBound_exponent_le), which also proves (ii) for every finite L/K.

towerProp1_3iiStatement states assertion (ii) with the hypotheses of page 12 (an intermediate field K₁ with L/K₁ Galois and K₁/K tame). It is a definition, not a theorem. It is proved for all parameters in DifferentBound.lean (diffBound_towerProp1_3iiStatement).

Not proved
  • The paper's proof of Proposition 1.3 (ii) (page 12: reduction to totally ramified extensions, induction on n_i through a Galois p-subextension of degree p, a primitive p-th root of unity with e_1 ≥ p/ε, the different of a Kummer extension x^p - ϖ_*) is not formalized; (ii) is proved by another route in DifferentBound.lean.
  • The converse of the tame equality over a general base (that equality in (i) forces tameness) is not formalized here; for k_0 = ℚ_p it is differentExponent_eq_ramificationIdx_sub_one_iff_padic.

theorem towerProp1_3ii_of_exponent_bound (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) [P₀.IsPrime]
  [P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])] (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L))
  [P.IsPrime] [P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])]
  (hbound : letI := isDedekindDomain_ringOfIntegers_padic p K
    letI := isDedekindDomain_ringOfIntegers_padic p L
    letI := towerAlgebra p K L
    letI := tower_isTorsionFree p K L
    differentExponent (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K) (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L) P ≤
      P.ramificationIdx (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K) - 1 +
        P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] * multiplicity p (P.ramificationIdx (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K))) :
  letI

Proposition 1.3 (ii) from an upper bound on the relative different (page 12). Assume the exponent of P in the different of R_L over R_K is at most e_{L/K} - 1 + e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}), where e_L = e_{L/ℚ_p}, so that e_L·v_p(e_{L/K}) is the valuation at P of the integer e_{L/K} (this is the classical upper bound for the different of an extension of local fields; it is not in Mathlib at the pinned version; it is proved in DifferentBound.lean as diffBound_exponent_le). Then 𝔡_L ≤ 𝔡_K + n + 1/e_K with n = v_p([L : K]), with no Galois or tameness hypothesis.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.towerProp1_3iiStatementdef

def towerProp1_3iiStatement : Prop :=
  IsGalois K₁ L →
    (∀ P₁ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K₁), P₁.IsPrime →
      P₁.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]) →
      letI := towerAlgebra p K K₁
      ¬ p ∣ P₁.ramificationIdx (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) →
    ∀ (P₀ : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K)) (P : Ideal (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L)),
      P₀.IsPrime → P₀.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]) →
      P.IsPrime → P.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]) →
      letI := isDedekindDomain_ringOfIntegers_padic p K
      letI := isDedekindDomain_ringOfIntegers_padic p L
      letI := isTorsionFree_ringOfIntegers_padic p K
      letI := isTorsionFree_ringOfIntegers_padic p L
      differentOrder ℤ_[p] (integralClosure ℤ_[p] L) P ≤
        differentOrder ℤ_[p] (integralClosure ℤ_[p] K) P₀ +
          (multiplicity p (Module.finrank K L) : ℝ) + 1 / P₀.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p]

The statement of IUT IV, Proposition 1.3 (ii) (page 12), for finite extensions ℚ_p ⊆ K ⊆ K₁ ⊆ L (the paper's k_0 ⊆ k_1 ⊆ k_i): if L is Galois over K₁ and K₁ is tamely ramified over K (p does not divide the ramification index of the prime of R_{K₁} over R_K), then 𝔡_L ≤ 𝔡_K + n + 1/e_K, where n = v_p([L : K]) (the paper's n_i, defined on page 11), 𝔡_K, 𝔡_L are the orders of the differents normalized by ord(p) = 1, and e_K is the ramification index of K over ℚ_p. Proved in DifferentBound.lean (diffBound_towerProp1_3iiStatement).

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.UnitVolume

IUT/PaperIV/LocalFields/UnitVolume.lean · imports IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.VolumeBridge

IUT IV Proposition 1.4 (ii): the log-volume of log_p(R^×)

Module documentation

Source: Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV, Proposition 1.4 (ii) and its proof, pages 13 and 14, with the notation of Propositions 1.1 and 1.2 on pages 9 and 10. Pages read for this file: 9, 10, 13 and 14. Pages checked against rendered images: the same. Displays relied on:

  • page 9: ord normalized by ord(p) = 1; R_i = 𝒪_{k_i} the ring of integers of a finite extension k_i of ℚ_p;
  • page 10: e_i the ramification index of k_i over ℚ_p; log_p the p-adic logarithm;
  • page 13, the preamble of Proposition 1.4: R_i^μ ⊆ R_i^× the torsion subgroup, R_i^{×μ} = R_i^× / R_i^μ, p ^ (f_i) the cardinality of the residue field of k_i, p ^ (m_i) the order of the p-primary component of R_i^μ, and "Thus, the order of R_i^μ is equal to p ^ (m_i) · (p ^ (f_i) − 1)"; assertion (i), the normalization μ^log(R_i) = 0, μ^log(p · R_i) = −log(p) "by dividing by the degree of the finite extension"; assertion (ii) μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) = −(1 / e_i + m_i / (e_i f_i)) · log(p);
  • page 14, the proof of (ii): μ^log(log_p(R_i^×)) = μ^log(R_i^{×μ}), e_i f_i μ^log(R_i^{×μ}) = e_i f_i μ^log(R_i^×) − log(p ^ (m_i) · (p ^ (f_i) − 1)), e_i f_i μ^log(R_i^×) = log(1 − p ^ (−f_i)), hence e_i f_i μ^log(R_i^{×μ}) = −(f_i + m_i) · log(p).
The objects

As in IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.VolumeBridge: L is a finite extension of ℚ_[p] normed by its spectral norm, with the Borel structure; R = integralClosure ℤ_[p] L; R^× is the image in L of the unit group of R; log_p is extLogUnit of Logarithm.lean; e = P.ramificationIdx ℤ_[p] for a prime P of R over p (there is only one); μ^log is padicMuLog, normalized at R and divided by [L : ℚ_p]. New here:

  • f = unitVolResidueDegree p L, Mathlib's Ideal.inertiaDeg of the maximal ideal of R; unitVol_card_residueField: the residue field R ⧸ P has p ^ f elements;
  • R^μ = CommGroup.torsion (R)ˣ, and m = unitVolTorsionExponent p L, defined by p ^ m = |CommGroup.primaryComponent (R)ˣ p|; unitVol_card_primaryComponent: this component (the elements of p-power order, which all lie in R^μ) is finite of order p ^ m.

The measure on R^× is the restriction of an additive Haar measure of L, as in the formula e_i f_i μ^log(R_i^×) = log(1 − p ^ (−f_i)) of page 14. The paper passes to the quotient R^{×μ} and uses the compatibility of the log-volume with log_p ([AbsTopIII] Proposition 5.7, (i), (c)); here that step is replaced by a counting argument inside L (below), so no measure on the quotient group and no result of [AbsTopIII] is used.

What is proved
  1. unitVol_ramificationIdx_mul_residueDegree: e f = [L : ℚ_p] (Mathlib's Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank with one prime, and IsIntegralClosure.rank); unitVol_card_residueField: |R ⧸ P| = p ^ f.
  2. unitVol_measure_units: μ(R^×) = μ(R) − p ^ (−f) μ(R) for every additive Haar measure: the nonunits are ϖ R, of measure ‖ϖ‖ ^ (e f) μ(R) = p ^ (−f) μ(R).
  3. unitVol_measure_logUnit_mul_card (with the normed form unitVol_measure_logUnit_mul_card_of_normed): log_p u = 0 exactly for u ∈ R^μ (unitVol_extLogUnit_eq_zero_iff), R^μ is finite, and μ(log_p(R^×)) · |R^μ| = μ(R^×). The proof takes r = 1 / (2p), so that x ↦ log(1 + x) maps the ball B_r = {‖x‖ ≤ r} bijectively onto itself (extLogOnePlus_image_closedBall, extLogOnePlus_injOn of Logarithm.lean); then U_r = 1 + B_r is a subgroup of R^× on which log_p is injective with image B_r, R^× is a disjoint union of [R^× : U_r] balls u + B_r, log_p(R^×) is a disjoint union of [log_p(R^×) : B_r] balls z + B_r (unitVol_measure_range_eq_index, which also gives the finiteness of the indices), and [R^× : U_r] = |ker log_p| · [log_p(R^×) : B_r] since log_p⁻¹(B_r) = ker log_p · U_r and ker log_p ∩ U_r = 1. An element of the kernel has its [R^× : U_r]-th power in U_r, hence equal to 1; so the kernel is R^μ.
  4. unitVol_card_torsion: |R^μ| = p ^ m (p ^ f − 1), the sentence of page 13. Reduction modulo P maps R^μ onto (R ⧸ P)^× (Hensel's lemma for X ^ (p ^ f − 1) − 1, from Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing and unitVol_isAdicComplete: R is P-adically complete), with kernel the p-primary component.
  5. Proposition 1.4 (ii): unitVol_muLog_logUnit_eq_card: μ^log(log_p(R^×)) = (log(1 − p ^ (−f)) − log |R^μ|) / (e f); unitVol_muLog_logUnit_eq_of_card: the value −(1 / e + m / (e f)) log p from the order count; unitVol_muLog_logUnit_eq: the same with the order count proved, for every additive Haar measure, with no hypothesis beyond the setting.
  6. unitVol_card_torsion_of_le: for p > 2 and e ≤ p − 2, |R^μ| = p ^ f − 1 and m = 0, by comparing with volBridge_muLog_logUnit_eq_of_le (the equality case of Proposition 1.2 (i)); so that value is the case m = 0 of (ii).
Not proved
  • The log-volume of [AbsTopIII] Proposition 5.7 itself, the quotient R^{×μ} with its induced log-volume, and the compatibility of log-volumes with log_p cited on page 14: the statement is proved for the Haar measure of L restricted to R^× and log_p(R^×), which is the model of μ^log used in VolumeBridge.lean.
  • Tensor packets: (ii) concerns one field k_i; the sums over i ∈ I used on page 14 for (iii) are not formalized here. For two factors, (iv), the second inequality of (iii) and the first inequality of (iii) when every e_i ≤ p − 2 are proved in TensorLogShell.lean, without the additivity over the factors.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.unitVol_measure_range_eq_indextheorem

theorem unitVol_measure_range_eq_index {K : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace K] [MeasurableSpace K]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace K] (μ : Measure K) {A : Type*} [Group A] (V : Subgroup A)
  (φ : A → K) (hφ : Function.Injective φ) {r : ℝ} {c : ENNReal}
  (hcoset : ∀ a : A, φ '' {b | a⁻¹ * b ∈ V} = Metric.closedBall (φ a) r)
  (hball : ∀ x : K, μ (Metric.closedBall x r) = c) (h0 : c ≠ 0)
  (htop : μ (Set.range φ) ≠ ⊤) :
  V.FiniteIndex ∧ μ (Set.range φ) = V.index * c

Counting cosets by measure. Let φ : A → K be an injective map from a group A to a metric space with a measure, and V a subgroup of A such that φ maps every left coset a V onto the closed ball of radius r around φ a. If these balls all have the same measure c ≠ 0 and φ (A) has finite measure, then V has finite index and μ (φ (A)) = [A : V] · c.

IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.unitVol_extLogUnit_multheorem

log (u v) = log u + log v for ‖u‖ = ‖v‖ = 1 in a finite extension of ℚ_p.
